title: Spare-teacher warning fires on units that are not teaching
description:
Raised by the navigator while replanning ah-dwk6 after its verification failed.

The navigator's words: "teaching warning should only be on units actually TEACHing this month. Only warn if they have free slots. Not someone not teaching."

Today the teacher-has-free-slots check offers any unit whose month is not otherwise spoken for as a candidate teacher for the students in its hex, and warns about the slots it is not filling. That is what Ordered::is_busy exists for (crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs:348-370): it answers "is this unit's month already spoken for by something other than teaching", and any unit for which it returns false becomes a candidate.

So a unit that is not teaching at all - and has no intention of teaching - can be warned about having free teaching slots. The warning should be about a unit that actually wrote a TEACH order this month and has capacity left over, not about every idle unit in the hex.

Evidence that the current shape is fragile rather than merely broad: is_busy's own doc comment records that getting its membership wrong once produced "one hex of turn 71 [with] twenty-nine findings that were all the same non-observation", and ah-90w had to write a regression test to stop BUILD dropping out of it. A check whose correctness depends on an exhaustive list of what everything else in the game does is a check pointed the wrong way round.

Narrowing it to units that actually TEACH would also remove the constraint that forced a compromise in ah-dwk6: the rules say CAST is not a full-month order, but ah-dwk6 had to keep is_busy treating CAST as busy anyway, because following the rules there would have added spare-teacher findings on every casting mage. If this check only looks at teachers, that exception can go and CAST can be classified by the rules everywhere.

Scope note for the planner: this changes a shipped warning's behaviour, so which units are warned and what the message says are the navigator's. Check whether the existing message still reads correctly once the subject is always a real teacher.
design:
## Context

The `teacher-has-free-slots` warning is aimed at the wrong units. `offer_free_slots`
(`semantics.rs:1284-1349`) is called for **every unit in the hex** (`check_teaching`, `:1182-1185`),
and the only thing standing between a unit and the warning is `Ordered::is_busy` (`:1297`). So any
unit whose month is not otherwise spoken for, and which out-ranks a studying unit in that unit's
skill, is told *"this unit has 30 teaching slots free and could teach unit 700"* — including a unit
that was never asked to teach anything and has no teaching plan at all.

The navigator, raising it while `ah-dwk6` was being replanned: *"teaching warning should only be on
units actually TEACHing this month. Only warn if they have free slots. Not someone not teaching."*
Ranked **P0**.

**The check's original purpose has been made redundant by `ah-dwk6`, and that is the strongest
argument for narrowing it.** `offer_free_slots`'s own doc comment says it exists for *"a teacher with
slots to spare while somebody studies untaught"* — that is, to catch an **idle skilled unit**. Since
`ah-dwk6`, an idle unit raises `has no order that spends the month` against that same unit, in the
same problems list. So the parked veteran in the example above is still caught, by the check that is
actually about being idle. **Narrowing this one loses no coverage; it deletes a duplicate that was
wearing the wrong label.**

Two further reasons the current shape is fragile rather than merely broad:

- Its correctness depends on an exhaustive list of what *everything else in the game* does. `is_busy`'s
  own doc comment (`:348-353`) records that getting that membership wrong once produced *"one hex of
  turn 71 … twenty-nine findings that were all the same non-observation"*, and `ah-90w` had to add a
  regression test to stop `BUILD` silently dropping out of it. A check pointed that way round is a
  standing liability.
- It forced a compromise in `ah-dwk6`. The rules say `CAST` is not a full-month order, but `ah-dwk6`
  had to keep `is_busy` counting `CAST` as busy anyway, because following the rules there would have
  added spare-teacher findings on every casting mage. **This bead removes that exception** — see
  *Files to change* §3.

**Ordered behind `ah-dwk6`** (`bd dep`: `ah-vw63` blocks-on `ah-dwk6`), because it deletes an
exception `ah-dwk6` introduces and rewrites tests `ah-dwk6` adds. Read `ah-dwk6`'s plan first;
its *Known traps* apply here.

Branch from `origin/main`; every line number here is that tree, **before** `ah-dwk6` lands. Expect
`is_busy` to look like `ah-dwk6`'s version rather than today's when you get there.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

One file: `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`. No new code, no new token, no settings change — the
`teacher-has-free-slots` toggle already exists (`SettingsDialog.tsx`, *Studying/Teaching* group) and
is untouched.

### 1. Only a unit that actually teaches — `offer_free_slots`

Two guards at the top of `offer_free_slots`, after the existing `options.emits` and `ruleset` checks
(`:1292-1295`) and beside the existing `is_busy` guard (`:1296-1299`):

```rust
    // Only a unit that actually wrote a TEACH order this month. Before ah-vw63 this ran for every
    // unit in the hex, so a unit that was never asked to teach was told it had teaching slots
    // free - and the idle-skilled-unit case this check was invented for is now `ah-dwk6`'s
    // `unit-does-nothing`, on the same unit and in the same list.
    if !teacher
        .intents()
        .any(|intent| matches!(intent, Intent::Teach { .. }))
    {
        return;
    }

    // A TEACH naming nobody this hex holds is already reported as `taught-not-here`, and its slots
    // are free only as a consequence of that mistake. One mistake, marked once.
    if !teaches_somebody_here(teacher, hex) {
        return;
    }
```

and the predicate, beside `taught_by` (`:1352-1366`), which it deliberately mirrors:

```rust
/// Whether this unit's TEACH orders name at least one unit the hex can resolve.
///
/// `Party::New`, `Party::Foreign` and `Party::Discard` never resolve: a unit formed this month has
/// no number yet, and another faction's unit is not ours to read. Those are doubt, not students.
fn teaches_somebody_here(teacher: &Ordered<'_>, hex: &Hex<'_>) -> bool {
    teacher
        .intents()
        .filter_map(|intent| match intent {
            Intent::Teach { students } => Some(students),
            _ => None,
        })
        .flatten()
        .any(|student| matches!(student, Party::Unit(id) if hex.find(id).is_some()))
}
```

**Keep the `is_busy` guard.** It is not made redundant: a unit that writes both `TEACH` and `WORK`
has an impossible month, and offering its slots would be advice about a turn nobody is playing. It
now runs *after* the TEACH guard, which is the order that matters for the CAST change in §3.

**Nothing else in the body changes.** `free` is still
`teacher.unit.men * STUDENTS_PER_TEACHER - taught_by(teacher, hex)` (`:1301`), and `taught_by`
already sums only students the hex can resolve — so a teacher whose slots are all taken still returns
early at `free <= 0` (`:1302-1304`). `could_take` (`:1306-1323`) already excludes the teacher itself,
anyone in the hex-wide `taught` set (which now always includes this teacher's own students) and
anyone leaving the hex, so the warning names only genuinely untaught pupils. The finding's anchor
(`:1343-1346`) is already `find(Intent::Teach { .. })`, which was `None` for every non-teacher before
this bead and is now **always `Some`** — that is the tell that the old shape was wrong, and it needs
no edit.

### 2. The message — `offer_free_slots:1339-1342`

```rust
            format!(
                "has {free} teaching slots still free and could also teach unit {}{and_others}",
                first.unit.unit_id,
            ),
```

was `"this unit has {free} teaching slots free and could teach unit {}{and_others}"`. Three changes,
all the navigator's: **"still free"** and **"could also teach"** both say the unit already has
students, and the leading **"this unit "** goes — the finding already carries the unit number, and
every message the recent warning beads added omits it. `and_others` (`:1329-1333`) is unchanged.

### 3. `ah-dwk6`'s CAST exception goes — `Ordered::is_busy`

`ah-dwk6` leaves `is_busy` carrying a deliberate exception, with a comment naming this bead as the
place to remove it. Requiring a `TEACH` order already excludes every casting mage that is not
teaching, so the exception has no work left to do:

```rust
    fn is_busy(&self) -> bool {
        self.intents()
            .any(|intent| spends_the_month(intent) && !matches!(intent, Intent::Teach { .. }))
    }
```

That is the plain form `ah-dwk6` wanted and could not have. **The behaviour it unlocks is real and
correct**: the rules say *"a CAST order is not a full month order; a mage may still MOVE, STUDY, or
use any other month long order"*, so a mage that writes both `CAST` and `TEACH` genuinely does have
teaching slots, and is now offered them. `spends_the_month` is unchanged — it already classifies
`CAST` by the rules — and this is the only caller of `is_busy` (verified: `semantics.rs:1297` is the
sole call site).

**Delete `ah-dwk6`'s `a_casting_mage_is_still_not_offered_as_a_spare_teacher`.** It exists to pin the
exception this bead removes, so it must fail, and replacing it is increment 3.

## Increments

1. **A unit that is not teaching is not offered as a teacher.**
   RED: `a_unit_that_is_not_teaching_is_not_offered_as_a_teacher` — the bead's whole point, written
   from the reported case: a level-3 combat veteran with **no orders at all** beside a unit studying
   combat, expecting **no** `teacher-has-free-slots` finding. It fails today, producing exactly the
   warning the navigator objected to.
   GREEN: the TEACH guard in §1.
   **Then rewrite the four existing tests the guard breaks** (see *The test plan*); each keeps its
   intent and gains a `TEACH` order for the teacher. Do this in the same increment — they are the
   same change seen from the other side, and leaving them red is leaving the suite red.

2. **A teacher whose student is not here is marked once.**
   RED: `a_teacher_whose_only_student_is_not_here_is_not_told_about_free_slots` — `TEACH 9999` with a
   studying unit in the hex, expecting exactly one finding, `taught-not-here`. It fails today with
   two.
   Also RED: `a_teacher_with_one_absent_student_and_one_real_one_is_still_told_about_free_slots` —
   `TEACH 700 9999`, expecting both findings, because a resolvable student means the TEACH order is
   real and the free slots are a separate fact.
   GREEN: `teaches_somebody_here` and its guard.

3. **A casting mage can teach.**
   RED: `a_mage_that_casts_and_teaches_is_offered_its_free_slots` — `CAST shield` plus `TEACH 700`
   with another untaught student in the hex, expecting the finding. It fails while `ah-dwk6`'s CAST
   exception stands.
   GREEN: delete the exception from `is_busy`, and delete
   `a_casting_mage_is_still_not_offered_as_a_spare_teacher` with it.
   Keep `a_unit_teaching_is_still_not_offered_as_a_spare_teacher` and
   `a_unit_building_is_not_offered_as_a_spare_teacher` green — the second is `ah-90w`'s regression
   guard and must survive this edit.

4. **The wording.**
   RED: increment 1's rewritten
   `a_teacher_with_free_slots_beside_an_untaught_student_is_pointed_out` asserts the full new string.
   GREEN: the `format!` in §2.

## The test plan

**Rust — `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`, `mod tests` at `:2292`.** `cargo test --workspace`.
Reuse the existing fixtures: `region(units)` `:2305`, `unit(id)` `:2327`, `with_men` `:2361`,
`with_silver` `:2343`, `with_skill` `:2366`, `check(regions, orders)` `:2430`, `only(findings)`
`:2472`, `codes(&findings)` `:2455`.

**Four existing tests assert the behaviour this bead removes** and must be rewritten, not deleted —
each still has something to say once its teacher actually teaches:

| Test | Today | Rewritten as |
|---|---|---|
| `a_teacher_with_free_slots_beside_an_untaught_student_is_pointed_out` `:3789` | unit 500 has **no orders**; expects the warning | 500 `TEACH 700`, 700 and 900 both `STUDY combat`; expects the warning naming **900**, and asserts the full new message |
| `a_unit_spending_its_own_month_is_not_offered_as_a_teacher` `:3812` | 500 `STUDY`s; silent | 500 `TEACH 700` **and** `STUDY combat`; still silent — this is the `is_busy` guard, and it must keep testing `is_busy` rather than the new TEACH guard |
| `a_unit_building_is_not_offered_as_a_spare_teacher` `:3829` | 500 `BUILD`s; silent | 500 `TEACH 700` **and** `BUILD`; still silent. **`ah-90w`'s regression guard — do not weaken it** |
| `a_teacher_who_could_take_several_students_is_reported_once` `:3847` | 500 has no orders, three study | 500 `TEACH 700`, with 800 and 900 studying untaught; expects `and 1 other` |

New:

| Test | Pins |
|---|---|
| **`a_unit_that_is_not_teaching_is_not_offered_as_a_teacher`** | the reported defect: no orders, no warning |
| `a_unit_that_gives_but_does_not_teach_is_not_offered` | not-teaching is the rule, not idleness |
| **`a_teacher_whose_only_student_is_not_here_is_not_told_about_free_slots`** | `TEACH 9999` → one finding, `taught-not-here` |
| `a_teacher_with_one_absent_student_and_one_real_one_is_still_told_about_free_slots` | `TEACH 700 9999` → both findings |
| `a_teacher_naming_only_a_new_unit_is_not_told_about_free_slots` | `TEACH NEW 1` never resolves |
| **`a_mage_that_casts_and_teaches_is_offered_its_free_slots`** | the CAST exception is gone |
| `a_teacher_with_every_slot_taken_is_silent` | `free <= 0`, unchanged |
| `a_teacher_whose_students_are_all_taught_by_others_is_silent` | the hex-wide `taught` set, unchanged |
| the disable table at `:~4775` | `teacher-has-free-slots` row unchanged |

**Deleted:** `ah-dwk6`'s `a_casting_mage_is_still_not_offered_as_a_spare_teacher`, which exists only
to pin the exception this bead removes.

**`crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs` should not move, and that is worth checking rather than
assuming.** The committed turn-71 template contains **no `TEACH` order at all** (verified by
`grep -inE '^[[:space:]]*@?teach' ` over the extracted template), so no unit can pass the new guard
and the expected finding list is unchanged — including the two `unit-does-nothing` entries `ah-dwk6`
adds. If that file goes red, the guard is wrong.

**Suites:** `cargo test --workspace` and `pnpm run check:fast`. No browser suite and no TypeScript
change — the code, its toggle and its settings entry all already exist.

## User-facing decisions

Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-19 over `.cerebro/scratch/ah-vw63-teachers.html`. The
chosen mockup is committed to `docs/ui/ah-vw63-teachers.html`.

**Q1 — the message.** Chosen: **`has {free} teaching slots still free and could also teach unit
{id}{and_others}`**. "still free" and "could also teach" both say the unit already has students,
which today's wording actively denies — *"could teach"* reads as though the unit were idle, and after
this bead it never is. The leading "this unit " goes, matching the messages the recent warning beads
use. Rejected: keeping today's string unchanged (not false of a real teacher, but it still reads as
idle); and `is teaching 10 of the 30 students it could take; unit 900 studies untaught` — the most
informative, but the longest and using a semicolon no other message here does.

**Q2 — a TEACH naming a unit that is not in the hex.** Chosen: **warn only about the unresolvable
student.** `taught-not-here` already says what is wrong, and the free slots exist only as a
consequence of that mistake. Rejected: both findings (each separately true, but two findings on one
unit about one mistake) and only the free-slots one (hides the reason).

**Q3 — `ah-dwk6`'s CAST exception.** Chosen: **remove it in this bead.** Requiring a TEACH order
already excludes casting mages that are not teaching, so the exception has no work left; removing it
here means `CAST` is classified by the rules in one place and a temporary exception does not outlive
its reason. Rejected: leaving it and filing a third bead for a two-line deletion.

**Not asked:** the two guards' order in `offer_free_slots`, and `teaches_somebody_here`'s treatment
of `Party::New` / `Party::Foreign` / `Party::Discard` as never resolving (architecture, and it
matches how `check_one_teacher` and `check_building` already read a `Party`).

## Out of scope

- **The other three teaching checks.** `taught-not-here`, `taught-not-studying`,
  `teacher-cannot-teach` and `teaching-oversubscribed` all live in `check_one_teacher`
  (`:1189-1268`), already require a `TEACH` order, and are not touched.
- **Whether the teacher is skilled enough to teach the pupils it is offered.** `could_take` already
  filters on `teacher.skill_level > pupil.skill_level` (`:1316-1322`) and that rule is unchanged.
- **`STUDENTS_PER_TEACHER`** (`:46`), the ten-students-per-man rule, and how `free` is computed.
- **The settings entry and its toggle.** The code already exists in `codes::ALL` and in the
  *Studying/Teaching* group; nothing is added or renamed, and no vocabulary regeneration is needed.
- **A warning for a unit that could teach but is not.** That coverage now belongs to `ah-dwk6`'s
  `unit-does-nothing`, and duplicating it here is what this bead removes.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test --workspace
pnpm run check:fast
```

Then by eye, in the running app:

1. **The reported case.** Find a hex with a skilled unit and a unit studying that skill. Give the
   skilled unit **no orders**. It must **not** say it has teaching slots free — it should instead
   carry `has no order that spends the month` from `ah-dwk6`, which is the same observation under the
   right name.
2. Give it `TEACH <the studying unit>` and add a **second** unit studying the same skill untaught.
   The warning appears, against the teacher, reading exactly
   `has 20 teaching slots still free and could also teach unit <n>` (the number of slots depending on
   the teacher's men).
3. Add the second student to the `TEACH` line. The warning goes.
4. Change the `TEACH` line to name a unit that is not in the hex. Exactly **one** finding —
   `unit <n> is not in this hex to be taught` — and no free-slots warning beside it.
5. Give a mage `CAST shield` and `TEACH <a studying unit>`, with another untaught student present.
   The warning appears. Before this bead it did not.
6. Settings → Warnings → *Studying/Teaching* → untick **Spare teachers**: the warning goes and the
   other teaching warnings stay.

## Known traps

- **This bead must land after `ah-dwk6`.** It deletes a test `ah-dwk6` adds and an exception
  `ah-dwk6` writes. Starting from a tree without `ah-dwk6` means the CAST work in §3 has nothing to
  remove, and increment 3 will look already-done when it is not.
- **`is_busy` has exactly one caller** (`semantics.rs:1297`), so removing its CAST exception cannot
  reach any other check. Verify that before editing rather than trusting this line — if a second
  caller has appeared, the blast radius is different and the navigator should be asked again.
- **Keep the `is_busy` guard.** It looks redundant once a TEACH order is required, and it is not: a
  unit writing both `TEACH` and `WORK` has an impossible month, and offering its slots is advice
  about a turn nobody is playing.
- **`a_unit_building_is_not_offered_as_a_spare_teacher` is `ah-90w`'s regression guard**, and this
  bead rewrites it. It must keep testing what it was written for — that `BUILD` still counts as
  spending the month — so give its unit a `TEACH` order and leave everything else alone. Weakening it
  to "silent because it is not teaching" would delete the guard while appearing to keep it.
- **The finding's anchor is already `find(Intent::Teach { .. })`** (`:1343-1346`) and was `None` for
  every non-teacher this check ever warned about — meaning those findings carried no line. That is
  the shape of the bug, and it is also why no test noticed: nothing asserted a line on them.
- **`taught_by` counts only resolvable students** (`:1360-1363`), so a teacher whose students are all
  absent has *full* free slots rather than none. That is what made the double-marking in Q2 possible.
- **The hex-wide `taught` set is built before the per-unit loop** (`:1170-1180`) and includes this
  teacher's own students, so `could_take` never offers a teacher the pupils it is already teaching.
  Do not add a second exclusion for that.
acceptance_criteria: The teacher-has-free-slots warning is raised only against a unit that has a TEACH order this month; a unit with no TEACH order raises it never, whatever else it is or is not doing. A TEACH order naming no unit the hex can resolve raises taught-not-here alone and no free-slots warning beside it, while a TEACH naming at least one resolvable unit raises both where both apply. The message reads exactly "has <n> teaching slots still free and could also teach unit <id>", with the existing " and 1 other"/" and <n> others" suffix unchanged. The four existing tests that assert the warning against units with no TEACH order are rewritten to the new rule rather than deleted, and a_unit_building_is_not_offered_as_a_spare_teacher keeps testing what ah-90w wrote it for. ah-dwk6's temporary CAST exception in is_busy is removed, so a mage that both casts and teaches is offered its free slots and CAST is classified by the rules in one place; ah-dwk6's a_casting_mage_is_still_not_offered_as_a_spare_teacher is deleted with it. The committed turn-71 template's expected findings are unchanged, the template containing no TEACH order. No settings, vocabulary or TypeScript change.

title: Warn when a unit has been given nothing to do this month
description:
A unit that is given no month-long order spends the month doing nothing, and it is easy to miss one
unit among many when writing a turn. Warn when a unit has no month-long order this month.

The orders crate has no notion of order duration today - nothing in `crates/core/src/orders/`
distinguishes a month-long order from an instant one, so the classification is new work. In Atlantis
the month-long orders are the ones that consume the unit's month: `WORK`, `TAX`, `PRODUCE`, `BUILD`,
`STUDY`, `TEACH`, `ENTERTAIN`, `MOVE`, `SAIL`; the rest (`GIVE`, `BUY`, `SELL`, `ENTER`, `LEAVE`,
`DECLARE` and so on) leave the month free.

For the planner:

- **Confirm the list against the game's rules**, including the ones that are arguable: `MOVE` and
  `SAIL` occupy the month but are not "work"; a unit ordered to `TEACH` needs students; `PILLAGE`
  and `ASSASSINATE` and the combat orders need placing.
- **Which units should be exempt.** A unit deliberately left idle - a garrison sitting on `GUARD`, a
  new unit formed to receive goods, a unit that will be disbanded - is a normal thing, and a warning
  on every one of them is noise. Whether that needs a per-unit "intentionally idle" mark, or whether
  the warning is quiet enough without one.
- Which warning category this joins, and its place among the warning toggles.
acceptance_criteria: An own unit whose orders contain nothing that spends its month raises a warning against that unit reading exactly "has no order that spends the month", anchored at the unit's first block line, or with no line when the document has no block for it. The month-long set is taken from the rules and stated once as an exhaustive match over Intent: ADVANCE, BUILD, ENTERTAIN, MOVE, PILLAGE, PRODUCE, SAIL, STUDY, TAX, TEACH, WORK, plus IDLE and ANNIHILATE. CAST is NOT month-long and a unit whose only order is CAST is warned; nor are ASSASSINATE, STEAL, TRANSPORT or DISTRIBUTE, and a unit whose only orders are free ones such as NAME, ADDRESS, ARMOR or ATTACK IS warned - that is the false negative this bead's first attempt shipped. Silence is reserved for a unit holding a keyword in neither classification, which after this bead means a typo or an order the game has and the list does not. There are no exemptions: an empty block warns and a unit on GUARD warns. The existing teacher-has-free-slots warning is unchanged, which requires is_busy to keep counting CAST as busy even though spends_the_month does not; a named regression test pins that, and ah-vw63 is where the exception is removed. The check has its own toggle in Settings -> Warnings -> Orders, titled "Units that do nothing", on by default. The committed turn-71 template's expected findings go from eight to ten, the two additions being this code against units 14451 and 13432 and nothing else.
notes:
Verification failed (2026-08-19, at origin/main 1de7528): the classifier treats many orders as spending the month when they do not. The navigator's words: "Lots of orders pass for month long, but should not: NAME, ADDRESS, ARMOR, ATTACK, ..." — an incomplete list, given as examples rather than as the whole set.

The effect is the bead's own purpose inverted: a unit given only NAME, ADDRESS, ARMOR or ATTACK (and by implication other same-shape orders) is counted as busy and never warned, so exactly the forgotten unit this check exists to catch stays silent. It is the false-negative direction, which is the worse one here — a warning that never fires is invisible, unlike a spurious one.

Whoever picks this up should not fix only the four orders named. The navigator's list trails off deliberately; the fix is to go through the order set and decide, order by order, which ones actually spend the unit's month, rather than patching the examples. Note the design's own trap: is_busy deliberately omits Intent::Teach, and that exclusion must survive.
Wolverine (implementer) claimed this in the race window before the `planned` label was removed, and stood down at Psylocke's request without opening a PR. Nothing was merged. One thing worth keeping for whoever replans it — the order-by-order classification the navigator asked for, read off the NewOrigins rules page (https://atlantis-pbem.com/rules):

Two passages settle almost the whole set. The enumerated list: "The orders which take an entire month are ADVANCE, BUILD, ENTERTAIN, MOVE, PILLAGE, PRODUCE, SAIL, STUDY, TAX, TEACH and WORK." And the Sequence of Events, which groups every other order under 'Instant orders' and the phases around it.

MONTH-LONG: ADVANCE, BUILD, ENTERTAIN, MOVE, PILLAGE, PRODUCE, SAIL, STUDY, TAX, TEACH, WORK — plus IDLE, which the enumerated list omits but the page describes as 'do nothing for the entire month'. (So the enumerated list is not exhaustive and cannot be used as one.)

FREE: ADDRESS, ARMOR, ASSASSINATE, ATTACK, AUTOTAX, AVOID, BEHIND, BUY, CAST, CLAIM, COMBAT, CONSUME, DECLARE, DESCRIBE, DESTROY, ENTER, EVICT, EXCHANGE, FACTION, FIND, FORGET, FORM, GIVE, GUARD, HOLD, JOIN, LEAVE, NAME, NOAID, NOCROSS, OPTION, PASSWORD, PREPARE, PROMOTE, QUIT, RESTART, REVEAL, SACRIFICE, SELL, SHARE, SHOW, SPOILS, STEAL, TAKE, WEAPON, WITHDRAW.

UNCERTAIN, and so still unjudgeable: ANNIHILATE and TRANSPORT (with its synonym DISTRIBUTE). Each gets a phase of its own after the month-long block and the page never says whether it consumes the month.

Two of these contradict the current plan's premises directly, and are the reason a patch of the four named orders would not have been enough:

1. The rules are explicit that 'STEAL and ASSASSINATE are not full month orders, and do not interfere with other activities'. The plan uses `ASSASSINATE 4021` as its worked example of an unread line that 'spends the month as surely as WORK does', and pins that in a test (`a_unit_with_an_order_we_cannot_read_is_silent`). The premise is wrong; only ANNIHILATE and TRANSPORT actually need the unread escape hatch.

2. The rules are explicit that 'a CAST order is not a full month order; a mage may still MOVE, STUDY, or use any other month long order.' `spends_the_month` currently returns true for `Intent::Cast`, and `intents.rs` justifies it with 'the rules make no promise about which' spells take a month. They do make a promise about CAST itself. Flipping it would change `is_busy`, and so the spare-teacher check — which is why it wants deciding in the plan rather than by an implementer.

title: The halved-magic-study warning reads where the unit stands, not where its orders leave it
description:
Found by the navigator on 2026-08-17 while verifying ah-9js (origin/main 8d62fe8). All six beads in that sitting passed; this is the follow-up filed alongside.

## What the reader sees

A mage sheltered in a building that seats mages, already at level 2 or above in a magic skill, studying that skill AND issuing LEAVE in the same orders block, is not warned - though it steps out of the building before the month's study happens, and half of that study is wasted. The engine's own advisory ('Magic study rate outside of a building cut in half above level 2.') would appear on the following turn's report.

The cost being paid: the check exists precisely so a player does not discover a wasted month a turn later. In this shape it stays silent on an order the player wrote deliberately, which is the one case where a warning would change what they do.

## The cause is exact

check_magic_study_outside_building (crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs:1545) computes 'sheltered' from the report's static picture alone:

    let standing_in = ordered.unit.structure_id.as_deref().map(|id| { ... });

structure_id is where the report says the unit stood when the turn was written. The unit's own intents are never consulted, so a LEAVE in the same block is invisible to the check.

## The mirror case, which should be checked at the same time

The same blindness runs the other way. A mage standing outside, at level 2+, that issues ENTER <building that seats mages> and studies is presumably warned today although it will be sheltered when the study happens - a false warning, which is worse than a missing one because it teaches the player to distrust the check. This was not observed, only deduced from the same lines; confirm before fixing.

## The fix has a template in the same file

is_aboard (semantics.rs:1636) already answers this exact question for fleets:

    /// Whether the unit is aboard  once this month's ENTER/LEAVE orders have run: the
    /// report's own structure first, then the last of this unit's ENTER/LEAVE intents in document
    /// order - which is the order the server itself would apply them in.

Intent::Leave and Intent::Enter { structure } are already modelled (orders/intents.rs:88, 313) and intents.rs:88 states the ordering rule this needs: 'LEAVE: the unit steps out of whatever it is in, before anything moves.' The shape wanted is the structure the unit is in *after* its ENTER/LEAVE orders have run, which is is_aboard generalised from a named fleet to 'whatever it ends in', and then the existing mage_capacity/needs test applied to that.

## Why this is a familiar shape

This is the ah-p1p / ah-l2i / ah-048 family again, one reader further on: a check answering from the report's static state where the player's orders have already changed the answer. Those three were about a SAIL order and three readers disagreeing about where a unit is; this is the same disagreement about what a unit is standing in. Worth asking at planning whether any other check in semantics.rs reads structure_id raw and has the same blind spot - a grep for structure_id would settle it - so this is fixed once for every reader rather than once per bug report.

## Acceptance

A mage at level 2+ in a magic skill, sheltered in a building that seats mages, that studies that skill and issues LEAVE, is warned. The same mage without the LEAVE is still silent. A mage outside that ENTERs such a building and studies is silent. An unfinished building, a Tower (which seats zero) and a structure the region does not list all keep their current behaviour. The warning stays advisory and never blocking.

## Out of scope

ah-9js's buildings reference and its source (verified, passing). Counting mages against a building's capacity - a Fort seats one, and two mages in one Fort is still unhandled and is its own bead. Every other rule inside the check: which skills are magic, the level threshold, the message wording.
design:
## Context

`check_magic_study` warns when a mage at level 2 or above studies a magic skill with nothing
housing it — half that month is wasted, and the engine only says so on the *next* turn's report,
which is the whole reason the check exists. It decides "sheltered" from the report's static
picture alone (`semantics.rs:1546`, `ordered.unit.structure_id`), so a mage that studies **and**
issues `LEAVE` in the same block is not warned, though it steps out before the month's study
happens. The check goes silent on exactly the order the player wrote deliberately.

**The mirror case is confirmed, not merely deduced.** A mage standing outside has
`structure_id == None`, so `standing_in` is `None`, `sheltered` is `false`, and the warning fires —
even when the block's own `ENTER <a building that seats mages>` will have housed it by the time it
studies. That is a false warning, which is worse than a missing one because it teaches the player
to distrust the check.

**A second check has the identical defect**, which is what the bead asked to be settled at planning
by grepping `structure_id`. `check_building` (`semantics.rs:1408`) reads
`worker.unit.structure_id` raw to decide whether the thing being BUILT is already finished, so a
unit that `ENTER`s an unfinished structure and BUILDs is judged against the structure it left, and a
unit that LEAVEs and BUILDs still gets the already-finished warning. ENTER and LEAVE run before
BUILD, so the intent-aware answer is the right one in both checks. This bead fixes both, from one
helper — which is what "fixed once for every reader rather than once per bug report" means.

Two readers below the orders layer ask the same question from the report alone
(`movement/mode.rs:286`, crew counted for sailing; `movement/fleet.rs:89`). They are **out of
scope** and filed separately; see *Out of scope*.

**When this lands**, a mage that studies and leaves is warned, a mage that studies and enters is
not, and the already-built warning follows the unit's own ENTER/LEAVE the same way.

`check_magic_study` was delivered by PR #393 and is on `origin/main` at `72c6cb8`. **Every line
number below is `origin/main`** — a checkout older than that does not contain the function at all.
Nothing blocks this bead.

## What the verification found, and what this plan now says (2026-08-18)

**This bead was built, verified and failed.** The generalisation it describes is sound and five of
the six verification cases passed; **one rule inside it is wrong**, and everything below has been
amended for it rather than rewritten.

Case A4, at `origin/main 43d1b73`: unit 1657 (unsheltered, force 3 / fire 2) in mountain (43,81) of
`neworigins-3.0.0-g7-f62-t17.rep`, given `@study fire` / `ENTER 5` / `LEAVE`, where Building [5] is a
Hermits hut seating one mage. The warning was shown; silence was expected.

The navigator, verbatim: *"Even though ENTER 5 comes before LEAVE in the order, they are processed
the other way around. I.e. LEAVE comes first and then ENTER 5. This means that the mage will be
sheltered during study."* Asked whether that is absolute or conditional, they answered **ALWAYS** —
every LEAVE is processed, then every ENTER, whatever order the lines were typed in. They were
certain rather than hedging, so this does **not** need re-confirming against the rules page.

So `structure_after_orders`' "last ENTER/LEAVE in document order wins" is not mis-ordered — it is
**the wrong shape**. Under LEAVE-before-ENTER, a block containing any ENTER can never end outside a
structure, so that branch has no correct use at all. The corrected rule:

> If the block has **any** ENTER, the unit ends in the **last** ENTERed structure. Otherwise, if it
> has any LEAVE, it ends in nothing. Otherwise it stays where the report found it. **Document order
> matters only among ENTERs.**

Passing in the same sitting, and not to be disturbed: A1 (study alone, unsheltered, warns), A2
(study + ENTER a Hermits hut, silent), A3 (study + ENTER an unfinished Stockade, still warns), B5
(sheltered mage studying, silent), B6 (sheltered mage + LEAVE, warns — the bug this bead was filed
for). The `check_building` reader shares the helper and inherits the same defect, so it takes the
same fix and needs its own case.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

Everything is in `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`. No TS, no shell, no boundary, no new
advisory code — `magic-study-outside-building` and `already-built` both already exist in
`codes::ALL` (`:104-126`), so `coreVocabulary.generated.ts` and the settings mirrors are untouched.

### The helper — generalise `is_aboard`

`is_aboard` (`:1633-1646`) already answers this exact question for one named fleet, and its doc
comment states the rule this bead needs:

```rust
/// Whether the unit is aboard `fleet_id` once this month's ENTER/LEAVE orders have run: the
/// report's own structure first, then the last of this unit's ENTER/LEAVE intents in document
/// order - which is the order the server itself would apply them in.
fn is_aboard(ordered: &Ordered<'_>, fleet_id: &str) -> bool {
    let mut aboard = ordered.unit.structure_id.as_deref() == Some(fleet_id);
    for placed in ordered.intents {
        match &placed.intent {
            Intent::Enter { structure } => aboard = structure == fleet_id,
            Intent::Leave => aboard = false,
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    aboard
}
```

Add, beside it, the "whatever it ends in" form:

```rust
/// The structure the unit is in once this month's ENTER/LEAVE orders have run, or `None` when it
/// ends the month in nothing.
///
/// **Every LEAVE is processed before any ENTER**, whatever order the lines were typed in - the
/// engine's own order, confirmed by the navigator on 2026-08-18 after a verification failed on
/// exactly this. So a block holding any ENTER ends inside the last structure entered, a block
/// holding only LEAVEs ends in nothing, and a block holding neither stays where the report found
/// it. Document order matters only among ENTERs; between an ENTER and a LEAVE it means nothing at
/// all.
///
/// Both run before anything else a block can ask for, so every check that asks "what is this unit
/// standing in when its orders happen" wants this rather than `unit.structure_id`, which is only
/// where the report found it.
fn structure_after_orders<'a>(ordered: &Ordered<'a>) -> Option<&'a str> {
    let mut entered: Option<&'a str> = None;
    let mut left = false;
    for placed in ordered.intents {
        match &placed.intent {
            Intent::Enter { structure } => entered = Some(structure.as_str()),
            Intent::Leave => left = true,
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    match (entered, left) {
        // An ENTER always wins: the LEAVE ran first, and the unit walked back in.
        (Some(structure), _) => Some(structure),
        (None, true) => None,
        (None, false) => ordered.unit.structure_id.as_deref(),
    }
}
```

The lifetime is `'a` from `Ordered<'a>` (`:280-283`, `unit: &'a ReportUnit, intents: &'a
[PlacedIntent]`), so both arms borrow for as long as the caller needs. `Intent::Enter`'s
`structure` is the raw number text (`intents.rs:313-315`), directly comparable with
`Structure::structure_id` (`report/model.rs:93`) — which is exactly what `is_aboard` relies on
today.

**Then rewrite `is_aboard` over it**, so there is one model of the rule rather than two:

```rust
fn is_aboard(ordered: &Ordered<'_>, fleet_id: &str) -> bool {
    structure_after_orders(ordered) == Some(fleet_id)
}
```

**This is equivalent for every block that holds one kind of order, and deliberately *not*
equivalent for a block that holds both** (2026-08-18). Today's `is_aboard` gives `false` for
`ENTER <fleet>` followed by `LEAVE`; the corrected helper gives `true`, because the LEAVE ran first
and the unit walked back aboard. That is the same correction this bead is making for buildings,
applied to fleets, and it is right — but it means increment 1 is no longer a pure refactor, and the
claim that the existing tests prove equivalence has to be checked rather than assumed.

Its existing tests (`a_unit_leaving_this_month_does_not_count` at `:5714`, the ENTER mirror at
`:5695-5711`, `a_unit_leaving_this_month_is_unloaded_weight` at `:5203`) each hold **one** kind of
order, so all three must still pass untouched. If any of them holds both, it encodes the old rule
and is to be rewritten with the rest of them - say so in the PR rather than quietly adjusting it. Keep `is_aboard`'s doc comment where it is; move
nothing else. **Leave `could_captain` (`:1648-1656`) alone** — it deliberately counts a unit that
also LEAVEs, because the server reads its SAIL line first, and its comment says so.

### `check_magic_study` (`:1496-1581`)

Replace `:1546-1551`:

```rust
        let standing_in = ordered.unit.structure_id.as_deref().map(|id| {
            hex.region.structures.iter().find(|structure| structure.structure_id == id)
        });
```

with the intent-aware lookup:

```rust
        let standing_in = structure_after_orders(ordered).map(|id| {
            hex.region.structures.iter().find(|structure| structure.structure_id == id)
        });
```

- **Your checkout may predate the function.** `check_magic_study` landed in PR #393 and is on

  longer one.
- **Every LEAVE runs before any ENTER.** This is the rule the first attempt got wrong, and it is
  the whole reason the bead came back. "Last ENTER/LEAVE in document order wins" is not a
  near-miss — under the real rule a block containing an ENTER can never end outside a structure, so
  that branch has no correct use. If the code you are writing folds ENTER and LEAVE into one
  running value, it is the old shape wearing new names.

  treat any other test whose *name* states an ordering rule with the same suspicion.

  `check_sailing` for overloading and crew, so read increment 1's note before touching it: blocks
  with one kind of order are unaffected, blocks with both now answer "aboard", and that is the same
  correction applied to fleets. What must not change is any answer for a block holding one kind.
- **Document order is slice order, and it now decides only which ENTER wins.**
  `read_intents` (`intents.rs:145`) walks the document top to bottom and pushes as it goes, so
  walking `ordered.intents` in slice order is walking in document order. Do not sort, and do not
  reach for `.rev().find(...)` — a unit written in two blocks has both concatenated (`OrderedUnits`,

  LEAVE.

  something this report does not list", and only the second is doubt. Flattening them with `??` or
  `.flatten()` turns a silence into a warning about every unit standing in an unlisted structure.
- **`worker`, not `ordered`, in `check_building`.** With `HELP`, the structure belongs to the helped
  unit and so do the ENTER/LEAVE orders that move it.

  (`movement/rules.rs:635-646`): the catalogue cannot say, versus the building seats nobody. The
  existing `is_some_and(|seats| seats >= 1)` already honours that; do not simplify it to
  `unwrap_or(0)`.

  (`:97-103`). Nothing here adds a code, so nothing there should move; if `check:generated`

    @study fire
    ENTER 5

The navigator's finding, verbatim: "Even though ENTER 5 comes before LEAVE in the order, they are
processed the other way around. I.e. LEAVE comes first and then ENTER 5. This means that the mage
will be sheltered during study. However, the warning is shown which means that ENTER and LEAVE in
the same order does not work."

So the expected result is SILENCE - the mage ends the phase inside Building [5] - and the warning is
shown instead.

## What is wrong, precisely

structure_after_orders (crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs) walks the unit's ENTER/LEAVE intents in
DOCUMENT order and lets the last one win. Its own doc comment states the assumption:

    the last of this unit's ENTER/LEAVE intents in document order - which is
    the order the server itself would apply them in

That clause is false. The engine runs every LEAVE before any ENTER, so a block containing both ends
with the unit inside the ENTERed structure regardless of which line was typed first. The unit test
a_mage_that_leaves_and_re_enters_is_judged_on_the_last_order encodes the same wrong rule and passes,
which is why this reached the navigator.

Note the practical consequence: with LEAVE-before-ENTER, a block containing an ENTER can never end
outside a structure, so the "last order wins" branch has no correct use at all - the rule is not
merely mis-ordered, it is the wrong shape.

## What was verified as correct in the same sitting

Cases A1 (study alone, unsheltered, warns), A2 (study + ENTER a Hermits hut, silent - the mirror bug
this bead fixed), A3 (study + ENTER an unfinished Stockade, still warns), B5 (sheltered mage studying,
silent) and B6 (sheltered mage + LEAVE, warns - the bug this bead was filed for) all behaved as
intended. The generalisation into structure_after_orders and its second reader (the BUILD /
already-built check) are sound; only the ordering rule inside it is wrong.

The BUILD check shares structure_after_orders, so it inherits the same defect and needs the same fix
and its own case.
## The rule, from the navigator (2026-08-18), to be planned against

Asked directly whether LEAVE-before-ENTER is absolute or conditional, the navigator answered:
ALWAYS - every LEAVE is processed, then every ENTER, regardless of the order the lines were typed in.

Two consequences the revised plan should state outright:

1. A block containing an ENTER can never end with the unit outside a structure. So the "last
   ENTER/LEAVE in document order wins" branch is not merely mis-ordered - it has no correct use at
   all, and the rule is the wrong shape rather than the wrong direction.
2. structure_after_orders wants: if the block has any ENTER, the unit ends in the LAST ENTERed
   structure; otherwise, if it has any LEAVE, it ends in nothing; otherwise it stays where the
   report found it. Document order matters only among ENTERs.

The doc comment on structure_after_orders and the unit test
a_mage_that_leaves_and_re_enters_is_judged_on_the_last_order both assert the wrong rule and must be
rewritten, not merely adjusted - a test asserting the old behaviour is what let this reach the
navigator.

The navigator was certain rather than hedging, so this does not need re-confirming against the rules
page before work starts.

title: Warn when a fleet is too heavy or too short-crewed to sail
description:
A fleet ordered to `SAIL` that is over its capacity, or crewed by too few sailors, does not sail. The
turn is lost and nothing warned about it beforehand.

Both failures are arithmetic the checker could do: what is aboard against what the ship can carry,
and the sailing skill aboard against what the ship needs.

## What exists, and the gap

- **Unit weight and capacity are in the report.** Unit lines carry `Weight: 10. Capacity:
  0/0/15/0.`, already parsed for movement (`movement/request.rs`).
- **Skills are parsed** — `ReportUnit.skills` — so a unit's SAIL level is available.
- **`MovementMode::Sail` exists** and `SAIL` is a known movement order.
- **Ships are not.** `Structure` carries `structure_id`, `name`, `kind`, `description` and `needs` —
  **no capacity, no crew requirement**. So the one number the check needs most is not modelled.

That is the real work in this bead, and it should be established before anything else: whether a
ship's capacity and required sailors can be read from the report at all, or must come from the
ruleset by `kind`, or are absent and this check cannot be built as asked.

## What "aboard" means

Everything the check counts is a question about which units are in the ship, and the report says who
is in a structure. Two things to settle rather than assume: whether a unit's own `Capacity` figure
should be added to the ship's (units can carry), and whether the men whose sailing skill counts are
only those aboard.

## For the planner to settle with the navigator

- **Where a ship's capacity and crew requirement come from**, per above. If neither the report nor
  the ruleset carries them, say so in the bead rather than hard-coding a table that is right for one
  ruleset and quietly wrong for the next.
- **One warning or two.** Overloaded and undercrewed are different mistakes with different fixes;
  separate codes let the Warnings tab turn one off and keep the other.
- **How close to the limit is worth saying.** Exactly at capacity sails; the interesting case may be
  "this is within a man of not sailing", which is a different check and probably a later one.

## Validation

A fleet loaded past its capacity and ordered to `SAIL`: warned, naming what is over. The same fleet
one unit lighter: silent. A fleet with too few sailors aboard: warned. A fleet that will sail
perfectly well: silent, including when its units carry cargo of their own.

bead; its seam is `fleet_load` below. Accept on doubt, exactly as `semantics.rs:1–17` says: a
number the report and the ruleset cannot supply, a unit whose weight is unstated, a foreign unit
aboard, or a `MOVE` that touches the fleet (whose ordering against the sail the server does not
promise) silences the check for that fleet rather than guessing.

Design choices that are mine: `SAIL` becomes its own intent (`Intent::Sail { steps }`, bare SAIL
included) because the check has to tell a fleet order from a unit walking off; `ENTER`/`LEAVE`
become intents (`Intent::Enter { structure }`, `Intent::Leave`) because they change who is aboard
and are instant orders that the server runs before movement; `sailing_requirement` in `mode.rs`
learns to work without a ruleset (stated numbers still count) and gains a sibling `cargo_capacity`;
the check itself is `check_sailing` in `semantics.rs`, next to the other three.

```rust
/// The sailing levels one unit supplies once this month's transfers of men have run.
///
/// A unit's skill level is held by each of its men - "the number of skill levels of the Sailing
/// skill that must be aboard the ship" - so men leaving take levels with them. Read from the
/// ledger for the same reason `weight_after_orders` is: the server runs every GIVE and TAKE
/// (phase 4) before it moves anybody (phase 9), so giving a gnoll away and sailing in the same
/// month is one turn, not two.
///
/// `None` - cannot say, so the caller silences the crew check for this fleet - when men arrive
/// rather than leave. The game merges given men into the receiving unit and recomputes its skill,
/// which this application does not model; counting them at the receiver's own level would turn two
/// unskilled gnolls into two sailors, and a warning that is wrong is worse than one that is missing
/// (this module's header, and the navigator's own answer on the amendment).
fn sailing_levels_after_orders(
    ordered: &Ordered<'_>,
    ledger: &Ledger<'_>,
    ruleset: Option<&Ruleset>,
) -> Option<i64> {
    let level: i64 = ordered
        .unit
        .skills
        .iter()
        .filter(|skill| skill.tag.eq_ignore_ascii_case("SAIL"))
        .map(|skill| i64::from(skill.level))
        .sum();

    // Without a catalogue there is no telling which tags name people, so no delta can be computed.
    let ruleset = ruleset?;

    let mut men_moved: i64 = 0;
    for ((unit_id, tag), balance) in &ledger.balance {
        if unit_id != &ordered.unit.unit_id || !ruleset.is_man(tag) {
            continue;
        }
        men_moved = men_moved.saturating_add(balance - ordered.holding(tag));
    }

    if men_moved > 0 {
        return None;                       // men arrived: the merged skill is unknowable
    }

    let men = ordered.unit.men.saturating_add(men_moved).max(0);
    Some(level.saturating_mul(men))
}
```

`ReportUnit.men` is `i64` (`crates/core/src/report/model.rs:142`), so no conversion is needed — only
`skill.level` is a `u32` and wants `i64::from`, exactly as `crew_sailing_levels`
