- Re-weighing units for `GIVE`/`TAKE`/`BUY` — delivered by `ah-eet` (closed). The amendment reads the
  ledger `ah-eet` built and **changes nothing on the load side**: `weight_after_orders`, the overload
  message and its `match` arms are all left exactly as they are.
- "Within a man of not sailing".
- A `SAIL` by a unit in no fleet, or by a unit not the owner — other checks.
- Whether the route itself is sailable (`plan_route` already refuses `CrewCannotSail`).
- Fleet speed.
- **Modelling what a merged unit knows.** R1 answers "men given into a unit aboard" with silence
  precisely so that nobody has to. Working out the receiving unit's skill after a merge is a piece of
  engine behaviour this application does not model anywhere, and it is not to be attempted here — if
  it is ever wanted it is a bead of its own.
- **`movement::mode::crew_sailing_levels`** (`movement/mode.rs:286`). It sums the report's figures for
  the route planner and is correct for that: the planner asks what a fleet can do now, not what this
  month's orders would leave it. Do not point it at the ledger, and do not make `check_sailing` call
  it — the amended check needs the aboard-after set, which `crew_sailing_levels` cannot see.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core
pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared exec vitest run src/workspace/SettingsDialog.test.tsx
pnpm run check:fast
```

And the look in increment 3.

**Re-verification, after the amendment (increment 0) — all four of Psylocke's cases, in this order.**
The bead has failed twice, so the whole set is re-run rather than the one case that broke; the notes on
this bead carry them, and they are repeated here so the implementer can check its own work before
handing back. Fixture `tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-g5-f21-t23.rep`, `Ship [218]` (Raft,
`Load: 70/450; Sailors: 2/2`), unit `Drones (9508)` = 2 gnolls at `SAIL 1`:

1. `unit 9508` + `sail N` alone → **silent.** (The first failure. 2 levels aboard, 2 needed.)
2. `unit 9508` + `give 0 1 GNOL` + `sail N` → **warns** `fleet-undercrewed` on the `sail` line, with
   the before-and-after sentence from item 7 of *User-facing decisions*. (The second failure, and what
   increment 0 is for.)
3. `unit 8333` + `ENTER 235` with a heavy load → **still warns** `fleet-overloaded`. (The load half must
   be undisturbed.)
4. The Warnings tab still shows the **Sailing** group with both toggles, on by default, and each one
   still silences its own code.

A human runs these — it is the point of verification — but the implementer should reproduce 1 and 2 as
unit tests before it opens a PR, which the test plan above requires anyway.

## Known traps

- **`ALL`'s length is a type** — count what is there when you arrive (`ah-yk7` may have added
  one) and add two.
- **`SAIL N` was an `Intent::Move`**; anything that matched `Move` to mean "goes away" needs `Sail`
  too — `leaves_the_hex` and `spends_the_month` are listed above; grep for `Intent::Move` before
  finishing.
- **`crew_sailing_levels` filters by the report's `structure_id`**, so a unit that ENTERs this month
  is invisible to it; sum over the aboard-after set yourself.
- **Doubt silences, never guesses**: an unknown hull with no stated numbers, a `None` weight, a
  foreign unit aboard, a `MOVE` touching the fleet — each is a `continue`, not a default.
- **`sailing_requirement`'s signature changes** (`Option<&Ruleset>`); the two callers in
  `movement/plan.rs` and `movement/trace.rs` pass `Some(ruleset)`.
- **The messages are asserted verbatim**; `label` comes from `fleet_label`, numbers are plain
  integers, no thousands separators.

Added by the 2026-08-17 amendment:

- **This bead has failed verification twice, and the two failures are opposite.** The first was a
  **false positive** (a fleet that sails, warned) and the second a **false negative** (a fleet that
  will not sail, silent). Every test in the amendment's list is there because one of those two
  directions was got wrong, so run the whole sailing test set and read the names — not just the new
  ones. `a_full_crew_that_gives_nothing_away_still_sails` is the first failure's regression and is the
  single most important assertion in the file.
- **`Option<i64>` summed over the aboard set is the doubt mechanism, and it must stay an `Option`.**
  `.sum::<Option<i64>>()` short-circuits to `None` on the first `None`, which is what makes one
  unknowable unit silence the whole fleet. Unwrapping early, or defaulting a `None` to `0`, turns R1's
  doubt into a claim that the fleet has no sailors — a false positive, and the failure mode this bead
  has already been sent back for once.
- **`ledger.doubted` guards the crew finding alone.** `check_sailing` does not consult it today
  (`semantics.rs:940`, `:954`, `:1047` are all inside `check_resources`), so adding it to the
  fleet-wide `continue` would silence overload warnings that currently ship. See *Increments*.
- **`Ruleset::is_man` is what decides a tag names people** (`crates/core/src/movement/rules.rs:598`).
  Do not hard-code race tags: `GNOL`, `LEAD`, `CTAU` and the rest are one ruleset's list, and a
  centaur is both a race and a mount — the catalogue settles that when it is scraped, as `is_man`'s
  own docstring says.
- **A `GIVE` of men to a unit outside the hull still reduces the crew.** The men have left the ship
  whether they went to another unit in the hex or to `0`. Only men arriving *into* a unit aboard is
  the doubt case, so the test is the sign of `men_moved` for the aboard unit, never who the
  counterparty was.
- **`men_estimated` doubt already exists and stays.** `headcount_is_doubtful` (`semantics.rs:1744`)
  came from a review comment on the original PR; the amendment adds `doubted_aboard` beside it rather
  than replacing it.
acceptance_criteria: 1) codes fleet-overloaded and fleet-undercrewed in codes::ALL; Intent::Sail/Enter/Leave recorded; mode.rs has cargo_capacity, fleet_label, sailing_requirement(Option<&Ruleset>); check_sailing emits one finding per code on the captain's SAIL line with the verbatim messages, counting report units aboard ± ENTER/LEAVE at report weights and sailing levels, silent on doubt (unknown hull, unstated weight, foreign unit aboard, MOVE touching the fleet). 2) The 14 semantics tests, 4 intents tests, 5 mode tests and two fixture rows pass; vocabulary regenerated. 3) Warnings tab group Sailing with 'Overloaded fleets' / 'Undercrewed fleets', on by default; SettingsDialog.test.tsx pins it. 4) pnpm run check:fast green. 5) ah-eet (scope C) exists and is not built here. AMENDED 2026-08-17 (second verification failure, plan at fault) — 6) sailing_levels_after_orders reads the ledger: men leaving a unit aboard reduce its sailing levels (level x men-after), men arriving into a unit aboard return None and silence that fleet's crew check for the month; Ruleset::is_man decides which tags are men and ruleset None silences it. 7) The aboard set is summed as Option<i64> so one unknowable unit silences the whole fleet's crew check; a None is never defaulted to 0. 8) ledger.doubted guards the crew finding alone, never the fleet-wide continue, so overload warnings that ship today are undisturbed. 9) The crew message says when the crew changed this month, verbatim: 'Raft [218] is short of sailors: 2 sailing levels aboard less 1 given away this month, it needs 2, so it will not sail'; unchanged crews keep the shipped sentence byte for byte. 10) The nine new semantics tests pass, a_full_crew_that_gives_nothing_away_still_sails included — that is the first failure's regression. 11) All four of Psylocke's verification cases re-run and pass: sail alone silent, give 0 1 GNOL warns undercrewed, ENTER 235 still warns overloaded, the Sailing group still toggles both codes. 12) The load half of check_sailing is unchanged.
notes:
Verification failed (2026-08-17, at origin/main cd092e6): case 3 of the verification, the silent case, warns. Fixture tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-g5-f21-t23.rep, Ship [218] at ocean (38,44), stated 'Load: 70/450; Sailors: 2/2'. Drones (9508) aboard is 2 gnolls with sailing [SAIL] 1; ordering it SAIL produces 'Raft [218] is short of sailors: 1 sailing levels aboard, it needs 2, so it will not sail'. The fleet sails perfectly well and the bead's own validation requires silence here.

Cause: crew_sailing_levels (crates/core/src/movement/mode.rs:267) sums each unit's SAIL skill level once per unit and ignores the number of men in the unit. Atlantis counts sailing levels as level x men, which is what the report's own 'Sailors: H/N' H figure states - here 2, not 1. Any fleet crewed by multi-man units of low skill is warned about wrongly, and a false positive on a warning check is worse than a miss.

Note the function predates this bead (ah-2vy.2 wrote it for the movement planner); ah-j0e is what turned it into a warning a player sees, and the planner's speed reckoning is likely wrong in the same way. Fixing it needs the men count per unit available alongside the skill.
Second evidence, from ah-paj (filed by Beast while planning ah-eet, closed as superseded by this bead on the navigator's decision 2026-08-17). Same defect, a different fixture, plus the rules quote and why it went unnoticed:

Found while planning ah-eet, on a real fixture report, not from reading the code.

The 'fleet-undercrewed' check sums each aboard unit's sailing skill *level*, once per unit
(crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs, check_sailing: '.flat_map(|ordered| ordered.unit.skills.iter())
.filter(tag == SAIL).map(level).sum()'). The engine counts a level per *man*: a unit of 2 gnolls at
sailing 1 supplies 2 sailing levels, not 1.

Evidence, tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-g5-f21-t24.rep:1359-1362 --

    + Ship [235] : Raft; Load: 220/450; Sailors: 2/2; MaxSpeed: 2.
      * Drones (10575), ... 2 gnolls [GNOL], 2180 silver [SILV]. Weight: 20.
        Skills: sailing [SAIL] 1 (30).
      * Drones (10594), ... 20 gnolls [GNOL]. Weight: 200. Skills: fishing [FISH] 1 (30).

The server states Sailors: 2/2 -- two levels aboard, two needed, so this Raft sails, and it does
sail in that turn's own orders template (line 2353, 'sail se ne'). Our sum is 1, so we warn
'Raft [235] is short of sailors: 1 sailing levels aboard, it needs 2, so it will not sail'. That is
a false warning on a committed fixture, against a fleet that sailed.

The rules agree with the server: 'The sailors are the number of skill levels of the Sailing skill
that must be aboard the ship' (tests/fixtures/ruleset/neworigins-rules.html:3747-3752), and a
unit's skill level is held by each of its men.

Why it went unnoticed: every unit in the Longship fixture ah-j0e was built against holds exactly
one man (neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t41.rep:2018-2025 -- one centaur at SAIL 2, one centaur at SAIL 2,
Sailors: 4/4), where per-unit and per-man agree. Every unit fixture in the semantics tests has
men: 1 for the same reason.

The fix is one multiplication -- level * unit.men -- plus a test with a multi-man crew, and the
same question should be asked of movement/mode.rs:220 crew_sailing_levels, which the route planner
uses and which sums the same way. Direction of the defect: false warnings, on every fleet crewed by
units of more than one man, which is most of them.

Not ah-eet's scope: that bead is the load half of this check, and touches nothing on the crew side.
Navigator at verification 2026-08-17: the build is wrong, not the plan - 'planned' stays and this goes straight back to the fleet as an ordinary P0. Cases 1, 2 and 4 of the verification all passed: ship 235 warned as undercrewed, ENTER 235 by unit 8333 warned as overloaded, and the Sailing group with its two toggles was present, on by default and working. Only the false positive in case 3 is at fault; re-verify all four after the fix.
Verification failed (2026-08-17, at origin/main 0ed5814): case 2, the genuinely-undercrewed case, is silent when the crew is reduced by an order given this month.

Fixture tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-g5-f21-t23.rep, Ship [218] (Raft) at ocean (38,44), stated 'Load: 70/450; Sailors: 2/2'. Unit Drones (9508) aboard is 2 gnolls at SAIL 1. Orders:

  give 0 1 GNOL
  sail N

After the GIVE the raft has 1 sailing level aboard against the 2 it needs, so it will not sail — and nothing warns. Case 1 (the previous failure, the false positive on the same ship) now passes: the per-man count from 8404597 is correct and is not what is wrong here.

Cause, and why it is the plan rather than the build: ah-j0e's own acceptance says the check counts 'report units aboard +/- ENTER/LEAVE at report weights and sailing levels' — a GIVE of men is not in that set, so the code matches its plan. ah-eet (scope C) then priced this month's GIVE/TAKE into each unit's *weight* and said in as many words that 'its sailors are still judged' on the report figures. So the crew side of a GIVE is covered by neither bead's design. The hole is in the plan, not in either implementation.

Navigator's call, 2026-08-17: plan wrong. For the amended plan to settle: whether the sailors count should follow this month's GIVE/TAKE of men the same way ah-eet made the load follow GIVE/TAKE of cargo (the symmetric answer, and the ledger ah-eet reused already tracks per-unit per-tag balances including men), and what 'silent on doubt' means here — a GIVE to a faction whose men have no known sailing level, or a TAKE bringing unknown men aboard. GIVE 0 (discarding men) is the case actually seen.
Verification passed 2026-08-17 at origin/main ec82563, on the third attempt. Both earlier failures re-checked and gone: the per-unit sailing count (fixed 8404597) and the crew unchanged by a GIVE of men (fixed ec82563, after Xavier amended the plan). The amended plan's answer - the sailors follow this month's GIVE/TAKE the way ah-eet made the load follow them - is what the message now states in as many words.

title: Beads wait ~7 minutes in a local gate CI repeats, and again on every BEHIND
description:
## Problem

Getting a bead from "implemented" to "merged" costs much more wall-clock than the actual build.
Measured on ah-k6i.4 (PR #284, a clean run with no rebase conflicts and zero review comments):

- Local `pnpm run check` before opening the PR: ~7 minutes wall clock, almost all of it the smoke
  suite (5.9m) plus build/pwa/rust/native on top. Lint/typecheck/unit were seconds.
- CI on the PR: ~3 minutes wall clock — the *same* suite, but parallelised across ~11 GitHub jobs.
- Review wait: ~2 minutes, running concurrently with CI since both start at PR-open.

So on a clean run, the single biggest cost is a local gate that duplicates work CI is about to do
anyway and is the thing that actually gates the merge — the local run only buys "catch it before a
human/reviewer sees it," which isn't worth ~7 minutes serialized on every bead.

It gets worse under fleet contention. `implement-bead`'s *Merging* section requires, on every
BEHIND: rebase locally, re-run the full local gate, wait for CI again — and the local gate takes a
machine-wide lock (the browser suites), so N implementers running concurrently queue behind each
other's local runs on top of paying the cost N times. With several implementers finishing near each
other, BEHIND keeps re-triggering and this cycle can repeat more than once per bead.

## Proposed changes (implement-bead skill + CI, for Xavier to plan and the navigator to decide)

1. **Stop running the full local `pnpm run check` before opening a PR.** Run only the fast, targeted
   checks locally (lint, typecheck, the touched package's unit tests) and let CI's parallel jobs do
   full verification — it's the thing that gates the merge regardless. Removes ~7 minutes and the
   local machine-wide lock's contention from every bead.

2. **Skip the local re-gate after a rebase when it's provably safe**, instead of always re-running
   the full local gate: if `git diff --stat <old-head>..<new-head> -- <touched files>` shows main's
   new commits didn't touch anything the bead's diff touches, push straight to CI rather than
   re-verifying locally first.

3. **Catch a BEHIND branch up on GitHub instead of locally.** Use the PR update-branch endpoint
   (`gh api -X PUT repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<n>/update-branch`) instead of
   `git fetch && git rebase && git push --force`. It performs a merge server-side rather than a
   rebase, which is fine here because every PR is squash-merged anyway — the branch's internal
   history never reaches main. This removes the local git mechanics and, combined with #1, removes
   the temptation to re-run a local gate against a checkout that was never touched. If the merge
   endpoint 422s on a real conflict, fall back to local resolution — no worse than today's rebase
   conflict case.

4. **Consider a GitHub merge queue** in front of `main`, configured to require "review requested +
   all checks green" before entering the queue. A queue serializes PRs, rebases/merges and runs CI
   once per entry — exactly what implementers currently do by hand, repeatedly, whenever several
   beads land in a short window. This is the highest-leverage change for the fleet-contention case
   specifically, but it's a repository-settings change (branch protection / merge queue config) the
   navigator has to make, not a skill-text change, so it may want to be split out or sequenced after
   1-3 are proven out.

5. **(Lower priority, worth a look)** Scope CI jobs by changed paths where safe — e.g. skip the
   `native` (Linux Tauri) job on a PR that touches nothing native-shaped. Needs care in a monorepo
   where shared UI code affects most things; likely only pays off for a subset of bead shapes.

## Scope

- In scope: `implement-bead`'s *Building* and *Merging* sections (what runs locally vs. what's
  trusted to CI, how BEHIND is resolved), and any CI workflow changes items 4-5 would need.
- Out of scope for this bead: actually enabling a merge queue (item 4) — file that as its own bead
  once 1-3 are validated, since it's a bigger repository-level decision with its own trade-offs
  (e.g. interaction with the existing "never --auto merge, Copilot review must land first" rule).

## Validation

- After the skill-text change, the next several beads' PR timelines (local time before PR open, CI
  wall clock, count of BEHIND-triggered rebase/re-gate cycles) should show local pre-PR time near
  zero and BEHIND recovery no longer paying a local gate run.
- No regression: a bead that would previously have failed CI must still fail CI (i.e. we are moving
  *where* verification happens, not skipping it) — nothing here proposes merging on local-gate-only
  or on CI-skipped state.

## Notes

Raised by the navigator after Wolverine's ah-k6i.4 run (PR #284); this bead only records and
proposes — the actual skill/CI edits are the navigator's and Xavier's to make, not an implementer's,
per CLAUDE.md's rule that changes to these instructions or the workflow itself need the navigator.
design:
## Context

Getting a bead from implemented to merged costs far more wall-clock than the build. Measured by the
navigator on ah-k6i.4 (PR #284, no conflicts, no review comments): the local `pnpm run check`
before the PR ~7 minutes (5.9 of them the smoke suite behind the machine-wide lock); CI on the PR
~3 minutes across ~11 parallel jobs — the same suite; and `implement-bead`'s *Merging* rule on
`BEHIND` (rebase → **local gate again** → CI again) repeats the 7 minutes, N times under
contention, with N implementers queuing on one lock. The local gate buys "catch it before the
reviewer sees it" and duplicates the thing that actually gates the merge.

Decided with the navigator (2026-08-15, all four as recommended): **(1)** before the PR, run
**fast checks only** — lint, typecheck, unit suites, cargo fmt/clippy — no browser suite, no lock;
CI is the gate. **(2)** on `BEHIND`, **update the branch on GitHub** (`update-branch`: a merge of
main into the branch, fine under squash-merge) and let CI rerun; **no local re-gate**; a 422 (real
conflict) falls back to a local rebase and push. **(3)** a merge queue is its own later bead —
**ah-jcr**, filed at P4. **(4)** CI's `changes` job — which already skips everything for prose-only
PRs — gains a second output that lets the slow, hang-prone **`native`** job skip when nothing
native-shaped changed. Rejected: fast checks plus the touched smoke project (adds ~3 min per bead for
a class CI catches anyway); a local rebase without re-gate (still local git mechanics under
contention); keeping the local re-gate.

**This is a workflow change**, which CLAUDE.md reserves for the navigator — they made it; the
implementer edits the texts. **Where the code lives.** cerebro submodule (`skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md`,
`agents/implementer.md`, `docs/agent-workflow.md`), PR 1 to `rmstdope/cerebro`; atlantis-hud PR 2:
`package.json` (`check:fast`), `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (`native` path scope), `CLAUDE.md` +
`.github/copilot-instructions.md` (byte-identical), and the bump. Line numbers against cerebro
`origin/main` `d05694b`+ (`SKILL.md` as of the ah-e0w/ah-2n3 edits — re-grep) and atlantis-hud
`origin/main` after #284.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### atlantis-hud `package.json`

Add beside `check`:

```json
"check:fast": "pnpm run lint && pnpm run typecheck && pnpm run test && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings"
```

— `check` minus `test:smoke`, `build:web`, `test:pwa`; `pnpm run test` is `scripts/runSuites.ts`
(every package's vitest, the tooling suite, `cargo test --workspace`; :23-27). Nothing else in
`package.json` changes; `check` stays for anyone who wants the full local run.

### atlantis-hud `.github/workflows/ci.yml`

- `changes` job (:32-75): a second output `native` (`steps.gate.outputs.native`), computed in the
  same step after `code`: `true` on a push (as `code` is), `true` when `FILES` is empty (fail open),
  `true` when any file matches
  `^(crates/|apps/desktop/|packages/core-client/|tests/native/|wdio\.conf\.ts$|\.github/workflows/|package\.json$|pnpm-lock\.yaml$|Cargo\.(toml|lock)$)`,
  else `false`. Comment: why each prefix (the Rust core and its Tauri wrappers, the desktop shell,
  the IPC adapter, the suite itself, the workflow, and the two lockfiles/manifests that change what
  the job installs), and that a shared-UI change does not need the native job because the native
  suite tests the IPC binding, not the UI (`tests/native/binding.spec.ts`'s header).
- `native` job (:422-425): `if: needs.changes.outputs.code == 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.native == 'true'`.
- Nothing else. **`scripts/ciDocsGate.test.ts`** pins the `changes` job's shape (it reads the
  `if:` at :32 and each job's gating at :94-158) — extend it: the `native` job is gated on both
  outputs, and the other jobs' assertions are unchanged; a unit case for the new path list if the
  file tests the shell logic (read it first — it may only assert the YAML shape).

### atlantis-hud `CLAUDE.md` and `.github/copilot-instructions.md` (byte-identical)

:331 "Before creating the PR, ALWAYS make sure all pre-commit checkpoints pass (see "Committing and
Merging to main" below)" — the section it points at does not exist; rewrite the bullet: before the
PR, `pnpm run check:fast` must pass; the browser suites and the PWA run are CI's job on the PR, and
a PR that is `BEHIND` is brought up to date on GitHub, not by a local rebase-and-re-gate (ah-s0m).
`diff CLAUDE.md .github/copilot-instructions.md` afterwards.

### cerebro `skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md`

- **Phase table** (:24-28): `*Building*, before pnpm check` → `before pnpm run check:fast`;
  the `*Merging*, on BEHIND` row → `--phase rebase` for the update, then `--phase ci` — the middle
  `gate` step goes. Keep the phase word `rebase` (the vocabulary in `agent-state` is fixed:
  `build|gate|review|ci|rebase|merge`); say it now means "catching the branch up".
- **Building** (:397-417): `pnpm run check:fast` replaces `pnpm check`; the paragraph about the
  machine-wide lock becomes one sentence — the browser suites are not run locally by default; run
  `pnpm run check` by choice when a smoke/pwa regression is suspected, and expect the lock. Keep
  the `test:native` sentence, plus: `native` runs in CI only when the diff touches native-shaped
  paths (list them).
- **Red CI** (:498-507): unchanged in rule; add one line — with no local browser run, a red smoke
  job is now the *first* sign, so read it as the gate rather than as a surprise; the flake rule
  ("reproduced locally once") stays, and reproducing locally means `pnpm run test:smoke` for that
  spec, not the whole `check`.
- **Merging** (:509-537): rewrite the `BEHIND` rule:

  ```bash
  .claude/cerebro/scripts/agent-state <name> working --bead <id> --phase rebase --pid $PPID
  gh api -X PUT "repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<n>/update-branch"      # main merged into the branch, on GitHub
  .claude/cerebro/scripts/agent-state <name> working --bead <id> --phase ci --pid $PPID
  # wait for CI on the new head; then merge as below
  ```

  With: why a merge is fine (squash-merge; the branch's history never reaches main); a **422**
  means a real conflict — `git fetch origin main && git rebase origin/main` in the worktree, resolve,
  `git push --force-with-lease`, back to `ci`; **no local gate in either path** — CI on the new head
  is the re-gate; `expect BEHIND on most merges` and the `--auto` warning stay word for word. The
  ah-u3i retrospective note about an empty bump PR after a rebase applies to the update path too
  (a merge that brings nothing new leaves the diff empty — close unmerged).
- **Traps** (:599 onward): drop any trap that presumes the local gate ran (grep "gate", "lock");
  keep the ones about CI.

### cerebro `agents/implementer.md` (:70) and `docs/agent-workflow.md` (:91-92)

The phase glossary: `gate` = "the fast local checks" (no longer "behind a machine-wide lock");
`rebase` = "catching the branch up on GitHub, or resolving a conflict locally".

### cerebro `README.md`, `emacs/README.md`

Nothing mentions the local gate by name (`grep -n "pnpm check\|local gate"`); confirm.

## Increments

1. atlantis-hud PR 2 first? No — **cerebro PR 1 first** is the usual order, but here the skill text
   names `check:fast`, which does not exist until PR 2 merges; and PR 2's CLAUDE.md names the new
   loop. Order: **PR 2 (atlantis-hud: `check:fast`, `native` scope, CLAUDE.md pair) first**, gated by
   today's rules; then **PR 1 (cerebro: the skill and docs)**; then **PR 3 (atlantis-hud: the
   bump)**. Say so in each PR body.
2. PR 2: RED — if `scripts/*.test.ts` pins the `changes` job's outputs, add the `native` cases
   (crates/ path → true, packages/shared/ path only → false, empty list → true); GREEN — the
   workflow edit; `check:fast` in `package.json`; run `pnpm run check:fast` locally to prove it
   passes and takes seconds; the CLAUDE.md pair. `@copilot`, CI, squash. `fix(ah-s0m): a fast local
   gate, and the native job runs only for native-shaped diffs`.
3. PR 1: the skill/docs edits; the ERT/bash suites unchanged (run them); `docs(ah-s0m): the
   implementer trusts CI: fast local checks, and BEHIND is caught up on GitHub`; `@copilot`; CI; squash.
4. PR 3: the bump. Close the bead. **Report to the navigator that running implementers keep the
   old text until restarted** — a session reads its skill at start.

## The test plan

- `pnpm run check:fast` green and timed (paste the wall clock in the PR).
- CI on PR 2: all jobs as before (the diff touches `.github/workflows/`, so `native` still runs).
- After merge: the next few PRs' timelines (the bead's own validation) — local pre-PR time near
  zero, no local re-gate on `BEHIND`; a shared-UI-only PR shows `native` skipped.

## User-facing decisions

None a player sees. Navigator (2026-08-15): the four decisions in *Context*, with the rejected
alternatives; ah-jcr filed for the merge queue.

## Out of scope

- Enabling a merge queue (ah-jcr).
- Scoping any job other than `native`.
- Changing the review rules, `--auto`, or the squash-merge rule.

## Validation

```bash
time pnpm run check:fast
diff CLAUDE.md .github/copilot-instructions.md
# after PR 1+3: a fresh implementer session's first gate is check:fast; on BEHIND it calls update-branch
```

Human check: none; Psylocke marks not-needed (harness/CI/docs).

## Known traps

- **Order of the three PRs** (above): the skill must not name a script main does not have.
- **`update-branch` needs the PR's head to be on the same repository** (it is; every branch is
  pushed to origin) and returns 202 — the merge commit appears a moment later; poll
  `gh pr view <n> --json mergeStateStatus` before waiting on CI.
- **The `changes` gate must fail open** — an empty file list or an API error means `native=true`;
  copy the existing `code` logic's shape.
- **Do not branch inside the shared `.claude/cerebro`**; worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/`
  (until ah-v82 moves them), absolute path for the cerebro one.
- **Running implementers do not reload the skill**; the change takes effect per session start.
acceptance_criteria: implement-bead's Merging section no longer requires a full local pnpm run check before every PR and after every BEHIND rebase; BEHIND recovery uses GitHub's update-branch endpoint instead of local rebase where no conflict exists; a merge-queue bead is filed separately rather than bundled in here

title: Hex-note pin: the count badge and the opened tags' text are too small to read
description:
Found during verification of ah-o1t.3 (map-visible hex notes shown as a pin). The navigator confirmed the feature works correctly — pin placement, click-to-open, count badge, Badges toggle, zoom behaviour and light theme all passed — but flagged two cosmetic sizing issues:

1. The count badge on the pin is too small; needs to be a bit larger.
2. The expanded tag's note text is too small — unreadable at all zoom levels. Needs to be noticeably larger than it currently is (more than the badge fix).

Relevant files: packages/shared/src/workspace/MapCanvas.tsx, packages/shared/src/workspace/mapNotes.ts, packages/shared/src/theme.css (from ah-o1t.3, PR #276).
design:
## Context

Psylocke's verification of ah-o1t.3 (map-visible hex notes as a pin, PR #276) passed on behaviour
and failed on legibility: the pin's count badge is a bit too small, and the expanded tags' note text
is unreadable at every zoom. Both are drawn in **constant screen pixels** — the whole pin group is
counter-scaled by `1 / scaleOf(view.step)` (`MapCanvas.tsx:1125-1129` on `origin/main` after #280 — `const scale = 1 / scaleOf(view.step)`),
so zooming the map never changes them — and the constants are simply small: badge `r=3.6` with
`fontSize={5}` digits (:1187-1197), tag text `fontSize={6}` on 8-px lines (:1214-1224), stamp
`fontSize={5}` (:1226-1233), wrapped at 28 characters (`mapNotes.ts:62`), tag geometry
`3.5 * chars + 8` wide and `8 * lines + 7 + 5` tall (`mapNotes.ts:113-129`).

The navigator chose **Option B** of `docs/ui/hex-notes-sizes.html` (committed by PR #282; 2026-08-15): the pin glyph
scaled ×1.3, the count badge `r 5.2` with 7.5-px digits, tag text **11 px on 14.5-px lines, 24
characters per line**, stamp 8 px, tag box `6.3 * chars + 12` wide. Everything else about the layer
— placement, click-to-open, the Badges toggle, the far-band cut-off, colours in both themes, the
four-line cut with "…", the tooltip — is unchanged and was verified passing.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/mapNotes.ts`

Replace `PIN_W`/`PIN_H` (:50-51) with the sizes as named constants, all in screen px:

```ts
/** The pin glyph is drawn at ×PIN_SCALE of its 9×10 path units; badge and tags are in screen px. */
export const PIN_SCALE = 1.3;
export const PIN_W = 9 * PIN_SCALE;    // 11.7
export const PIN_H = 10 * PIN_SCALE;   // 13
/** The count badge, in screen px: centred on the glyph's top-right corner (4.5, -5 path units). */
export const BADGE = { cx: 4.5 * PIN_SCALE, cy: -5 * PIN_SCALE, r: 5.2, fontSize: 7.5, baseline: 2.7 };
/** The expanded tags, in screen px (docs/ui/hex-notes-sizes.html, Option B). */
export const TAG = { fontSize: 11, lineHeight: 14.5, maxChars: 24, charWidth: 6.3, pad: 12, stampFontSize: 8 };
```

- `wrapNoteLines(text, maxChars = TAG.maxChars, maxLines = 4)` (:62) — default only; the function is
  unchanged.
- `noteTagLayout` (:113-129): `width = TAG.charWidth * widestLine + TAG.pad`;
  `height = TAG.lineHeight * lines.length + (stamp ? TAG.stampFontSize + 2 : 0) + 5`;
  `x: PIN_W / 2 + 5` and `y` starting at `-PIN_H / 2`, `y += height + 3` — as today, through the
  new constants.

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/MapCanvas.tsx` (:1122-1240)

- Wrap the three glyph `<path>`s (:1176-1186) in `<g transform={\`scale(${PIN_SCALE})\`}>` — the
  glyph paths themselves unchanged. `role="button"`, `aria-*`, `data-testid="map-note-pin"`, the
  click handler and `<title>` stay on the outer `<g>` as today.
- The badge (:1187-1197): `<circle cx={BADGE.cx} cy={BADGE.cy} r={BADGE.r} …/>` and
  `<text x={BADGE.cx} y={BADGE.cy + BADGE.baseline} textAnchor="middle" fontSize={BADGE.fontSize} …>` —
  outside the scaled group, so it is in screen px.
- Tag text (:1214-1224): `x={tag.x + TAG.pad / 2}`, `y={tag.y + TAG.lineHeight * 0.85 + i * TAG.lineHeight}`,
  `fontSize={TAG.fontSize}`; stamp (:1226-1233): `y={tag.y + TAG.lineHeight * 0.85 + tag.lines.length * TAG.lineHeight}`,
  `fontSize={TAG.stampFontSize}`. The tag `<path>` (:1209-1213) reads `tag.x/y/width/height` and
  needs no change; its little pointer (`l-3 -4z`) stays.
- Import `BADGE`, `PIN_SCALE`, `TAG` from `./mapNotes` (:43).

### Tests — `packages/shared/src/workspace/mapNotes.test.ts`

- `wrapNoteLines` "at most 28 characters a line" (:65-76) → 24, reading `TAG.maxChars`; the
  four-line cut and newline cases unchanged.
- `noteTagLayout` (:96-110): keep; add one assertion pinning the geometry:
  `note({ text: "hi", turn: 71 })` → `width` = `6.3 * 2 + 12`, `height` = `14.5 + 10 + 5`, `x` =
  `PIN_W / 2 + 5`, first `y` = `-PIN_H / 2` — via the constants, `toBeCloseTo`.
- New: `it("exports the chosen sizes", …)` — `PIN_SCALE` 1.3, `BADGE.r` 5.2, `BADGE.fontSize` 7.5,
  `TAG.fontSize` 11, `TAG.lineHeight` 14.5, `TAG.maxChars` 24, `TAG.stampFontSize` 8 — the numbers
  the navigator chose, so a later "tidy" cannot silently shrink them again.
- Smoke (`tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts:3185-3220`): unchanged — it asserts presence and
  open/close, not sizes; must stay green.

## Increments

1. RED: the two `mapNotes.test.ts` changes and the new sizes test. GREEN: `mapNotes.ts`.
2. `MapCanvas.tsx` through the constants; `pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared typecheck`; the smoke
   note cases (`pnpm run test:smoke -- --grep "note"` — check the exact test names at :3185); full
   gate; PR `fix(ah-j3p): the hex-note pin's badge and tags are large enough to read`, `@copilot`,
   CI, squash. Close.

## The test plan

- Unit: `mapNotes.test.ts`; typecheck; `pnpm run check`.
- Smoke note cases green in both projects (web and desktop-shell).

## User-facing decisions

Navigator (2026-08-15), from `docs/ui/hex-notes-sizes.html`: **Option B** — pin ×1.3, badge r 5.2 /
7.5-px digits, tag text 11 px on 14.5-px lines, 24 chars/line, stamp 8 px (rejected: Option A —
pin ×1.15, badge r 4.6 / 6.5 px, tag text 9 px on 12-px lines, 26 chars — readable but still small
at arm's length; keeping the pin glyph at today's size with only badge and tags enlarged — a bigger
badge overhangs the 9×10 glyph). Wrap width goes 28 → 24 characters so a four-line tag stays about
160 px wide; the four-line cut and "…" are unchanged. Colours unchanged in both themes.

## Out of scope

- Any change to where the pin sits (`PIN_OFFSET`), the far-band rule, the Badges toggle, or the
  notes section in the region panel.
- Making sizes zoom-dependent.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared test -- mapNotes && pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared typecheck
pnpm run check
```

Human check (Psylocke, this is her follow-up): load a report with two notes on one hex — the badge
digit is legible without leaning in; click the pin — the tag text is comfortably readable at any
zoom; a long note wraps at 24 characters and cuts at four lines with "…"; light theme the same.

## Known traps

- **Screen px, not world units**: the pin group is counter-scaled at :1125-1129; keep the badge and
  tags *outside* the new `scale(PIN_SCALE)` group or they scale twice.
- **The tag box is laid out from character counts** (`charWidth`), not measured text — 6.3 px per
  character at 11 px Helvetica/Arial is the mockup's number; if a line visibly overflows the box on
  the desktop shell (WebKit's fallback font is wider), raise `charWidth`, not `maxChars`.
- **The smoke suite takes the machine-wide lock**; run it once at the end.
- ah-k6i slices are moving `AppShell.tsx`, not `MapCanvas.tsx`/`mapNotes.ts` — no rebase risk from
  them; ah-o1t.3 (#276) is the base, already on main.

title: The multi-report batch import is a testable module the shell only applies
description: Sixth slice of ah-k6i. importReports, runBatch and chooseOrdersImport - reading, sniffing, walking and committing a dropped batch, and the pending-batch and pending-orders-import prompts they raise - move out of AppShell.tsx into a plain module, built on ah-k6i.5's report-load module. The batch's parallel-list invariants and its progress reporting get unit tests.
design:
## Context

Sixth and last slice of **ah-k6i**, on **ah-k6i.1** and **ah-k6i.5** (both planned; both block
this — read both plans: .1 gives `runReported`/`failedStatus`; .5 gives `reportLoad.ts` with
`reportParser`, `factionLabelOf`, `applyReport` through `loadTurn` and the shell's `applyLoadedTurn`).
What remains inline in `AppShell.tsx` (`origin/main` `deb434a`, before those land) is the batch and
the orders-file drop: `importReports` (:1418-1522) — one file goes to `loadReport` or, if it sniffs
as orders, to `chooseOrdersImport`; several files are read and parsed up front into a
`PreparedBatch` (:289-300), then `chooseViewerFaction` (`reportBatch.ts:67`) either asks (the
`pendingBatch` prompt with faction options, :1508-1518) or runs; `runBatch` (:1287-1416) — plan
(`planReportBatch`, `reportBatch.ts:126`), walk the steps committing or merging with per-step failure
demoted to a skip and progress reported, then read the map back once and either apply the batch's
newest own turn through `applyReport(…, memory)` or refresh the map under the unchanged turn, then
the summary; `chooseOrdersImport` (:1230-1285) — refuse an orders file with no turn or the wrong
faction, else hold a `PendingOrdersImport` snapshot (:262-287); `replaceOrdersImport` (:2157-2222) —
apply the held orders, validate, summarise or report. `reportBatch.ts` already holds every *planning*
decision, tested; the reading, the walk, the summary assembly and the orders-file routing are the
parts that cannot be tested from inside the component.

This bead moves those into two plain modules and leaves the shell four `runReported` calls plus the
state they set. **No player-visible change** — every message, prompt, progress count and summary is
as today.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### New: `packages/shared/src/batchImport.ts`

```ts
import type { CoreClient, OpenedGame, ParsedReport } from "@atlantis/core-client";
import { commitTurn, mergeTurn } from "./gameMemory";
import { planReportBatch, type BatchCandidate, type BatchSkip, type BatchStep, type ReportBatchPlan } from "./reportBatch";
import type { ImportSummary } from "./importSummary";
import { factionLabelOf } from "./reportLoad";
import { describeError } from "./workspace/shellAction";

/** Moved from AppShell.tsx:289-300 with its doc comment. */
export type PreparedBatch = { read: ({ text: string; report: ParsedReport } | null)[]; candidates: BatchCandidate[]; unreadable: BatchSkip[] };

/** As much of a `File` as reading a batch needs - the tests hand in object literals. */
export type ChosenFile = { name: string; text: () => Promise<string> };

/**
 * Reads and parses every chosen file before a word is written (:1452-1481). A file that will not
 * read or parse costs the batch that file: it stays a candidate (so indices stay the chosen files'
 * indices), with `read[i] === null` and an `unreadable` entry whose reason is
 * `could not be read: <error>`. Never rejects for a per-file failure.
 */
export async function prepareBatch(files: ChosenFile[], parse: (text: string) => Promise<ParsedReport>): Promise<PreparedBatch>;

/** The prompt's options when the batch cannot say whose it is (:1510-1518): a label per faction id, `faction <id>` when no report names it. */
export function viewerFactionOptions(batch: PreparedBatch, factionIds: string[]): { factionId: string; label: string }[];

/** What the walk left behind, for the shell to finish (read the map back, apply, summarise). */
export type BatchWalk = {
  plan: ReportBatchPlan;
  /** Steps that landed - `plan.steps` minus the failures. */
  landed: BatchStep[];
  /** Plan skips (with the unreadable reason where there is one) plus walk failures, by index. */
  skipped: BatchSkip[];
  /** The step whose report goes on screen - the LAST landed own import of the plan's final turn (:1360-1373) - and its source; null when none of the viewer's own turns landed. */
  finish: { step: BatchStep & { kind: "import" }; source: { text: string; report: ParsedReport } } | null;
};

/**
 * Walks the plan (:1292-1358): commits an own report (a commit *warning* is a failure here -
 * :1327-1329), merges an ally's under the viewer's faction and the ally's turn, demotes any failure
 * to a skip with `describeError`'s reason, calls `onProgress(done, total)` after every step (total
 * is the step count, not the file count - :1300-1303). Rejects only for something outside a step.
 */
export async function walkBatch(
  client: CoreClient, game: OpenedGame, batch: PreparedBatch, viewerFactionId: string,
  workingTurn: number | null, rulesetText: string | null, now: () => string,
  onProgress: (done: number, total: number) => void
): Promise<BatchWalk>;

/** The summary dialog's contents (:1397-1403). */
export function batchSummary(walk: BatchWalk, viewerReport: ParsedReport | null): ImportSummary;
```

The `!game || !source` guard at :1310-1320 goes: `game` is non-null by the signature, and a
`null` `source` cannot be a step (a file that did not parse is never planned) — keep a comment
saying so, and treat it as a failure with the same reason if it ever is (`"there was no open game
to import it into"` becomes `"the file could not be read"` — no: keep the string as it is; it is
unreachable and the string is what a summary would show).

### `packages/shared/src/ordersImport.ts` (existing; add)

```ts
/** Moved from AppShell.tsx:262-287 with its doc comment. */
export type PendingOrdersImport = { … as today … };

export type OrdersImportRoute =
  | { kind: "refuse"; message: string }
  | { kind: "ask"; pending: PendingOrdersImport };

/**
 * What an orders file dropped on the Import target does (:1230-1285): refused with
 * `no turn to apply orders to` when no turn is on screen; refused with
 * `<file> is orders for faction <id|unknown>, not <viewer label|your faction>` when the factions
 * differ; otherwise held, with the counts worked out now from the document on screen.
 */
export function routeOrdersImport(
  viewer: { game: OpenedGame | null; parsed: ParsedReport | null }, text: string, fileName: string, ordersDocument: string
): OrdersImportRoute;
```

(`factionLabelOf` from `./reportLoad`; `describeOrdersImport`, `ordersFileFaction` are already here.)

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx`

- Delete `PreparedBatch` (:289-300) and `PendingOrdersImport` (:262-287, doc comment included); import them.
- `chooseOrdersImport(text, fileName)`: `const route = routeOrdersImport({ game, parsed }, text, fileName, ordersDocument); if (route.kind === "refuse") { setStatus(failedStatus(route.message)); return; } setPendingLoad(null); setPendingOrdersImport(route.pending);` — keep the comment at :1268-1270.
- `replaceOrdersImport` (:2157-2222): the stale-turn guard and its message stay (:2166-2178); the
  body becomes `void runReported(async () => { setOrdersDocument(pending.text); writer.markDirty(game, draftKey, pending.text); const result = await client.validateOrders(…); if (result.diagnostics.length > 0) setOrdersImportSummary({…}); else setStatus({ regionCount: 0, unitCount: pending.unitCount, message: \`orders imported: ${pending.unitCount} unit${pending.unitCount === 1 ? "" : "s"}\`, failed: false, warning: false }); }, (m) => setStatus(failedStatus(m)), { busy: setBusy, prefix: \`could not import ${pending.fileName}\` })`.
- `runBatch(batch, viewerFactionId)`:
  ```ts
  runReported(async () => {
    if (!game || !viewerFactionId) return;                       // today's guards, kept as one early exit
    const walk = await walkBatch(client, game, batch, viewerFactionId, parsed?.header.turnNumber ?? null, rulesetText, () => new Date().toISOString(), (done, total) => setImportProgress({ done, total }));
    if (walk.finish) {
      const memory = await readMemory(client, game, viewerFactionId, walk.finish.step.turnNumber);   // :1376-1379's comment
      await applyReport(walk.finish.source.report, walk.finish.source.text, walk.finish.step.fileName, memory);
    } else {
      const memory = await readMemory(client, game, viewerFactionId, parsed?.header.turnNumber ?? null);   // :1381-1391
      setRemembered(memory.remembered); setMergedReports(memory.merged);
    }
    setImportSummary(batchSummary(walk, walk.finish?.source.report ?? parsed));
  }, (m) => setStatus(failedStatus(m)), { busy: (b) => { setBusy(b); if (!b) setImportProgress(null); } })
  ```
  Today `runBatch` has no `catch` — a rejection outside a step was unhandled; now it is reported.
  The message the player would see is `describeError`'s text with no prefix (there was none to keep).
- `importReports(files)`: single-file path unchanged except `setStatus(failedStatus(…))`; the batch
  path becomes `const batch = await runReported(async () => { await flush(); return prepareBatch(files, reportParser(client, ruleset)); }, (m) => setStatus(failedStatus(m)), { busy: (b) => { setBusy(b); if (!b) setImportProgress(null); }, prefix: "could not start the import" }); if (!batch) return;` — `setImportProgress({ done: 0, total: files.length })` before it as today (:1446); then `chooseViewerFaction` as today, `setPendingBatch({ batch, options: viewerFactionOptions(batch, choice.factionIds) })` or `await runBatch(batch, choice.factionId)`.
- The prompt JSX (:2891-2903) unchanged.

### Tests

- New `packages/shared/src/batchImport.test.ts`: `prepareBatch` — three files, one whose `text()`
  rejects and one whose parse rejects → `read` has nulls at those indices, `candidates` keeps all
  three (`factionId: null` for the failed), `unreadable` has two entries with `could not be read:`
  reasons; `viewerFactionOptions` — label from the report naming the faction, `faction 95` when
  none; `walkBatch` — with a fake client and `vi.mock`ed or stubbed `commitTurn`/`mergeTurn` (use
  `gameMemory.test.ts`'s approach): an own step commits, an ally step merges under the viewer's
  faction and the ally's turn, a commit warning becomes a skip with that warning as reason, a
  rejecting merge becomes a skip with `describeError`'s text, `onProgress` is called once per step
  with a total of steps not files, `finish` is the last own import of `plan.finalTurn` when two files
  describe that turn, and `null` when only ally reports landed; `batchSummary` — steps/skipped sorted
  by index/finalTurn null when no finish/viewer label falls back to `an unnamed faction`.
- `ordersImport.test.ts` (existing — extend): `routeOrdersImport` — no turn → refuse
  `no turn to apply orders to`; wrong faction → the exact `… is orders for faction 17, not Borg TNG
  (95)` string, and `unknown`/`your faction` fallbacks; matching → `ask` with the snapshot's
  `gameId`/`factionId`/`turnNumber`/counts from `describeOrdersImport`.

## Increments

1. RED: `routeOrdersImport` cases in `ordersImport.test.ts`. GREEN: the function and moved type;
   `chooseOrdersImport` and `replaceOrdersImport` rewritten (typecheck).
2. RED: `prepareBatch`, `viewerFactionOptions`. GREEN.
3. RED: `walkBatch`, `batchSummary`. GREEN.
4. `runBatch` and `importReports` rewritten; typecheck; the shared suite; the full gate.
5. PR `refactor(ah-k6i.6): the batch import and the orders-file drop live in batchImport.ts and
   ordersImport.ts`, `@copilot`, CI, squash. **Close the bead and the epic** (this is the last
   child): `bd close ah-k6i.6 …` then `bd close ah-k6i --reason "all six slices merged"`.

## The test plan

- Unit: `batchImport.test.ts` (new), `ordersImport.test.ts` (extended), `reportBatch.test.ts`,
  `importSummary` tests, `reportLoad.test.ts` (from .5), whole shared suite.
- `pnpm run check`; the smoke suite drags a batch and imports an orders file
  (`grep -n "batch\|orders file\|Replace" tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts`).

## User-facing decisions

None — every string quoted above is today's; the prompts, the progress `done/total`, the summary
dialog and the busy flag behave as before. (Navigator not asked; nothing to choose. The one silent
failure fixed — a rejection outside a batch step — now shows `describeError`'s text on the status
line, which is what every other failure in the shell does.)

## Out of scope

- `reportBatch.ts`'s planning rules, `importSummary.ts`, the two prompt components.
- The single-file path (`loadReport`, ah-k6i.5) beyond the `failedStatus` builder.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared test -- batchImport ordersImport reportBatch reportLoad
pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared typecheck && pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared lint
pnpm run check
```

Human check (Psylocke): drop three turns of one faction plus one ally report — progress counts
steps, the newest own turn lands with the ally merged, the summary lists what landed and what was
skipped; drop a batch of two factions' reports — the viewer prompt appears with labels; drop an
orders file for the open turn — Replace prompt with counts, then `orders imported: N units`.

## Known traps

- **Read the map back, never re-commit the finishing turn** (:1374-1379): `applyReport(…, memory)`
  with `readMemory`'s outcome, or the ally contributions to shared hexes are lost. `walkBatch` must
  not call `applyReport`/`loadTurn` itself for the same reason — it walks and stops.
- **A commit warning is a batch failure but a single-load warning** (:1327-1329 vs `loadTurn`) —
  keep the asymmetry and its comment.
- **Progress totals are steps, not files** (:1300-1303) — the smoke suite may assert the `n/m` text;
  check before changing anything.
- **`prepareBatch` never rejects per file** — the `runReported` around it exists for `flush()` and
  the "could not start the import" case only (:1483-1494's comment moves onto the call).
- **No DOM renderer**; **`pnpm run check`'s tooling worktree test** may fail on scratch worktrees
  (ah-efj) — finish the gate by hand and say so.
- `AppShell.tsx` moves under .2-.5; re-grep every line above when branching.

title: Loading a report into the workspace is a testable module the shell only applies
description: Fifth slice of ah-k6i, the largest. applyReport, storeReportOnly, loadReport, switchFaction and mergeReport - the path from a chosen file to a turn on screen - move out of AppShell.tsx into a plain module that returns what changed (parsed turn, remembered map, merged reports, orders document, saved state, status) for the shell to apply in one place; the pending-load prompt's snapshot rule and the older-report store-only rule get direct unit tests.

title: Export actions (orders, map, game backup) live in a testable module
description: Fourth slice of ah-k6i. deliverOrdersExport and deliverGameBackupExport leave AppShell.tsx for an exports module (their tests in AppShell.test.ts go with them), and exportMap's body - the last inline exporter - is extracted the same way, so a fourth exporter starts from the module rather than from the component.
design:
## Context

Fourth slice of **ah-k6i**, on **ah-k6i.1** (planned; blocks this — `runReported` in
`packages/shared/src/workspace/shellAction.ts`). The three exporters the shell owns are in three
states of extraction (`origin/main` `deb434a`, before .1): `deliverOrdersExport`
(`AppShell.tsx:172-206`) and `deliverGameBackupExport` (:207-220) were pulled out of the component
by ah-7pa and ah-jfx — the same defect three times, a desktop export landing wherever the webview put
it — but still live in the component's file with their tests in `AppShell.test.ts:23-125`; the map
export (`exportMap`, :2368-2404) is the last one still inline, with its own `exportBusy` /
`exportError` / `exportOpen` shape (:451-454). This bead gives the three one home,

title: Game picker actions (open, create, delete, ruleset, backup) live in a testable module
description: Second slice of ah-k6i. openGameById, changeRuleset, createGame, deleteGame, exportGameBackup, importGameBackup and refreshGames move out of AppShell.tsx into a plain module the shell only applies - the same setBusy/setGameError/try/finally shape written seven times becomes one call through the ah-k6i.1 helper, and the decisions (which game to land on after a delete, whether a cancelled backup save closes the picker) get unit tests.
design:
## Context

Second slice of **ah-k6i**, on top of **ah-k6i.1** (planned; blocks this — read its plan: it gives
you `runReported` and `describeError` in `packages/shared/src/workspace/shellAction.ts`). The seven
game-management handlers in `AppShell.tsx` — `refreshGames` (:1702), `openGameById` (:1766),
`changeRuleset` (:1794), `createGame` (:1823), `deleteGame` (:1886), `exportGameBackup` (:1917),
`importGameBackup` (:1940); lines against `origin/main` `deb434a`, before .1 lands — are seven
copies of one shape: `setBusy(true); setGameError(null); try { await flush(); …; await
refreshGames(); setPickerOpen(false); } catch { setGameError(describeError(e)) } finally {
setBusy(false) }`. The decisions inside them that are not already in
`packages/shared/src/gameSession.ts` (which owns `newestGame`, `gameAfterDelete`, `newGameManifest`,
`newGameId`, `openNewestGame`, all tested) are: the delete sequence (discard the open draft only when
the deleted game is the open one, then land on the next or close), the ruleset-change guards (same
ruleset → nothing; unknown ruleset → an error, no busy), and a cancelled backup save leaving the
picker open. None of that can be unit-tested while it sits in the component.

This bead moves the async doing into a plain module beside `gameSession.ts` and collapses the seven
handlers to one-line `runReported` calls through a local `runGameAction`. **No player-visible
change** — same messages, same busy flag, same picker behaviour. `enterGame` (:1713-1764) is pure
state setting and stays in the shell; the startup effect (:1849-1873) stays as it is (it has its own
cancellation flag; out of scope).

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### New: `packages/shared/src/gameActions.ts`

```ts
import type { CoreClient, GameManifest, OpenedGame } from "@atlantis/core-client";
import { gameAfterDelete, newGameId, newGameManifest } from "./gameSession";
import { rulesetById } from "./rulesets";

/** The slice of the client these actions need - a fake in the tests is an object literal. */
export type GameClient = Pick<
  CoreClient,
  "listGames" | "openGame" | "createGame" | "deleteGame" | "exportGame" | "importGame" | "setGameRuleset"
>;

/** What a game action leaves behind for the shell to apply. */
export type GameActionOutcome = {
  /** The game now open, when the action opened one; the shell enters it. `null`: leave the shell alone. */
  opened: OpenedGame | null;
  /** The list of games after the action, for the picker. */
  games: GameManifest[];
};

export async function openGame(client: GameClient, gameId: string, now: string): Promise<GameActionOutcome>;
export async function createGame(client: GameClient, name: string, rulesetId: string, now: string): Promise<GameActionOutcome>;
export async function importGameBackup(client: GameClient, backupJson: string, now: string): Promise<GameActionOutcome>;

/**
 * Deletes GAME-ID and lands the player somewhere. `discardOpenDraft` is called - before the delete -
 * only when the deleted game is `openGameId`: its database is about to go, so nothing may be
 * flushed into it (AppShell's `writer.discard()`). Resolves `{ opened: next-or-null, games }` when
 * the open game was deleted (`opened: null` there means "close the workspace"), and
 * `{ opened: null, games }` when some other game was.
 */
export async function deleteGame(
  client: GameClient, gameId: string, openGameId: string | null, now: string, discardOpenDraft: () => void
): Promise<GameActionOutcome & { closedOpenGame: boolean }>;

/**
 * Moves GAME to RULESET-ID. `null` when there is nothing to do (same ruleset). Throws
 * `Error("unknown ruleset: <id>")` for a ruleset this build does not ship - the caller's reporter
 * turns that into the same `gameError` text as today. Resolves the new manifest and the games list.
 */
export async function changeRuleset(
  client: GameClient, game: OpenedGame, rulesetId: string
): Promise<{ manifest: OpenedGame["manifest"]; games: GameManifest[] } | null>;
```

`openGame`: `const opened = await client.openGame(gameId, now); return { opened, games: await
client.listGames() }`. `createGame`: `client.createGame(newGameManifest(name, rulesetId, now,
newGameId()))` then list. `importGameBackup`: `client.importGame(backupJson, now)` then list.
`deleteGame`: as the inline code at :1886-1914, using `gameAfterDelete(remaining, gameId)`.
`changeRuleset`: guards as at :1796-1802, then `client.setGameRuleset(...)` and list. Header doc:
why a module (the same sentence `gameSession.ts:4-6` uses — testable without rendering), and that
`flush()`, `enterGame`, the store and the picker are the shell's business (see below).

`exportGameBackup` **stays in the shell** for now (its body is `deliverGameBackupExport`, which
**ah-k6i.4** moves into an exports module; do not move it here) — but it goes through
`runGameAction` like the rest.

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx`

- One local closure right after the state declarations that these use (`busy` :401, `gameError`
  :466):

  ```ts
  /** Every game action runs through here: clears the last error, holds `busy`, reports a failure. */
  const runGameAction = useCallback(
    (work: () => Promise<void>, prefix?: string) => {
      setGameError(null);
      return runReported(work, setGameError, { busy: setBusy, prefix });
    },
    []
  );
  ```

- The handlers become (each keeps its doc comment, trimmed of the shape it no longer has):
  - `openGameById(gameId)`: `runGameAction(async () => { await flush(); const o = await openGame(client, gameId, new Date().toISOString()); enterGame(o.opened!); setGames(o.games); setPickerOpen(false); })` — `opened` is non-null for `openGame`; type it so (`opened: OpenedGame` on a narrower return type, or a `!` with a one-line comment; prefer a narrower type: make `openGame`/`createGame`/`importGameBackup` return `{ opened: OpenedGame; games }` and only `deleteGame` the nullable form).
  - `createGame(name, rulesetId)`: same with `createGame`.
  - `importGameBackup(file)`: `runGameAction(async () => { await flush(); const o = await importGameBackup(client, await file.text(), now); enterGame(o.opened); setGames(o.games); setPickerOpen(false); setSettingsOpen(false); }, \`could not import ${file.name}\`)` — the prefix reproduces today's `could not import <name>: <error>` (:1956).
  - `changeRuleset(rulesetId)`: `if (!game) return; runGameAction(async () => { await flush(); const r = await changeRuleset(client, game, rulesetId); if (!r) return; setGame({ ...game, manifest: r.manifest }); updateGameRulesetInStore(rulesetId); setGames(r.games); })`. Note today's "unknown ruleset" path did not toggle `busy`; going through `runGameAction` it briefly does — accepted (a synchronous throw inside `work` still settles in the same tick).
  - `deleteGame(gameId)`: no `flush()` (:1878-1880 says why — keep that comment). `runGameAction(async () => { const r = await deleteGame(client, gameId, game?.manifest.metadata.gameId ?? null, now, () => writer.discard()); setGames(r.games); if (r.closedOpenGame) { if (r.opened) enterGame(r.opened); else { setGame(null); closeGameInStore(); } } setPickerOpen(false); })`.
  - `exportGameBackup(gameId)`: body unchanged, wrapped: `runGameAction(async () => { await flush(); const backup = await client.exportGame(gameId, now); const path = await deliverGameBackupExport(saveTextFile, gameId, backup); if (path === null) return; setPickerOpen(false); })`.
  - `refreshGames` (:1702-1704) is deleted: every action now returns `games`, and its only callers
    were these handlers (check with grep before deleting; if anything else calls it, keep it).
- The JSX `void handler(...)` sites (:2659, :2683-2684, :2709-2713) are unchanged in text — the
  handlers now return `runReported`'s never-rejecting promise, so the `void` is honest.
- Remove the imports of `newGameManifest`, `newGameId`, `gameAfterDelete` from `AppShell.tsx` if
  they become unused (`openNewestGame` stays for the startup effect).

### Tests

New `packages/shared/src/gameActions.test.ts` (vitest, plain-module style of
`gameSession.test.ts`; a fake `GameClient` is an object literal of `vi.fn()`s):

- `openGame` resolves the opened game and the refreshed list, in that order (`openGame` before
  `listGames`).
- `createGame` hands `client.createGame` a manifest whose name/ruleset/time come from the arguments
  (spy on the manifest's `metadata.gameName`, `rulesetId`, `createdAt`).
- `deleteGame`: deleting the open game discards the draft **before** `client.deleteGame` (record
  call order), lands on the next most recent (`opened` = that game, `closedOpenGame: true`), or
  `opened: null` when it was the last; deleting another game never discards and returns
  `opened: null, closedOpenGame: false`.
- `changeRuleset`: same ruleset → `null` and no client call; unknown ruleset → rejects with
  `Error("unknown ruleset: nope")` and no client call; a known one → `setGameRuleset` called and the
  manifest returned. Use a ruleset id `rulesetById` knows (see `gameSession.test.ts:66-71` for the
  fixture it uses).
- `importGameBackup` passes the JSON through and returns opened + list.

`AppShell.test.ts` unchanged.

## Increments

1. RED: `gameActions.test.ts` — `openGame`, `createGame`, `importGameBackup`. GREEN: the module.
2. RED: `deleteGame` and `changeRuleset` cases. GREEN.
3. `runGameAction` + the six handler rewrites + delete `refreshGames`; typecheck and the shared
   suite are the tests (the shell cannot be rendered). Then the full gate.
4. PR `refactor(ah-k6i.2): game picker actions live in gameActions.ts and run through one reporting
   path`, `@copilot`, CI, squash. Close the bead, not the epic.

## The test plan

- Unit: `gameActions.test.ts` (new), `gameSession.test.ts`, `shellAction.test.ts` (from .1), and the
  whole shared suite.
- `pnpm run check`; the smoke suite exercises the picker (open/create/delete) — `grep -n
  "picker\|Create game\|Delete" tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts` to see which cases must stay green.

## User-facing decisions

None — every message the player can see keeps its exact text: `unknown ruleset: <id>`,
`could not import <file>: <error>`, and the raw `describeError` text for the others; busy and the
picker behave as before, including a cancelled backup save leaving the picker open. (Navigator was
not asked; there is nothing to choose.)

## Out of scope

- `exportGameBackup`'s delivery (ah-k6i.4) — only wrapped here.
- The startup effect that reopens the newest game (:1849-1873).
- `enterGame` and the workspace-store calls — shell state, stays.
- Any change to `GamePicker`/`GameGate` props.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared test -- gameActions gameSession shellAction AppShell
pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared typecheck && pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared lint
pnpm run check
```

Human check (Psylocke, optional — behaviour is unchanged): create a game, switch, delete the open
one and land on the next, delete the last and reach the gate, change ruleset, export a backup and
cancel the save dialog on desktop (picker stays open).

## Known traps

- **`ah-k6i.1` must have merged** (`runReported`, `describeError` in `shellAction.ts`); the dep is
  wired, so `bd ready` will not offer this early — but check the import exists before branching.
- **`ah-k6i.4` will move `deliverGameBackupExport`** out of `AppShell.tsx`; if it has merged first,
  import it from wherever .4 put it — do not re-inline it.
- **Order matters in `deleteGame`**: discard before delete (the draft writer would otherwise flush
  into a database that is gone — the comment at :1878-1880 is the reason; keep it on the module
  function).
- **No DOM renderer** — assert nothing about the component; if a decision needs a test, it belongs
  in the module.
- **`pnpm run check`'s tooling worktree test** can fail on the machine's scratch worktrees (ah-efj);
  say so in the PR and run the remaining steps by hand, as ah-k6i.1's plan notes.

title: Every async shell action reports its failure on screen instead of dying as an unhandled rejection
description: First slice of ah-k6i. One shared 'run this and report' helper (packages/shared/src/workspace/shellAction.ts) that every async handler AppShell fires with void goes through: busy flag on/off, one try/catch, the failure put on the channel the caller names. describeError moves out of AppShell.tsx beside it, and the two ImportStatus shapes AppShell hand-builds fifteen times (a failed status, a warning status with counts zero) get builders. The unguarded handler Bishop found (handleOpenTurnPicker) is the first through it. Later slices move the handler bodies out by feature and call this.
design:
## Context

First slice of **ah-k6i** (epic; six children, this one first, the other five build on it).
`AppShell.tsx` (3127 lines on `origin/main` `deb434a`) fires every async handler with `void`, and
each handler is responsible for its own try/catch and for putting its failure somewhere a player can
see. One that forgot was a P0 (ah-6l2: a comparison click that resolved to nothing); a sibling has
the same shape today — `handleOpenTurnPicker` (:2412-2423) awaits `client.listImportedTurns` with no
try/catch and is `void`-called at :2721, so a failed listing is an unhandled rejection and the picker
opens with whatever list it had before. Bishop's sweep counts 52 of 238 first-parent commits touching
this file and three fixes that began by extracting a seam.

This bead puts in place **the one path an async shell action runs through** — busy flag on and off,
one try/catch, the failure described and handed to whichever channel the caller names — and takes the
one unguarded handler through it. It also moves `describeError` (:150-161, used 20 times in
`AppShell.tsx` and nowhere else) out of the component into that module, and gives the two
`ImportStatus` shapes the shell hand-builds again and again — a **failed** status with zero counts
(11 sites) and a **warning** status with zero counts (2 sites) — a builder each. Nothing about what
the player sees changes except the picker failure, which the navigator settled (below). Slices .2-.6
then move the handler bodies out by feature and call this helper; do not start any of that here.

Line numbers below are against `origin/main` at **`deb434a`**; re-grep, the file moves.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### New: `packages/shared/src/workspace/shellAction.ts`

```ts
/** Turns whatever was thrown into something a user can act on. (Moved verbatim from AppShell.tsx.) */
export function describeError(error: unknown): string;

export type FailureReporter = (message: string) => void;

export type RunReportedOptions = {
  /** Called with `true` before `work` starts and `false` once it has settled - a busy flag. */
  busy?: (busy: boolean) => void;
  /** Put in front of the described error, joined with ": " - e.g. "could not import turn.rep". */
  prefix?: string;
};

/**
 * Runs an async shell action so that it cannot fail silently: a rejection is described and handed
 * to `report` (with `prefix` in front when given), `busy` is released whatever happened, and the
 * returned promise never rejects. Resolves with the work's value, or `undefined` when it threw.
 * The shell fires it as `void runReported(...)` from a JSX handler - the `void` is then safe.
 */
export async function runReported<T>(
  work: () => Promise<T>,
  report: FailureReporter,
  options?: RunReportedOptions
): Promise<T | undefined>;
```

Semantics, exactly: `options.busy?.(true)`; `try { return await work(); } catch (error) {
report(options.prefix ? `${options.prefix}: ${describeError(error)}` : describeError(error));
return undefined; } finally { options.busy?.(false); }`. `describeError`'s body is the one at
`AppShell.tsx:150-161` (Error → `.message`; non-empty string → itself; otherwise
`JSON.stringify(error) ?? "unknown error"`, and `"unknown error"` if stringify throws) — copy it,
keep its comment about Tauri rejecting with strings, delete it from `AppShell.tsx`, and import it
there (`import { describeError, runReported } from "./shellAction";`).

Module doc: why this exists (ah-k6i, ah-6l2), and that every later slice's actions go through it.

### New: `packages/shared/src/workspace/shellStatus.ts`

```ts
import type { ImportStatus } from "./AppHeader";
/** A status line for something that did not happen: red, and it hides the turn-messages chip. */
export function failedStatus(message: string): ImportStatus;   // {regionCount:0, unitCount:0, message, failed:true,  warning:false}
/** A status line for something worth saying about a turn that is fine: amber, chip stays. */
export function warningStatus(message: string): ImportStatus;  // {regionCount:0, unitCount:0, message, failed:false, warning:true}
```

Comment on `warningStatus`: it is what earns the status line its room in `AppHeader` (which hides a
message-less, un-flagged status — see `AppShell.tsx:1078-1080`'s comment, which moves here). The
type stays in `AppHeader.tsx:5-16` (moving it is ah-9gk's business).

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx`

- Delete `describeError` (:143-161 including its doc comment); import it from `./shellAction`.
- Replace these eleven literals with `setStatus(failedStatus(<the same message expression>))`:
  :1024, :1053, :1138, :1209, :1233, :1435, :1488, :1681, :1979, :2173, :2209 — each is
  `{ regionCount: 0, unitCount: 0, message: …, failed: true, warning: false }`. Keep any comment
  that sits above the literal.
- Replace the two zero-count warnings: :1071-1081 (`storeReportOnly`) →
  `setStatus(warningStatus(warning ?? \`turn ${report.header.turnNumber} stored for history; still showing turn ${currentTurn}.\`))`,
  moving its comment to the builder; and :2444 (`reportComparisonFailure`) →
  `setStatus(warningStatus(message))`.
- Leave every literal that carries real counts (:996-1004 `applyReport`, :1211-1217 merge,
  :2200-2206 orders imported) as it is.
- **`handleOpenTurnPicker`** (:2412-2423) becomes:

  ```ts
  const handleOpenTurnPicker = useCallback(async () => {
    const opening = !turnPickerOpen;
    setTurnPickerOpen(opening);
    if (!opening || !game || !parsed?.header.factionId) {
      return;
    }
    const gameId = game.manifest.metadata.gameId;
    const factionId = parsed.header.factionId;
    const summaries = await runReported(
      () => client.listImportedTurns(game.databasePath, gameId),
      (message) => {
        // Nothing to pick from, so nothing to show: same exit as a comparison that would not load.
        setStatus(warningStatus(message));
        setTurnPickerOpen(false);
      },
      { prefix: "could not list the turns to compare" }
    );
    if (summaries !== undefined) {
      setTurnSummaries(summaries.filter((summary) => summary.key.factionId === factionId));
    }
  }, [client, game, parsed, turnPickerOpen]);
  ```

  Add to its doc comment the sentence: a listing that fails closes the picker and warns, because an
  open picker over a stale list would claim turns that may be gone (ah-k6i.1). The `void`-call at
  :2721 is unchanged.
- No other handler is touched. In particular the JSX `void handler(...)` sites (:2659-3082) and the
  effects with `void (async () => …)()` stay — slices .2-.6 own them.

### Tests

- New `packages/shared/src/workspace/shellAction.test.ts` (vitest; the plain-module style of
  `packages/shared/src/reportLoadDecision.test.ts`):
  - `describeError`: an `Error("boom")` → `"boom"`; `"locked"` → `"locked"`; `"   "` → `"\"   \""`
    (JSON of a blank string — pins today's behaviour rather than improving it); `{ code: 5 }` →
    `'{"code":5}'`; `undefined` → `"unknown error"`; a circular object → `"unknown error"`.
  - `runReported`: resolves the work's value and never calls `report`; on a throw resolves
    `undefined` and calls `report` once with `describeError`'s text; with `prefix: "could not x"`
    the message is `"could not x: boom"`; `busy` is called `true` then `false` in that order on
    success **and** on a throw (record calls in an array); the returned promise never rejects even
    when `report` itself throws? — no: `report` throwing is a programming error and may propagate;
    do not test for it and do not swallow it.
- New `packages/shared/src/workspace/shellStatus.test.ts`: `failedStatus("x")` and
  `warningStatus("x")` equal the exact objects above (`toEqual`).
- `AppShell.test.ts` unchanged.

## Increments

1. RED: `shellAction.test.ts` (`describeError` cases first, then `runReported`). GREEN: the module;
   then move `describeError` out of `AppShell.tsx` and import it (typecheck is the test for that
   step).
2. RED: `shellStatus.test.ts`. GREEN: the builders; then the thirteen literal replacements in
   `AppShell.tsx` — mechanical; `pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared typecheck` and `test` after.
3. `handleOpenTurnPicker` through `runReported` (no unit test can render the shell — the helper's
   tests and typecheck cover it); doc comment.
4. Full gate (`pnpm run check`), PR `refactor(ah-k6i.1): async shell actions run through one
   reporting path, and the turn picker's listing can no longer fail silently`, `@copilot`, CI,
   squash. Close the bead; do **not** close the epic — five children remain.

## The test plan

- Unit (`packages/shared`): the two new files above; the whole shared suite (`pnpm --filter
  @atlantis/shared test`) — every existing `AppShell.test.ts` case still passes.
- `pnpm run check` before the PR: lint, typecheck, unit, smoke (`tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts`
  covers the turn picker's happy path at :177 and the status line at :437 — both must stay green),
  build, pwa, clippy.

## User-facing decisions

Only one, settled with the navigator (2026-08-15): **when the turn picker cannot list the game's
turns, the picker closes and the header status line shows an amber warning** reading
`could not list the turns to compare: <error>` (rejected: keep the picker open and empty with the
same warning — a picker over no rows or stale rows says nothing useful). Everything else in this
bead is invisible: the eleven failed and two warning statuses keep their exact messages.

## Out of scope

- Moving any handler body out of `AppShell.tsx` (slices .2-.6), and converting the JSX `void`
  sites — they call handlers that the later slices rewrite.
- Moving `ImportStatus` out of `AppHeader.tsx`, or a status channel that is not an import status
  (ah-9gk).
- Statuses that carry counts (three sites) — they are not the shape the builders describe.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared test -- shellAction shellStatus AppShell
pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared typecheck && pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared lint
pnpm run check
```

Human check: none possible for the one behaviour change (it needs a database read to fail);
Psylocke may mark it not-needed on that ground, or verify that the turn picker still opens and
compares as before (a regression check, not a proof).

## Known traps

- **No DOM renderer in this project's tests** — `AppShell` itself cannot be unit-tested; anything
  that needs asserting must live in the plain module, which is the whole point of the epic.
- **`describeError` must keep its exact behaviour** — three status messages and `gameError` embed
  its text, and the smoke suite matches some of them (`grep -n "could not" tests/smoke/*.spec.ts`
  before changing anything).
- **`pnpm run check`'s tooling suite fails on a scratch worktree outside `.claude/worktrees/`**

  the repository", that is the machine, not your change; say so in the PR and run the remaining
  gate steps by hand as the ah-sup retrospective describes.
- **The smoke suites take a machine-wide lock** and rebuild the web bundle; run `check` once, at

- **Rebase risk**: `AppShell.tsx` moves under every merged bead; re-grep the line numbers above the
