title: Psylocke's work list fills with bd's own audit-event beads, one more per pass
description:
Psylocke's steady-state query (closed beads with no verification:* label, or verification:failed) picks up bd's own 'State change: verification -> X' event beads that bd set-state spawns as an audit trail. Each event bead is itself closed and unlabeled, so it shows up in the very next pass's work list; labeling it (as not-needed, since it has no commit and touches nothing) spawns another event bead recording that label, which shows up the pass after, forever. Observed during a verification pass on 2026-08-15: chains up to ah-o1t.1.1.1.1.1.1.1 accumulated across a handful of passes, and multiple independent chains (ah-kgc.*, ah-ymn.*, ah-o1t.1.*, ah-2n3.1.*) were growing in parallel.

Fix: Psylocke's work-list query (and/or the verifier.md agent definition) should filter out issue_type == event before checking for a verification:* label, since an event bead never has a commit and can never be application-touching. Alternatively, bd set-state could skip spawning an audit event bead when the bead being labelled is itself of type event, or the audit event bead could be created pre-labelled so it never enters anyone's unverified work list.

Navigator decided (2026-08-15) during a live verification pass: stop labeling event-bead tails going forward (leave existing unlabeled tails alone, harmless) and file this bead to fix the root cause.
design:
## Context

`bd set-state <id> verification=<x>` — the command Psylocke uses for every verdict — creates an
**event bead** (`issue_type: "event"`, title `State change: verification → <x>`, id `<id>.1`,
`<id>.1.1`, …) as its audit record. An event bead is closed and carries no labels, so Psylocke's
steady-state work list (closed beads with no `verification:*` label) picks it up on the very next
pass; marking it `not-needed` spawns another, which shows up the pass after, forever. Observed
2026-08-15: chains to `ah-o1t.1.1.1.1.1.1.1`, several growing in parallel. Today the unfiltered
query returns 10 ids, of which only 3 are real beads (63 of the 163 closed beads are events).

The navigator decided during that pass to stop labelling the tails (existing unlabelled event
beads are harmless and are left alone) and to fix the root cause here: **the closed-bead queries
must exclude `event`**. `bd list --exclude-type event` does exactly that (verified: 163 → 100
closed, 0 events left). Cerebro's own closed-bead queries — the shipped counts and the
"merged but unverified" list in `agents/orchestrator.md` — have the same hole and get the same
one-flag fix in the same PR; the Emacs bead panel already excludes events (`cerebro.el:1178-1184`,
with the comment that explains why) and is the pattern.

**Where the code lives.** cerebro submodule, docs only: `agents/verifier.md`,
`agents/orchestrator.md`. PR 1 to `rmstdope/cerebro`, PR 2 the atlantis-hud pointer bump. Line
numbers against cerebro `origin/main` at `e4503a8`; ah-cuc/ah-bri/ah-2n3.x do not touch these
passages, but re-grep.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `agents/verifier.md`

- *The work list* (:29-37): the query becomes

  ```bash
  bd list --status closed --exclude-type event --json | jq -r '.[]
    | select(.issue_type != "event")
    | select(([.labels[]? | select(startswith("verification:"))] | length == 0)
             or ([.labels[]?] | index("verification:failed")))
    | .id'
  ```

  Both filters on purpose — the flag is what does the work; the `jq` guard makes the query safe
  under a `bd` whose `--exclude-type` does not know `event`. Add one paragraph after it: **why** —
  `bd set-state` writes an event bead per call, closed and unlabelled, one more per verdict, so
  without the exclusion each pass finds the record of the last pass and labels it, which writes
  another (ah-9gm). And the rule that follows from it: **never label an event bead**; a chain that
  already exists is left as it is.
- *The first pass ever* (:44-62) needs no change (events carry no `verification:*` label, and the
  count is a count of labels).

### `agents/orchestrator.md`

- The three shipped-window queries (:550-556): `--exclude-type epic` → `--exclude-type epic,event`
  in each. Add to the bullet at :559-560: "**and `event`**, which is bd's own audit record of a
  `set-state` — one closed, unlabelled bead per verdict Psylocke records; counting them reports her
  bookkeeping as delivery."
- The "merged but unverified" query (:575-577): same `--exclude-type epic,event`.

## Increments

1. Both files, one commit: `fix(ah-9gm): closed-bead queries exclude bd's own audit event beads`.
   Run each edited query in the atlantis-hud checkout and paste the before/after counts into the PR
   body (the work list today: 10 → 3 ids; `bd list --status closed --json | jq length` vs with the
   flag). `@copilot`; CI (ERT only, untouched); squash. PR 2 the bump.

## The test plan

No automated test — prose in agent definitions. The check is the pasted counts and the human check
below. ERT/byte-compile untouched; run them anyway before the PR.

## User-facing decisions

None a player sees. Navigator (2026-08-15, during the verification pass that found it): stop
labelling event-bead tails, leave existing tails alone, fix the query. Ranked P0 at triage. Rejected
(not ours to change): asking `bd set-state` not to spawn an event for an event, or to pre-label it —
`bd` is a third-party tool. Rejected: replacing `set-state` with `bd label add/remove` to avoid events
altogether — the event carries the `--reason`, which is the only place the sha a verdict was rendered
against is recorded.

## Out of scope

- Deleting or labelling the existing 63 event beads.
- Any `bd` change; the Emacs bead panel (already correct).
- Xavier's and the implementers' queries (`--status open` never sees a closed event bead).

## Validation

```bash
cd <atlantis-hud checkout with the bumped submodule>
bd list --status closed --exclude-type event --json | jq '[.[] | select(.issue_type=="event")] | length'   # 0
# the new work-list query prints only real bead ids - none of the form <id>.1, <id>.1.1
```

Human check: Psylocke's next pass reports a work list without `State change` beads and creates no
new `<id>.1` chain link. Psylocke marks this bead itself not-needed (docs-only) — and that
`set-state` will create `ah-9gm.1`, which the fixed query then ignores: the proof.

## Known traps

- **Do not branch inside the shared `.claude/cerebro`**; cerebro worktree under
  `.claude/worktrees/` (absolute path — ah-3bl's retrospective), then the bump from an atlantis-hud
  worktree.
- **`--exclude-type` takes a comma list**; `--exclude-type epic --exclude-type event` also works
  (repeatable), but keep the comma form so the three near-identical lines stay one shape.
- The atlantis-hud `CLAUDE.md` mirrors nothing from these two files; no consumer-side doc edit.

title: Refactoring: AppShell's async actions report their failures, and its handlers live in testable modules
description:
## The cost being paid
A 3081-line component holds every handler inline and fires each async one with `void`; nothing in it can be unit-tested until a piece is first pulled out, and each handler is responsible for surfacing its own failure. 52 of the 238 first-parent commits touch AppShell.tsx (7 of the 28 fix commits). Three fixes each began by extracting a seam with the same sentence in the commit; a P0 was a handler that had forgotten its try/catch and failed silently as an unhandled rejection; a sibling handler still has the identical shape today.

## Evidence
- 4573b49 fix(ah-7pa): deliverOrdersExport "pulled out so it can be tested without rendering the shell"
- 7600c20 fix(ah-jfx): deliverGameBackupExport "pulled out the same way deliverOrdersExport was so it can be tested without rendering the shell"
- 9cb908b fix(ah-6l2): loadComparisonTurn, same sentence a third time (AppShell.test.ts:126–181); bead ah-6l2 (P0) notes: "handleSelectComparisonTurn (~2145-2179): zero try/catch … its only caller does void handleSelectComparisonTurn(turnNumber) … becomes an unhandled promise rejection: nothing shown to the user, exactly the reported symptom"; the diagnosis also had to rule out "two comparison-clearing effects (AppShell.tsx ~836 new-working-turn, ~1533 game-change)"
- Today: handleOpenTurnPicker (:2370–2381) awaits client.listImportedTurns with no try/catch, void-called at :2679; 13 `void handler(...)` call sites at :2617–3036

## Where
packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx; packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.test.ts

## What a refactoring would change
A shared "run this and report on the status line" path for async shell actions (one place for try/catch and the status message), and the handler bodies moved out of the component into testable modules by feature (import, export, comparison, game switching) so the next fix does not start with an extraction.

Filed by Bishop, weekly sweep of 2026-08-15 (first sweep, whole of origin/main), range e60bbbd..150ba17.

title: A bumped cerebro agent or skill stays invisible until the symlinks are synced by hand
description:
Adding an agent or a skill to cerebro and bumping the submodule is not enough: the new file is
invisible until somebody runs `sync-symlinks.sh` by hand. Bishop failed to start for exactly this
reason, silently, and the same will happen to the next agent and to every new skill.

cerebro ships hooks that do this automatically — `githooks/post-merge` and `post-checkout`, which
re-sync whenever the `.claude/cerebro` gitlink moves. **They cannot be installed here.**

## Why

Git has one `core.hooksPath` and beads has it:

    core.hooksPath = /Users/henrikku/repos/atlantis-hud/.beads/hooks

`githooks/install.sh` checks for exactly this and refuses rather than clobbering — correctly, since
taking the path would disable the beads hooks that keep the exported database in step. So the
guard works and the outcome is that the sync never runs automatically in the one repository that
needs it most.

## The shape of a fix

Two mechanisms, one path. Options, roughly in order of how well they age:

- **Beads' hooks call cerebro's.** A line in `.beads/hooks/post-merge` and `post-checkout` invoking
  `.claude/cerebro/githooks/sync-if-changed.sh`. Simple, and it lives in a directory beads owns and
  may overwrite on upgrade.
- **A dispatcher directory of our own.** `core.hooksPath` points at a third directory whose hooks
  call both beads' and cerebro's. Survives upgrades of either, one more thing to understand.
- **Drop the hooks and make it impossible to forget instead.** The launchers could sync themselves
  when they notice a missing agent (see ah-bri), or the fleet view could sync on startup. No hooks,
  no path conflict, and the cost is doing it on every launch rather than once per bump.

## For the planner to settle with the navigator

- Which of the three, given that beads is a third-party tool whose hook directory is not ours to
  own.
- Whether cerebro's `install.sh` should offer to append to an existing hooks directory rather than
  only refusing — the refusal is right, but it currently leaves the navigator with no next step.
- Whether the sync is cheap enough to run unconditionally on fleet-view startup, which would make
  the whole question moot for anyone running from Emacs.

## Validation

Bump the submodule to a commit that adds an agent, without running anything by hand, and confirm
the agent is linked and startable afterwards.
design:
## Context

Bumping the cerebro submodule to a commit that adds an agent or a skill is not enough to make it
usable: Claude Code discovers `.claude/agents/*.md` and `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md`, and those are
symlinks into `.claude/cerebro/` that only `scripts/sync-symlinks.sh` creates. Nothing runs it.
Bishop failed to start for exactly that — `claude --agent architect` exited at once because
`.claude/agents/architect.md` did not exist — and the row went dead with nothing to read.

Cerebro ships git hooks for this (`githooks/post-merge`, `post-checkout` → `sync-if-changed.sh`),
but they cannot be installed here: `core.hooksPath` is `.beads/hooks`, and `githooks/install.sh`
rightly refuses to take it. Two facts found while planning made the hook route the wrong one even
if it could be installed, and the navigator chose against it (2026-08-15): `git pull` fires
`post-merge` **before** `git submodule update` brings the new files, so a hook-time sync runs
against the old submodule content and misses the new agent anyway; and the hooks only help
checkouts whose `hooksPath` is configured. Also found: **every committed link is absolute**
(`/Users/henrikku/repos/atlantis-hud/.claude/cerebro/…` — see `git ls-files -s .claude/agents`),
which is why a bump PR built in a worktree cannot carry its own link (the sync would write a
worktree path) and why the sync would dirty the tree on any other machine. That is the same knot,
so it is fixed here too.

**The fix, as chosen:** every launcher (`scripts/run-*`) syncs the links itself, quietly, right
before `exec claude`, and only when it is sitting inside a consumer repo; and `sync-symlinks.sh`
writes **relative** links (`../cerebro/agents/<x>.md`, `../cerebro/skills/<name>`), so the same
link is correct in the main checkout, in every worktree and on every machine, and a bump PR can
commit the link it needs. The git hooks stay as an optional extra; `install.sh`'s refusal names
the way out. After this, "bump the submodule, press `s`" is enough — the launcher links whatever the
bump brought — and a sync that cannot proceed aborts the launch with the sync's own message on
stderr, which is the loud failure ah-bri (P3, separate) generalises.

**Where the code lives.** cerebro submodule (`scripts/`, `githooks/install.sh`, `tests/`,
`README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`), PR 1 to `rmstdope/cerebro`; then PR 2 in atlantis-hud: the pointer bump
**plus the nine existing links re-committed as relative**. Line numbers against cerebro `origin/main`
at `e4503a8`. ah-2n3.1 (Wolverine, in flight) renames `scripts/implementer-state` and touches
launcher docs — rebase before opening PR 1; it does not touch `sync-symlinks.sh` or the launchers'
`exec` lines.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `scripts/sync-symlinks.sh` (cerebro)

- **Guard the consumer layout.** After `CLAUDE_ROOT` is computed (:13) and its `-d` check (:16-19), require
  `[[ "$SOURCE_ROOT" == "$CLAUDE_ROOT"/* ]]`; otherwise print
  `sync-symlinks.sh: must run from a consumer repo's .claude/cerebro (found $SOURCE_ROOT)` to stderr
  and `exit 1`. Today a standalone clone at `~/repos/cerebro` would pass the `-d "$CLAUDE_ROOT"`
  check (it resolves to `~/.claude`, which exists) and link skills into the user's global config.
- **Relative targets.** In `sync_links` (:30-77) replace `ln -sfn "$item_path" "$target"` (:72) with a
  link whose target is `../<submodule dir>/<kind>/<name>`: compute once, before the loops,
  `REL_SOURCE="../${SOURCE_ROOT#"$CLAUDE_ROOT/"}"` (→ `../cerebro`), read it inside `sync_links` as a
  global (the function already reads nothing else from outside; a fifth positional would be noise), and link
  `ln -sfn "$REL_SOURCE/$(basename "$source_dir")/$item_name" "$target"`. `$dest_dir` is always one
  level under `$CLAUDE_ROOT` (`agents/` or `skills/`), so one `..` is exact. Keep the
  "Refusing to link over the directory" branch (:65-70) as it is. Update the README's example
  (`.claude/skills/plan-bead -> .claude/cerebro/skills/plan-bead`, README.md:68) to the real
  `../cerebro/skills/plan-bead`.

### `scripts/ensure-symlinks` (cerebro, new, `chmod +x`)

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Sync cerebro's skill and agent links when this checkout is a consumer's .claude/cerebro;
# do nothing at all otherwise (a standalone clone of cerebro has nothing to link into).
# Every launcher runs this immediately before `exec claude` (ah-cuc), so an agent or skill a
# submodule bump brought in is linked before the session that needs it starts. Quiet on
# success; sync-symlinks.sh's own stderr comes through on failure, and the non-zero exit
# aborts the launch under the launcher's `set -e`.
set -euo pipefail
script_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
parent="$(cd "$script_dir/../.." && pwd)"                    # .claude, in a consumer
[[ "$(basename "$parent")" == ".claude" ]] || exit 0
consumer="$(cd "$parent/.." && pwd)"
[[ "$(git -C "$consumer" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" == "$consumer" ]] || exit 0
exec "$script_dir/sync-symlinks.sh" >/dev/null
```

The `git rev-parse` guard means a clone at `~/.claude/cerebro` still does nothing.

### The six launchers (cerebro `scripts/run-implementer`, `run-planner`, `run-orchestrator`, `run-user-feedback`, `run-psylocke`, `run-bishop`)

One line each, **immediately before `exec claude`** and after every argument check — in
`run-implementer` that is after the roster/`--roster` handling (:37-90), because `cerebro.el` calls
`run-implementer --roster` (cerebro.el:789-797) and `implementer-state` calls it on every state
write; neither must sync:

```bash
# ah-cuc: link whatever a submodule bump brought in, so `claude --agent <role>` finds it.
"$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/ensure-symlinks"
```

Under `set -euo pipefail` (present in all six) a failing sync aborts the launch with the sync's
message. Say in the file-head comment of `run-implementer` ("it writes no files") that the one
exception is the links, and why.

### `githooks/install.sh` (cerebro, :21-25)

After "Merge them by hand instead." add one line to the same `>&2` block:
`Or skip the hooks: every launcher syncs the links itself before it starts a session (scripts/ensure-symlinks).`

### Tests (cerebro `tests/`, plain bash like `tests/launchers.sh`)

- **New `tests/sync-symlinks.sh`**, same `fail`/`pass` shape as `launchers.sh` (:14-21). Build a
  throwaway consumer under `mktemp -d`: `T/repo` with `git init -q`, `T/repo/.claude/cerebro/scripts/`
  (copy `sync-symlinks.sh` in), `T/repo/.claude/cerebro/skills/demo/SKILL.md`,
  `T/repo/.claude/cerebro/agents/demo.md`. Assert, after running
  `T/repo/.claude/cerebro/scripts/sync-symlinks.sh`:
  `readlink T/repo/.claude/agents/demo.md` is exactly `../cerebro/agents/demo.md`;
  `readlink T/repo/.claude/skills/demo` is `../cerebro/skills/demo`; both `-e`; a second run leaves
  both unchanged and exits 0. Then the guard: `T/.claude/` (a directory) plus a copy of the script
  at `T/x/cerebro/scripts/sync-symlinks.sh` → exit 1, stderr contains `must run from a consumer
  repo`, and `T/.claude/skills` does not exist afterwards.
- **`tests/launchers.sh`** — three additions:
  1. The existing standalone runs must keep passing unchanged (that *is* the "does nothing outside a
     consumer" assertion — the repo root's parent is not `.claude`).
  2. Consumer layout: `T/repo` git-inited, `T/repo/.claude/cerebro/{scripts,agents,skills}` copied
     from `$repo_root`; `run_launcher`-style call of `T/repo/.claude/cerebro/scripts/run-bishop`
     with the stub `claude` → the stub is reached (`ARG:--agent` present) **and**
     `readlink T/repo/.claude/agents/architect.md` is `../cerebro/agents/architect.md`.
  3. Failure aborts the launch: same layout but with a real directory at
     `T/repo/.claude/skills/plan-bead` → non-zero exit, stderr contains
     `Refusing to link over the directory`, and the stub is **not** reached.

  `run_launcher` (:40-43) hard-codes `$repo_root/scripts/$1`; add `run_launcher_at <scripts-dir> <name> [args…]`
  beside it, same stub-PATH trick, and use it for additions 2 and 3.

### Docs (cerebro)

- `README.md` *sync* section (:50-70): open with "You do not normally run this by hand: every
  launcher runs it before starting a session, so a bumped agent or skill is linked the first time
  something is started (ah-cuc)." Fix the example link to the relative form. Mention that
  `githooks/` is optional and refused where `core.hooksPath` is taken (beads), which is fine.
- `CLAUDE.md` *Gotchas* (:136-140): name `scripts/ensure-symlinks` beside `sync-symlinks.sh` as
  consumer-only, and that the launchers call it.

### atlantis-hud, PR 2

- Bump `.claude/cerebro` to the merged sha.
- **Re-commit the nine links as relative**: with the submodule in your atlantis-hud worktree
  initialised and checked out at that sha (`git submodule update --init` in the worktree — see the
  ah-4ao/ah-aao retrospectives), run `.claude/cerebro/scripts/sync-symlinks.sh` there and check
  `for l in .claude/agents/*.md .claude/skills/*; do readlink "$l"; done` prints only
  `../cerebro/…` paths (nine lines: six agents, three skills). `git status` shows the gitlink and
  nine typechanged links and nothing else; commit them in the bump commit.
- No `CLAUDE.md` change needed in atlantis-hud (it does not mention the sync). Nothing under
  `packages/` or `crates/`.

## Increments

1. RED: `tests/sync-symlinks.sh` (relative targets + guard) fails against today's script. GREEN:
   the guard and `REL_SOURCE` change.
2. RED: `tests/launchers.sh` additions 2 and 3 fail (no `ensure-symlinks`, launchers do not sync).
   GREEN: `scripts/ensure-symlinks` and the one line in each of the six launchers; addition 1 and
   every existing launcher assertion still pass; `bash tests/implementer-state.sh` still passes.
3. `install.sh` line, README and CLAUDE.md; PR 1 `fix(ah-cuc): launchers sync the skill and agent
   links before starting, and the links are relative`; `@copilot`; CI (ERT only — run the bash
   suites locally and paste their output in the PR body); squash.
4. PR 2 in atlantis-hud: bump + the nine relative links, as above.

## The test plan

- `bash tests/sync-symlinks.sh` (new), `bash tests/launchers.sh` (extended),
  `bash tests/implementer-state.sh` — all from the cerebro worktree root.
- ERT suite and byte-compile unchanged (`cerebro.el` is not touched) — run them anyway; CI runs
  only those.

## User-facing decisions

None a player sees. Navigator (2026-08-15): **P0**; mechanism **launchers sync on start**
(rejected: beads' hooks calling `sync-if-changed.sh` outside the markers — supported by beads, but
`post-merge` fires before the submodule tree updates and needs `hooksPath` configured; the fleet
view syncing on startup — misses a bump made while Emacs is up and every terminal start). Relative
links are my scope call, and the reason is in *Context*.

## Out of scope

- Appending to `.beads/hooks/*` (rejected route); a dispatcher hooks directory.
- The launcher preflight messages for a *missing* agent file, `claude` not on PATH, etc. — that is
  ah-bri (P3), which builds on this: after ah-cuc a missing agent file after a sync means the
  submodule is not updated, and ah-bri's message can say so.
- Any change to `cerebro.el`.

## Validation

```bash
cd .claude/worktrees/<cerebro worktree>
bash tests/sync-symlinks.sh && bash tests/launchers.sh && bash tests/implementer-state.sh
emacs --batch -L emacs -f batch-byte-compile emacs/cerebro.el
emacs --batch -L emacs -l cerebro-test -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit
```

Human check (the bead's own, after PR 2 and `git submodule update` in the main checkout): remove
`.claude/agents/architect.md`, press `s` on Bishop in the fleet view (or run
`.claude/cerebro/scripts/run-bishop`) — the link reappears as `../cerebro/agents/architect.md` and
Bishop starts; `git status` in the main checkout is clean apart from anything unrelated. Psylocke
marks this not-needed (nothing under the application).

## Known traps

- **`sync-symlinks.sh` outside a consumer links into `~/.claude`.** `CLAUDE_ROOT` climbs three
  levels from the script; in a standalone clone that lands on the user's own `~/.claude`, which
  exists. Never run it from the cerebro worktree itself; the guard in increment 1 is what makes that
  safe, and `ensure-symlinks` skips before ever getting there.
- **`run-implementer --roster` is polled** by `cerebro.el` and by `implementer-state`; the sync line
  goes after that early exit, right before `exec claude`, or every state write and every roster
  read would sync.
- **Do not branch inside the shared `.claude/cerebro`**; worktree of the cerebro repo under
  `.claude/worktrees/` (absolute target path — ah-3bl's retrospective), then the bump from an
  atlantis-hud worktree with the submodule initialised there.
- **The transitional dirty tree.** Once PR 1's sha is checked out in the main checkout and any agent
  is launched, the nine tracked absolute links become relative in the working tree — nine
  `typechange` entries in `git status` until PR 2 lands. Expected; PR 2 is what makes it go away, so
  do it straight after PR 1 merges.
- **A peer's bump can absorb your sha** (ah-u3i's retrospective) but not your nine links — PR 2 will
  not go empty; if the pointer part is already on main, the PR still carries the links.
- **macOS bash is 3.2**: no `declare -A`, no `readlink -f` assumptions in the tests — plain
  `readlink` on the link itself is enough and portable.
acceptance_criteria: After the cerebro submodule is bumped to a commit that adds an agent or a skill, that agent or skill is usable without anyone running sync-symlinks.sh by hand. The beads hooks that maintain the exported database still run. Whatever mechanism is chosen survives an upgrade of beads.

title: Psylocke must verify against a fresh build of current main, and prove it
description:
Twice now, a verification has been run against a build that was not the merged work. A verification
against the wrong build is worse than no verification at all: it produces a verdict — `passed` or
`failed` — about behaviour that was never shipped, and both directions do damage. A false pass
certifies something nobody has actually seen work. A false fail reopens a finished bead at P0 and
sends the fleet to rebuild something that was never broken.

**The rule: every verification runs against a fresh build of the current `origin/main`, and Psylocke
proves it before the navigator is asked to look at anything.**

## Why it happens

`agents/verifier.md` says *what* to run — `pnpm --filter @atlantis/web dev`, the Tauri dev command,
which fixture pair to load. It says nothing about *which tree those commands run in*. There is no
step that fetches, no check that HEAD contains the bead's commit, and nothing that says a build must
have happened after the merge.

Worse, the file contains advice that actively causes this:

> Both run `build:wasm` first, which is minutes on a cold cache. **Warm it before asking whether the
> navigator is ready** — start the dev server once ahead of time […] never after they have said yes.

That is sound advice about the navigator's time and a trap about correctness. A server started ahead
of time was started against whatever the tree held *then* — before the merge, or before a fetch —
and it goes on serving that bundle happily while the checkout moves underneath it.

This project has already recorded both failure modes for implementers, in the
`test-driven-development` skill: a leftover preview server reused instead of rebuilding, and
`build:wasm` not rerunning so a stale wasm artifact is served by a fresh-looking server. Psylocke
inherits neither warning.

## What the role should require

Before any of the preparation it already does:

1. **Get to a known tree.** `git fetch origin`, then be exactly at `origin/main` — a dirty tree or a
   different branch is a refusal, not something to work around.
2. **Prove the work is in it.** `git merge-base --is-ancestor <bead's commit> HEAD`. If the commit is
   not an ancestor of what is about to be built, stop; there is nothing to verify yet.
3. **Make sure nothing is already serving.** Check the ports before starting anything and refuse to
   reuse a server found running — that is precisely the stale bundle this bead exists to stop.
4. **Build after the checkout, never before it.** Warming remains fine, but it warms *the tree that
   will be verified*, which means fetching first and warming second.
5. **Record what was verified.** Put the HEAD sha in the `verification:passed` note. A verdict that
   does not say which build it judged cannot be checked afterwards — including by whoever
   investigates the third occurrence of this.

If any of that cannot be satisfied, the bead stays `verification:pending` and Psylocke says why. She
already has that path for a navigator who is busy; this is the same restraint for a tree that is not
ready.

## For the planner to settle with the navigator

- **Where she builds.** The navigator's own checkout is shared — they may be working in it, which is
  exactly when it is dirty and cannot be reset. A dedicated worktree isolates her but costs a full
  build and a submodule init, and the fleet has recorded worktree/submodule trouble twice already.
- **How hard "refuse" is.** A dirty tree with unrelated changes is arguably fine to verify against;
  a dirty tree touching the app is not. Simplest is to refuse on any dirt.
- **Psylocke has no retrospective.** `docs/retrospectives/` is written by implementers only, so a
  role that has now failed the same way twice has nowhere to record it. Worth extending, and worth
  doing as part of this rather than after a third time.

## Validation

Merge something visible, then verify it: confirm Psylocke fetches, reports the sha she is building,
and that the running app shows the merged change. Then the negative case — put the checkout on an
older commit or leave a dev server running from a previous build, and confirm she refuses rather
than proceeding.
design:
## Context

Twice a verification verdict was rendered against a build that was not the merged work — a server
started before the merge, or a tree that never fetched. `agents/verifier.md` says what to run and
nothing about which tree it runs in, and its "warm the build before asking" advice (lines 98–100)
actively invites the stale bundle. This bead makes the rule explicit and provable: **every
verification runs against a fresh build of current `origin/main`, in Psylocke's own worktree, and
the verdict records the sha it judged.**

Settled with the navigator (details under *User-facing decisions*): Psylocke builds in **her own
persistent worktree** `.claude/worktrees/psylocke`, reset hard to `origin/main` before every
verification (so "how hard is refuse" dissolves — dirt is impossible there, and the navigator's
checkout is never touched); `prune-worktrees.sh` keeps that one worktree by name; and
`docs/retrospectives/` is **extended to every role**, with a non-implementer's file named
`<bead>-<role>.md`.

**Where the code lives.** Two repos again: the cerebro submodule (`agents/verifier.md`,
`scripts/prune-worktrees.sh`, `docs/cerebro-jobs.md`, `docs/agent-workflow.md`) with a PR to
`rmstdope/cerebro`, then an atlantis-hud PR that bumps the pointer **and** edits
`docs/retrospectives/README.md`. Line numbers are against cerebro `origin/main` at **`8549679`**
(ah-3bl's PR #18, which added `## Starting the architect` to `docs/agent-workflow.md` at line 209 —
the verifier section is unchanged at 168–208). No application code moves.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `agents/verifier.md` (cerebro)

1. **A new `### The tree you verify in` subsection**, inserted before `### Preparing, before you ask
   for anything` (line 86), containing, in this order and with these commands verbatim:

   ```bash
   # Once, if the worktree does not exist yet (a pruned or first-run tree comes back the same way):
   git fetch origin main
   git worktree add --detach .claude/worktrees/psylocke origin/main
   # Before EVERY verification, whether or not the tree existed a minute ago:
   git -C .claude/worktrees/psylocke fetch origin main
   git -C .claude/worktrees/psylocke reset --hard origin/main
   git -C .claude/worktrees/psylocke clean -fd
   git -C .claude/worktrees/psylocke submodule update --init --recursive
   (cd .claude/worktrees/psylocke && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile)
   git -C .claude/worktrees/psylocke rev-parse --short HEAD        # the sha you will build — say it
   ```

   And the rules around them, in the file's own voice:
   - **Detached, no branch.** `--detach` so there is nothing for `prune-worktrees.sh` to delete a
     branch of and nothing that could drift from `origin/main`. Never `checkout -b` here, never
     commit here.
   - **Prove the work is in it**, per candidate: `git -C .claude/worktrees/psylocke merge-base
     --is-ancestor <bead's commit> HEAD` (the commit she already finds with `git log origin/main
     --grep "(<id>):" -F`). Non-zero → say "`<id>` is not in `origin/main` yet at `<sha>`", leave
     the bead `verification:pending`, and move on; nothing to verify.
   - **Nothing already serving.** Before starting a server:
     `lsof -nP -iTCP:5173 -sTCP:LISTEN` (web) / `lsof -nP -iTCP:4174 -sTCP:LISTEN` (desktop's vite).
     Anything listening → **refuse to start and refuse to reuse it**: tell the navigator the port and
     the pid ("something is already serving on 5173 (pid 41210); I will not verify against a server
     I did not start — stop it and say when"), and wait. Never kill it — it may be theirs.
   - **Build after the reset, never before it.** Warming stays allowed and encouraged, but it is
     `pnpm --filter @atlantis/browser-core build:wasm` **run inside the worktree after the reset
     above** — the reset is what makes the warm build the right build. Rewrite the existing warming
     bullet (lines 98–100) to say exactly that and to point at this subsection.
   - **Every app command runs in the worktree**: `(cd .claude/worktrees/psylocke && pnpm --filter
     @atlantis/web dev)` and `(cd .claude/worktrees/psylocke && pnpm --filter @atlantis/desktop exec
     tauri dev)` — edit the two "What to run" bullets (lines 95–97) accordingly. `bd` commands are
     unaffected wherever they run.
   - **The sweep keeps this tree** (see `prune-worktrees.sh` below); if it is nevertheless gone,
     the "once" block above recreates it and the cold build is the cost — say so, warm, and carry on.
2. **The briefing** (`### Briefing and launching`, line 118) says the sha: "verifying `<id>` at
   `origin/main` `<short sha>`, fetched `<time>`" as its first line.
3. **The verdict records the sha** (`### Taking the verdict`, lines 123–185): every `set-state`
   reason gains it — `--reason "verified by the navigator at <short sha>"` (passed, both variants)
   and `--reason "failed verification at <short sha>"` (failed) — and the failed path's
   `--append-notes "Verification failed (<date>, at <short sha>): …"`. A verdict without a sha
   cannot be checked afterwards; that sentence goes in the file.
4. **A retrospective for Psylocke.** A new short `## When a verification itself goes wrong`
   section before `## Sleeping without dying` (line 186): when a verification is found to have run
   against the wrong build, or a verdict has to be withdrawn, she writes
   `docs/retrospectives/<bead>-verifier.md` in the README's format with `**Role:** verifier` in
   place of the `Implementer:` line, from a worktree of her own (`.claude/worktrees/<bead>-retro`,
   never the psylocke tree and never the shared checkout — the same rule the planner follows for a
   mockup PR), as a `docs(<bead>): verifier retrospective` PR merged on green CI without a review,
   under the same docs-only exception the mockup PR uses.
5. **The never list** (line 203 on) gains: never verifies outside `.claude/worktrees/psylocke`;
   never against a server she did not start this pass; never records a verdict without the sha.

### `scripts/prune-worktrees.sh` (cerebro)

In `sweep()`'s loop, right after `name="$(basename "$tree")"` (line 119) and before the dirty check,
one keep:

```bash
    if [ "$name" = "psylocke" ]; then
      reason="it is Psylocke's verification tree, reset to origin/main before every use (ah-p31)"
    elif [ -n "$(git -C "$tree" status --porcelain 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
```

(i.e. the existing `if` becomes `elif`). Update the header comment's list of keep rules to name it.

### `docs/cerebro-jobs.md` and `docs/agent-workflow.md` (cerebro)

- `cerebro-jobs.md` line 39–41: add "…and one named worktree, `psylocke`, that is kept by name
  because it is reset rather than merged" to the guards sentence.
- `agent-workflow.md` `## Starting a verifier` (lines 168–208, before `## Starting the architect` at 209): a paragraph saying she verifies in
  `.claude/worktrees/psylocke`, reset to `origin/main` each time, tells you the sha before you look,
  refuses a port already in use rather than reusing what is on it, and writes a retrospective of her
  own when a verification goes wrong.

### `docs/retrospectives/README.md` (atlantis-hud, in the bump PR)

- Line 3: "written by the implementer that built it" → "written by whichever role hit the problem —
  usually the implementer that built it, sometimes Psylocke after a verification". A new sentence
  after the file-naming rule: "A non-implementer names its file `<bead id>-<role>.md`
  (`ah-p31-verifier.md`), so it never collides with the implementer's `<bead id>.md`."
- The format block: `- **Implementer:** <name>` → `- **Implementer:** <name>` *or*
  `- **Role:** <role>` — say the first is for implementers and the second for every other role.
- The bump PR also carries `.claude/cerebro` → the merged cerebro sha. Nothing else.

## Increments

1. **prune-worktrees keeps `psylocke`.** RED: there is no test harness for this script; the check
   is a throwaway consumer: `git worktree add --detach .claude/worktrees/psylocke origin/main`,
   `touch -t 202601010000 .claude/worktrees/psylocke`, `bash .claude/cerebro/scripts/prune-worktrees.sh
   --dry-run` prints `would remove psylocke` before the change and `keeping psylocke — it is
   Psylocke's verification tree…` after. GREEN: the `if`/`elif`. Remove the trial worktree after
   (`git worktree remove .claude/worktrees/psylocke`).
2. **verifier.md.** No automated test; the check is `bash tests/launchers.sh` still green (the file
   is not parsed by anything) and a read-through as Psylocke: every command in the new subsection
   runs from an atlantis-hud root as written — run each once by hand in the shared checkout
   (they only touch `.claude/worktrees/psylocke`), including the `lsof` lines with nothing
   listening (empty output, exit 1 — say in the file that exit 1 means the port is free).
3. **Docs** — the two cerebro docs, then PR 1 to `rmstdope/cerebro`
   (`fix(ah-p31): Psylocke verifies a fresh build of origin/main in her own worktree, and says the
   sha`), `@copilot`, every comment answered, CI green, squash.
4. **PR 2** in an atlantis-hud worktree: bump + `docs/retrospectives/README.md`
   (`fix(ah-p31): bump cerebro to the provable verification, and open retrospectives to every
   role`). Normal flow. Close the bead when it lands.

## The test plan

- `bash tests/launchers.sh` and the ERT suite in the cerebro worktree (unchanged, must stay green;
  CI runs the ERT half).
- The prune dry-run above, before and after.
- No atlantis-hud suite is affected; the bump PR runs CI as usual.

## User-facing decisions

None a player sees. The navigator settled the two open questions the bead names, 2026-08-15:

1. **Where she builds — her own persistent worktree, reset to `origin/main` each time** (chosen).
   Rejected: *the shared checkout with refuse-on-dirt* (she could only verify when the navigator's
   checkout is clean and on main — when they stop working); *a fresh worktree per verification* (a
   `pnpm install` and a cold wasm build, minutes, before every single look).
2. **How hard "refuse" is** — dissolved by 1: the tree is reset and cleaned, so there is never dirt
   to judge; the one remaining refusal is a port already in use, which is a hard refusal without a
   kill.
3. **Retrospectives for Psylocke — yes, any role, `<bead>-<role>.md`** (chosen). Rejected: *same
   filename appended* (breaks "never edited afterwards"); *not in this bead*.

Wording that ships, verbatim: the refusal "something is already serving on <port> (pid <pid>); I
will not verify against a server I did not start — stop it and say when"; the briefing's first line
"verifying `<id>` at `origin/main` `<sha>`, fetched <time>"; the reasons "verified by the navigator
at <sha>" / "failed verification at <sha>"; the prune keep reason "it is Psylocke's verification
tree, reset to origin/main before every use (ah-p31)".

## Out of scope

- Any change to what Psylocke verifies or how verdicts propagate (reopen, P0, Moira's comments).
- Making Cerebro or the fleet view aware of the psylocke worktree beyond the prune keep.
- Killing a stray server for the navigator.
- Any change to `implement-bead`'s retrospective section — implementers keep `<bead>.md`.
- Bishop (ah-3bl) reading the new retro files needs nothing: it reads the whole directory.

## Validation

```bash
# cerebro worktree
bash tests/launchers.sh
emacs --batch -L emacs -l cerebro-test -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit
# atlantis-hud shared checkout, before/after the script change
bash .claude/cerebro/scripts/prune-worktrees.sh --dry-run
```

Human check (the navigator, after PR 2 merges — Psylocke will mark this bead not-needed herself,
harness-only, which is fine): start `run-psylocke` on a day with a merged, application-touching
bead; she should say the sha before asking, run the app from `.claude/worktrees/psylocke`, and the
`verification:passed` reason should carry the sha (`bd show <id> --json | jq '.[0].labels'` plus
the event/notes). The negative case from the bead: leave a `pnpm --filter @atlantis/web dev` running
in the shared checkout and start her — she must refuse to start a second one and name the pid.

## Known traps

- **Do not branch inside `.claude/cerebro` of the shared checkout** — worktree/clone of the cerebro
  repo under `.claude/worktrees/`, exactly as ah-u3i / ah-3bl. The bump PR from an atlantis-hud
  worktree, updating **that worktree's** submodule checkout.
- **`git worktree add --detach` needs `origin/main` fetched first** in the shared checkout; the
  "once" block fetches. `reset --hard origin/main` inside a detached worktree moves HEAD to the
  fetched ref — it does not need a branch.
- **`prune-worktrees.sh` deletes the branch of a removed worktree**; the psylocke tree has none, and
  the keep means it is never removed anyway — but if you test the keep by name with a *branched*
  trial worktree, the branch survives with it; use `--detach` for the trial too.
- **`lsof` exit 1 with no output means nothing listens** — the file must say so or she reads it as
  a failure.
- **`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` in the psylocke tree after every reset** — a lockfile that
  moved since the last install otherwise breaks `build:wasm` with an error that looks like a
  broken worktree.
- **The two docs PRs are not the same exception**: PR 1 changes an agent's behaviour and gets the
  Copilot review like any bead; the retrospective PRs Psylocke will write later are the docs-only
  exception. Do not merge PR 1 unreviewed because it "only touches markdown".
acceptance_criteria: Before any verification, Psylocke fetches and confirms the tree is exactly origin/main, confirms the bead's commit is an ancestor of what will be built, and refuses to reuse an already-running dev server. The build happens after that checkout, not before it. The recorded verdict names the commit that was verified. If the tree cannot be brought to that state, the bead stays verification:pending with the reason given, and no verdict is recorded.

title: Bishop, the technical-debt agent, and one fewer implementer
description:
Nobody in the fleet looks at the shape of the code. Xavier plans a bead, an implementer builds it
under TDD and Copilot reviews that one diff; Psylocke asks whether merged work does what it claimed.
Across all of it, no one asks whether fifty merged beads have left the codebase harder to change
than they found it. Architecture erodes one reasonable local decision at a time, and only a reader
looking at the whole thing sees it.

**The request:** a fifth interactive agent, **Bishop**, whose subject is technical debt.

- **Daily**: every commit on main since the last sweep. Read the architecture and the design, look
  for smells that would repay a refactoring, and file a bead for each one worth doing.
- **Weekly**: the same reading over the entire codebase, not just what changed.
- Beads it files must say in the **title** that they are refactoring work.
- Fable, at **xhigh** reasoning.

**The name comes back from the implementer roster.** Bishop is removed from `ROSTER` in
`scripts/run-implementer` — thirteen implementers, not fourteen — and becomes the agent's name. It
has never held a bead and has no state file, so nothing is stranded by taking it.

## Not refactoring for its own sake

This is the whole risk. An agent at xhigh reasoning, asked to find problems in a codebase, will
always find some — and a stream of "this violates the single responsibility principle" beads would
cost the fleet real hours and teach the navigator to ignore the queue.

The bar should be a **cost already being paid**, stated concretely: a bug that recurred in the same
place, a change that had to touch six files, a test that could not be written without a seam, a
module two agents both misread. A principle violated is not a cost. Something worth writing into the
role: a finding that cannot name what it is costing today is not filed.

## Following Psylocke rather than inventing

`agents/verifier.md` is the closest precedent and the one to copy, including its restraint — "a
quiet pass is the normal case". Its best idea is that her "since my last pass" is **stateless**: it
falls out of labels already on the beads, so a session that dies remembers nothing and needs to.

Bishop needs the same trick, and the choice is the main design question:

- **A time window.** Daily reads `git log --since="24 hours ago"`, weekly reads everything. No state
  at all, and no watermark to corrupt — but a day the agent does not run is a day nobody reads, and
  nothing says so.
- **A watermark.** The last swept commit, kept somewhere durable. No gaps, but `.claude/` is
  gitignored in the consumer, so a file there dies with the checkout; a git tag or a bead would
  survive.

## Duplicates

Daily and weekly sweeps will find the same smell, and so will two consecutive weeks if nobody fixed
it. Bishop must check the open beads before filing, the way Moira checks `--external-ref` before
creating one from an issue. Worth deciding whether a repeat finding updates the existing bead (a
"seen again" note, which is evidence it is getting worse) or is simply skipped.

## What adding an interactive agent touches

Psylocke's PR (#7, `16429b0`) is the checklist, and it is more places than it looks:

- `agents/<role>.md` — the agent definition, with `model: fable` and `effort: xhigh`;
- `scripts/run-bishop` — the launcher, one interactive `claude` and nothing else;
- `emacs/cerebro.el` — `cerebro-interactive-agents`, `cerebro--role-launch-commands`, and the
  commentary that counts the roster;
- `scripts/run-implementer` — Bishop out of `ROSTER`;
- `agents/orchestrator.md` — Cerebro's X-Men list and its view of the fleet;
- `docs/agent-workflow.md`, `emacs/README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`;
- `emacs/cerebro-test.el` — the fleet list's expectations.

## For the planner to settle with the navigator

- **Stateless window or watermark**, per above.
- **How Bishop runs a schedule.** The other interactive agents loop with a sleep. A session that
  lives for a week accumulates context the way an implementer used to across beads, which is the
  problem one-bead-per-session was invented to solve. A sweep per session, started by something
  outside it, may suit better.
- **What priority its beads get.** P4 and unplanned, for Xavier to triage with the navigator, is the
  house rule and the safe answer.
- **Whether it gets a skill** of its own, like `plan-bead` and `implement-bead`, or a single agent
  file like Psylocke. That depends on how long the procedure turns out to be.
- **Whether it may read the retrospectives** in `docs/retrospectives/`. They record what actually
  cost an implementer time, which is exactly the evidence this role is supposed to be filing on.

## Validation

Run a daily sweep against a day with several merges and confirm: findings name a cost, titles say
refactoring, beads are unplanned at P4, and a smell already filed is not filed twice. Confirm the
fleet list shows Bishop as an interactive agent, and that `scripts/run-implementer Bishop` now
refuses.

fifty merges nobody asks whether the codebase got harder to change. This bead adds **Bishop**, a
sixth interactive agent whose whole subject is technical debt: it reads what merged since its last
sweep (daily) or the whole codebase (weekly), and **files a bead** — never a fix — for each
refactoring that can name a **cost already being paid**. The name comes off the implementer roster:
thirteen implementers, and `run-implementer Bishop` refuses.

Settled with the navigator (the full interview is under *User-facing decisions*): the watermark
lives in **bd memory** (`--key bishop-watermark`, `--key bishop-weekly`); Bishop is **one sweep per
session** — you start it, it sweeps, reports, and tells you to end it; a repeat finding gets a
**seen-again note** on the existing bead, never a second bead; it **reads and cites
`docs/retrospectives/`**; its beads are titled **`Refactoring: …`**, filed **on its own at P4,
unranked**, and its role word in the fleet view (and its agent file) is **`architect`**.

**Architecture (planner's decisions):** a single agent file `agents/architect.md`, no skill — the
procedure is one sweep, about the length of `agents/verifier.md`, and Psylocke is the precedent for
an interactive role with no skill. Bishop has **no state file** and is not supervised by
`cerebro.el`: it appears in `cerebro-interactive-agents`, is started with `s` / `run-bishop`, shows
`up`/`dead` from `--name Bishop` in the process args like Xavier, and is ended with `k`. When the
sweep is done Bishop **ends its turn** — deliberately, unlike every other role, because it holds no
claim, no lease and no loop, so nothing waits on it; the agent file says so and why. Reading is
allowed to fan out to subagents (weekly), judgement and filing are Bishop's alone. Every finding
carries the label `refactoring` — that label is what makes the duplicate check a one-line query.

**Where the code lives.** Everything but the last increment is in the **cerebro submodule**
(`https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro`, checked out at `.claude/cerebro`), followed by a
submodule-pointer bump in atlantis-hud — the same two-PR delivery as ah-lyc / ah-b8o / ah-u3i (read
`bd show ah-u3i --json | jq -r '.[0].design'` for a recent one). Line numbers below are against
cerebro `origin/main` at **`de85a84`** ("Disclose Moira as an agent…", PR #17). Psylocke's PR
(`16429b0`, cerebro #7) is the checklist of places a new interactive agent touches; this plan walks
the same list.

Model and effort are the bead's: **Fable at xhigh**, in both the frontmatter and the launcher.

### A. `agents/architect.md` (new, cerebro repo)

Frontmatter, exactly:

```yaml
---
name: architect
description: Bishop, the technical-debt session for atlantis-hud. Once per session it sweeps what merged since its last sweep — or the whole codebase, weekly — and files a Refactoring bead for each smell that names a cost already being paid, never a fix. Started by `.claude/cerebro/scripts/run-bishop`, interactive by design, and finished when its report says so.
model: fable
effort: xhigh
---
```

Body, in this order, in the voice and density of `agents/verifier.md` (which is the file to copy —
same headings style, same "never" list at the end). The rules below are the substance; the prose is
yours.

1. **Opening.** "**You are Bishop.** Say so in your first message." Then the reason the role exists
   (the first paragraph of *Context* above, in your words) and the one-sentence bar: **a finding
   that cannot name what it is costing today is not filed.**

2. **The bar: a cost already being paid, not a principle violated.** State it as a closed list of
   what counts, each with the citation it must carry:
   - a defect fixed twice (or more) in the same place — cite both commits or beads;
   - one concept whose change had to touch several files — cite the commit and the file count;
   - a test that could not be written without a seam, or a retrospective that says a change cost
     time for a structural reason — cite `docs/retrospectives/<id>.md` and the section;
   - a module two agents misread the same way — cite both retrospectives or PR threads;
   - a bug hand-back or a `human`-queue escalation whose notes blame the code's shape — cite the
     bead.
   And what does **not** count, said plainly: a named principle (SRP, DRY, "too long"), "could be
   cleaner", a cost that might arrive later, style. Bishop at xhigh will always find something; the
   list is what stops a stream of principle-violation beads.

3. **What you do, once per session** — numbered, with these commands verbatim:

   ```bash
   bd dolt pull
   git fetch origin main                       # from the consumer root; never checkout or branch here
   bd recall bishop-watermark                  # "<full sha> <ISO-8601 UTC>", or exit 1 = never swept
   bd recall bishop-weekly                     # "<ISO-8601 UTC>" of the last weekly, or exit 1
   ```

   **Decide the sweep, and say which and why:** *weekly* if `bishop-weekly` is absent or seven or
   more days old, or if `bishop-watermark` is absent (a first run reads everything); otherwise
   *daily*. Say the range in the first message: "daily, since `<sha>` (`<n>` commits over `<d>`
   days)" — and if `<d>` is more than two, say out loud that nobody read main for that long.

   **Daily reads:**

   ```bash
   git log --first-parent --format='%h %ad %s' --date=short <watermark-sha>..origin/main
   git diff --stat <watermark-sha>..origin/main
   git show --format='%h %s' <sha>             # each commit in turn
   git diff --name-only <watermark-sha>..origin/main -- docs/retrospectives/   # new retrospectives: read each
   ```

   If the range includes a change to the `.claude/cerebro` gitlink, also read
   `git -C .claude/cerebro log --first-parent --format='%h %s' <old>..<new>` (`git diff
   <watermark-sha>..origin/main -- .claude/cerebro` shows both shas): the harness is code the fleet
   pays for too. Nothing in the range → say so, move nothing, report, finish.

   **Weekly reads:** all of `packages/`, `crates/`, `apps/`, plus `.claude/cerebro/emacs` and
   `.claude/cerebro/scripts`, plus every file in `docs/retrospectives/`. That is ~70k lines; do not
   read it in one context. **Delegate the reading per top-level directory** (`packages/shared`,
   `packages/core-client`, `packages/browser-core`, `packages/ruleset`, `crates/core`,
   `crates/core-persistence`, `crates/core-tauri`, `crates/core-wasm`, `apps/desktop`, `apps/web`,
   `.claude/cerebro/emacs`, `.claude/cerebro/scripts`) to subagents (the `Agent` tool,
   `general-purpose`), each given the bar from section 2 verbatim and asked to return candidates in
   a fixed shape: `path(s) · the smell in one line · the cost and its citation · confidence`. Read
   the retrospectives yourself. **The subagents find; you judge and file.** Never file a candidate
   whose citation you have not opened.

4. **Before filing: the duplicate check.**

   ```bash
   bd list --label refactoring --status open --json \
     | jq -r '.[] | "\(.id)\t\(.title)\n\(.description)\n---"'
   ```

   Read the titles and descriptions and compare **by the module and the cost**, not by wording. A
   smell already filed gets a note, never a second bead:

   ```bash
   bd update <id> --append-notes "Seen again by Bishop on <YYYY-MM-DD>: <one line of new evidence, with its citation>"
   ```

   Only when there is new evidence — a new commit, a new retrospective, a new file it touched — is
   the note worth writing; a repeat with nothing new is skipped, and the report says it was seen.
   The label is the whole index, so a Bishop bead without `refactoring` on it is a bead the next
   sweep will file again — every `bd create` below carries it.

5. **Filing.** One bead per finding:

   ```bash
   bd create --title "Refactoring: <the cost, not the module>" --type task -p 4 \
     --labels refactoring \
     --description "$(cat <<'EOF'
   ## The cost being paid
   <what it costs today, concretely: the two fixes, the six files, the hour in the retrospective>

   ## Evidence
   - <commit sha and subject> / <bead id> / docs/retrospectives/<id>.md §<section>
   - ...

   ## Where
   <the files or modules, paths from the repository root>

   ## What a refactoring would change
   <three to five lines on the shape — the seam, the move, the merge. Not a plan: Xavier plans it.>

   Filed by Bishop, <daily|weekly> sweep of <YYYY-MM-DD>, range <sha>..<sha>.
   EOF
   )"
   bd dolt push
   ```

   `-p 4` always — unranked, and Xavier triages it with the navigator like everything else. Never a
   `--design`, never a `planned` label, never a priority. The title after the prefix follows the
   house title rule (name the effect, no module names unless the module is the subject, about
   seventy characters).

6. **Move the watermark — after filing, never before**, so a session that dies mid-sweep re-reads a
   range rather than skipping it (the duplicate check makes re-reading cheap):

   ```bash
   bd remember "$(git rev-parse origin/main) $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" --key bishop-watermark
   bd remember "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" --key bishop-weekly     # weekly sweeps only
   bd dolt push
   ```

   `--key` updates in place (verified: `bd remember … --key k` twice leaves one memory; `bd recall
   k` prints the content alone). Memories are injected into every session's `bd prime` — that is the
   accepted cost of keeping the watermark in the database every agent already pushes.

7. **The report, then finish.** One message: sweep kind and range; beads filed (id and title);
   seen-again notes written; findings read and **not** filed and the one-line reason (at most five —
   the rest is noise); the gap warning if there was one. Then, verbatim in spirit: "This sweep is
   finished. Nothing waits on me — end this session with `k` in the fleet view; the next `run-bishop`
   starts from the watermark." **Then end the turn.** Say in the file why this differs from every
   other role's "wait by blocking": Bishop holds no claim, no lease and no PR, so an ended turn
   strands nothing, and a session that lived through a second sweep would carry the first sweep's
   reading in its context — the exact rot one-bead-per-session was invented to stop.

8. **What Bishop never does** — the closing list, in the shape of verifier.md's:
   never edits code (if you are in `packages/`, `crates/`, `apps/` or `emacs/` with an editor open,
   wrong job); never claims a bead; never sets a priority; never plans (no `design`, no `planned`);
   never files without a cost and a citation; never a second bead for a known smell; never posts to
   GitHub; never moves the watermark before the beads are pushed; never has a state file; never
   `git checkout`/`switch`/`stash` in the shared checkout — reading is `git show`/`git log`/`git
   diff` against `origin/main` only; never sweeps twice in one session.

## User-facing decisions

No player sees any of this — the surface is the fleet view and the backlog, and the person who sees
those is the navigator, who filed the bead and answered every question below on 2026-08-15. No
mockups: the surfaces are a terminal launcher, a 13-character Role column and bead titles.

1. **Watermark: bd memory** (chosen) — `bd remember "<sha> <date>" --key bishop-watermark` and
   `--key bishop-weekly`; durable in the Dolt DB every agent pushes, no tag noise, the report names
   the gap. Rejected: *stateless time window* (a day nobody starts Bishop is a day nobody reads and
   nothing says so); *git tag on atlantis-hud* (an agent force-pushing a tag next to the release
   tags Cerebro reads).
2. **Lifecycle: one sweep per session** (chosen) — the navigator starts it, it decides daily vs
   weekly itself from the memories, sweeps, reports, says it is finished, and is ended with `k`.
   Rejected: *looping session like Psylocke* (a week of sweeps in one context is the rot
   one-bead-per-session was invented against); *fleet-view restart on a state file* (a new
   supervision path in cerebro.el for one agent).
3. **Duplicates: append a seen-again note** (chosen) — `--append-notes "Seen again by Bishop on
   <date>: …"`, never a second bead. Rejected: *skip silently* (loses the evidence it is getting
   worse); *note only on new evidence* was offered separately and not chosen — but the plan still
   requires the note to carry a citation, so a repeat with nothing new to cite is reported rather
   than noted (this is a narrowing the navigator's choice permits, not a reversal of it).
4. **Retrospectives: yes, read and cite them** (chosen). Rejected: *only the daily window's* (the
   weekly reads them all anyway); *no*.
5. **Title: prefix `Refactoring: …`** (chosen). Rejected: suffix `(refactoring)`; free wording.
6. **Role word: `architect`** (chosen; the navigator picked it over my recommendation `debt`) —
   so `agents/architect.md`, `--agent architect`, `("Bishop" . "architect")`, `("architect" .
   "run-bishop")`. Rejected: `debt`, `refactoring`.
7. **Filing: on its own, at P4** (chosen). Rejected: *ask per sweep* (findings lost when the
   navigator is away); *capped per sweep*.
8. **Priority of its beads: P4, unranked** (chosen; the house rule). Rejected: a standing P3.
