   for, and if it reads badly the choice was wrong and is worth saying so.
4. **Lair**: no `Built with` row at all.
5. **Road N**: `Built with Building 2` — roads are buildable and are easy to forget.

## Known traps

- **`buildSkill` is a tag, not a name.** Printing it raw gives `Built with BUIL 1`, which is worse
  than nothing. It must be resolved against the skills the dictionary already holds.
- **36 of 58 have it.** The field is conditional, like every other one here. An unconditional render
  puts an empty or `undefined` row on 22 entries.
- **A tag that resolves to nothing must render nothing** — not a dead link, and not a bare level. It
  should not happen; it must still be survivable.
- **Do not touch `packages/ruleset/`.** The data is already committed; this bead reads it.
- **Reuse the existing cross-reference button** (`:259-266`) rather than writing a new one — same
  testid shape, same `onFollow`, same classes. `ah-5jkt.1` set that pattern and a second one would
  diverge.
- **"Requires" is taken.** It already means a skill's prerequisites in this dialog, which is why the
  navigator chose "Built with".
acceptance_criteria: GameDataDialog's building detail shows the skill and level needed to build a structure, labelled 'Built with' and rendered beside cost and materials as, for example, 'Built with mining 3'. The skill is resolved from the stored tag (BUIL, MINI) to the dictionary's own skill entry and rendered as a cross-reference into the Skills tab, reusing the existing game-data-link button pattern rather than a new one, so following it opens that skill's entry. The field is conditional: of the 58 buildings, the 36 carrying buildSkill and buildLevel show it and the other 22 - lairs, ruins, monoliths - show nothing about building. A tag that resolves to no skill entry renders nothing rather than a dead link or a bare level, and does not throw. Roads show it too. No change under packages/ruleset/, no scraping and no Rust: ah-bwly.1 already committed the data and git grep buildSkill over packages/shared/src currently finds nothing.

title: Record what the Playwright container costs docs-only PRs, and keep it
description:
Raised by the Copilot review on PR #465 (ah-f9q9), and correct.

ah-f9q9 put a job-level 'container:' on ci.yml's smoke job. smoke is deliberately always-running and always expands its matrix, because a job skipped by a job-level if: never expands its matrix and the four required 'smoke (<project>, <shard>, <total>)' contexts would then never report (ah-2m2). Every step inside it is gated on needs.changes.outputs.code == 'true'.

A job-level container is pulled by the runner BEFORE any step gate is evaluated. So on a prose-only PR all four shards now pull the Playwright image - roughly 2 GB each - and then skip every step. That is a new cost on the docs path, paid for nothing.

It is a straight trade against what ah-f9q9 bought: no apt on the code path, where every measured stall happened. Prose-only PRs are the cheaper and rarer case, and the pull is cached per-runner and bounded, so the trade is defensible - but it was not weighed when ah-f9q9 was planned and it should be measured rather than assumed.

What to do about it is a real decision, not an oversight to correct:
- measure it first: the wall-clock a docs-only PR's four smoke shards now cost, against the same before ah-f9q9.
- if it matters, the options are (a) run the container per-step via 'uses: docker://...' on the test step only, so the pull is gated with everything else, or (b) revisit ah-2m2's always-expand approach so the job can be skipped outright. (b) is a larger change to a structure that exists for a reason.

Do not 'fix' this by putting a job-level if: back on smoke - that is exactly the bug ah-2m2 removed.
design:
## Context

The Copilot review on PR #465 (`ah-f9q9`) raised something that bead's plan did not weigh, and it was
right to.

`smoke` is deliberately always-running and always expands its matrix, because a job skipped by a
job-level `if:` never expands it and the four required `smoke (<project>, <shard>, <total>)` contexts
would then never report (`ah-2m2`). Every *step* inside it is gated on
`needs.changes.outputs.code == 'true'`. But **a job-level `container:` is pulled by the runner before
any step gate is evaluated** — so since `ah-f9q9`, a prose-only PR pulls the Playwright image in all
four shards and then skips every step.

**The bead asks for a measurement before choosing a fix. Here it is**, from two one-file,
documentation-only mockup PRs opened by this planner either side of `ah-f9q9` landing — the same
shape of change, the same author, the same repository:

| shard | PR #461, before | PR #467, after |
|---|---|---|
| `smoke (web, 1, 2)` | 6s | 31s |
| `smoke (web, 2, 2)` | 5s | 43s |
| `smoke (desktop-shell, 1, 2)` | 4s | 32s |
| `smoke (desktop-shell, 2, 2)` | 6s | 29s |
| **total runner time** | **21s** | **135s** |

The four shards run in parallel, so **a docs-only PR's smoke stage costs about 37 seconds more
wall-clock and roughly two extra runner-minutes.** That is far less than "2 GB in each of four
shards" suggests — the pull is fast in practice.

Against that, `ah-f9q9` removed a step that ran on **every** code PR, on a cache hit as well as a
miss, and stalled **25 to 55 minutes, four times in five days** (`ah-3c80`).

**The navigator was shown these numbers and chose to keep the trade.** So this bead ships no change to
the container: it writes the measurement down where the next reader will find it, and closes.

Branch from `origin/main`; every line number here is that tree.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### 1. The comment says the trade was weighed — `.github/workflows/ci.yml`

The `container:` line on `smoke` (`:294`) already carries a comment explaining what the image buys.
It gains what it costs, so nobody has to rediscover this:

```yaml
    # The libraries Playwright links against are baked into this image, so no apt runs here at all -
    # which is the failure `timeout-minutes` above exists to bound (ah-3c80, four stalls in five
    # days). The tag must match the version in pnpm-lock.yaml; `scripts/playwrightImage.test.ts`
    # fails the gate if they drift (ah-f9q9).
    #
    # The cost, measured rather than assumed (ah-vzj9): a job-level container is pulled before any
    # step gate is evaluated, and this job deliberately always expands its matrix so the four
    # required contexts always report (ah-2m2). So a prose-only PR pulls the image four times and
    # then skips every step. Two one-file docs PRs either side of the change: 21s of runner time
    # before, 135s after - about 37s more wall-clock, the shards being parallel. Weighed against a
    # step that stalled 25-55 minutes four times in five days on the code path, and kept.
    container: mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.62.1-noble
```

The same note, one line of it, goes on `pwa`'s `container:` pointing here.

### 2. Nothing else

**No workflow structure changes.** In particular:

- **Do not put a job-level `if:` back on `smoke`.** That is exactly the bug `ah-2m2` removed: the
  matrix would stop expanding and the four required contexts would never report, so every PR would
  wait for checks that cannot arrive.
- **Do not move the container to the step** (`uses: docker://…`), and **do not split the job** into a
  context-reporting shell plus a containerised worker. Both were considered with the measurement in
  hand and declined; see *User-facing decisions*.

## Increments

1. **The numbers are written down.**
   RED: none — this is a comment.
   GREEN: the comment on `smoke`, the one-liner on `pwa`.
2. **Nothing moved.**
   RED: none — the check. `git diff --stat` shows `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and nothing else, and
   the diff is comment lines only.

## The test plan

**There is nothing to test**, and saying so is part of the plan rather than an omission: the change
is two comments.

| Check | How |
|---|---|
| the diff is comments only | `git diff` — no YAML key added, changed or removed |
| CI is unaffected | the PR's own run, green, with smoke durations unchanged from the 135s baseline |
| the structure is untouched | `smoke` still has no job-level `if:`, still expands its matrix, and all four contexts report on this very PR |

That last row is worth doing deliberately: **this PR is itself a docs-shaped change**, so its own run
is another sample of the number being recorded. If its shards come in far from ~30s each, the
measurement in the comment is wrong and should be updated before merging.

## User-facing decisions

**Nothing reaches a player**, and there is no mockup — the artefact is a comment.

**The decision was the navigator's**, because it is a cost/benefit on their fleet rather than a
technical choice, and because `ah-f9q9`'s plan had failed to weigh it. Shown the measurement above,
they chose: **record it and close, keeping the trade.**

Rejected, all three with the numbers in hand:

- **Move the container to the test step** (`uses: docker://…`), so the pull is gated with everything
  else and docs PRs pay nothing. Fiddly — the other steps run on the host, so host-installed
  `node_modules` would have to work inside a container step, which wants proving — and it buys back
  37 seconds.
- **Split the job**: a lightweight always-running job reporting the four required contexts, plus a
  containerised job that runs only when code changed. The cleanest end state, and it reworks
  `ah-2m2`'s structure, which exists for a reason, to save the same 37 seconds.
- **Leave it open and watch it.** Rejected because an open bead with no trigger is a bead nobody
  closes; the number is knowable now and is written down instead.

**If this becomes wrong later**, the trigger is concrete: the docs path costing materially more than
~37 seconds, or GitHub changing how images are pulled. Re-file with a fresh measurement rather than
reopening on suspicion.

## Out of scope

- **Any change to `smoke`'s gating, matrix or `if:`** — `ah-2m2` owns that shape.
- **The container itself, its tag, and the drift test** — `ah-f9q9`.
- **`timeout-minutes`** — `ah-3c80`.
- **`deploy.yml` and `release.yml`**, which still use the composite action and still run apt; that was
  `ah-f9q9`'s deliberate scope.
- **Making docs-only PRs skip more of CI generally.** A bigger question about the `changes` filter,
  not this bead's.

## Validation

```bash
git diff origin/main -- .github/workflows/ci.yml     # comments only, no key changed
```

Then on the PR itself:

1. All four `smoke` shards report and pass — this PR is prose-only, so it is the exact case being
   documented.
2. **Read their durations.** They should be about 30 seconds each. If they are, the comment's numbers
   stand; if they are materially different, correct the comment before merging — a measurement
   written down wrongly is worse than none, because it will be trusted.
3. `pwa` reports and passes.

## Known traps

- **Never put a job-level `if:` on `smoke`.** The matrix stops expanding, the four required contexts
  never report, and every PR waits for checks that cannot arrive. `ah-2m2` removed exactly that.
- **This bead ships no behaviour change.** If the diff contains a YAML key rather than comment lines,
  something has been "fixed" that the navigator decided to keep.
- **The numbers are from two one-file docs PRs**, #461 and #467. They are a sample of two, and the
  comment should say so rather than presenting them as a benchmark.
- **The PR's own run is a third sample.** Use it — it is free, and it is the same shape of change.
acceptance_criteria: ci.yml's container: comment on the smoke job records the measured cost of a job-level container on the docs path - that it is pulled before any step gate is evaluated, that smoke deliberately always expands its matrix so the four required contexts report (ah-2m2), and the figures: two one-file docs-only PRs either side of ah-f9q9 went from 21s to 135s of runner time across four parallel shards, about 37s more wall-clock - weighed against a step that stalled 25-55 minutes four times in five days on the code path, and kept. The pwa job's container carries a one-line pointer to it. The diff is comment lines only: no YAML key is added, changed or removed, smoke still has no job-level if:, and all four smoke contexts plus pwa report and pass on the PR - which is itself a prose-only change and so a third sample, used to confirm the recorded figures before merging. No change to the container, its tag, the drift test, timeout-minutes, or deploy.yml and release.yml.
notes: Filed by Wolverine while implementing ah-f9q9. Unranked, per CLAUDE.md: the urgency argument is in the description, not the number.

title: A new advisory check renegotiates fixtures written for every other one
description:
## The cost being paid

Advisory checks ship default-on into one globally-enabled set, and every fixture in the repo — Rust
unit fixtures, the real-turn corpus test, and the smoke suite's single turn-71 report — is asserted
against *all* checks at once. So check N+1 is a fleet-wide fixture migration rather than a feature.
Because `check:fast` excludes the browser suites, roughly half that migration is only discovered in
CI, a sharded round trip at a time.

Eleven of the 23 codes in `codes::ALL` landed inside this one sweep's range, and four beads paid for
the coupling in the same way, two of them naming each other as the same class.

## Evidence

- docs/retrospectives/ah-dwk6.md §"A new default-on check broke thirty-odd fixtures the plan did not name, in two suites" (commit 1de7528, PR #433, **10 files**) — ~37 broken assertions: 26 `semantics` tests, 2 in `lib.rs`, 4 in `shortcuts.spec.ts`, 5 in `workspace.spec.ts`. **Three CI cycles (~7 min each) plus ~25 min of local smoke runs.** Its Seen before: "**ah-djq — same class, same two smoke jobs, same 'check:fast does not run the browser suites' root... This is the second sighting.**"
- docs/retrospectives/ah-djq.md §"A new default-on check broke smoke fixtures that gave to a real turn-71 unit number" (commit 2f13b2b, PR #357, 8 files) — 5 specs in `workspace.spec.ts`; two CI cycles plus a rebase.
- docs/retrospectives/ah-vkut.md §"A new advisory check fired on six fixtures written for other checks" (~15 min) — and it names the hazard: "the next new-advisory-check bead will hit it, and... **the wrong fix — weakening the new check until the old fixtures go quiet — is both available and hard to spot in review.**"
- docs/retrospectives/ah-a2k.2.md §"The committed corpus contradicted the plan, and only the gate said so" (commit c63ab13, 8 files) — ~40 min and **two navigator questions**. "it asserts the committed turn is silent except for a named list, so **any new check that fires on real data breaks it**."
- docs/retrospectives/ah-oq3.md §"A rebase's git-level auto-merge left a tuple-arity mismatch that no conflict marker flagged" — two PRs each appending to `codes::ALL` and to the same `every_advisory_code_can_be_silenced` tuple list; git's line-based merge left a wrong tuple arity with **no conflict marker**, a compile error `git rebase --continue` could not catch. Its Prevent by asks for exactly this judgement: "Recorded so a second sighting shows whether it is common enough around `codes::ALL`-shaped fixtures to be worth a structural fix (e.g. giving each case its own named function instead of a shared tuple type)."

## Where

- `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` — `CheckOptions` is a single `disabled: BTreeSet<String>`; `CheckOptions::default()` disables exactly one of 23 codes, and `check_turn` calls every check function unconditionally per hex. There is no notion of a check being off-by-default or scoped to a fixture set. Its test module has accreted four opt-*out* helpers, one per over-broad check: `check`, `check_ignoring_transfer_targets`, `check_ignoring_empty_builds`, `check_idle`.
- `crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs` — `the_committed_turn_has_no_semantic_problems_either` asserts an absolute finding count behind a growing comment log of exceptions; 4 of that block's 5 edits are new-check beads (ah-1uj, ah-dbb.2, ah-a2k.2, ah-dwk6).
- `tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-g7-f95-t71.rep` via `packages/fixtures/src/index.ts` — loaded by 10 of 12 smoke spec files; `workspace.spec.ts` alone holds ~85 exact-count assertions against it, silenced by clicking through the Settings dialog.
- `packages/shared/src/settingsStore.ts` — `DEFAULT_ADVISORY_CHECKS` re-derives the Rust default independently.
- `package.json` — `check:fast` omits `test:smoke`/`test:pwa`; `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs them as 4 sharded jobs, which is why a smoke break costs a round trip rather than a local rerun.

## What a refactoring would change

The seam is opt-in instead of opt-out: a fixture declares the code it is about, so the other 22 checks
cannot perturb it, retiring the four `check_ignoring_*` helpers rather than adding a fifth per
over-broad check. On the corpus side, stop asserting an absolute total — a per-code expectation table
means a new check adds a row instead of renegotiating the count and its comment log. Giving each case
in `every_advisory_code_can_be_silenced` its own named function, as ah-oq3 proposed, removes the
shared tuple type that git auto-merged wrongly.

**Note for triage — this one may cost more than it saves.** Every incident was a *true positive*: the
fixtures were under-specified and the new check was right about them. No bead was handed back, no
`human` escalation blamed the code. The opt-in seam is a mechanical change across ~200 Rust fixtures.
And 11 of 23 checks landing in one burst is a backlog burn-down, so "every future check pays this" may
extrapolate from a spike that is over. The cheap subset — the corpus expectation table and the
`codes::ALL` tuple — may be all that is worth doing.

design:
## Context

Advisory checks ship default-on into one globally-enabled set, and every fixture is asserted against
*all* checks at once. So check N+1 is a fleet-wide fixture migration rather than a feature, and
because `check:fast` excludes the browser suites, roughly half of it is discovered only in CI, a
sharded round trip at a time.

Forge measured four beads paying it the same way — `ah-dwk6` broke ~37 assertions across two suites
and cost three CI cycles plus ~25 minutes of local smoke runs; `ah-djq` five specs and two cycles;
`ah-vkut` six fixtures; `ah-a2k.2` ~40 minutes and two navigator questions.

**And it names a failure worse than the time:** *"the wrong fix — weakening the new check until the
old fixtures go quiet — is both available and hard to spot in review."* A check that has been quietly
narrowed to keep somebody else's fixture green is a check nobody knows is weak.

### The scope, which is a judgement and is the planner's

**Forge's own triage note argues against the large version of this bead**, and it is right:

> Every incident was a *true positive*: the fixtures were under-specified and the new check was right
> about them. No bead was handed back, no `human` escalation blamed the code. The opt-in seam is a
> mechanical change across ~200 Rust fixtures. And 11 of 23 checks landing in one burst is a backlog
> burn-down, so "every future check pays this" may extrapolate from a spike that is over. **The cheap
> subset — the corpus expectation table and the `codes::ALL` tuple — may be all that is worth doing.**

**This plan does the cheap subset and nothing else**, for four reasons worth writing down because the
next reader will be tempted by the large version:

1. **Every incident was the system working.** The fixtures really were under-specified; the checks
   really were right. Loud is not the same as wrong.
2. **~200 fixtures is a mechanical rewrite of the tests that protect the checks** — the highest-risk
   place in the repository to do a large mechanical change, and the one where a mistake is least
   visible.
3. **The burst is plausibly over.** Eleven of twenty-three codes landed inside one sweep. Sizing a
   refactor on that rate assumes it continues.
4. **The cheap subset is what attacks the dangerous failure.** A per-code expectation table makes "a
   check went quiet on the real corpus" a *row that changed*, where an absolute total hides it in a
   number. That is the correctness half, and it is the cheap half.

**The opt-in fixture seam is filed separately** as `ah-i7we`, at P4, carrying Forge's caveat — so
that if the next new-check bead does pay the full cost again, the evidence accumulates against a bead
that exists rather than being rediscovered.

Branch from `origin/main`; every line number here is that tree.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

Two files. **No production code at all** — nothing in `codes`, no check function, no
`CheckOptions`. If this bead changes behaviour, it has gone wrong.

### 1. A per-code expectation table — `crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs`

Three assertions repeat the same knowledge in three shapes: `the_committed_turn_has_no_semantic_problems_either`
asserts a positional `vec![…]` of eight code strings; the `damaged` case at `:204-216` repeats those
eight plus `not-enough-silver`; and `a_whole_map_pass_re_reads_neither_the_report_nor_the_ruleset`
asserts `expected.len() == 8` (`:253`). Four of the five edits to that block were new-check beads.

Replace all three with one table and one helper:

```rust
/// What the committed turn genuinely contains, per code.
///
/// A table rather than a list of codes or a total, because those made every new advisory check
/// renegotiate this file: a positional list moves when a check is added anywhere, and a count of
/// eight says nothing about *which* eight (ah-11lh). A new check adds a row here and touches
/// nothing else - and, more importantly, a check that stops firing on real orders shows up as a row
/// that changed rather than disappearing into a total.
///
/// The turn is not clean and is not meant to be: these are real findings about real orders, listed
/// in `the_committed_turn_has_no_semantic_problems_either`'s own comment history.
const EXPECTED: &[(&str, usize)] = &[
    ("magic-study-outside-building", 6),
    ("not-enough-items", 1),
    ("study-at-maximum", 1),
];

/// The findings by code, so an expectation can be read as a table.
fn counts(findings: &[Finding]) -> BTreeMap<&str, usize> {
    let mut seen = BTreeMap::new();
    for finding in findings {
        *seen.entry(finding.code.as_str()).or_insert(0) += 1;
    }
    seen
}
```

with the assertion becoming `assert_eq!(counts(&findings), EXPECTED.iter().copied().collect())`.

**The numbers above are illustrative and must be read off the real run, not copied.** The current
list is eight findings — six `magic-study-outside-building`, one `study-at-maximum`, one
`not-enough-items` — and **`ah-dwk6` and `ah-3cj4.1` are both in flight and both change this file's
expectations.** Build the table from what the suite actually reports at the moment of implementation,
and if it disagrees with the eight named in the existing comments, **stop and find out why** rather
than writing down whatever came out.

The `damaged` case then derives rather than repeats:

```rust
    let mut expected: BTreeMap<&str, usize> = EXPECTED.iter().copied().collect();
    *expected.entry("not-enough-silver").or_insert(0) += 1;   // the shortfall this case introduces
    assert_eq!(counts(&findings), expected, "{findings:?}");
```

and `expected.len() == 8` becomes a sum over the table, so the three places cannot drift apart.

**Keep every explanatory comment.** The block's comment log is why anyone believes the turn is not
clean; it moves onto the table, it does not get deleted.

### 2. Named fields instead of a four-tuple — `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs:5768-5773`

`every_advisory_code_can_be_silenced` builds its cases as:

```rust
        type Case = (
            Code,
            Vec<ReportRegion>,
            &'static str,
            Option<(&'static str, i64, i64)>,
        );
```

Twenty-three of these in one `vec![]`, each a bare tuple whose fourth element is itself a tuple.
Forge's point is precise: two beads appending a case each can be **auto-merged into a valid but
wrong tuple**, silently.

A struct fixes exactly that, and cheaply:

```rust
    /// One code, and the smallest fixture that makes it fire.
    ///
    /// Named fields rather than a tuple (ah-11lh): two beads adding a case each used to auto-merge
    /// into a case that still compiled and asserted the wrong thing. Interleaved named fields do
    /// not compile, so a bad merge is a build error instead of a silent one.
    struct Case {
        code: Code,
        regions: Vec<ReportRegion>,
        orders: &'static str,
        /// A `Faction Status:` allowance the case's report should carry - `None` for every per-hex
        /// check, and what `too-many-quartermasters` and `too-many-trade-regions` need instead of
        /// a hex.
        allowance: Option<(&'static str, i64, i64)>,
    }
```

Every case becomes `Case { code: codes::…, regions: …, orders: "…", allowance: None }`. Mechanical,
23 times, and the compiler catches any that is wrong.

**Do not split it into 23 `#[test]` functions.** That is the other way to fix the merge hazard and it
trades one problem for 23 copies of the harness; the struct removes the silent-merge failure, which
is the actual complaint.

## Increments

1. **The corpus expectation becomes a table.**
   RED: none — the behaviour under test does not change. Write `counts` and `EXPECTED`, and make
   `the_committed_turn_has_no_semantic_problems_either` assert against them. **It must pass first
   time**; if it does not, the table was written from the comments rather than from the run.
   GREEN: the same test, green, with the table in place of the positional list.

2. **The other two assertions derive from it.**
   RED: temporarily add a bogus row to `EXPECTED` and confirm **all three** assertions fail. That is
   the only way to prove they are actually reading it; revert.
   GREEN: the `damaged` case and the fifty-pass case rewritten against the table.

3. **The cases get names.**
   RED: none. Convert `Case` to a struct; the compiler names every site that has not been updated.
   GREEN: `cargo test --workspace` green, with `every_advisory_code_can_be_silenced` asserting
   exactly what it did before.

4. **Nothing moved.**
   RED: none — this is the check. `cargo test --workspace` and `pnpm run check:fast` green, and
   `git diff --stat` touches exactly two files, neither of them production code.

## The test plan

**This bead's output is tests, so the test plan is mostly "prove the tests still test something".**

| Check | How |
|---|---|
| the corpus expectation is real | increment 2's deliberate bogus row must fail all three assertions |
| no behaviour changed | `cargo test --workspace` green with **no** production file in the diff |
| the silencing test still proves both directions | `every_advisory_code_can_be_silenced` still asserts present-when-enabled and absent-when-disabled for all 23 |
| a new check adds one row | add a throwaway row by hand, confirm the corpus tests fail with a message naming the code, remove it |
| the comment history survives | the block's explanatory comments are on the table, not deleted |

**Suites:** `cargo test --workspace` and `pnpm run check:fast`. **No browser suite** — this bead
touches neither the smoke fixtures nor anything they render, which is deliberate: the smoke half of
the coupling is the expensive half and is out of scope.

## User-facing decisions

**None.** Nothing here reaches a player, and nothing changes what any check does or says. No mockup —
there is no interface.

**The one decision worth recording is the scope**, and it is the planner's rather than the
navigator's: Forge's *"Note for triage"* argues the full opt-in seam may cost more than it saves, and
this plan agrees and does the cheap subset only. The four reasons are in *Context*; the large version
is filed as `ah-i7we` at P4 with Forge's caveat attached. **The navigator ranked this P1 on the
recurring cost, so if they wanted the fixture seam itself, this plan is not it** — and that is worth
saying to them rather than leaving it to be discovered when the diff turns out to be two files.

## Out of scope

- **The opt-in fixture seam** — a fixture declaring the code it is about so the other 22 cannot
  perturb it, and retiring `check`, `check_ignoring_transfer_targets`, `check_ignoring_empty_builds`
  and `check_idle`. Filed as `ah-i7we`, P4. This is the ~200-fixture half.
- **The smoke suite's ~85 exact-count assertions** against the turn-71 report, and the fact that
  `check:fast` does not run them. That is the expensive half of the coupling and the reason a break
  costs a CI round trip; it is not touched here.
- **`DEFAULT_ADVISORY_CHECKS` re-deriving the Rust default** in `settingsStore.ts`. A real
  duplication, and a different one.
- **Any change to a check, a code, or `CheckOptions`.** If production code appears in the diff, the
  bead has gone wrong.
- **Splitting `every_advisory_code_can_be_silenced` into 23 tests**, considered and rejected above.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test --workspace
pnpm run check:fast
git diff --stat origin/main
```

The last one is the real check: **exactly two files**, `crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs`
and `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`, and within the second only its `#[cfg(test)]` module.
Anything else in that list means behaviour changed.

Then, by hand, the two experiments that prove the tests still bite:

1. Add `("nonsense-code", 1)` to `EXPECTED`. All three corpus assertions must fail, and the message
   must name the code rather than only a count. Remove it.
2. Take one case out of `every_advisory_code_can_be_silenced`'s vector. The test must fail saying
   that code has no fixture — that is what stops a code being added without one. Put it back.

## Known traps

- **`ah-dwk6` and `ah-3cj4.1` are in flight and both change what the committed turn produces.**
  `ah-dwk6` adds two `unit-does-nothing` findings; `ah-3cj4.1` rebuilds `ruleset.json`, which this
  file's checks run against. **Build `EXPECTED` from a live run at the moment of implementation**,
  and rebase before opening the PR. Copying the eight codes out of the existing comments will be
  wrong by then.
- **If the live run disagrees with the comments, stop.** This bead is about making a disagreement
  visible; silently writing down whatever the run produced is the exact failure it exists to prevent.
- **No production code.** The temptation is to "just fix" an over-broad check while in here. That is
  the wrong fix Forge names, and it is what this bead is trying to make hard.
- **The four `check_ignoring_*` helpers stay.** They are the symptom, not the target; retiring them
  is the opt-in seam.
- **Keep the comment log.** It is the only record of why the committed turn is not clean, and it is
  what a reader needs to judge whether a new row is legitimate.
- **A `BTreeMap` comparison must name what differed.** `assert_eq!` on two maps prints both, which is
  what makes this readable; do not reduce it to comparing lengths.
acceptance_criteria: crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs expresses what the committed turn contains as a single per-code table, built from a live run at implementation time rather than copied from the existing comments, with all three assertions - the clean-turn case, the damaged case, and the fifty-pass case - deriving from that one table so they cannot drift apart; the damaged case adds its introduced shortfall to the table rather than repeating it, and the block's explanatory comments survive on the table. Adding a deliberate bogus row makes all three fail, and the failure names the code rather than only a count. every_advisory_code_can_be_silenced's cases are a struct with named fields rather than a four-tuple, so an interleaved auto-merge is a compile error, and the test still proves both directions for all 23 codes. Removing any one case still fails with a message saying that code has no fixture. No production code changes at all: git diff --stat shows exactly two files, and within semantics.rs only its cfg(test) module, so no check, code or CheckOptions is touched. cargo test --workspace and pnpm run check:fast pass. The opt-in fixture seam and the smoke suite's exact-count assertions are explicitly not in this bead; they are ah-i7we.

title: The launcher suite tests the machine it runs on, and writes to it
description:
## The cost being paid

`.claude/cerebro/tests/launchers.sh` — the documented validation step for a bead touching the
launchers — asserts against the *real enclosing consumer*: its uncommitted `.cerebro/models.conf`,
its `.claude/` links, and whichever checkout it happens to be run from. So it is red on the
navigator's machine and green in CI, and an implementer cannot tell a real failure from the
machine's own configuration. Four separate retrospectives are about running this one suite locally.

Worse than red: running it **mutates the navigator's checkout**. The roster loop calls
`run_launcher launch "$name"` against the real submodule inside the real consumer, and
`launch` → `launch-preflight` → `sync-symlinks.sh` resolves `consumer-root` and writes symlinks into
`.claude/` as a side effect of running the tests.

**Red right now, verifiable without running anything.** The suite asserts `--effort` equals the
role's agent-file frontmatter, while this machine's `.cerebro/models.conf` says `planner opus medium`
against frontmatter `high`, and `architect opus high` against frontmatter `xhigh`. Two roster rows
fail before anyone changes a line.

## Evidence

- docs/retrospectives/ah-bqi.md §"`tests/launchers.sh` fails locally for whatever this machine's `.cerebro/models.conf` says" — **~10 min**, "all of it spent deciding whether a red suite in a bead touching `scripts/` was mine": two runs, a stash/unstash, a `gh run list` against the submodule's main. Its verdict: "**a suite whose result depends on an uncommitted, per-machine file cannot be part of a documented validation step**, and this is now the fourth separate retrospective about running this one suite locally." It counts them: ah-rnz (wrong bash on PATH), ah-cuc (a consumer fixture's symlinks), ah-goz (red on the HEAD it was run against), ah-2sy.
- docs/retrospectives/ah-2sy.md §"`tests/launchers.sh` failed only when run from inside a real implementer worktree's own `.claude/cerebro` copy" — **~15 min**: a full `tests/*.sh` pass with an unexplained failure, a `BEADS_ACTOR` check, an `env -u` retry, and finally a second full `git clone` into `/tmp` to get an authoritative run.
- Live, on this machine: `.cerebro/models.conf` rows `planner opus medium` and `architect opus high` against `.claude/agents/planner.md` `effort: high` and `.claude/agents/architect.md` `effort: xhigh`.

## Where

- `.claude/cerebro/tests/launchers.sh` — `run_launcher`, and the roster loop that calls it against the live checkout. Contrast the fabricated consumer further down the same file (built with `git init` + `cp -R`), which the `models.conf` cases already use correctly via `run_launcher_at`.
- `.claude/cerebro/scripts/launch`, `.claude/cerebro/scripts/launch-preflight`, `.claude/cerebro/scripts/sync-symlinks.sh`, `.claude/cerebro/scripts/consumer-root`.

## What a refactoring would change

The seam already exists in the same file: the fabricated consumer the `models.conf` cases run through.
Move the roster and override cases onto it too, so `run_launcher` against the live checkout disappears
entirely — build the fixture once at the top and make it the only consumer any assertion ever sees.
That removes the per-machine `models.conf` dependence, the run-from-a-worktree dependence, and the
write into the navigator's `.claude/`, in one move, and makes a red suite mean what it says.

Note for triage: the four cited causes are genuinely four different bugs sharing a filename, and only
ah-bqi is squarely "the enclosing checkout leaked in". The cost also lands on whoever edits the
submodule rather than on the application. The side-effect write into the shared checkout is the part
that stands on its own.

## Context

`.claude/cerebro/tests/launchers.sh` — the documented validation step for a bead touching the
launchers — asserts against the **real enclosing consumer**: its uncommitted `.cerebro/models.conf`,
its `.claude/` links, and whichever checkout it happens to be run from. So it is **red on the
navigator's machine and green in CI**, and an implementer cannot tell a real failure from the
machine's own configuration.

**And running it writes to the navigator's checkout.** The roster loop calls
`run_launcher launch "$name"` against the real submodule inside the real consumer, and
`launch` → `launch-preflight` → `sync-symlinks.sh` resolves `consumer-root` and **writes symlinks
into `.claude/` as a side effect of running the tests**.

**Red right now, verifiable without running anything.** This machine's `.cerebro/models.conf` says
`planner opus medium` against `agents/planner.md`'s `effort: high`, and `architect opus high` against
`agents/architect.md`'s `effort: xhigh`. Two roster rows fail before anyone changes a line.

Four retrospectives are about running this one suite locally — `ah-bqi` (~10 min, *"all of it spent
deciding whether a red suite in a bead touching `scripts/` was mine"*), `ah-2sy` (~15 min, ending in a
second `git clone` into `/tmp` to get an authoritative run), `ah-rnz`, `ah-cuc`, `ah-goz`. `ah-bqi`'s
verdict is the bead: *"a suite whose result depends on an uncommitted, per-machine file cannot be
part of a documented validation step."*

**The seam already exists in the same file.** `run_launcher_at` (`tests/launchers.sh:48-57`) runs a
launcher *"against a launcher living at an arbitrary scripts directory — used to prove a launcher
syncs the symlinks of the consumer repo it is actually running from, not this checkout (ah-cuc)"*,
and a fabricated consumer is already built twice for it (`:288-292`, `:402-406`):

```bash
consumer_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
git init -q "$consumer_dir"
cp -R "$repo_root" "$consumer_dir/.claude/cerebro"
```

**So the fix is one helper, not fourteen call sites** — see §1. That is the whole reason this bead is
small.

### This lands in a different repository, and it is ordered against `ah-puoj`

`.claude/cerebro` is a submodule with its own remote (`rmstdope/cerebro`), its own CI and its own
`tests/`. This is **two PRs**: the change in cerebro, then a submodule pin bump in `atlantis-hud`.

**`ah-puoj` must not land first, and there is now a `bd dep` saying so.** That bead gives
`launch-preflight` a `git fetch` and a `merge --ff-only` on the enclosing consumer. Combined with
`run_launcher` invoking the real launchers against the real checkout, **running the test suite would
fetch and fast-forward the navigator's working tree** — and `ah-puoj`'s own validation runs
`for t in tests/*.sh`. This bead removes that reach first, after which the fabricated consumer is a
fresh `git init` with **no remote**, which `ah-puoj`'s "nothing known to be stale" path handles
cleanly.

Branch from `origin/main` of the cerebro repository.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

One file: `tests/launchers.sh`, in the cerebro repository. **No script changes at all** — if anything
under `scripts/` appears in the diff, the bead has gone wrong.

### 1. One fabricated consumer, built once, used by everything

Build the fixture next to the existing `stub_dir` (`:30`), using the recipe already proven at
`:288-292`, and then **redefine `run_launcher` in terms of `run_launcher_at`**:

```bash
# --- the one consumer any assertion ever sees ---------------------------------------------------
#
# Every launcher case used to run `$repo_root/scripts/...` - the real submodule inside the real
# enclosing checkout - so the suite asserted against that machine's uncommitted
# `.cerebro/models.conf`, was red on the navigator's machine and green in CI, and *wrote symlinks
# into their `.claude/`* as a side effect of running (ah-dy4x). A throwaway consumer removes all
# three at once: no models.conf unless a case writes one, no dependence on where the suite is run
# from, and every write lands in a temp directory.
fixture_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
mkdir -p "$fixture_dir/.claude"
git init -q "$fixture_dir"
cp -R "$repo_root" "$fixture_dir/.claude/cerebro"
trap 'rm -rf "$stub_dir" "$fixture_dir"' EXIT

run_launcher() {
  # Against the fabricated consumer, never the enclosing one. `run_launcher_at` already existed for
  # exactly this (ah-cuc); this makes it the only way in.
  run_launcher_at "$fixture_dir/.claude/cerebro/scripts" "$@"
}
```

**Every one of the ~14 existing call sites is then correct unchanged** — `:151`, `:185`, `:197`,
`:209`, `:218`, `:227`, `:242`, `:249`, `:254`, `:261`, `:270`, `:280` and the rest keep calling
`run_launcher launch Xavier` and now get the fixture. That is the entire behavioural change.

Two details that decide whether it works:

- **`consumer-root` resolves from the script's own location**, which is why this is sufficient: with
  the launcher living under `$fixture_dir/.claude/cerebro/scripts`, `sync-symlinks.sh` writes into
  `$fixture_dir/.claude`, and `launch-preflight`'s toplevel check sees `$fixture_dir` — a real git
  working tree, because of the `git init`.
- **The fixture has no `.cerebro/models.conf`**, because that file lives in the *consumer*, not the
  submodule, and `cp -R` copies only the submodule. So the roster and effort cases compare launcher
  output against the **committed** frontmatter in `agents/*.md`, which is deterministic. That is the
  whole of the per-machine dependence, gone.

### 2. Retire the two ad-hoc consumers — `:288-292` and `:402-406`

Both build their own `consumer_dir` for the `models.conf` and symlink cases. Point them at
`$fixture_dir` unless a case genuinely needs a *separate* consumer — the `models.conf` override cases
do, because they write that file and must not leak it into the roster cases that assume its absence.

**Keep a second fixture where isolation is the point, and say so in a comment.** A case that writes
`.cerebro/models.conf` and a case that asserts the default effort cannot share a consumer; that is
not duplication, it is the test being honest. What must go is the *enclosing* checkout, not every
extra temp directory.

### 3. Say what the suite now promises — the file header

`tests/launchers.sh`'s header (`:3`) describes what it proves. Add one line:

```
# Every assertion runs against a fabricated consumer under `mktemp -d`, never the checkout this is
# run from: the suite used to read that machine's uncommitted `.cerebro/models.conf` and write
# symlinks into its `.claude/` (ah-dy4x). Nothing here should ever touch the enclosing tree.
```

This is the line that stops the next contributor reaching for `$repo_root/scripts` again.

## Increments

1. **The suite stops reading this machine.**
   RED: run `bash tests/launchers.sh` on the navigator's machine **before any change** and record the
   failures — the two `models.conf`-versus-frontmatter rows named in *Context*. That is the
   reproduction, and it costs nothing.
   GREEN: the fixture and the `run_launcher` redefinition. The suite goes green **on the same machine
   with `.cerebro/models.conf` untouched.**

2. **The suite stops writing to this machine.**
   RED: `git status` in the consumer before and after a run. Today the run can create or refresh
   symlinks under `.claude/`; afterwards the two `git status` outputs must be **identical**, and
   `$fixture_dir` must contain the symlinks instead.
   GREEN: nothing further, if increment 1 routed every call. **If `git status` still differs, some
   call site was missed** — grep for `$repo_root/scripts` and for `run_launcher_at` with a
   non-fixture path.

3. **It still fails when the launchers are wrong.**
   RED: break something real and cheap — rename a role in `scripts/roster`, or make `launch` pass the
   wrong `--model` — and confirm the suite goes red. Revert. **A suite that passes against a
   fabricated consumer no matter what is worse than one that is red for the wrong reason.**

4. **The fleet gets it.** The `atlantis-hud` submodule pin bump.

## The test plan

**The artefact is a test suite, so the test plan is how to prove it still tests something.**

| Check | How |
|---|---|
| **it is green on this machine** | `bash tests/launchers.sh` with `.cerebro/models.conf` exactly as it is — the two failing rows are the acceptance |
| **it writes nothing** | `git status --porcelain` in the consumer, identical before and after |
| it is green in CI | the cerebro repo's own workflow, `for t in tests/*.sh` |
| the other suites still pass | `for t in tests/*.sh; do bash "$t"; done` |
| **it still catches a real fault** | increment 3's deliberate break |
| nothing under `scripts/` changed | `git diff --stat` names one file |

**No `atlantis-hud` suite covers this**, and none should. The `atlantis-hud` PR is a pin bump whose
only check is that CI stays green.

## User-facing decisions

**None.** Nothing reaches a player; no mockup, since the artefact is a shell test.

One decision was the planner's, as tooling, and is recorded because it goes slightly beyond Forge's
proposal: **`ah-puoj` is now ordered behind this bead** (`bd dep add ah-puoj ah-dy4x`). Forge did not
raise it, because `ah-puoj` was filed in the same sweep. The reason is concrete: `ah-puoj` gives
`launch-preflight` a `fetch` and a `merge --ff-only` on the enclosing consumer, and this suite invokes
the real launchers against that consumer — so with `ah-puoj` first, **running the tests would
fast-forward the navigator's working tree**, and `ah-puoj`'s own validation runs the suite. That is a
worse version of the defect this bead exists to remove.

## Out of scope

- **`scripts/` — any of it.** The launchers are not at fault; the suite's reach is.
- **The `.cerebro/models.conf` mismatch itself** — `planner opus medium` against `effort: high`.
  Whether this machine's overrides *should* differ from the frontmatter is the navigator's business,
  and after this bead the suite has no opinion about it.
- **The other three causes Forge cites** — wrong bash on PATH (`ah-rnz`), a consumer fixture's
  symlinks (`ah-cuc`), red on the HEAD it was run against (`ah-goz`). Forge's own note says these are
  *"genuinely four different bugs sharing a filename"*; only the enclosing-checkout leak is this bead.
- **`ah-puoj`'s change to `launch-preflight`.** Ordered after this, not included in it.
- **Making `tests/launchers.sh` faster.** `cp -R` of the submodule twice is not cheap, and building
  one fixture instead of two happens to help — but speed is not the goal and must not drive
  collapsing fixtures that need to be separate.

## Validation

```bash
cd .claude/cerebro
git status --porcelain > /tmp/before.txt
bash tests/launchers.sh
git -C "$(scripts/consumer-root)" status --porcelain > /tmp/after.txt
diff /tmp/before.txt /tmp/after.txt          # must be empty
for t in tests/*.sh; do bash "$t"; done
```

Then, in order:

1. **The reproduction first.** On the navigator's machine, with `.cerebro/models.conf` untouched, the
   suite is red on two roster rows *before* the change. Record what it says; that is the bead in one
   line.
2. After the change, **green on the same machine, same `models.conf`, nothing stashed.** If it needed
   the file moved aside, the bead is not done.
3. **Nothing written.** The `diff` above must be empty, and `.claude/agents/*.md` symlinks must have
   the same mtimes as before the run.
4. **It still bites.** Rename a role in `scripts/roster` and confirm the suite fails; revert.
5. Confirm `git diff --stat` in the cerebro repo names **only** `tests/launchers.sh`.

## Known traps

- **`run_launcher_at` already exists and already does the right thing** (`:48-57`). The temptation is
  to write a new mechanism; the fix is to make the existing one the only way in.
- **`consumer-root` resolves from the script's own location**, which is the entire reason copying the
  submodule into a temp consumer works. Anything that instead passes a path *to* the launcher will
  not exercise what the launchers really do.
- **The fixture must be a real git working tree.** `launch-preflight` checks
  `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` equals the consumer and **exits 0 (skipping its checks) if not** —
  so a fixture without `git init` would make the launcher cases silently assert nothing.
- **Do not collapse fixtures that must stay separate.** A case writing `.cerebro/models.conf` and a
  case asserting the default effort cannot share a consumer. Fewer temp directories is not the goal.
- **`trap ... EXIT` must clean up both** the stub dir and the fixture; the existing trap covers only
  the stub.
- **Run the suite once *before* changing anything.** The two failing rows are the evidence, and after
  the fix they are unobtainable — a green suite cannot demonstrate what it used to do.
- **This is the cerebro repository.** Two PRs, and the `atlantis-hud` pin bump is what actually
  delivers it.
- **`ah-puoj` is ordered behind this.** If it has somehow landed first, expect the suite to fetch and
  fast-forward the enclosing checkout while running, and fix that before anything else.

The suite is green on the navigator's machine with .cerebro/models.conf exactly as it is, nothing stashed or moved aside - the two roster rows that fail today, planner medium against frontmatter high and architect high against xhigh, must be recorded as red before the change and green after. Running the suite writes nothing to the enclosing checkout: git status --porcelain in the consumer is byte-identical before and after, and the symlinks land in the fixture instead. Fixtures that must stay separate stay separate, with a comment saying why - a case writing models.conf cannot share a consumer with one asserting the default effort. The suite still fails when the launchers are genuinely wrong, verified by renaming a role in scripts/roster and reverting. The file header says the suite never touches the enclosing tree. Nothing under scripts/ changes: git diff --stat names one file. Delivered as a cerebro PR plus an atlantis-hud submodule pin bump, and ah-puoj is ordered behind it.

title: A session starts from a stale checkout and reads instructions that no longer apply
description:
## The cost being paid

Every session's instructions are read from the shared main checkout at session start — `CLAUDE.md`,
and the skills, which are symlinks into whatever commit `.claude/cerebro` is pinned to *in that
tree*. Nothing refreshes either. `launch-preflight` runs on every launch and checks claude-on-PATH,
that the role's agent file exists, and syncs symlinks; it never fetches, never fast-forwards, never
runs `git submodule update`. Its only response to a stale submodule is to print "the submodule is
behind; run `git submodule update --init --recursive` and try again" — a manual step with no owner.

So a session can be launched against a `main` and a submodule pin that are days old, and it has no
signal at all: its own instructions describe a repository that no longer exists.

**This is live right now.** At the start of this sweep the shared checkout was at 66dbd85 while
`origin/main` was at cec1dd0 — 22 commits behind, spanning two days.

## Evidence

- docs/retrospectives/ah-mi7.md §"The session's own instructions were already stale: the shared checkout's `main` was five commits behind, mid-`.cerebro/` migration" — **~20 min**: a red `check:fast`, tracing it to `AGENT_WORKSPACES`, `git pull --ff-only` on the shared checkout, worktree removed and recreated, dependencies reinstalled. Its Why: "the shared checkout's own working copy of `CLAUDE.md`, the skills, and `.claude/cerebro` itself are read from whatever `main` happens to be checked out to locally, and **nothing keeps that current**."
- docs/retrospectives/ah-yvf.md §"A session's own CLAUDE.md was two commits stale, and its worktree ended up in a location `main` no longer used" — **~10 min**, one red gate, worktree relocated, submodule re-initialised, reinstall. Same mechanism, different session, same day.
- docs/retrospectives/ah-gdp.md §"The main checkout's stale `.claude/cerebro` pin served a fresh session skill text one submodule bump behind" — the pin rather than the branch; the session was handed `implement-bead` text describing `git worktree add` + `pnpm install`, one bump behind 3621c84's `prepare-worktree`. Its Why: "**`git submodule update` there is a manual step nobody owns**, so `origin/main`'s content and what a freshly-started session reads via the symlinked skill can disagree for as long as that gap lasts... ah-2sy's own fix... does not help the *main checkout* itself go stale in the same way." Its Cost names "the four-retrospectives-in-two-days shape".
- Probably a fourth: docs/retrospectives/ah-0fa.md §"A fresh worktree still has no wasm build — third sighting" says `implement-bead`'s Workspace block "does not mention it", which was false of the text that had been on `origin/main` for 14 hours when it was written (3621c84 landed 08:25; ah-0fa merged 22:52). That reads as a session served stale skill text, i.e. a symptom of this.

## Where

- `.claude/cerebro/scripts/launch-preflight` — owns "this session cannot start yet, and here is why", but starts one step too late. `grep -nE 'pull|fetch' scripts/run-implementer scripts/launch scripts/launch-preflight` returns nothing.
- `.claude/cerebro/scripts/launch`, `.claude/cerebro/scripts/run-*`.
- What they gate: `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/skills/*` → `.claude/cerebro/skills/*`, symlinks into whatever pin the tree holds.

## What a refactoring would change

Give `launch-preflight` the shared checkout's currency, since it already owns the refuse-to-launch
decision: fetch `origin/main`, fast-forward `main` if it is checked out and clean, and
`git submodule update --init --recursive` to the tracked pin. Where the tree is dirty or diverged,
**refuse to launch with one line rather than touching the navigator's work** — a launcher writing
into a tree the navigator is editing is its own hazard, and is not what this asks for.
`prepare-worktree` already does exactly this for a worktree; the main checkout is the tree that never
got the same owner.

Note for triage: the two costly sightings both date from the `.claude/worktrees/` →
`.cerebro/worktrees/` migration, and a convention move that large is rare — so this can be read as
"one migration cost two sessions 30 minutes". The counter is ah-gdp and ah-0fa, both after that
migration, and the 22-commit gap standing today.

design:
## Context

Every session reads its instructions from the shared main checkout at start-up — `CLAUDE.md`, and
the skills, which are symlinks into whatever commit `.claude/cerebro` is pinned to *in that tree*.
**Nothing refreshes either.** `launch-preflight` runs on every launch and checks that `claude` is on
PATH, that the role's agent file exists and that the link resolves; `grep -nE 'pull|fetch'` over the
launchers returns nothing. Its only response to a stale submodule is to print *"the submodule is
behind; run `git submodule update --init --recursive` and try again"* — a manual step with no owner.

So a session can start against a `main` and a submodule pin that are days old, **and it has no signal
at all**: its own instructions describe a repository that no longer exists.

**This is live, and it is affecting this session.** Measured on 2026-08-19 while planning this bead:

```
main vs origin/main:  0 ahead, 28 behind
tracked changes:      none
untracked:            .claude/agents/reviewer.md
submodule:            e7b23cd (heads/main)
```

Twenty-eight commits, and the tree is otherwise **perfectly fast-forwardable**. The planner writing
this plan read every source file through `git show origin/main:<path>` precisely because the working
tree could not be trusted — had it read from the working tree, every line number in every plan
written today would have been from a two-day-old tree.

Forge's four sightings — `ah-mi7` (~20 min), `ah-yvf` (~10 min), `ah-gdp` (the *pin* rather than the
branch: a session was served `implement-bead` text describing a workflow that had already changed),
and probably `ah-0fa` — are the same mechanism from four angles.

**This bead changes a different repository from every other bead in the backlog.** See below; it is
the single most important thing to know before starting.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### 0. Where this work happens — read this first

`.claude/cerebro` is a **git submodule with its own remote**, `https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro.git`,
its own `main`, its own CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, which runs `for t in tests/*.sh`) and its own
test suite under `tests/`. `launch-preflight` lives there, not in `atlantis-hud`.

So this bead is **two pull requests**:

1. **In `rmstdope/cerebro`** — the change and its test. Branch, commit, PR, review, merge there.
2. **In `atlantis-hud`** — a one-line submodule pin bump so the fleet actually gets it, from a
   worktree under `.cerebro/worktrees/` as usual.

Do **not** try to do this from an `atlantis-hud` branch alone: editing `.claude/cerebro/scripts/…`
in the superproject changes a checked-out submodule and commits nothing that anyone else receives.

### 1. The currency check — `scripts/launch-preflight` (in the cerebro repo)

The script's shape is already right for this: it owns *"this session cannot start yet, and here is
why"*, and its own header says every check it owns *"exits 2 with one line on stderr naming what is
wrong and the command that fixes it"*. The new check follows that convention exactly.

**Where it goes: immediately after the git-toplevel guard, and before the agent-file check.** That
order is load-bearing — a stale submodule is *why* the agent-file check fires today, and its own
error message says so. Bringing the tree current first turns that failure into a success rather than
a second error.

The rule, stated so there is nothing to infer:

```bash
# The tree these instructions are read from - CLAUDE.md, and the skills, which are symlinks into
# whatever the submodule is pinned to here - is never refreshed by anything (ah-puoj). A session
# started on a stale one describes a repository that no longer exists and cannot find that out.
#
# Untracked files never block this: the consumer routinely carries some, and refusing on them
# would refuse every launch.
head="$(git -C "$consumer" rev-parse HEAD)"
git -C "$consumer" fetch --quiet origin main 2>/dev/null || true   # offline is not staleness
target="$(git -C "$consumer" rev-parse origin/main 2>/dev/null || echo "")"
```

Then exactly three outcomes:

| State | Action |
|---|---|
| `target` empty (never fetched, no remote, offline on a fresh clone) | **Proceed.** Nothing is known to be stale; being offline is not a staleness this can fix. |
| `head` == `target` | **Proceed.** Already current. |
| on `main`, no tracked changes, and strictly behind | **Fast-forward, update the submodule, proceed.** |
| anything else | **Refuse**, exit 2, one line. |

"On `main`, clean, strictly behind" is:

```bash
branch="$(git -C "$consumer" rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)"
dirty="$(git -C "$consumer" status --porcelain --untracked-files=no)"
ahead="$(git -C "$consumer" rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD)"
```

— `branch` is `main`, `dirty` is empty, `ahead` is `0`. **`--untracked-files=no` is the whole of the
untracked-file rule**; without it the one stray file in the consumer today refuses every launch.

Then:

```bash
git -C "$consumer" merge --ff-only origin/main --quiet
git -C "$consumer" submodule update --init --recursive --quiet
```

`--ff-only` rather than `pull`: it cannot merge, cannot rebase, and fails rather than inventing a
commit in the navigator's checkout.

**The submodule update is guarded the same way.** If the submodule itself has tracked changes,
refuse rather than clobber them — somebody is editing cerebro in place, which is exactly how this
bead is being built:

```bash
if [[ -n "$(git -C "$parent/cerebro" status --porcelain --untracked-files=no)" ]]; then
  echo "cerebro: .claude/cerebro has uncommitted changes - commit or stash them before starting $name" >&2
  exit 2
fi
```

The refusal messages, in the house style (one line, name the fix):

```
cerebro: the checkout is 28 commits behind origin/main and has uncommitted changes - commit or stash them, then git merge --ff-only origin/main, before starting Cyclops
cerebro: the checkout is on branch <b>, not main - the fleet's instructions are read from main; switch back before starting Cyclops
cerebro: main has 2 commits origin/main does not - push or reset them before starting Cyclops
```

**Standalone clones are unaffected.** The existing `consumer-root` guard (`exit 0`) and the
toplevel check already return early for anything that is not a consumer, and the new code sits after
both.

### 2. The test — `tests/launch-preflight.sh` (new, in the cerebro repo)

Follow **`tests/consumer-root.sh`**, which is the right model and already in the repo: plain bash,
`set -euo pipefail`, `fail`/`pass` helpers, and — the important part — it builds a **throwaway
consumer in `mktemp -d`**, `git init`s it, and symlinks the script under test into
`$consumer/.claude/cerebro/scripts/`. Nothing about the enclosing machine is asserted.

**Do not extend `tests/launchers.sh`.** It asserts against the real enclosing consumer, is red on the
navigator's machine for reasons unrelated to the code, and *writes symlinks into their checkout as a
side effect of running* — that is `ah-dy4x`, filed and ranked P1. Building on it would inherit both
problems and make `ah-dy4x` harder.

Each case builds a temp consumer plus a temp "origin" it can be behind:

| Case | Set up | Expect |
|---|---|---|
| `a current checkout launches` | consumer at origin/main | exit 0, HEAD unmoved |
| **`a behind but clean checkout is fast-forwarded`** | origin ahead by 2, tree clean | exit 0, HEAD == origin/main |
| **`an untracked file does not stop it`** | as above plus an untracked file | exit 0, HEAD == origin/main, file still there |
| `a dirty checkout is refused` | origin ahead, one tracked file modified | exit 2, message names uncommitted changes, **HEAD unmoved and the edit intact** |
| `a diverged checkout is refused` | one commit on main that origin lacks | exit 2, message names it, HEAD unmoved |
| `a checkout on another branch is refused` | HEAD on `wip` | exit 2, message names the branch |
| `no remote is not a failure` | consumer with no origin | exit 0 |
| `a standalone clone is untouched` | no consumer layout | exit 0, as today |

**Assert the tree afterwards, not only the exit code.** The dirty and diverged cases are about *not
writing to somebody's work*, so the test that matters is that the edit and the commit are still
there.

### 3. The pin bump — `atlantis-hud`

Once the cerebro PR is merged, a second small PR in `atlantis-hud`, from a worktree under
`.cerebro/worktrees/` as every other bead does: `git submodule update --remote .claude/cerebro`,
commit the new pin, PR, merge. That is the commit that actually gives the fleet the fix.

## Increments

1. **The test says what should happen.**
   RED: `tests/launch-preflight.sh` with all eight cases. Every case that expects a fast-forward
   fails, because nothing fetches.
   GREEN: nothing yet — write the test first and watch it fail for the right reason. The
   `a standalone clone is untouched` and `a current checkout launches` cases should pass immediately;
   if they do not, the harness is wrong before the feature is.

2. **A clean tree comes current.**
   RED: `a behind but clean checkout is fast-forwarded` and `an untracked file does not stop it`.
   GREEN: the fetch, the three-way decision, `merge --ff-only`.

3. **A tree with work in it is refused, not touched.**
   RED: `a dirty checkout is refused`, `a diverged checkout is refused`,
   `a checkout on another branch is refused` — each asserting the tree is unchanged afterwards.
   GREEN: the guards and the three messages.

4. **The submodule follows the branch.**
   RED: a case where origin's new commit bumps the pin, asserting `.claude/cerebro` moves to it; and
   one where the submodule has a tracked change, asserting exit 2 and that the change survives.
   GREEN: `submodule update --init --recursive`, and its dirty guard.

5. **Offline is not staleness.**
   RED: `no remote is not a failure`.
   GREEN: the `|| true` on the fetch and the empty-`target` branch.

6. **The fleet gets it.**
   RED: none. The `atlantis-hud` pin bump, and one real launch watched from a deliberately
   stale checkout.

## The test plan

**Shell — `tests/launch-preflight.sh` in the cerebro repo**, run by that repo's CI
(`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `for t in tests/*.sh`) and locally with `bash tests/launch-preflight.sh`
from the submodule root. The eight cases are tabulated in §2.

**Nothing in `atlantis-hud`'s suite covers this**, and nothing should: `pnpm run check:fast` and
`cargo test` know nothing about the launchers. The `atlantis-hud` PR is a pin bump whose only check
is that CI stays green.

**The one thing tests cannot prove** is that a real session, started by a real launcher, ends up
current — the tests exercise `launch-preflight` directly. That is *Validation* step 3, and it must
actually be done.

## User-facing decisions

Nothing here reaches a player, but two decisions are the navigator's because they change what happens
when *they* type a launcher. Interviewed 2026-08-19; no mockup — a shell script has no interface to
draw, and the messages are quoted in §1 instead.

**Q1 — what to do when the checkout cannot be brought current.** Chosen: **refuse to launch, naming
what to fix.** A session started on a stale tree reads instructions describing a repository that no
longer exists and has no way to discover that; better not to start than to start wrong. Rejected:
**warn loudly and launch anyway** (never blocks the fleet, but the warning scrolls past in start-up
output, which is exactly where nobody reads it) and **refuse for implementers, warn for the
interactive roles** (matches who can actually react, at the cost of two behaviours to remember).

**Q2 — whether to update the submodule too.** Chosen: **yes, to the tracked pin.** It is the file the
skills are read from, and the pin is recorded in the commit just fast-forwarded to, so this completes
that move rather than making a new decision — and `ah-gdp` is a sighting where the branch was current
and the *pin* was behind. Refuse rather than write if the submodule itself is dirty. Rejected:
fetching the branch only and reporting a stale pin, which leaves `ah-gdp`'s failure exactly as it is.

**Decided here, not asked, as tooling:** that untracked files never block (grounded — the consumer
carries one today, and blocking on it would refuse every launch); that a failed fetch is not a
failure, because being offline is not a staleness this can fix; `--ff-only` rather than `pull`; and
placing the check before the agent-file check so a stale submodule stops being an error at all.

## Out of scope

- **`tests/launchers.sh`'s own problems** — that it asserts against the real machine and writes to
  it. That is `ah-dy4x`, P1, and this bead deliberately does not build on it.
- **Worktrees.** `prepare-worktree` already does this job for a bead worktree; the main checkout is
  the tree that never got the same owner. Nothing about worktrees changes.
- **Keeping a *running* session current.** This is a start-up check. A session already running when
  `main` moves is unaffected, and making it otherwise would mean reloading instructions mid-flight.
- **Any change to `CLAUDE.md` or the skills themselves**, which would be a workflow change and the
  navigator's.
- **The `.cerebro/models.conf` mismatch** `ah-dy4x` names. Different bead.
- **Auto-pushing or auto-committing anything.** The launcher fast-forwards and updates a submodule
  pin; it never creates a commit.

## Validation

```bash
cd .claude/cerebro && bash tests/launch-preflight.sh     # the new suite
for t in tests/*.sh; do bash "$t"; done                  # the rest, still green
```

Then by hand, and **step 3 is the one that actually proves the bead**:

1. **The refusal.** In the consumer, `touch` a tracked file so the tree is dirty, then run
   `.claude/cerebro/scripts/run-planner`. It must refuse with one line naming the uncommitted
   changes, and **`git status` must show your edit exactly as it was**. Revert.
2. **The branch case.** `git switch -c wip`, launch, see it refused naming the branch, `git switch
   main`.
3. **The real thing.** Put the consumer deliberately behind — it is 28 commits behind as this is
   written, so this may need no setup at all — and start a session. It should come up current: check
   `git rev-parse HEAD` equals `origin/main`, and `git submodule status` shows the pin that commit
   records. **Then ask the session what its `CLAUDE.md` says about something recently changed**, and
   confirm it is the new text.
4. **Untracked files survive.** With `.claude/agents/reviewer.md` still untracked, launch. It must
   still be there afterwards, and must not have blocked anything.
5. **Offline.** Disconnect and launch. It must start, not refuse.

## Known traps

- **This is a change to a different repository.** `launch-preflight` is in `rmstdope/cerebro`, a
  submodule with its own remote, CI and tests. Editing it from an `atlantis-hud` branch changes a
  checked-out submodule and delivers nothing. Two PRs: the change in cerebro, then the pin bump here.
- **`--untracked-files=no` is not optional.** The consumer carries an untracked file today; without
  the flag this refuses every launch, which is a far worse failure than the one being fixed.
- **A failed fetch must not refuse.** Offline is not staleness. `|| true`, and treat an empty
  `origin/main` as "nothing known to be stale".
- **`merge --ff-only`, never `pull`.** `pull` can merge or rebase and can leave a commit — or a
  conflict — in the navigator's checkout, which is precisely the thing this bead promises not to do.
- **The check goes before the agent-file check**, not after. A stale submodule is why that check
  fires; running afterwards means refusing with the old message on exactly the case now fixable.
- **The submodule can be dirty**, and often is while cerebro itself is being worked on — including
  while building this bead. Refuse rather than clobber.
- **`tests/launchers.sh` runs the real launchers against the real checkout until `ah-dy4x` lands**,
  and this bead is ordered behind it for that reason. If the order has somehow been reversed, do not
  run `tests/launchers.sh` while validating: with this change in place it would fetch and
  fast-forward the navigator's working tree. Do not add cases to it either way.
- **`consumer-root` resolves the *enclosing* tree; `--shared` resolves the main one.** The preflight
  already uses the plain form and that is right here — it is the tree the session will read from.
- **The eight test cases each need their own temp consumer.** Reusing one across cases leaks the
  fast-forward from an earlier case into a later one, and the failure looks like a logic bug.
acceptance_criteria: launch-preflight brings the shared checkout current before the checks that depend on it: it fetches origin/main, and when HEAD is already origin/main it proceeds, when the checkout is on main with no tracked changes and is strictly behind it fast-forwards with merge --ff-only and then runs git submodule update --init --recursive, and in every other case it refuses with exit 2 and one line on stderr naming what is wrong and the command that fixes it - matching the script's existing convention. Untracked files never block a launch, asserted by a test, because the consumer carries one today. A failed fetch is not a failure: offline starts normally. A dirty or diverged checkout, a checkout on another branch, and a submodule with tracked changes are each refused with the working tree left byte-identical, asserted by tests that check the tree afterwards and not only the exit code. Standalone clones are unaffected. The new check runs before the agent-file check, so a stale submodule stops being an error. Covered by a new tests/launch-preflight.sh in the cerebro repository, hermetic in the manner of tests/consumer-root.sh - a throwaway consumer under mktemp -d, nothing asserted about the enclosing machine - and NOT by extending tests/launchers.sh, which is ah-dy4x. Delivered as two pull requests: the change and its test in rmstdope/cerebro, then a submodule pin bump in atlantis-hud. Verified by hand by starting a real session from a deliberately stale checkout and confirming it comes up on origin/main with the recorded pin.

title: The ruleset scraper can misread the page and its own tests stay green
description:
## The cost being paid

`packages/ruleset/src/data.ts` is a hand-rolled regex parser over a scraped HTML page whose grammar
is asserted in prose. The package's own suite cannot catch a misread of that grammar, because
`committed.test.ts` asserts that `config/public/ruleset.json` equals what the scraper produces from
the committed fixture — which is true by construction whenever the parser is wrong and the JSON was
regenerated from it. Its own doc comment names what it catches: "A hand edit, or a scraper change
nobody regenerated after." A *wrong* scraper change that *was* regenerated passes.

Two consecutive beads on this module each shipped a wrong `config/public/ruleset.json`, and neither
was caught by the package. One was caught by two unrelated Rust tests, the other by a human reviewer.

## Evidence

- docs/retrospectives/ah-9js.md §"The plan's parser rule and the plan's expected result disagreed, and only the Rust suite said so" (commit a262d59, PR #401): "Implemented literally, the rule produces 58 entries... **Nothing in the TypeScript suite objected — the parser tests I wrote from the plan all passed.** Two pre-existing Rust tests... failed." Cost: "About twenty minutes: one wrong implementation, **one regeneration of `config/public/ruleset.json`**, one round of test edits."
- docs/retrospectives/ah-6qp.md §"The plan measured the page's grammar and got it wrong, and I coded the measurement rather than the page" (commit 72c6cb8, PR #412): the `" and "` split "silently dropped the middle requirement" of two three-requirement sentences. "The Copilot review found it... and pointed out that **the regenerated `config/public/ruleset.json` was wrong too**." And: "**My own check while building reproduced the same number the same way, which read as confirmation rather than as the same mistake twice.**" Cost: one review round and one extra CI cycle, roughly 20 minutes.
- ah-6qp's own Seen before names ah-3ej as "same file, previous bead" and the same shape.
- The construct that cost ah-6qp is still live one function away: `packages/ruleset/src/data.ts` `readCastCost` splits a cast-cost list on `" and "`, the exact grammar assumption the requirement parser was rewritten to remove.

## Where

- `packages/ruleset/src/data.ts` — ~673 lines, roughly 20 regex grammar claims about the page.
- `packages/ruleset/src/committed.test.ts` — the tautological check described above.
- `packages/ruleset/src/data.test.ts` — parser tests written from the same assumption as the parser.
- `tests/fixtures/ruleset/neworigins-data.html`, `config/public/ruleset.json`.

## What a refactoring would change

The seam is a check that reads the *fixture page* rather than the parser's assumptions. For each
field the scraper claims to read, count the page's own marker phrase — "This skill requires", "via
magic at a cost of", "provides defense to the first" — and assert the parsed catalogue carries
exactly that many entries, none of them empty. That turns "my grammar is right" from prose into a
test that fails the moment the page carries a form the parser does not understand, and it fails
whether or not the JSON was regenerated. Then finish the separator removal ah-6qp started, so every
list parse reads self-delimiting `[TAG] n` pairs out of the sentence and `readCastCost`'s `" and "`
split goes with the rest.

Note for triage: both sightings were the same implementer and both retrospectives blamed the plan
rather than the code, so a reviewer could read this as a planning-discipline cost. The counter is
that the artifact shipped wrong twice and the package's own suite was green both times.
