- **An `AbortController`** held in a ref for the in-flight request, so Cancel and Escape can abort it.
- Pass `onSendOrders`, `canSend` and `sendDisabledReason` to `<AppHeader` (opens at line 2587, the export
  props sit at 2701-2706), and render `<SendOrdersDialog>` beside the existing `<MapExportDialog>` at
  line 2965.

**`apps/web/src/App.tsx` is not touched.** Web passes no `uploadOrders`, so `canSendOrders` is false, so
`onSendOrders` is undefined, so the button never renders.

## Increments

Each opens with the named failing test.

1. **The button appears, and only where it should.**
   `packages/shared/src/workspace/AppHeader.test.tsx` → `"shows no Send button when the shell cannot send"`
   and `"shows a Send button when the shell can"`. Add the three props and the markup. Component tests here
   render to static markup with `renderToStaticMarkup` from `react-dom/server` — follow the existing
   `AppHeader.test.tsx`, not Testing Library.
2. **The button is disabled without a faction header.**
   `AppHeader.test.tsx` → `"disables Send and gives the reason when the orders carry no faction"`. Assert
   `disabled` and the exact `title` string quoted in *User-facing decisions*.
3. **The dialog's resting state.** New `SendOrdersDialog.test.tsx` →
   `"names the faction, the turn and the server, and cannot send an empty password"`. Assert the meta line
   and that the Send control is disabled while the field is empty.
4. **The password rules.** `SendOrdersDialog.test.tsx` →
   `"refuses a password containing a double quote, and says why"`. Uses `passwordIsSendable` from
   `ah-etb0.1`. Assert the exact message.
5. **The three outcome states.** `SendOrdersDialog.test.tsx` → `"reports an acceptance, a refusal and an
   unreachable server, each in its own words"`. Assert all three agreed strings, and that the refusal shows
   the server's own sentence when `reason` is non-null and the fallback when it is null.
6. **The server's report.** `SendOrdersDialog.test.tsx` →
   `"shows the server's report only when it is not the clean one"`. Two cases:
   `serverReport: "No errors found."` renders no report block; anything else renders it.
7. **Wiring, and the flush before the send.** `AppShell` — the send path, the abort controller, the derived
   values, and the dialog rendered. A test that a send flushes the draft before calling the uploader.

## The test plan

**Unit, vitest, co-located** (`<Component>.test.tsx`), rendering to static markup:

| File | Pins |
|---|---|
| `packages/shared/src/workspace/AppHeader.test.tsx` | increments 1 and 2, added to the existing file |
| `packages/shared/src/workspace/SendOrdersDialog.test.tsx` | increments 3-6, new |
| `packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.test.tsx` | increment 7, if a suitable harness exists there; otherwise cover the send path by extracting it as a small pure helper and testing that |

**One security test that must exist**, and it is the point of this bead's review:

- Render the dialog in every phase with a `serverReport` and a `reason` taken from `ah-etb0.1`'s scrubbed
  accepted fixture, and assert the rendered markup contains neither `#atlantis` nor the fixture's password
  token. This is the regression test for the whole feature's one real hazard.

**Browser:** add a case to `tests/smoke/` covering only that the Send button is **absent** in the web
project — cheap, and it pins the decision that web omits the feature. Do not attempt a real upload from
any automated suite.

**Suites to run:** `pnpm run check:fast`, plus `pnpm run test:smoke` because this bead changes the header
strip, which the smoke suite asserts against.

## User-facing decisions

The full interview, in the order it was held. Mockups:
`docs/ui/ah-etb0-placement.html` and `docs/ui/ah-etb0-dialog.html`.

**Placement.** Offered: (A) a Send button of its own, right of `Export ▾`; (B) a fourth item inside the
Export popover, below a divider; (C) a split `Send / ▾` control replacing the Export button.
**Chosen: A.** Rejected B because it costs two clicks every turn for the action you most want to be one,
and hides it behind a menu named for something this is not. Rejected C because it removes the Export button
players know by name and introduces a split-button idiom used nowhere else in this application.

**Whether web shows it.** Offered: hide entirely; show disabled with an explanation; build a proxy so web
works. **Chosen: hide entirely.** The server sends no CORS headers, so a browser could fire the request but
never read the reply. Rejected the disabled control as a permanently dead item in the toolbar; rejected the
proxy as much larger scope with a security question of its own — it would see the password in transit.

**The resting state's wording.** Offered: (A) one plain line, `Green Tide (4) · turn 71 · atlantis-pbem.com`;
(B) three labelled lines, Faction / Turn / Server. **Chosen: A**, for reading at a glance. Rejected B as
three lines of chrome above a one-field form.

**Cancel and Escape while the request is in flight.** Offered: abort the request and close; close and let
it finish unseen; disable both until it resolves. **Chosen: abort and close** — the button says Cancel and
it cancels. Rejected the second outright. Rejected disabling because a hung request would trap the player.
**Consequence the implementer must honour:** an aborted upload may already have reached the server, so the
dialog must not claim anything about what happened. It simply closes.

**After a successful send.** Offered: stay until Close is pressed; close itself after about two seconds;
close at once and confirm in the header. **Chosen: stay until Close.** This is the one irreversible action
in the application and it is worth a click. Rejected the timeout because a player who looked away is left
unsure; rejected the header notification as needing a mechanism this app does not have.

**Orders with no `#atlantis` line.** Offered: disable the Send button and explain on hover; open the dialog
and explain there; both. **Chosen: disable and explain on hover.** You never open a dialog that cannot do
anything.

**Unsaved edits.** Offered: flush the draft first then send; send what is on screen and leave autosave
alone; refuse while edits are unsaved. **Chosen: flush first.** Rejected the third as a control that
flickers out of reach for five seconds after every keystroke.

**A password containing a double quote.** Offered: refuse and say why; send it anyway with the header left
untouched; ignore the case. **Chosen: refuse.** The password is written into `#atlantis <id> "<password>"`
and the format has no escape for a quote.

**The refusal text.** Offered: the server's own sentence with ours as a fallback; always our fixed string.
**Chosen: the server's own sentence**, which stays right when the server rewords things and can explain
refusals nobody anticipated.

**The server's order report.** The server always reports something on a successful upload —
`No errors found.` when the orders are clean, presumably a list when they are not. Offered: show it only
when it is not the clean one; show it always; never show it. **Chosen: only when it is not
`No errors found.`** Rejected always-on as a block of text every turn saying nothing happened. The known
cost, stated and accepted: the test is on the server's exact wording and will silently stop matching if
they reword it — so treat any unrecognised text as worth showing, which is what the rule already does.

**A long report.** Offered: scroll inside a fixed-height box; grow the dialog up to the window height.
**Chosen: scroll in a fixed-height box** (about five lines), so the dialog stays a predictable size and
Close never moves out of reach.

### The strings, verbatim

Approved as mocked. Use these exactly.

| Where | String |
|---|---|
| Header button | `Send` |
| Dialog title and `aria-label` | `Send orders to the server` |
| Meta line | `<factionLabel> · turn <n> · <serverHost>` — e.g. `Green Tide (4) · turn 71 · atlantis-pbem.com` |
| Password field label | `Faction password` |
| Password field placeholder, when empty | `Required` |
| In flight | `Sending orders…` |
| Success | `Orders for turn 71 were accepted by the server.` — the turn number interpolated |
| Server report heading | `The server reported` |
| Refusal, when the server gave a sentence | that sentence, verbatim, from `refusalReason` |
| Refusal, fallback when it did not | `The server refused the orders. Check the faction password and try again.` |
| Unreachable | `Could not reach the server. Your orders were not sent — export them to a file if the turn is due.` |
| Quote in password | `A faction password cannot contain a double quote.` |
| Send button `title` when disabled | `These orders have no #atlantis line, so the server cannot tell which faction they belong to.` |
| Footer buttons | `Cancel` and `Send`; after an outcome, a single `Close` |

Turn number: when `turnNumber` is null, the success line reads
`Orders were accepted by the server.` — the same fallback spirit as `deliverOrdersExport`'s
`orders-turn-unknown.txt` at `exportActions.ts:33`.

### Keyboard, focus and layout

As mocked, section 3 of `docs/ui/ah-etb0-dialog.html`:

- Focus lands in the password field when the dialog opens.
- **Enter** in the field sends, when the field is non-empty and `passwordIsSendable` is true.
- **Escape** closes and discards the typed password; while a request is in flight it aborts it and closes.
- Focus returns to the Send button when the dialog closes.
- Clicking the backdrop closes it, with the same abort behaviour.
- **No global shortcut** for Send — it is not an every-minute action.
- On a narrow window the footer buttons stack, **Send above Cancel**, so the primary action stays nearest
  the field. The header strip already wraps as one unit and the Send button joins that wrapping.
- After an outcome the field is cleared. On a refusal the field keeps focus so the password can simply be
  retyped; on an unreachable server the typed password is kept, since nothing suggests it was wrong.

## Out of scope

- **The sending machinery.** Every function this bead calls comes from `ah-etb0.1`. If something is missing
  there, that is a defect in `ah-etb0.1`, not something to reimplement here.
- **The web build.** No file under `apps/web/` changes.
- **A settings field for the upload address.** It comes from the ruleset; see `ah-etb0.1`.
- **Downloading turn reports**, which the same server offers on the same pattern.
- **Remembering the password**, in any form, for any duration, by any mechanism. Not a "remember for this
  session" checkbox, not a ref, not a variable outside the dialog. This is the bead's hard constraint.
- **Parsing the server's report into structured errors** or linking them to units. It is shown as text.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run check:fast
pnpm run test:smoke
```

Both green.

**Then a person must do this, and only a person can.** Launch the desktop shell, open a game with a real
orders template, and:

1. Confirm **Send is absent** in the web build (`pnpm --filter @atlantis/web run dev`) and **present** in
   the desktop build.
2. With a document that has no `#atlantis` line, confirm Send is greyed and hovering gives the reason.
3. Send with a **deliberately wrong password**. It must report the refusal, showing the server's own
   sentence — *"Faction password is incorrect. Try again or contact the Game Masters on Discord to change
   your password."* — and must **not** claim success. This is the single most important check in the bead;
   both outcomes are `200 OK`, so a mistake here reports a turn as sent when it was not.
4. Send with the **correct password**. It must report acceptance and, since the orders will be clean,
   show no report block.
5. Disconnect the network and send. It must report the unreachable message, not a refusal.

## Known traps

- **The response body carries the faction password in cleartext.** Never render it, log it, or put it in an
  error. Only `refusalReason` and `serverErrorReport` may reach the screen. The security test in *The test
  plan* is what holds this.
- **A 200 is not a success.** Both outcomes are `200 OK` with HTML. `interpretOrdersUploadReply` already
  handles this; do not add any `response.ok` check on top of it.
- **The password must not outlive the dialog.** Keep it in the dialog's own `useState`. Lifting it into
  `AppShell` so the "retry" case is easier would put it in a component that lives for the whole session.
- **Do not log the rejected-promise error on the unreachable path.** An HTTP client's error object can
  carry the response body, and that body has the password in it.
- **WebKit's driver returns `""` for text it considers clipped**, so an assertion that passes in the
  Chromium smoke project can pass while the native shell is broken. Relevant here because the report block
  is a fixed-height scrolling region — assert on its presence and on `textContent`, not on visible text.
- **`ordersExportText(document, template, false)`** — the plain form. Passing `true` sends the
  with-descriptions form, which is for a human reading a file, not for the server to parse.
- **The header strip already wraps.** Adding a fourth control changes where it breaks; check the narrow
  window before merging, and expect the smoke suite's header assertions to need updating rather than
  assuming a failure there is a real regression.
- **Work in a worktree under `.cerebro/worktrees/`**, never the main checkout, per `CLAUDE.md`.

title: Post orders to the game server and understand the reply
description: The sending machinery for ah-etb0, with no control to trigger it yet. Adds an HTTP port to the desktop shell, builds the multipart upload body, substitutes the typed password into the #atlantis header, and interprets the server's HTML reply as accepted or refused. Nothing the player can see changes; ah-etb0.2 adds the Send button and dialog on top of this.
design:
## Context The player exports orders to a file and uploads them to the game server by hand. `ah-etb0` removes that step. This bead is the first half: everything needed to actually put orders on the server and to know what the server said, with **no control anywhere in the interface to trigger it**. `ah-etb0.2`, which is blocked on this one, adds the Send button and the dialog. Nothing a player can see changes when this lands. What lands is a shared, unit-tested pure core plus one new desktop-only port, so `ah-etb0.2` is UI work against an interface that already exists and is proven. **The server protocol is established, not guessed.** It was read off the live page at `https://atlantis-pbem.com/game` and confirmed against two real uploads the navigator performed on 2026-08-18: ``` POST https://atlantis-pbem.com/game/upload-orders Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary= factionId the in-game faction number, e.g. 4 (verified against all 120 faction rows on that page) password the faction password orders the orders document, as a file part ``` No session, no cookie, no CSRF token — it is a plain Bootstrap modal form. **Both outcomes answer `200 OK` with an HTML page**, so the status code cannot distinguish them: | Outcome | Body, observed | |---|---| | Accepted | ~61 KB. Echoes the whole orders document inside a `
` and ends, after the `#end` line, with `No errors found.` No `alert-danger` anywhere. |
| Wrong password | ~6 KB. Contains `
` wrapping `
Faction password is incorrect. Try again or contact the Game Masters on Discord to change your password.
` |

**The success page echoes the password back in cleartext** — the `
` opens with
`#atlantis 42 "tinto2760"`. That is why the response body is treated as secret throughout this
bead: it is never logged, never stored, and never shown to the player except through the two narrow
extractors specified below, neither of which can reach the header line.

**Web is out of scope by decision, not by omission.** `atlantis-pbem.com` sends no
`Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header (verified: a `HEAD` on `https://atlantis-pbem.com/game` returns only
`X-Powered-By`, `Content-Type`, `Content-Length`, `ETag`, `Date`, `Connection`, `Keep-Alive`). A browser
would be allowed to *send* a multipart form post — it is CORS-safelisted, so no preflight — but could
never *read* the reply, so the web build could not tell the player whether the turn went in. The port
below is therefore desktop-only, and its absence is what hides the button in `ah-etb0.2`.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### New — `packages/shared/src/workspace/ordersUpload.ts`

The whole of the pure logic. Everything here is platform-free and unit-tested; nothing in it performs I/O.

```ts
/** One prepared upload, ready for a shell to put on the wire. */
export type OrdersUpload = {
  url: string;
  contentType: string;
  body: string;
};

/** What a shell got back. `body` is secret: it echoes the orders, password and all. */
export type OrdersUploadReply = {
  status: number;
  body: string;
};

/** The desktop shell's HTTP port. Rejects when the request could not be made at all. */
export type OrdersUploader = (upload: OrdersUpload, signal: AbortSignal) => Promise;

/** What the player is told. Never carries the response body. */
export type OrdersUploadOutcome =
  | { kind: "accepted"; serverReport: string | null }
  | { kind: "refused"; reason: string | null }
  | { kind: "unreachable" };

export function ordersUploadBody(
  factionId: string,
  password: string,
  ordersText: string,
  boundary: string
): { contentType: string; body: string };

export function passwordIsSendable(password: string): boolean;

export function interpretOrdersUploadReply(reply: OrdersUploadReply): OrdersUploadOutcome;

export function serverErrorReport(body: string): string | null;

export function refusalReason(body: string): string | null;
```

Behaviour, exactly:

- **`ordersUploadBody`** returns `contentType: \`multipart/form-data; boundary=${boundary}\`` and a body
  of three parts in this order — `factionId`, `password`, `orders` — matching the order the real form
  submits. Line endings are CRLF, as RFC 7578 requires; the `orders` part carries
  `Content-Disposition: form-data; name="orders"; filename="orders.txt"` and
  `Content-Type: text/plain`, and the other two carry `Content-Disposition: form-data; name="…"` only.
  The body ends with the closing delimiter `----\r\n`. The boundary is a parameter rather than
  generated inside, so tests are deterministic; the caller supplies it (see below).
- **`passwordIsSendable`** returns `false` when the password is empty, is only whitespace, or contains a
  double quote. The quote case exists because the password is written back into the `#atlantis` line as
  `#atlantis  ""` and the Atlantis format has no escape for a quote inside it. See
  *User-facing decisions*.
- **`interpretOrdersUploadReply`** — `refused` when `refusalReason(body) !== null` **or** when
  `status >= 400`; `accepted` otherwise, carrying `serverErrorReport(body)`. `unreachable` is never
  produced here: it is what `ah-etb0.2` shows when the `OrdersUploader` promise rejects.
- **`refusalReason`** finds the first `alert-danger` block in the body, takes the text of the first
  `
` inside it, strips tags, decodes `& < > " '`, collapses whitespace, and
  returns it — or `null` when there is no such block. Returns `null` rather than a truncated string if
  the result is empty after stripping.
- **`serverErrorReport`** returns the text of the echoed `
` **after the last `#end` line only**,
  trimmed, or `null` when there is no `
` or nothing follows `#end`. Taking only the tail is what
  keeps the password out of it: the `#atlantis` line is the first line of that block and can never be
  reached by a function that starts after `#end`. It must never be widened to return the whole `
`.

### New — `packages/shared/src/ordersDocument.ts`, one added export

```ts
export function withFactionPassword(document: string, password: string): string;
```

Rewrites the first line that `trim().startsWith("#atlantis")` so it reads `#atlantis  ""`,
keeping the id it already carried and leaving **every other byte of the document untouched** — the same
splice-and-rejoin discipline `writeUnitOrders` uses at `ordersDocument.ts:103-120`. Returns the document
unchanged when there is no such line. It sits in this module because that is where the `#atlantis` line is
already understood; the module doc at `ordersDocument.ts:3-13` states the password "is never surfaced and
never logged", and this function must not break that — it writes the password in, and returns; it does not
read one out.

Reuse `ordersFileFaction` (`packages/shared/src/ordersImport.ts:45`,
`(text: string) => string | null`) for the faction number rather than writing a second parser. Its own doc
already promises it reads only the first token after the keyword and never the password.

### Changed — `packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx`

A fourth injected shell port, following exactly the pattern the file states at lines 211-214 (*"A prop
rather than a Tauri import in here, because `packages/shared` is what makes the two builds identical"*) and
already used for `saveTextFile`, `registerBeforeQuit` and `appUpdate`:

```ts
export function AppShell({
  client,
  platformLabel,
  registerBeforeQuit,
  saveTextFile,
  appUpdate = UNSUPPORTED_UPDATES,
  uploadOrders          // new, optional
}: {
  client: CoreClient;
  platformLabel: string;
  registerBeforeQuit?: RegisterBeforeQuit;
  saveTextFile: TextFileSaver;
  appUpdate?: AppUpdateControl;
  uploadOrders?: OrdersUploader;   // absent on web
})
```

Optional, and **absent on web** — `apps/web/src/App.tsx:14-21` is not touched at all. This bead adds the
prop and nothing that consumes it; `ah-etb0.2` reads it.

### Changed — `packages/shared/src/rulesets.ts`

The upload address belongs to the game, and the game already carries a ruleset
(`GameMetadata.rulesetId`, `packages/core-client/src/index.ts:63-68`), which the player can already change
in Settings → Per game. So:

```ts
export type Ruleset = { id: string; label: string; url: string; ordersUploadUrl: string };

export const RULESETS: readonly Ruleset[] = [
  { id: "neworigins", label: "NewOrigins", url: "/ruleset.json",
    ordersUploadUrl: "https://atlantis-pbem.com/game/upload-orders" }
] as const;
```

`rulesetById(rulesetId)` already exists in the same file and is how the address is resolved. This was
chosen over a new `ordersUploadUrl` field on `GameMetadata`: that field would need a Rust struct change,
a `#[serde(default)]`, and a mirror in `persist_game_snapshot`, and — because the settings UI that would
write it is a later bead — could only ever hold the default. See *User-facing decisions* and *Out of scope*.

### Changed — the desktop shell

- **`apps/desktop/package.json`** — add `"@tauri-apps/plugin-http": "^2"` to `dependencies`, alongside the
  existing `@tauri-apps/plugin-dialog ^2.7.2`, `@tauri-apps/plugin-fs ^2.5.1`, `@tauri-apps/plugin-opener ^2.5.4`.
- **`apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml`** — add `tauri-plugin-http = { version = "2", optional = true }`
  and name it in the `desktop-runtime` feature list, exactly as the other three optional plugins are.
- **`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/`** — register it in the builder chain:
  `.plugin(tauri_plugin_http::init())`, beside the existing `tauri_plugin_dialog` / `tauri_plugin_fs` /
  `tauri_plugin_opener` registrations, under the same `desktop-runtime` cfg gate they use.
- **`apps/desktop/src-tauri/capabilities/default.json`** — a scoped grant, in the object form the file
  already uses for `opener:allow-open-url`:

  ```json
  { "identifier": "http:default", "allow": [{ "url": "https://atlantis-pbem.com/*" }] }
  ```

  Scoped to that host and no wider, for the reason the file's own `description` gives about
  `opener:allow-open-url` — extend that description with a sentence covering this grant, since the file
  documents every permission it holds.
- **`apps/desktop/src/desktopPlugins.ts`** — extend `DesktopPlugins` with the HTTP call, so the Playwright
  `window.__ATLANTIS_DESKTOP_PLUGINS__` stand-in can fake it the way it already fakes `save` and
  `writeTextFile` (bead `ah-9lv`, the reason this seam exists):

  ```ts
  export type DesktopPlugins = {
    save(options: { defaultPath?: string; filters?: { name: string; extensions: string[] }[] }): Promise;
    writeTextFile(path: string, text: string): Promise;
    httpPost(url: string, contentType: string, body: string, signal: AbortSignal): Promise<{ status: number; body: string }>;
  };
  ```

- **New — `apps/desktop/src/uploadOrders.ts`**, mirroring `apps/desktop/src/saveTextFile.ts:48`:

  ```ts
  export function desktopOrdersUploader(plugins: DesktopPlugins | undefined = desktopPlugins()): OrdersUploader;
  ```

  The returned uploader calls `plugins.httpPost(...)` and returns `{ status, body }`. When `plugins` is
  `undefined` it rejects — same shape `desktopTextFileSaver` uses for the no-runtime case.

  The real implementation of `httpPost` inside `desktopPlugins()` uses
  `import { fetch } from "@tauri-apps/plugin-http"` with `method: "POST"`, the `Content-Type` header set
  from `contentType`, the string body, and the `signal` passed straight through. It reads
  `await response.text()`.

- **`apps/desktop/src/App.tsx`** — pass `uploadOrders={desktopOrdersUploader()}` alongside the existing
  `saveTextFile={desktopTextFileSaver()}` at lines 16-24.

**Where state lives:** none of this holds state. The password exists only as an argument, from the moment
`ah-etb0.2` reads it out of an input to the moment the promise settles. Nothing in this bead has a store, a
module-level variable, a cache or a persisted field.

## Increments

Each opens with the named failing test.

1. **The multipart body.** `ordersUpload.test.ts` → `"builds the three parts the server's own form posts, in order"`.
   Write `ordersUploadBody`. Assert the exact bytes for a fixed boundary: three `--` delimiters,
   the three `Content-Disposition` lines, CRLF throughout, closing `----\r\n`.
2. **Password validity.** `ordersUpload.test.ts` → `"a password containing a double quote cannot be sent"`.
   Write `passwordIsSendable`. Cases: `""`, `"   "`, `"secret"`, `'has"quote'`.
3. **The header rewrite.** `ordersDocument.test.ts` → `"writes the typed password into the #atlantis line and changes nothing else"`.
   Write `withFactionPassword`. Reuse the existing `const DOCUMENT` literal at `ordersDocument.test.ts:18`,
   which already opens `'#atlantis 95 "secret"'`. Assert the id survives, the rest of the document is
   byte-identical, and a document with no header comes back unchanged.
4. **Reading the refusal.** `ordersUpload.test.ts` → `"reads the server's own sentence out of an alert-danger page"`.
   Write `refusalReason` against the real 6 KB refusal body, saved as a fixture (see *The test plan*).
5. **Reading the acceptance.** `ordersUpload.test.ts` → `"reports what the server said after #end, and never the echoed password"`.
   Write `serverErrorReport`. Two assertions that matter: it returns `"No errors found."`, and the returned
   string does **not** contain `#atlantis` or the fixture's password.
6. **Deciding the outcome.** `ordersUpload.test.ts` → `"a 200 carrying alert-danger is a refusal, not an acceptance"`.
   Write `interpretOrdersUploadReply`. Cases: the real accepted body at 200 → `accepted`; the real refusal
   body at 200 → `refused` with the sentence; `{ status: 500, body: "" }` → `refused` with `reason: null`.
7. **The port and its desktop implementation.** `apps/desktop/src/uploadOrders.test.ts` →
   `"posts through the shell's http plugin and returns what it answered"`, with a fake `DesktopPlugins`
   exactly as `apps/desktop/src/saveTextFile.test.ts` installs one. Then add the plugin dependency, the
   Cargo entry, the builder registration and the capability grant, and thread `uploadOrders` through
   `AppShell` and `apps/desktop/src/App.tsx`.

Increments 1-6 are pure TypeScript in `packages/shared` and need no toolchain change; 7 is the only one that
touches Rust or Tauri configuration. Doing it last keeps a red-green loop fast for the parts with logic in
them.

## The test plan

**Unit, vitest, co-located beside the source** (`.test.ts`, no `__tests__` folder — the convention
throughout this repository):

| File | Pins |
|---|---|
| `packages/shared/src/workspace/ordersUpload.test.ts` | every case in increments 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 |
| `packages/shared/src/ordersDocument.test.ts` | increment 3, added to the existing file |
| `apps/desktop/src/uploadOrders.test.ts` | increment 7, fake `DesktopPlugins`, including the `undefined` plugins rejection |

**Two fixtures, and they must be scrubbed.** Save the two real response bodies as
`packages/shared/src/workspace/fixtures/upload-accepted.html` and `upload-refused.html`, read with
`readFileSync` in the test. **Before committing them, replace the faction password in the echoed
`#atlantis` line with `REDACTED`** — the real password is in the live bodies and must not enter the
repository. Keep the surrounding structure byte-for-byte otherwise, or the extractors are being tested
against something other than what the server sends. Trim the accepted body's `
` to a few units; its
value is the `#atlantis` line at the top, the `#end` line and the `No errors found.` tail, not its length.

**The security assertions are tests, not review notes.** At least these:

- `serverErrorReport` on the accepted fixture returns a string containing neither `#atlantis` nor the
  fixture's password token.
- `refusalReason` on the refused fixture returns a string containing neither.
- No `OrdersUploadOutcome` variant carries a `body` field — assert structurally, so a later widening of the
  type fails a test rather than leaking silently.

**Suites to run:** `pnpm run check:fast` (lint, typecheck, unit and tooling suites, `cargo fmt --check`,
`cargo clippy`). The browser suites are not needed — nothing in this bead renders anything.

## User-facing decisions

Nothing in this bead is visible to a player, so there is nothing here for a player to decide. Four
decisions taken with the navigator during this interview nevertheless *bind this bead*, because the
functions above implement them; the interview in full, including the choices that produced the dialog,
is recorded on `ah-etb0.2`.

- **Where the upload address lives.** Offered: (a) derive it from the game's ruleset; (b) a real
  `ordersUploadUrl` field on `GameMetadata`, Rust and TypeScript. **Chosen: (a).** The navigator's earlier
  answer had been "a per-game field with no settings UI"; when it was put to them that this yields a field
  nothing can ever write until the settings bead lands, they moved to the ruleset. Rejected (b) for that
  reason. The known weakness, stated and accepted: two games on different servers sharing one ruleset would
  collide.
- **A password containing a double quote.** Offered: refuse and say why; send it anyway with the header
  left alone; ignore the case. **Chosen: refuse.** `passwordIsSendable` is that decision. The wording the
  player sees for it belongs to `ah-etb0.2`, which has it verbatim.
- **The `#atlantis` header on the uploaded copy.** Offered: substitute the typed password into it; post the
  document byte for byte as Export does; strip the password from it. **Chosen: substitute**, because the
  Atlantis engine traditionally authenticates from that line, so a stale or blank header password could
  have the turn rejected after the upload appeared to succeed. Rejected byte-for-byte for that risk, and
  stripping as an unverifiable guess about what the server tolerates. `withFactionPassword` is that
  decision, and **nothing on disk changes** — the substitution is made on a copy, in memory.
- **The refusal text.** Offered: show the server's own sentence with ours as a fallback; always use our
  fixed string. **Chosen: the server's own sentence**, since it stays right when the server changes its
  messages and can explain refusals nobody anticipated. `refusalReason` is that decision.

## Out of scope

- **Any control that triggers a send.** The button, the dialog, the password field, every string a player
  reads — all of that is `ah-etb0.2`, which is blocked on this bead.
- **The web build.** `apps/web/src/App.tsx` is not touched. The port is optional precisely so web omits it.
- **A settings field for the upload address.** Deliberately not built; the address comes from the ruleset.
  A later bead can add a real per-game field and the UI to edit it, when a second server exists to justify
  it.
- **The password already sitting in the saved orders on disk.** The `#atlantis` line in a player's draft
  may hold a real password, written there by the server's own template and stored in the `order_drafts`
  table long before this feature existed. The navigator's decision was to leave it alone here and file a
  separate bead: stripping it would change the byte-for-byte rule that import, export and the editor all
  depend on. That bead is **ah-d7ih**, already filed and unranked; nothing about it is this bead's work.
- **Downloading turn reports.** The same page offers `POST /game/download-report` and
  `/game/download-json-report` on the same faction-id-plus-password pattern. Obvious future work, and not
  this bead.
- **Surfacing the server's order errors in the interface.** `serverErrorReport` extracts them, and
  `ah-etb0.2` displays them. This bead only has to return the string.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run check:fast
```

Everything green. That covers lint, typecheck (`pnpm -r run typecheck` plus `cargo check --workspace`),
the vitest suites and `cargo fmt --check` / `cargo clippy` — which is what will catch a malformed
`Cargo.toml` feature list or an unregistered plugin.

Then, because increment 7 changes Tauri configuration that no unit test exercises:

```bash
pnpm --filter @atlantis/desktop run tauri build --debug
```

It must build. A capabilities file that names a permission the plugin does not provide fails **here**, at
build time, not at runtime — so skipping this check means shipping a shell that cannot start.

**Not checkable by a person in this bead**, and deliberately so: there is no way to trigger a send, so
nobody can watch one happen. Verification of the real round trip belongs to `ah-etb0.2`. Do not add a
temporary button to try it out.

## Known traps

- **The response body contains the faction password in cleartext.** The accepted page echoes the whole
  orders document, `#atlantis  ""` first line and all. Never `console.log` a reply, never put
  one in an `Error` message, never store one, and never widen `serverErrorReport` to return the whole
  `
`. `deliverOrdersExport` at `exportActions.ts:33-39` logs its failures with `console.error` — do
  **not** copy that pattern here; it is safe there only because the thing being logged is a file-save
  error.
- **A 200 does not mean it worked.** Both outcomes are `200 OK` with `Content-Type: text/html`. Any code
  path that treats `response.ok` as success is wrong, and it fails in the worst direction: a player told
  their turn was sent when the password was refused.
- **`@tauri-apps/plugin-http` must not be imported from `packages/shared`.** `AppShell.tsx:211-214` states
  the rule: reaching for a Tauri import from shared code puts half a desktop in the web bundle. The import
  lives in `apps/desktop/src/desktopPlugins.ts` and nowhere else.
- **Do not build the body with `FormData`.** It would delegate the multipart encoding to whatever the
  plugin does with a `Request` body, which is unverified here and untestable in a unit test. The hand-built
  string is deterministic, and increment 1 pins it byte for byte.
- **The boundary must not occur in the orders text.** Generate it in the desktop shell as
  `----atlantis-hud-${crypto.randomUUID()}` and pass it in. A UUID makes collision impossible in practice,
  and passing it as a parameter is what makes increment 1's assertions exact.
- **The scoped capability is a URL prefix, not a host.** `{ "url": "https://atlantis-pbem.com/*" }`. Getting
  this wrong produces a runtime rejection from the ACL that reads like a network failure, which is the
  hardest kind of bug to place.
- **`bd` and cargo find configuration by walking up.** Work in a worktree under `.cerebro/worktrees/`, as
  `CLAUDE.md` requires; a worktree outside the repository gets its own empty bead database and its own
  multi-gigabyte target directory.

title: Send orders to the game server without leaving the app
description:
Orders can be exported to a file, which the player then sends to the server themselves. Add a Send
button next to Export that posts the orders straight to the game server. For New Origins that is
`https://atlantis-pbem.com/game`.

**The password is asked for at send time and MUST NEVER be stored in persistent storage at any
time.** Not in settings, not in the game workspace, not in a keychain, not in a log line, not in an
error message, not in a crash report. It is held only for the duration of the request.

What exists today:

- `packages/shared/src/workspace/exportActions.ts` - `deliverOrdersExport` builds the orders text and
  hands it to a `TextFileSaver`. The Send path wants the same text and a different delivery.
- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/capabilities/default.json:11` allows HTTP to
  `https://github.com/rmstdope/atlantis-hud/*` only, so the desktop build needs the game host added
  to that allowlist. There is no HTTP client in the Rust core.

Things the planner must settle, the first two before anything else:

- **How the server actually accepts orders.** The URL is a page, not a documented endpoint - whether
  it takes a form post, a file upload, a login session first, and what a success and a failure look
  like. This has to be established against the real server before the rest of the design means
  anything.
- **The web build.** A browser posting to another origin needs that server to allow it, which it
  very likely does not. The feature may be desktop-only, or may need a proxy. Whether the button is
  hidden or disabled on web.
- **Where the password comes from, and the interaction with the orders document.**
  `packages/shared/src/ordersDocument.ts:12` notes the `#atlantis` line carries the faction
  password, the document is preserved byte for byte, and the document is saved with the game
  (`AppShell.tsx:2165`). So a player whose orders file has a real password in its header may already
  have it on disk. Whether Send takes the password from the prompt and substitutes it into the
  header it posts, and whether anything should be done about the stored one, is part of this bead.
- **Per-game server address.** New Origins is one game; the URL belongs with the game rather than
  hard-coded.
- What Send does about unsaved edits, and what the player sees while it is in flight and after it
  succeeds or fails.
acceptance_criteria: A Send button next to Export posts the current orders to the game server, asking for the password each time. The password is never written to persistent storage of any kind, never logged, and never included in an error message - and a test pins this. The player is told clearly whether the send succeeded or failed, and a failure says why. The server address is configured per game rather than hard-coded.
close_reason: All children closed; last was ah-etb0.2, delivered in PR #434

title: Warn when a BUILD order has nothing to build
description:
A unit with the Building skill can write `BUILD` or `BUILD COMPLETE` while it is not inside a
structure. Neither form names what to build, so both only make sense for a unit that is already in
the structure it is working on - from outside, the order does nothing and the month is wasted. The
other forms (`BUILD <name>`, `BUILD <name> COMPLETE`, `BUILD HELP <unit>`) each say what to work on
and are fine from outside.

This should be a warning, not an error: the report is a snapshot, and a unit that enters a structure
earlier in the same month may be inside by the time the order runs.

Both pieces already exist:

- `crates/core/src/orders/intents.rs:271` parses the BUILD forms. The bare form and the `COMPLETE`
  form both yield `Intent::Build { founding: None, helping: None }`, which is exactly the pair to
  warn on - the other forms carry a `founding` or a `helping`.
- `crates/core/src/report/model.rs:159` has `pub structure_id: Option<String>`, documented as "Set
  when the unit sits inside a structure". `None` is the outside case.

So the rule is: warn when `Intent::Build` has neither `founding` nor `helping` and the unit's
`structure_id` is `None`.

For the planner:

- Whether the entering-a-structure case (`ENTER` earlier in the same month's orders) should suppress
  the warning, or whether the warning is worth having even then.
- Which warning category this joins, and whether it belongs behind one of the warning toggles.
design:
## Context

A unit with the Building skill can write `BUILD` or `BUILD COMPLETE` while standing in no structure
at all. Neither form names what to work on, so from outside the order does nothing and the unit's
whole month is spent for nothing. The same waste happens a second way: `BUILD HELP 4021` when 4021
is one of our own units that has no BUILD order of its own — there is nothing to help with, so the
helper's month goes too.

Both are warnings rather than errors: the report is a snapshot, and the orders can move a unit
before the BUILD runs.

**This is the sibling of `ah-90w`, which is merged.** That bead landed everything this one builds
on — the `Intent::Build { founding, helping }` shape (`intents.rs:90-101`), the `check_building`
function, `structure_after_orders`, and the **Building** group in the Warnings tab. It deliberately
went silent on a unit in no structure, calling that in its own plan *"a different mistake and not
this bead's"* — `semantics.rs:1408-1410` is the `continue` where it does so. This bead is that
different mistake.

**The bead grew by one check during the interview.** Its filed acceptance criteria said the HELP
forms raise nothing "whether or not the unit is inside a structure". The navigator kept that for the
*outside-a-structure* rule but added a second, different rule about HELP: warn when the helped unit
is one of ours and is not building at all. The acceptance criteria below supersede the filed ones.

Branch from `origin/main`; every line number here is that tree.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### Two new codes — `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`

Append to `mod codes` (`:73-124`), beside `ALREADY_BUILT` at `:91`:

```rust
    pub const BUILD_OUTSIDE_STRUCTURE: Code = Code("build-outside-structure");
    pub const BUILD_HELP_NOT_BUILDING: Code = Code("build-help-not-building");
```

and append both to `ALL`, **last, in that order**, bumping its length: `pub const ALL: [Code; 20]`
(`:104`) becomes `[Code; 22]`. The array's own doc comment (`:97-103`) states the rule this follows:
new-*here*-last regardless of where the codes land in the settings UI, because the generated
TypeScript copies this array's order.

### Two new checks — `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`

**Two functions, not one, and not an extension of `check_building`.** `check_building` early-returns
on `!options.emits(codes::ALREADY_BUILT)` at `:1374`, so anything hosted inside it would be silently
switched off by the *"Building what is built"* toggle. Each check gates on its own code. (Navigator
confirmed, round two.)

Register both in `check_turn`'s per-hex call list (`:221-232`), immediately after the existing
`check_building(&hex, &options, &mut findings);` at `:226`:

```rust
        check_building_outside(&hex, &options, &mut findings);
        check_build_help(&hex, &options, &mut findings);
```

Findings are sorted within the hex by line afterwards (`:237`), so the call order does not decide the
displayed order.

#### `check_building_outside`

```rust
/// Every own unit whose bare `BUILD` or `BUILD COMPLETE` is written from inside no structure at
/// all. Neither form names what to work on, so from outside the order does nothing.
fn check_building_outside(hex: &Hex<'_>, options: &CheckOptions, findings: &mut Vec<Finding>)
```

For each `ordered` in `hex.units` (own units only — `Hex::read` filters `unit.own`, `:286`):

1. The **first** `Intent::Build` in the block, exactly as `check_building` does at `:1379-1385`
   (`ordered.intents.iter().find(...)`); none, `continue`. One warning per unit, on the first BUILD —
   navigator confirmed.
2. `founding.is_some()` → `continue`. `BUILD Tower` names what to found and is fine from outside.
3. `helping.is_some()` → `continue`. The HELP forms name whose structure to work on; they are the
   other check's business, and they are silent here whether or not either unit is in a structure.
4. `structure_after_orders(ordered)` (`:1656`) — `Some(_)` → `continue`; `None` → warn.
5. `findings.push(ordered.finding(hex, codes::BUILD_OUTSIDE_STRUCTURE,
   "is in no structure to build in".to_string(), Some(placed)))`.

The message is a fixed string — it names nothing variable — but it is still built at the point of
emission like every other one, and it carries no trailing full stop and no leading capital, matching
`"Soggy Saw Mill is already finished"` (`:1426`).

**Step 4 is the whole of the ENTER/LEAVE behaviour, and it is deliberate.** `structure_after_orders`
answers "what is this unit standing in when its orders happen", and its doc comment (`:1640-1656`)
says every such check wants it rather than `unit.structure_id`. So `ENTER 4` then `BUILD` is silent —
the unit is inside 4 by the time BUILD runs, which is the normal correct way to write it — and
`LEAVE` then `BUILD` warns even though the report shows the unit safely inside a structure. **The
navigator was shown that consequence and accepted it**; the two cannot be separated, since reading
`unit.structure_id` instead would warn on the common `ENTER`/`BUILD` pattern.

#### `check_build_help`

```rust
/// Every own unit whose `BUILD HELP` names one of our own units in this hex that has no BUILD
/// order of its own. There is nothing to help with, so the helper's month is spent for nothing.
fn check_build_help(hex: &Hex<'_>, options: &CheckOptions, findings: &mut Vec<Finding>)
```

For each `ordered` in `hex.units`:

1. The first `Intent::Build` in the block; none, `continue`.
2. `helping` is `Some(Party::Unit(id))` — anything else (`None`, `Party::New`, `Party::Foreign`,
   `Party::Discard`) → `continue`. `Party` is `crates/core/src/orders/forms.rs:43-52`; the same
   match `check_building` uses at `:1397-1406`.
3. `hex.find(id)` (`:299`) — `None` → `continue`. A unit the report does not show in this hex, or
   one forming this month with no number yet, cannot be judged. `hex.units` holds own units only, so
   this also enforces "one of our own units".
4. Does the helped unit build? `helped.intents.iter().any(|placed| matches!(placed.intent,
   Intent::Build { .. }))` — `true` → `continue`. **Any** BUILD counts, `BUILD Tower` included:
   founding is building, so there is work to help with. Whether that unit's own BUILD is any good is
   judged on that unit's own line, by `check_building` or by `check_building_outside`.
5. `false` → warn: `format!("unit {id} is not building")`, pushed with
   `ordered.finding(hex, codes::BUILD_HELP_NOT_BUILDING, message, Some(placed))`.

**One mistake is marked once, where it was made.** A helper whose target *is* building but is
itself in no structure stays silent — the target's own line carries that warning. Navigator chose
this over marking every helper, explicitly accepting that it differs from `ah-90w`'s helper
behaviour: six units helping one builder produce one warning here, not seven.

### The settings tab — `packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.tsx`

Two entries appended to the existing **Building** group (`:437-446`, which today holds only
`already-built` at `:443-447`), keeping its `heading: "Building"` unchanged:

```tsx
      {
        code: "build-outside-structure",
        title: "Building outside a structure",
        description: "A bare BUILD or BUILD COMPLETE by a unit that is in no structure."
      },
      {
        code: "build-help-not-building",
        title: "Helping a unit that is not building",
        description: "A BUILD HELP naming a unit with no BUILD order of its own."
      }
```

All four strings are the navigator's, chosen as drawn in the mockup. **Two toggles, not one** — two
genuinely different mistakes, each switchable alone, as every other group in the tab does it.

**Nothing to change in `settingsStore.ts`.** `DEFAULT_ADVISORY_CHECKS`
(`packages/shared/src/settingsStore.ts:26-35`) derives its defaults as `code !== "hex-unguarded"`, so
both new codes are **on by default** with no edit. `reconcileAdvisoryChecks` (`:42`) folds them into
settings saved before this bead. Nor is there anything to change at the two call sites that compute
the disabled list, `AppShell.tsx:1902` and `:2079` — both filter over `ADVISORY_CHECK_CODES`.

### The generated vocabulary

`packages/core-client/src/coreVocabulary.generated.ts` mirrors `codes::ALL` (`ADVISORY_CHECK_CODES`,
`:5-25`). Regenerate rather than hand-edit:

```bash
ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test generated_ts
```

## Increments

1. **A BUILD from nowhere warns.**
   RED: `semantics.rs` tests — `a_bare_build_outside_any_structure_warns`, a hex with one own unit
   whose `structure_id` is `None` ordering `BUILD`, expecting one finding with code
   `build-outside-structure`, `unit_id` `Some("4021")`, `line` `Some(2)` and message
   `is in no structure to build in`. Fails: no such code, no such check.
   GREEN: `codes::BUILD_OUTSIDE_STRUCTURE`, `ALL` at `[Code; 21]`, `check_building_outside`, and its
   call in `check_turn`.

2. **BUILD COMPLETE is the same mistake, and the named forms are not.**
   RED: `build_complete_outside_any_structure_warns`, `founding_a_structure_from_outside_is_silent`
   (`BUILD Tower`), `a_unit_inside_a_structure_is_not_told_it_is_outside` (`in_structure(unit("4021"),
   "1")` with an unfinished building, ordering `BUILD`), and
   `a_foreign_unit_building_outside_is_not_warned_about`,
   `a_build_help_is_not_told_it_is_outside_a_structure` (`BUILD HELP 4021` from outside → nothing
   from this check, whatever `check_build_help` later says), and
   `only_the_first_build_in_a_block_is_warned_about` (a block with two bare `BUILD` lines → one
   finding, on line 2).
   GREEN: the `founding.is_some()`, `helping.is_some()` and `structure_after_orders` branches, and
   the `.find(...)` that takes only the first intent. `BUILD COMPLETE` needs no code of its own —
   `intents.rs:271-274` already gives it `founding: None, helping: None`.

3. **ENTER and LEAVE decide where the unit is.**
   RED: `a_unit_that_enters_a_structure_this_month_is_not_told_it_is_outside` (`ENTER 1` then
   `BUILD`, unit outside per the report → silent) and
   `a_unit_that_leaves_its_structure_this_month_is_told_it_is_outside` (`LEAVE` then `BUILD`, unit
   inside per the report → warns). The second is the navigator's accepted consequence and must be
   pinned, or a later reader will "fix" it.
   GREEN: nothing, if increment 1 used `structure_after_orders`. If either fails, that is the bug
   this increment exists to catch.

4. **Helping somebody who is not building.**
   RED: `helping_a_unit_that_is_not_building_warns` — a hex with own units 4021 (ordering `WORK`)
   and 4117 (ordering `BUILD HELP 4021`), expecting exactly one finding, on 4117, code
   `build-help-not-building`, message `unit 4021 is not building`.
   GREEN: `codes::BUILD_HELP_NOT_BUILDING`, `ALL` at `[Code; 22]`, `check_build_help`, and its call.

5. **Every silence the HELP check owes.**
   RED: `helping_a_unit_that_is_building_is_silent`, `helping_a_unit_that_is_founding_is_silent`
   (`BUILD Tower`), `helping_a_unit_not_in_this_hex_is_silent` (`BUILD HELP 9999`),
   `helping_a_new_unit_is_silent` (`BUILD HELP NEW 1`),
   `a_helper_whose_target_builds_from_outside_is_not_warned_too` — the double-marking case: 4021
   outside a structure ordering `BUILD`, 4117 ordering `BUILD HELP 4021`, expecting exactly **one**
   finding, on 4021.
   GREEN: the `Party` match and the `any(Intent::Build)` branch.

6. **Both toggles switch their own check off, and only their own.**
   RED: `the_build_outside_check_can_be_turned_off` and `the_build_help_check_can_be_turned_off`,
   using the existing `disabling(code)` helper (`:4775`); plus the disable table these tests sit
   beside gaining a row for each code.
   GREEN: nothing, if the gates were written as specified. This pins that neither check hid behind
   `ALREADY_BUILT`'s gate.

7. **The vocabulary and the tab.**
   RED: `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test generated_ts` fails
   (`core_client_vocabulary_matches_the_core`, `generated_ts.rs:52`), and
   `SettingsDialog.test.tsx`'s first case fails on its hard-coded `titles` array.
   GREEN: regenerate the vocabulary; add the two `WARNING_GROUPS` entries; add both titles to the
   `titles` array at `SettingsDialog.test.tsx:67-85`, positioned to match the rendered order.

## The test plan

**Rust — `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`, `mod tests` at `:2292`.** Naming convention is a
full sentence in snake_case with no `test_` prefix. Reuse the existing fixtures rather than writing
new ones: `region(units)` `:2305`, `unit(id)` `:2327`, `in_structure(unit, id)` `:3963`,
`unfinished_building(id)` `:3954`, `finished_mill(id)` `:3931`; drivers `check(regions, orders)`
`:2430`, `only(findings)` `:2472`, `codes(&findings)` `:2455`, `disabling(code)` `:4775`. A unit is
outside a structure by default — `unit(id)` leaves `structure_id` as `None` — so the warning case
needs no fixture at all beyond `region(vec![unit("4021")])`.

| Test | Pins |
|---|---|
| `a_bare_build_outside_any_structure_warns` | code, unit, line 2, `is in no structure to build in` |
| `build_complete_outside_any_structure_warns` | `BUILD COMPLETE` is the same mistake |
| `founding_a_structure_from_outside_is_silent` | `BUILD Tower` → nothing |
| `a_unit_inside_a_structure_is_not_told_it_is_outside` | the ordinary correct case |
