   --test corpus_errors` then passes. Read the table: if a row looks like a wrapped-line fragment
   or a unit name survived, `normalise` is wrong — fix it, regenerate.
3. **The findings and the beads.** README as above, then the beads, then their ids into the README.
4. `pnpm run check:fast` (the new test runs inside `cargo test`; `cargo clippy --all-targets`
   sees the file — `-D warnings`, so no dead code).

## The test plan

- `crates/core/tests/corpus_errors.rs`: `normalise` ×5; `corpus_error_table_matches_the_corpus`
  (the gate — it is what makes the table trustworthy next year).
- No TypeScript, no browser suite. `pnpm run check:fast`.
- The classification is reviewed by reading: the PR body links `docs/order-checks/README.md`, and
  Copilot's review is the second pair of eyes as for any bead.

## User-facing decisions

None. Documents and beads; nothing a player sees changes.

## Out of scope

- Building any check. Every check is its own bead, filed here at P4 and ranked by the navigator.
- Reading `Events during turn` (`header.events`) — events are what happened, not what was refused;
  if a refusal turns out to live there in some fixture, note it in the README and leave it.
- Any change to the parser or the fixtures crate.
- Extending the corpus.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test corpus_errors
pnpm run check:fast
test -s docs/order-checks/corpus-errors.generated.md && test -s docs/order-checks/README.md
bd list --status open --json | jq -r '.[] | select(.dependencies // [] | any(.depends_on_id=="ah-v25")) | .id'   # the filed beads
```

And a read: every generated-table row has a README row with a group, a reason and a `Covered by`
entry that is a code, a bead id, a source or `—`.

## Known traps

- **Grep is wrong here.** The report wraps at ~70 columns; only the parser's `header.errors` gives
  whole messages. The sample in *Context* came from grep and double-counts the wrapped `MOVE`
  message for exactly that reason.
- **The gate fails on a fresh corpus, by design.** Adding a fixture later means regenerating; the
  failure message says how. Do not weaken the assertion to a subset check.
- **Numbers become `N` — but not the unit id in the prefix**, which is stripped, not replaced. If a
  message keeps a `(N)` that is a *target*, that is right (`Nonexistant target (N)`).
- **`-D warnings` on `--all-targets`**: `Tally` and `normalise` are used by the test; a helper you
  write and stop using fails clippy.
- **`bd create` defaults to P2.** `-p 4`, explicitly, on every bead. And `bd dolt push` after,
  or the beads exist only on this machine.
- **Do not classify by how easy the check is to build.** The groups are about whether the
  information existed on the player's screen; difficulty goes in the bead's body.
acceptance_criteria: 1) crates/core/tests/corpus_errors.rs exists: normalise (5 unit tests) and the generated/gated table docs/order-checks/corpus-errors.generated.md listing every distinct engine error with order, occurrences, turns, games. 2) docs/order-checks/README.md classifies every row into one of the three groups with a reason and a 'Covered by' (code, bead id, rules source or —), lists the beads filed, the checks whose error never appears, and the messages existing checks already cover. 3) One P4 bead per catchable, uncovered message, related to ah-v25 by bd dep --type relates-to, each with the evidence/what-it-needs/must-not/validation body. 4) pnpm run check:fast green.

title: Item shortfalls count what sharing units in the hex hold, and any unit may borrow, as the engine does
description:
Silver already gets the full treatment: `GIVE` orders inside the hex are credited to the receiving
unit (`silver_given_inside_the_hex_is_credited_to_the_unit_receiving_it`), and units carrying the
`sharing` flag have their purses pooled — added after turn 71, where sixteen units of one fleet each
reported a shortfall for a study the game paid for without complaint.

**Items get neither.** The pooled purse in `semantics.rs` is silver by construction:

    let purse: i64 = sharers.iter().map(|o| balance_of(ledger, &o.unit.unit_id, SILVER)).sum();

`SILVER` is hard-coded, so a hex where one unit holds the herbs and its neighbour is ordered to use
them warns about a shortfall the game will resolve by borrowing, exactly as it used to for silver.

**The request:** `not-enough-items` should count what a unit can actually reach — its own holdings,
what other units in the hex `GIVE` it this turn, and what sharing units in the hex hold.

## What to reuse rather than rebuild

The silver path already establishes the shape and the traps:

- **The ledger** tracks a running balance per unit and tag, so incoming gives are already expressible
  per item — `balance_of(ledger, unit, tag)` takes a tag.
- **`doubted`** exists because a pool is only as trustworthy as its members: if any sharer's own sums
  cannot be trusted, the whole pool is skipped rather than reported wrongly. Items need the same
  restraint.
- **`shares()`** reads the `sharing` flag and needs no change.

A false shortfall is worse than a missed one here. The warning's job is to catch a turn that will not
run as intended; one that cries wolf on every hex with a shared stock trains the navigator to ignore
the panel, which is what the sharing work fixed for silver.

## For the planner to settle with the navigator

- **Which items pool.** Silver is fungible and the flag says "resources"; whether the check treats
  every tag alike, or only consumables, is a rules question worth confirming against the engine.
- Whether a shortfall against a pool should read differently from one against a unit's own holdings
  — "the hex is short" is a different sentence from "this unit is short".

## Validation

A hex where one unit holds a stock, a second is ordered to spend it, and either a `GIVE` or a
`sharing` flag covers it: no warning. The same hex without either: warned. A hex where the pool is
genuinely short: warned once, about the pool.
design:
## Context

Filed by the navigator on 2026-08-16; planned by Beast the same day. Blocks ah-dbb (spell reagents),
which is the second consumer of "what can this unit actually reach".

Today `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` models the `sharing` flag for **silver only**:
`report_shared_purse` (:783) sums the silver of the units that share, and a sharing unit's own
silver shortfall is skipped (:735). Two things are wrong against the game itself, and I checked
them in the engine's source rather than the rules page (which does not describe SHARE at all):

- **Items are never pooled.** `SILVER` is hard-coded into the purse, so a hex where one sharing
  unit holds the swords and its neighbour is ordered to give or sell them warns about a shortfall
  the game will not have. (`GIVE`s inside the hex *are* already credited to the receiver for every
  tag — `transfer` at :488 is tag-generic and `items_given_between_units_in_the_hex_go_round`
  pins it. What is missing is the sharing half.)
- **The borrower need not share.** `Unit::GetSharedNum(item)` in the engine's `unit.cpp` counts
  *the unit itself, plus every unit of the same faction in the region carrying `FLAG_SHARING`* —
  the calling unit's own flag is not consulted. `DoGiveOrder` and `DoSell` (`runorders.cpp`)
  check and consume through it for items, `DoBuy` and `Do1StudyOrder` (`monthorders.cpp`)
  through `GetSharedMoney`, `Run1BuildOrder`/`consume_production_inputs` for materials; the one
  exception is `IT_MAN` (men are never borrowed). So a non-sharing unit studying next to a sharing
  treasurer is paid for by the game and warned about by the HUD — the test
  `a_unit_that_does_not_share_cannot_borrow_from_one_that_does` (:1389) pins the wrong behaviour.

**After this bead** there is one rule for every tag, and it is the engine's: what a unit can reach
is its own balance plus the balances of the units in the hex that share. When a hex has sharers, a
tag's shortfall is judged for the hex as one pool (the sharers' net balances against the overdrafts
of the units that must borrow from them) and reported once, against the hex — because the engine
drains sharers in order, so which borrower "went short" is genuinely undeterminable. When a hex has
no sharers, per-unit findings stay exactly as they are. Silver stops being special: the purse code
becomes the general pooled path, and a non-sharer may draw on it as the engine allows.

The navigator decided the three user-visible points on 2026-08-16 (see *User-facing decisions*).

For ah-dbb: nothing new is needed at the seam — a spell that consumes reagents will `charge()` the
mage's balance for the reagent tag, and this bead's `report_shortfalls` pools it like any item.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` — the only code file

**Delete `report_shared_purse` (:783–826)** and fold its job into `report_shortfalls` (:706), which
becomes:

```rust
fn report_shortfalls(ledger, hex, ruleset, options, findings) {
    // The units whose stock the engine lets everyone in the hex draw on (`FLAG_SHARING`).
    let sharers: Vec<&Ordered<'_>> = hex.units.iter().filter(|o| o.shares()).collect();
    // A pool is only as trustworthy as its members (the existing rule, kept): one doubted sharer
    // silences every pooled tag in the hex.
    let pool_trusted = !sharers.iter().any(|o| ledger.doubted.contains(&o.unit.unit_id));
    // Men are the engine's one exception (`IT_MAN` in GetSharedNum): never borrowed. Without a
    // ruleset every tag pools.
    let pooled = |tag: &str| !sharers.is_empty() && !ruleset.is_some_and(|r| r.is_man(tag));

    // tag → the overdrafts of the units that must borrow it (non-sharers, not doubted, balance < 0)
    let mut claims: BTreeMap<String, i64> = BTreeMap::new();
    // every pooled tag any unit is short of (a sharer's own overdraft is inside the pool sum)
    let mut pooled_tags: BTreeSet<String> = BTreeSet::new();

    for ordered in &hex.units {
        if doubted → continue;
        for (tag, balance) in <this unit's negative balances, the existing range() scan :721–727> {
            if pooled(tag) {
                pooled_tags.insert(tag.clone());
                if !ordered.shares() { *claims.entry(tag.clone()).or_insert(0) += -balance; }
                continue;
            }
            <the existing per-unit finding, :737–768, unchanged except the item verb (below)>
        }
    }

    if !pool_trusted { return; }
    for tag in pooled_tags {
        let code = if tag == SILVER { NOT_ENOUGH_SILVER } else { NOT_ENOUGH_ITEMS };
        if !options.emits(code) { continue; }
        let pool: i64 = sharers.iter().map(|o| balance_of(ledger, &o.unit.unit_id, &tag)).sum();
        let short = claims.get(&tag).copied().unwrap_or(0) - pool;
        if short <= 0 { continue; }
        // What the pool's members and its borrowers actually hold, so the message can say
        // "they can have X and their orders spend Y" the way the per-unit one does.
        let held: i64 = hex.units.iter()
            .filter(|o| o.shares() || (!ledger.doubted.contains(&o.unit.unit_id) && balance_of(ledger, &o.unit.unit_id, &tag) < 0))
            .map(|o| o.holding(&tag)).sum();
        findings.push(hex.finding(code, <message, below>));
    }
}
```

`Ruleset::is_man(tag)` exists (`crates/core/src/movement/rules.rs:540`) and takes the uppercase
tag the ledger keys by. `Hex::finding` (:228, used by the old purse; `Ordered::finding` at :324 is the per-unit form) is unchanged. `Ordered::holding`
(:317) and `balance_of` (:679) are the existing helpers. Delete the `if tag == SILVER && ordered.shares() { continue; }` at :735 —
it is subsumed by `pooled(tag)`. Keep the `range()` scan comment (:721–724).

**Messages** (every string quoted from *User-facing decisions*; the per-unit silver one is unchanged):

- per-unit item (:761–767): `format!("short {short} {name}: this unit can have {} and its orders give away or sell {}", ordered.holding(tag), ordered.holding(tag) + short)`
- hex-level silver: `format!("the units in this hex are short ${short} between them: they can have ${held} and their orders spend ${}", held + short)`
- hex-level item: `format!("the units in this hex are short {short} {name} between them: they can have {held} and their orders give away or sell {}", held + short)` with `name = item_name(&tag, hex, ruleset)` — **change `item_name` (:826) to drop its `ordered` parameter** and search the hex's inventories only (it already chains them after the unit's own); update its one existing caller at the per-unit message.

**Docs in the file:** the module header's "Accept on doubt" paragraph stands. Replace the doc on
`report_shared_purse` (:779–782, "Sixteen units of turn 71…") with a doc on `report_shortfalls`
that says the engine rule (`GetSharedNum`: own + same-faction sharers in the region, borrower's
own flag irrelevant, men excepted) and why the pooled case is reported against the hex. Update
`Ordered::shares`' doc (:305–308) — "puts its stock, silver included, at the disposal of the
others in the hex".

### `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` — tests (`mod tests`, helpers at :1084–1201: `region`, `unit`, `with_silver`, `with_item`, `with_men`, `sharing` (:1369), `check`, `codes`, `only`)

Change:
- `a_unit_that_does_not_share_cannot_borrow_from_one_that_does` (:1389) → rename
  `a_unit_that_does_not_share_may_still_draw_on_one_that_does`; expect `vec![]`; doc: the
  engine's `GetSharedNum` does not consult the borrower's flag.
- `a_shared_purse_that_runs_dry_is_the_hex_s_problem` (:1417): the message assertion becomes
  `finding.message.contains("short $70") && finding.message.contains("the units in this hex")`.
- `a_unit_giving_away_more_of_an_item_than_it_holds_is_warned_about` (:1656): also assert
  `finding.message.contains("give away or sell")`.
- The comment block above `sharing` (:1360–1368) — add the engine reference.

Add, after the sharing tests:
- `a_sharing_unit_s_stock_covers_a_neighbour_that_gives_it_away`: `unit("5")` (no items) and
  `sharing(with_item(unit("7"), 10, "sword", "SWOR"))`; orders `"unit 5\nGIVE 9 10 swords\n"` → `vec![]`.
- `a_sharing_unit_s_stock_covers_a_neighbour_that_sells_it`: same units, region with
  `hex.wanted.push(MarketItem { amount: 20, name: "sword", tag: "SWOR", price: 30 })` (the shape at
  :1512); orders `"unit 5\nSELL 10 swords\n"` → `vec![]`.
- `a_shared_stock_that_runs_dry_is_the_hex_s_problem`: `unit("5")` gives 30 swords, sharer 7 holds
  20 → `only(...)`, code `not-enough-items`, `unit_id == None`, `line == None`, message equals
  `"the units in this hex are short 10 sword between them: they can have 20 and their orders give away or sell 30"`
  (assert the whole string — this is the agreed wording).
- `a_stock_a_unit_keeps_to_itself_is_not_lent`: non-sharer 5 holds 10 swords, non-sharer 7 gives
  10 swords holding none, sharer 9 holds no swords → one `not-enough-items` finding for the hex
  (`unit_id == None`) short 10 — the sharer's empty stock is the pool; 5's swords are not.
- `men_are_never_borrowed_from_a_sharing_unit`: `unit("5")` and `sharing(with_item(unit("7"), 10, "human", "HUMN"))`;
  orders `"unit 5\nGIVE 9 10 HUMN\n"` → `only(...)` is `not-enough-items` **on unit 5**
  (`unit_id == Some("5")`), because `HUMN` is `ItemKind::Man` in the committed ruleset.
- `a_doubted_sharer_silences_the_stock_it_shares`: sharer 7 holds 20 swords and `WITHDRAW 10 grain`
  (doubts it), unit 5 gives 30 swords → `vec![]` (the item twin of
  `a_doubted_unit_silences_the_purse_it_shares`).
- `a_hex_without_sharers_still_reports_each_unit_on_its_own`: two non-sharers each giving swords
  they lack → two `not-enough-items` findings, each with its `unit_id` and `line`.

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.tsx:335`

`description: "Orders give away or sell more of an item than the unit or the hex holds."`
`SettingsDialog.test.tsx` asserts the title "Overdrawn items" (:54) and never the description —
no test change.

### `crates/core-wasm`, `crates/core-tauri`, `packages/core-client` — untouched

`Finding` and the codes are unchanged; only messages and which findings are emitted differ.

## Increments

Rust: `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core semantics`. Each opens with the named failing test.

1. **The item verb.** RED: `a_unit_giving_away_more_of_an_item_than_it_holds_is_warned_about` with
   the added `"give away or sell"` assertion. One string edit.
2. **A non-sharer may draw on sharers (silver).** RED: the renamed
   `a_unit_that_does_not_share_may_still_draw_on_one_that_does` (`vec![]`). Rewrite
   `report_shortfalls` as above (delete `report_shared_purse`); fix
   `a_shared_purse_that_runs_dry_is_the_hex_s_problem`'s message assertion; the other silver
   sharing tests (:1375, :1402, :1440) stay green.
3. **Items pool.** RED, one at a time: `a_sharing_unit_s_stock_covers_a_neighbour_that_gives_it_away`,
   `…_that_sells_it`, `a_shared_stock_that_runs_dry_is_the_hex_s_problem`,
   `a_stock_a_unit_keeps_to_itself_is_not_lent`, `a_doubted_sharer_silences_the_stock_it_shares`,
   `a_hex_without_sharers_still_reports_each_unit_on_its_own`. Most go green with increment 2's
   rewrite; the run-dry one pins the exact wording.
4. **Men are the exception.** RED: `men_are_never_borrowed_from_a_sharing_unit`; add the
   `is_man` clause to `pooled`.
5. **Settings text.** `SettingsDialog.tsx`; `pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared test`.
6. **Gate.** `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --check`;
   `pnpm run check:fast`; `pnpm run check` once. PR
   `feat(ah-j2w): item shortfalls count what sharing units in the hex hold, as the engine does`;
   request `@copilot`; CI green; squash.

## The test plan

- Rust `semantics.rs::tests`: 1 renamed/inverted, 2 assertions tightened, 8 new (increments 1–4).
  Pins: every tag pools; the borrower's own flag is irrelevant; the pool is the sharers only; men
  do not pool; a doubted sharer silences the pool; no sharers → per-unit as before; the exact
  hex-level and per-unit wording.
- TS `SettingsDialog.test.tsx` unchanged (it does not assert the description).
- Suites: `cargo test --workspace`, `pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared test`, `pnpm run check:fast`;
  `pnpm run check` once.

## User-facing decisions

Asked 2026-08-16 (Beast → navigator), all four answered with the recommended option:

1. **Who may borrow.** Follow the engine: any unit of the faction draws on its own holdings plus
   every sharing unit in the hex; the borrower need not share; one rule for silver and items.
   Rejected: keeping today's sharers-only pool for silver — it contradicts `GetSharedNum` and
   keeps a false warning for a unit drawing on a sharing treasurer.
2. **Hex-level wording** when the pool is short — option A, verbatim:
   - silver: `the units in this hex are short $70 between them: they can have $30 and their orders spend $100`
   - items: `the units in this hex are short 12 herbs between them: they can have 20 and their orders give away or sell 32`
     (`herbs` here is the catalogue name — `item_name` — as the per-unit message already uses it;
     no pluralisation logic, the name is printed as the catalogue spells it, e.g. `10 sword`).
   Rejected B: `$70 short in this hex, even borrowing from the 2 sharing units: they can have $30 between them and their orders spend $100`.
3. **Per-unit item verb:** `short 5 herbs: this unit can have 3 and its orders give away or sell 8`
   (was `give away`). Rejected: leaving it, since a SELL also charges the item.
4. **Settings › Warnings › Overdrawn items** description:
   `Orders give away or sell more of an item than the unit or the hex holds.` (was
   `Orders give away more of an item than the unit holds.`). Rejected: leaving it.

Not asked, decided by me as rules facts verified in the engine source: men never pool; a hex-level
finding carries no unit or line (the engine drains sharers in order, so blame is undeterminable —
same reasoning the silver purse already recorded).

## Out of scope

- `GIVE … ALL <item>` by a unit that can borrow: the engine gives the *shared* total
  (`amt = u->GetSharedNum(item)`), the ledger charges only the giver's own balance. A missed
  warning at worst, never a false one; left as is.
- Orders not modelled as intents (BUILD, PRODUCE, CAST reagents — ah-dbb, maintenance).
- Attributing a pooled shortfall to a unit or a line.
- Any change to codes, `CheckOptions`, the wire, or the shell beyond the one settings string.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core semantics
cargo test --workspace
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --check
pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared test
git grep -n 'report_shared_purse' crates   # → nothing
git grep -n 'give away more' packages/shared/src   # → nothing (the settings string is updated)
pnpm run check:fast && pnpm run check
```

Human check (Psylocke): load `g7f95t71` on either shell; unit 14451 (Drones, sharing) and its
neighbours — order a non-sharing unit in the same hex to `GIVE` an item only a sharing unit holds:
no warning; give more than every sharing unit holds together: one warning on the hex, in the
agreed words.

## Known traps

- **`pooled_tags` must be collected before the pool pass and include tags only a sharer is short
  of** (a sharer overdrawn on its own is inside the pool sum with no `claims` entry). The loop
  above inserts the tag for sharers and non-sharers alike; do not key the pool pass on `claims`.
- **A doubted sharer silences the pooled tags but not the men/no-sharer per-unit findings** —
  `return` after the per-unit loop, not before it.
- **The tags in the ledger are uppercase** (`credit`/`charge` uppercase them; `Ruleset::is_man`
  looks up by tag exactly) — pass the ledger's tag through unchanged.
- **`item_name` today takes an `Ordered`** to search that unit's inventory first; a hex-level
  message has no unit. Drop the parameter (search the hex's inventories, which it already chains)
  rather than passing an arbitrary unit.
- **`Ordered::holding` reads the report, `balance_of` reads the ledger** — `held` in the message
  is the former (what they *can have*), `short` comes from the latter; mixing them prints nonsense.
- **The smoke suite rebuilds the web bundle with the service worker disabled**; run `pnpm run check`
  as one command rather than `test:smoke` then `test:pwa` by hand.
acceptance_criteria: A unit ordered to spend items it does not hold is not warned about when another unit in the hex gives it those items this turn, or when a sharing unit in the hex holds them. A hex whose pooled stock is genuinely short is still warned about. Silver's existing behaviour is unchanged.

title: Dropping a file that names no faction is refused and leaves the loaded turn on screen
description:
Found during verification of ah-9gk at 5d6c7a0 (unrelated to that bead's diff).

Loading a report file with no faction id — even a completely empty file — is accepted by the app as a valid (empty) new turn rather than rejected as a failure. gameMemory.ts:147 returns a *warning* ("the report does not name its faction, so it cannot be remembered"), not a rejection, so loadTurn's atomicity guarantee (packages/shared/src/reportLoad.ts) applies it as a successful load: the previously-loaded turn's map and regions are silently replaced by the new, effectively-empty report. The player has to load a different game and reload this one to get their data back — nothing in the UI warns that this is about to happen before it does.

Traced to gameMemory.ts / reportLoadDecision.ts, last touched by ah-u4e.3 (#313), well before ah-9gk. Reproduced with both a plain garbage .txt file and a completely empty file.

Worth considering: should a report with no identifiable faction be a hard failure (nothing applied, old state kept) rather than a warning that still replaces the screen?
design:
## Context

Psylocke found this verifying ah-9gk (unrelated to that diff): drop a file that parses to **no
faction id** — an empty file, "this is not a report", a truncated report — on the single-file
importer and it becomes the working turn. `decideReportLoad`
(`packages/shared/src/reportLoadDecision.ts:80–82`) treats a null incoming faction as "not evidence
of another faction: it just loads"; `commitTurn` (`packages/shared/src/gameMemory.ts:146–148`)
answers the missing faction with a *warning* ("the report does not name its faction, so it cannot
be remembered"); `loadTurn` (`packages/shared/src/reportLoad.ts:82–130`) treats a warning as a
successful load, by design; and `applyLoadedTurn` replaces the map, the regions and the orders
document with an empty report. The player sees eleven regions vanish, an amber line, and no way
back short of switching game and back. Nothing is lost on disk — the stored turn is untouched
because the commit never happened.

The batch importer already does the right thing for the same file: `planReportBatch`
(`packages/shared/src/reportBatch.ts:139–145`) skips a candidate with `factionId === null` with the
reason `"the report does not name its faction"`. The smoke test at
`tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts:437–447` currently pins the *wrong* single-file behaviour ("Junk
parses to a turn that names no faction, which cannot be remembered - a warning the player should
see") and must change with this bead.

**Decided with the navigator (2026-08-16), see *User-facing decisions*:** a single dropped file
whose report names no faction is **rejected** — red status
`could not read <file>: the report does not name its faction`, nothing on screen changes — using
the batch importer's exact reason string, whether or not anything is on screen yet.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `packages/shared/src/reportLoadDecision.ts`

The reason string moves here and both paths read it:

```ts
/**
 * Why a report cannot become the working turn at all. One reason today: a report that names no
 * faction is not a report the application can do anything with - not remembered, not compared,
 * not routed - so it is refused before age or ownership are looked at (ah-brd). The batch importer
 * skips such a file with the same words.
 */
export const REPORT_NAMES_NO_FACTION = "the report does not name its faction";
```

`ReportLoadDecision` (`:26–39`) gains a first variant:

```ts
  /** Cannot become the working turn at all; `reason` is shown to the player as it stands. */
  | { kind: "reject"; reason: string }
```

`decideReportLoad` (`:66+`) checks it **before** `!current` — the file is unusable whatever is on
screen, including nothing:

```ts
export function decideReportLoad(current, incoming): ReportLoadDecision {
  if (incoming.factionId === null) {
    return { kind: "reject", reason: REPORT_NAMES_NO_FACTION };
  }
  if (!current) {
    return { kind: "load" };
  }
  … unchanged …
```

The comment at `:80` ("A report whose faction cannot be read is not evidence of another faction:
it just loads.") now describes only `current.factionId === null` — reword it: "A screen whose
faction cannot be read is not evidence of another faction: the incoming report just loads."
Also update the module doc (`:1–18`) with one sentence naming the rejection and ah-brd.

### `packages/shared/src/reportLoad.ts`

`ReportRoute` (`:222–225`) gains `| { kind: "reject"; reason: string }`; `routeReport` (`:231`)
returns it first:

```ts
  if (decision.kind === "reject") {
    return { kind: "reject", reason: decision.reason };
  }
```

Module doc (`:1–20`): add a sentence after the atomicity paragraph: "One thing *is* a failure and not a
warning since ah-brd: a report that names no faction is refused before anything is committed or
shown (`routeReport` → `reject`)."

### `packages/shared/src/reportBatch.ts:143`

`reason: REPORT_NAMES_NO_FACTION` (import from `./reportLoadDecision`), so the two paths cannot
drift apart again.

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx` — `loadReport` (`:940–975`)

Right after `const route = routeReport(parsed, report, text, fileName);` (`:950`):

```ts
          if (route.kind === "reject") {
            // Thrown rather than reported here, so `runReported`'s `could not read <file>: …`
            // prefix and red status apply exactly as they do to a file that would not parse.
            throw new Error(route.reason);
          }
```

`runReported` (`packages/shared/src/workspace/shellAction.ts:51–66`) turns that into
`setStatus(failedStatus("could not read junk.rep: the report does not name its faction"))` and
releases `busy`. Nothing else in the callback runs, so `setParsed`, the map, the orders document and
the selection are untouched — the guarantee this bead exists for. `flush()` (`:946`) has already
run: the draft is saved, which is right (it belongs to the turn that stays on screen).

### `packages/shared/src/gameMemory.ts:146–148`

Unchanged. `commitTurn`'s own guard becomes unreachable from the working-turn path but stays as
defence for any future caller; add "(unreachable from `loadTurn` since ah-brd — `routeReport`
refuses such a report first)" to its comment.

## Increments

1. **The decision.** RED, `packages/shared/src/reportLoadDecision.test.ts`: new
   `rejects a report that names no faction, whatever is on screen` —
   `decideReportLoad(null, { factionId: null, turnNumber: null })`,
   `decideReportLoad(borgTng, { factionId: null, turnNumber: 71 })` and
   `decideReportLoad(borgTng, { factionId: null, turnNumber: 2 })` (older — rejection wins over
   storeOnly) all equal `{ kind: "reject", reason: "the report does not name its faction" }`; and
   `REPORT_NAMES_NO_FACTION` equals that string. Rewrite the existing
   `does not raise the question over a faction it cannot read` (`:90–99`) to keep only its first
   expectation (current faction null, incoming borg → `load`) and move its two incoming-null
   expectations into the new test as rejects. GREEN: the const, the variant, the branch.

2. **The route.** RED, `packages/shared/src/reportLoad.test.ts` under `describe("routeReport")`
   (`:303`): `rejects a report with no faction and says why` —
   `routeReport(report({ turnNumber: 71 }), report({ factionId: null, factionName: null, turnNumber: null }), "junk", "junk.rep")`
   equals `{ kind: "reject", reason: "the report does not name its faction" }`, and the same with
   `null` as the viewer. The file's `report(overrides)` helper (`:67`) takes
   `Partial<ParsedReport["header"]>`, so `factionId: null` is accepted. GREEN: `ReportRoute` + `routeReport`.

3. **The batch reads the same string.** `packages/shared/src/reportBatch.test.ts:202` and `:281`
   assert the literal `"the report does not name its faction"`; leave those literals as they are
   (they pin the words the player sees) and change `reportBatch.ts:143` to
   `reason: REPORT_NAMES_NO_FACTION`. No RED here — the string is the same; the point is one
   definition. `pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared test` stays green.

4. **The shell.** The `AppShell.tsx` branch above (no unit test — no DOM renderer; the smoke test is
   the test). Update `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts:437–447`: keep the same `junk.rep` drop; the
   assertions become `await expect(status).toContainText("could not read junk.rep: the report does not name its faction")`,
   `await expect(status).toContainText("11 regions")` is *not* right (the status now shows the
   error) — instead assert the screen kept the turn: the region count element / map that
   `loadReport(page)` populated is still there. Use whatever the same file already asserts on after
   `loadReport(page)` at `:432` (`"11 regions"` was read from `import-status`); pick a stable
   on-screen witness of the loaded turn — the unit table or a region in the map list — and assert
   it is still visible after the junk drop, and that the status line's width is `> 1` (it earns its
   room back on failure, as the test's comment says). Rewrite the comment above the drop to say what
   is now expected: junk is refused and the turn stays.

## The test plan

- `reportLoadDecision.test.ts`: the new reject test; the rewritten null-faction test; every other
  case unchanged.
- `reportLoad.test.ts`: `routeReport` reject test.
- `reportBatch.test.ts`: reason string via the shared const.
- `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts`: the junk-drop assertions (CI runs it; run
  `pnpm run test:smoke -- -g "keeps quiet"` locally by choice — the test is
  `the header keeps quiet about routine state`, `:421`).
- `pnpm run check:fast`.

## User-facing decisions

Asked 2026-08-16, both answered:

1. *What should a single dropped file with no faction id do?* Options: **reject it, screen
   untouched** (chosen; consistent with the batch importer's existing skip, applies also when
   nothing is on screen); ask before replacing (a new confirm prompt — rejected: a dialog for a
   wrong-file drop); keep loading it but make the warning red (rejected: the screen still empties).
2. *The message, exactly as it ships:* **`could not read <file>: the report does not name its
   faction`** (chosen; identical to the batch importer's skip reason, one string serves both);
   `could not read <file>: not an Atlantis report (no faction named)` and `could not read <file>:
   this is not a turn report` were rejected.

The status line is the existing red `import-status` bar; no new control, no mockup.

## Out of scope

- A report *with* a faction but no turn number (`isOlderTurn` already handles null; unchanged).
- Removing `commitTurn`'s now-defensive guard.
- The orders-file sniff (`isOrdersFile`, `AppShell.tsx:1157`) — an orders file still routes to
  the orders import, before any of this.
- The batch importer's behaviour (already right).

## Validation

```bash
pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared test
pnpm run check:fast
```
Human (Psylocke): with a turn loaded, drop an empty `.txt` — red status
`could not read <name>: the report does not name its faction`, map and units unchanged, orders
editor unchanged. Repeat with no turn loaded in a fresh game — same status, still empty screen.

## Known traps

- **Rejection must come before the `!current` branch** in `decideReportLoad`, or a fresh game's
  first drop of junk still loads it as an empty turn.
- **Throw inside `runReported`, do not `setStatus` directly** in `loadReport`: only the throw path
  releases `busy` and prefixes the file name the same way a parse failure does.
- **The smoke test at `workspace.spec.ts:437–447` pins the old behaviour** and will fail in CI
  until it is rewritten — it is part of this bead, not a flake.

title: Every agent session starts with Remote Control on, named after its agent
description:
An agent session can only be reached from the machine it runs on. Remote Control is what Claude Code
offers for that, and no launcher enables it.

**The request:** every agent session starts with Remote Control on.

## The flag

    --remote-control [name]    Start an interactive session with Remote Control enabled
                               (optionally named)
    --remote-control-session-name-prefix <prefix>    (default: hostname)

Every agent is already an interactive session, so all six launchers can take it:
`run-planner`, `run-orchestrator`, `run-user-feedback`, `run-psylocke`, `run-forge` and
`run-implementer`.

**Name the session after the agent.** The optional name is the difference between a remote list of
`hostname-1`, `hostname-2`, `hostname-3` and one reading `Xavier`, `Storm`, `Forge`. With up to
eighteen sessions the auto-generated names are unusable, and the agent's name already exists at that
point in every launcher.

A workaround exists today and shows the shape: each launcher passes `"$@"` through to `claude`
before the prompt, so `run-implementer Storm --remote-control Storm` already works. This bead is
about it being the default rather than something remembered.

## Watch for

**Liveness detection reads process arguments.** `cerebro--name-in-args-p` looks for `--name <Name>`
as a whole word to decide an interactive agent is up. Adding `--remote-control Storm` puts the name
in the arguments a second time; adding `--remote-control-session-name-prefix` puts the string
`-name-` there too. Neither should match the needle — it requires a literal `--name` before the
whitespace — but this is the check that decides whether an agent shows as running at all, and it is
worth proving rather than reasoning about.

**A launcher must not fail because Remote Control cannot start.** If it needs an account, a network,
or anything else that can be absent, the flag turning the fleet off is a far worse outcome than a
session nobody can reach remotely. Behaviour when it is unavailable needs establishing — and if it
does fail hard, the flag wants to be conditional rather than unconditional.

## For the planner to settle with the navigator

- **Whether it is genuinely every session.** An implementer is replaced after each bead, so the
  remote list gains a new entry per bead and loses one - eighteen agents turning over could make the
  remote view noisy. The interactive five are long-lived and are the ones worth reaching.
- **Names, given implementers restart.** `Storm` reused for each successive session is what a person
  wants to see; whether Remote Control minds a name coming back is worth checking.
- **What it exposes.** A remote-controlled session can be driven from elsewhere, which is the point
  and also a consideration on a machine holding a private repository.

## Validation

Start each kind of agent and confirm it appears under its own name in the remote list, and that the
fleet view still shows it as running. Then confirm a launcher still starts an agent on a machine
where Remote Control cannot be enabled.
design:
## Context

**This is the cerebro submodule** (`https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro`, mounted at
`.claude/cerebro`), delivered the way ah-goz/ah-5pp/ah-6uo were: a PR to cerebro, then a one-line
submodule bump PR here. **Blocked by ah-goz** (`bd dep`): its cerebro PR (#39, `8d9bfef`) has merged
and is what this bead edits — `scripts/launch` is now the only place a session is started. Line
numbers below are against cerebro `origin/main` at `8d9bfef`. If the consumer's pointer has not
been bumped to it yet when you start, that changes nothing here: you work in a cerebro clone, and
your bump PR moves the pointer past ah-goz's as a matter of course.

An agent session can only be reached from the machine it runs on. Claude Code's Remote Control
(`claude --remote-control [name]`) connects an interactive session to claude.ai/code and the Claude
mobile app so it can be read and steered from anywhere; no launcher enables it, and the navigator
has been passing it by hand (`run-implementer Storm --remote-control Storm` — the launcher's `"$@"`
already forwards it). After this bead every session `scripts/launch` starts — implementers and the
interactive five alike — starts with Remote Control on and is listed remotely under the agent's
name.

Facts this plan rests on (docs: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control.md, read
2026-08-16 against Claude Code 2.1.233, which is what `claude --version` says on the fleet machine
and whose `--help` lists `--remote-control [name]` and `--remote-control-session-name-prefix
<prefix>`):

- **It degrades, it does not fail.** "Without an eligible login, `claude remote-control` exits with
  an error, while `claude --remote-control` still starts an interactive session and shows a Remote
  Control failure notification shortly after launch." The launcher uses the flag form, so a machine
  where it cannot connect (no Pro/Max/Team login, API-key auth, `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` pointing away
  from `api.anthropic.com`, or `DISABLE_TELEMETRY`/`DO_NOT_TRACK`/
  `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC`/`DISABLE_GROWTHBOOK` set) still gets its agent. **The
  flag is therefore unconditional** — no environment switch, no capability probe.
- **The remote title is the `--name` value first**, then `--remote-control`'s name, then `/rename`.
  Every launch already passes `--name "$name"`, so the name would arrive anyway; the plan passes it
  to `--remote-control` too, explicitly, because the flag's value is *optional* and an optional-value
  flag left bare would swallow whatever follows it (see *Known traps*).
- The docs are silent on reusing a name (Storm restarts after every bead) and on limits; the title
  is a label, not an identity, and the navigator has run the same name repeatedly by hand already.
- `remoteControlAtStartup: true` in `~/.claude/settings.json` exists as an alternative and is
  rejected: it is per-user, per-machine configuration that also switches on every session the
  navigator drives by hand, and it is not something a launcher in this repository can rely on being
  set. The fleet's behaviour lives in the fleet's launcher.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

Everything is in the cerebro repository unless marked *(atlantis-hud)*.

### `scripts/launch` (:68-76, the `exec claude` block)

Add one argument pair, directly after `--name "$name"` and before the model, so it sits before
`"$@"` and a caller's own `--remote-control X` still wins as the later occurrence:

```bash
exec claude \
  --agent "$role" \
  --name "$name" \
  --remote-control "$name" \
  ${model:+--model "$model"} \
  ${effort:+--effort "$effort"} \
  --permission-mode auto \
  "$@" \
  "You are $name. …"            # unchanged
```

Add to the header comment (after the paragraph ending at :16), verbatim:

```
# Every session starts with Remote Control on, named after its agent, so it can be read and steered
# from claude.ai/code or the Claude app (ah-qym). `--remote-control` degrades rather than fails —
# without an eligible login or network it shows a notification and the session runs on as a normal
# one — so it is unconditional. The name is passed explicitly: the flag's value is optional, and a
# bare `--remote-control` would take the next argument as the session name.
```

Nothing else in `launch` changes. The shims (`run-*`) forward to it and need nothing.

### `tests/launchers.sh` (the generic loop :127-158)

Inside the `while IFS=$'\t' read -r name role kind; do` loop, after the `--name` assertion (:133),
add:

```bash
  echo "$out" | grep -A1 '^ARG:--remote-control$' | grep -q "^ARG:${name}\$" \
    || fail "launch $name: expected --remote-control $name, got: $out"
```

and extend the loop's `pass` line (:158) to `…right actor, agent, name, remote-control name, model,
effort`. One more block after `# --- launch overrides ---` (:159-170), following its shape:

```bash
# --- launch overrides: a caller's own --remote-control comes after the launcher's ---
out="$(run_launcher launch Xavier --remote-control Elsewhere)"
first="$(echo "$out" | grep -n '^ARG:--remote-control$' | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)"
second="$(echo "$out" | grep -n '^ARG:--remote-control$' | tail -1 | cut -d: -f1)"
[[ -n "$first" && -n "$second" && $first -lt $second ]] \
  || fail "launch Xavier --remote-control Elsewhere: expected the launcher's flag before the caller's, got: $out"
echo "$out" | sed -n "$((second+1))p" | grep -q '^ARG:Elsewhere$' \
  || fail "launch Xavier --remote-control Elsewhere: caller's name should follow its flag, got: $out"
pass "launch Xavier --remote-control Elsewhere: launcher's Xavier before the caller's Elsewhere"
```

### `emacs/cerebro-test.el` — prove the liveness needle ignores the new flags

`cerebro--name-in-args-p` (`emacs/cerebro.el:106-109`) decides an interactive agent is *up* from a
process's argument string by matching `--name[ \t]+NAME\_>`. The new arguments put the name into
that string a second time (`--remote-control Xavier`) and put the substring `-name-` there
(`--remote-control-session-name-prefix`, if a caller ever passes it). Add, next to
`cerebro-test/derive-interactive-up-from-process-args` (:81-87):

```elisp
(ert-deftest cerebro-test/name-in-args-reads-only-the-name-flag ()
  ;; ah-qym: every launch now carries `--remote-control NAME' too. The needle must still key on
  ;; `--name' alone - a name that appears only as the remote-control value, or a flag that merely
  ;; contains "-name-", must not make an agent look up.
  (should (cerebro--name-in-args-p
           "Xavier" '("claude --agent planner --name Xavier --remote-control Xavier --permission-mode auto")))
  (should-not (cerebro--name-in-args-p
               "Xavier" '("claude --agent planner --remote-control Xavier --permission-mode auto")))
  (should-not (cerebro--name-in-args-p
               "Xavier" '("claude --remote-control-session-name-prefix Xavier --name Storm")))
  (should (cerebro--name-in-args-p
           "Storm" '("claude --remote-control-session-name-prefix Xavier --name Storm"))))
```

This test is expected to pass against the unchanged function — it pins the invariant the bead asks
to have proved rather than reasoned about; say so in its comment (done above) and do not change
`cerebro--name-in-args-p`.

### `README.md` (cerebro, the launcher section :26-40)

After the sentence "The `run-*` scripts are shims over `launch`; the roster is the one place the
fleet is declared." (:35) add, as its own paragraph:

```
Every session starts with Remote Control on and is listed under its agent's name at
[claude.ai/code](https://claude.ai/code) and in the Claude app, so an agent can be read and steered
from another device. It needs a Pro/Max/Team login; where it cannot connect the session shows a
notification and runs on as a normal one, so nothing here depends on it.
```

### *(atlantis-hud)* the bump only

`chore(ah-qym): bump cerebro to remote-controlled sessions` — the `.claude/cerebro` pointer and
nothing else. `CLAUDE.md` is **not** edited by this bead: a change to it needs the navigator under the
Four Eye Principle, and the README sentence above is where the fleet's own behaviour is documented.

## Increments

Work in a clone of cerebro **outside** `.claude/cerebro` (see *Known traps*), branch
`ah-qym-remote-control` from cerebro `origin/main`. Every increment: RED, GREEN,
`bash tests/launchers.sh` + `bash tests/agent-state.sh` + the ERT suite green, commit.

1. **The flag.** RED: the new `--remote-control` assertion in the generic loop of `tests/launchers.sh`
   fails for the first roster row ("expected --remote-control Xavier"). GREEN: the one line in
   `scripts/launch` and its header paragraph. Then add the override block: it passes at once when
   the flag sits before `"$@"` and fails if it were after — it is the pin on the placement, not a
   RED of its own. Commit.
2. **The needle.** Add `cerebro-test/name-in-args-reads-only-the-name-flag`; run
   `emacs --batch -L emacs -l cerebro-test -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit` — green on the first
   run, by design (see above). Commit.
3. **The README paragraph.** Commit.
4. **Delivery, two PRs, the ah-goz shape.** (a) cerebro PR `feat(ah-qym): every session starts with
   Remote Control on, named after its agent`, `gh pr edit <n> --add-reviewer @copilot`, CI green
   (kick `ci.yml` by `workflow_dispatch` if no run appears within two minutes — retrospective
   ah-6uo), answer every comment, squash. (b) atlantis-hud worktree under
   `.cerebro/worktrees/ah-qym`: `git -C .claude/cerebro fetch && git -C .claude/cerebro checkout
   <merged sha>`, `git add .claude/cerebro`, commit `chore(ah-qym): bump cerebro to remote-controlled
   sessions`, normal PR flow (`@copilot`, CI, squash). Close the bead only after (b) merges.

## The test plan

- `tests/launchers.sh` (bash, by hand — CI does not run it, see ah-30t): the generic-loop assertion
  and the override block. macOS bash 3.2 and Linux.
- ERT: the one new test plus the whole suite, and the byte-compile step, both in cerebro CI
  (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, Emacs 28.2 and 30.1).
- atlantis-hud: the bump PR's normal CI only.

## User-facing decisions

Nothing a player sees. Three questions the bead reserved for the navigator, asked 2026-08-16:

- **Which sessions.** Offered: all of them (every session `launch` starts, implementers included),
  or the interactive five only (a quieter remote list, since implementers are replaced per bead).
  **Chosen: all of them.** The churn of implementer names in the remote list is accepted.
- **Naming.** Offered: the bare agent name (`--remote-control "$name"`: `Xavier`, `Storm`, `Forge`,
  reused on every restart), or host-prefixed (`$(hostname -s)-$name`, telling two machines' fleets
  apart). **Chosen: bare agent name** — the same name the fleet view and `BEADS_ACTOR` use.
- **Exposure.** Stated: while connected the transcript (messages, tool activity) is stored on
  Anthropic's servers; execution stays local, outbound HTTPS only, no inbound port; steerable from
  any device signed into the account; `disableRemoteControl` turns it off org-wide. Offered: go
  ahead unconditionally, or only behind an opt-in variable. **Chosen: go ahead, unconditional.**

## Out of scope

- `CLAUDE.md` in atlantis-hud (navigator's document; the cerebro README carries the sentence).
- Any probe for whether Remote Control *can* connect, or a switch to turn it off per launch: the
  flag degrades gracefully by the docs, and a caller who wants it off has `"$@"` and
  `--remote-control` semantics to argue with claude directly.
- `remoteControlAtStartup` (user settings) — rejected above.
- Anything about the fleet view starting or showing remote status; `cerebro.el` is untouched
  beyond the test.
- Running `tests/launchers.sh` in cerebro CI (ah-30t).

## Validation

In the cerebro clone:

```bash
bash tests/launchers.sh            # ends "all launcher tests passed"
bash tests/agent-state.sh
emacs --batch -L emacs -f batch-byte-compile emacs/cerebro.el          # no warnings
emacs --batch -L emacs -l cerebro-test -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit
grep -c -- '--remote-control "\$name"' scripts/launch                     # exactly 1
```

By hand, in the consumer after the bump: start the next implementer from the fleet view (or
`.claude/cerebro/scripts/run-implementer <free name>`) and find it by that name, with the green
dot, at https://claude.ai/code within a minute; the fleet view still lists it as running. For the
degradation case: `DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 .claude/cerebro/scripts/launch Cerebro` in a spare terminal
— Cerebro is the one role that does nothing until asked — shows the Remote Control failure
notification shortly after starting and is otherwise a normal session; Ctrl-C it. Report both
outcomes in the PR body; if the degradation case does *not* start (the docs are wrong for this
version), stop and escalate rather than adding a probe — that is a design change.

## Known traps

- **`--remote-control [name]` takes an *optional* value.** Keep `"$name"` right after it, and never
  let the flag be the last thing before `"$@"` or before the prompt: a bare `--remote-control` would
  take the next argument — the prompt, a positional string — as the session's remote name, and the
  agent would start with no instructions. The launchers.sh assertion (`--remote-control` followed by
  `NAME`) is what pins this.
- **Never branch inside `.claude/cerebro`** of the shared checkout — every running agent's skills
  and agent files are symlinks into it, so a checkout there moves them under live sessions. Clone
  `https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro.git` elsewhere (e.g. `/tmp/cerebro-ah-qym`) for the PR. The
  bump PR here is from a worktree under `.cerebro/worktrees/`, and will likely be `BEHIND` — follow
  the merge-state check in `implement-bead`.
- **`launch` before preflight must stay builtins-only** (ah-goz's trap: the claude-missing test runs
  `launch Forge` with a `PATH` of only `dirname` and `bash`). The new line is inside `exec claude`,
  after preflight — do not move it or add a probe before preflight.
- **The stub `claude` in `tests/launchers.sh` prints one `ARG:` line per argument**; the prompt is
  the last argument and has an embedded newline, so it prints as the last two lines — the loop's
  `tail -2` reads it. Adding an argument pair before the prompt does not disturb that; adding one
  after it would.
- **The consumer's `.claude/cerebro` pointer may still be at `3e37827`** (pre-ah-goz) when you
  start; `git -C .claude/cerebro fetch` before reading anything there, and cite `origin/main`.
acceptance_criteria: Every agent launcher starts its session with Remote Control enabled and named after the agent, so sessions are identifiable remotely. The fleet view still detects each running agent by its process arguments. A launcher still starts its agent where Remote Control cannot be enabled.

title: Nexus and underworld hexes are filed on the surface, sharing its hexes
description:
The nexus appears at (0,0) on the surface, sharing a hex with whatever is genuinely there. It is a
plane of its own and belongs on a level of its own.

## The line that does it

`parse_coordinate` in `crates/core/src/report/scan.rs`:

    let z = match parts.next() {
        None => 1,
        Some(level) => level.parse::<u32>().ok().unwrap_or(1),
    };

A region header reads `nexus (0,0,nexus) in the Nexus`. The third field is the word `nexus`, not a
number, so `parse::<u32>()` fails, `unwrap_or(1)` supplies the surface, and the nexus is filed at
`(0,0,1)` — the same coordinate as the surface hex at the origin.

The fallback is doing exactly what it was written to do. It was written for a level it could not
read; it also silently absorbs a level that is not a number by design.

## Why it matters beyond the map

`Coordinate.id()` builds the region id from x, y and z, so the nexus and the surface origin produce
the **same id**. Anything keyed by region id — units in a hex, orders addressed to it, the diff
between two turns, the map's own lookup — cannot tell the two apart. The visible symptom is one hex
on the wrong level; the underlying one is two regions sharing an identity.

Worth checking as part of this: whether a report with both a nexus and a surface (0,0) currently
loses one of them, and which.

## What "its own level" should mean

`z` is a `u32` and levels count from 1 at the surface, so the nexus needs a value that cannot
collide with a real level. That is a decision, not a detail, and it reaches the map's level control,
the export (`level_suffix` in `report/export.rs` writes `,{z}` for anything but 1), and any stored
game that already holds the wrong coordinate.

## For the planner to settle with the navigator

- **Which value the nexus gets.** A sentinel like `0` reads naturally as "above the surface" and is
  cheap; a named variant is honest about the nexus not being an ordinary depth but changes the type
  everywhere `z` is a number.
- **What the level control shows.** The nexus is a single hex — whether it appears as a level in the
  usual list, or is reached some other way, is a thing a player will meet.
- **Reports already imported.** A stored game holds the coordinate as it was parsed. Whether opening
  it re-parses, migrates, or leaves the old placement in place needs an answer.
- Whether any other non-numeric level exists in Atlantis reports, so the fix is shaped for the class
  rather than for this one word.

## Validation

Load a report containing a nexus region: it is not at (0,0) on the surface, and the surface origin
shows whatever genuinely sits there. Confirm units and orders in the nexus are attributed to the
nexus. Confirm a report with no nexus is completely unaffected.
design:
## Context

The third field of a report coordinate is a **name**, not a number. The engine
(Atlantis-PBEM/Atlantis `aregion.cpp`, `ARegion::short_print`; NewOrigins config in
`neworigins/rules.cpp`: `NEXUS_EXISTS 1`, `EASIER_UNDERWORLD 1`, `UNDERWORLD_LEVELS 1`,
`UNDERDEEP_LEVELS 0`, `ABYSS_LEVEL 0`) numbers its levels internally — nexus `0`, surface `1`,
underworld `2`… — and prints the level array's *name*: nothing for the surface, `nexus` for the
nexus, `underworld` for the underworld. Every shipped ruleset (`standard`, `basic`, `fracas`,
`havilah`, `kingdoms`, `neworigins`) creates its levels with exactly four names — `nexus`,
`underworld`, `underdeep`, `abyss` — and NewOrigins, the game this client targets, can only ever
print `nexus` and `underworld`. Two rarer spellings exist in the engine for other configurations:
with `EASIER_UNDERWORLD` and more than one underground level the field is `2 <underworld>` (number,
space, name in angle brackets); without `EASIER_UNDERWORLD` and several levels of one kind it is
`deep underworld`, `very deep underworld` (one `very ` per level below "deep").

`parse_coordinate` (`crates/core/src/report/scan.rs:64-76`) reads the field with
`level.parse::<u32>().ok().unwrap_or(1)`, so **`nexus` and `underworld` both become the surface**.
The nexus is filed at `(0,0,1)` — the same coordinate and the same `Coordinate::id()` (`"1:0,0"`,
`report/model.rs:24-26`) as the surface hex at the origin — and every underworld hex a faction ever
sees is filed on top of the surface hex at its own x,y. Everything keyed by region id (units in a
hex, orders, the turn comparison, the known map, sightings in the store) cannot tell the two apart.
The fixture reports show it: every `*-t0.rep` is one region, `nexus (0,0,nexus) in The Void.`
(`tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-g2-f42-t0.rep:93`), and turn 1's events say
`Walks from nexus (0,0,nexus) in The Void to mountain (36,4) in Slounspifra.` No fixture has an
underworld region, which is why the second half of the bug was never noticed.

**What changes when this lands.** The core keeps `z: u32` as the engine's own level index and owns
the vocabulary that maps a name to it and back: `nexus`→0, (absent)→1, `underworld`→2,
`underdeep`→3, `abyss`→4, `N <name>`→N, a bare `N`→N. Region ids come out distinct (`0:0,0` for the
nexus, `2:7,53` underground). The known map reports the levels it holds with their names, the level
control above the map prints those names, the region panel names the level of an unexplored hex,
and a stored nexus sighting written before this fix (`1:0,0`, terrain `nexus`) is repaired when
the known map is resolved, so a game imported before this bead is right after it without a
re-import or a store migration.

### 1. Core vocabulary — new `crates/core/src/report/level.rs`, wired in `report/mod.rs`

One module owns "how a report names a level and how the core numbers it". Add `pub mod level;` to
`crates/core/src/report/mod.rs` (the `pub mod` list at :7-19).

```rust
//! Map levels: how a report names one in a coordinate's third field, and how the core numbers it.
//! The numbers are the engine's own (`ARegion::zloc`): nexus 0, surface 1, underworld 2, and the
//! two deeper kinds no shipped ruleset turns on at 3 and 4.

pub const NEXUS: u32 = 0;
pub const SURFACE: u32 = 1;
pub const UNDERWORLD: u32 = 2;
pub const UNDERDEEP: u32 = 3;
pub const ABYSS: u32 = 4;

/// The level a coordinate's third field names. `None` for a field the engine never prints.
///
/// Accepts every spelling the engine has: `nexus`; `underworld`, `underdeep`, `abyss`, each with
/// any number of leading `very ` and one `deep ` adding one level per word; `2 <underworld>` (the
/// EASIER_UNDERWORLD multi-level form — the leading number is authoritative and the rest is
/// ignored); and a bare number, which is what this client wrote until now.
#[must_use]
pub fn parse_level(field: &str) -> Option<u32>;

/// The word the level control shows: `nexus`, `surface`, `underworld`, `underdeep`, `abyss`, and
/// `level 5` for a number no shipped ruleset names.
#[must_use]
pub fn level_name(z: u32) -> String;

/// The third field the report prints for the level: `None` on the surface, otherwise the name
/// (`nexus`, `underworld`, `underdeep`, `abyss`) or the bare number for a level with no name.
/// `parse_level` reads back everything this writes.
#[must_use]
pub fn level_field(z: u32) -> Option<String>;
```

`parse_level` algorithm, in this order, on the trimmed field:
1. If it starts with an ASCII digit: take the leading run of digits, `parse::<u32>()`, return it.
   Nothing after the digits is looked at (`2 <underworld>` → 2, `2` → 2).
2. Otherwise: `extra = 0`; while the text starts with `"very "` strip it and `extra += 1`; if it then
   starts with `"deep "` strip it and `extra += 1`. Match the remainder exactly: `"nexus"` → `NEXUS +
   extra`, `"underworld"` → `UNDERWORLD + extra`, `"underdeep"` → `UNDERDEEP + extra`, `"abyss"` →
   `ABYSS + extra`. Anything else → `None`.

`level_name`: `0 → "nexus"`, `1 → "surface"`, `2 → "underworld"`, `3 → "underdeep"`, `4 → "abyss"`,
else `format!("level {z}")`. `level_field`: `1 → None`, `0/2/3/4 → Some(level_name(z))`, else
`Some(z.to_string())`.

Mockup: `docs/ui/map-levels.html` (PR #314; drafted as `.cerebro/scratch/xavier/ah-4b4-levels.html`).

  shallowest first (`nexus` / `surface` / `underworld`), supplied by the core; B: capitalised
  (`Nexus` / `Surface` / `Underworld`); C: name and depth number (`0 · nexus`). **Chosen: A.** B was
  rejected because it changes the case of the existing `surface` word and stops quoting the report;
  C because the number is this client's bookkeeping and the game never shows the player one, and it
  widens a control in a strip that shares the top band with the zoom cluster. The words, exactly:
  `nexus`, `surface`, `underworld`, `underdeep`, `abyss`, `level 5` (fallback for a nameless level).
  Order: ascending `z`. The static one-level word follows the same names (turn 0 reads `nexus`).
- **Q2 — the nexus after the faction has left it.** Offered A: shown only while the report describes
  it (not remembered; no `nexus` entry from turn 1; the legacy row simply dropped); B: remembered like
  any other hex, the control offering it for the life of the game. **Chosen: B**, against my
  recommendation — consistency: a hex seen is a hex remembered, no exception. Consequence accepted by
  the navigator: a game imported before this bead keeps a mis-filed nexus row, which is why §4's
  read-time repair exists (a store migration in both SQLite and IndexedDB was the alternative and is
  not wanted).
- **Q3 — the region panel on an unexplored hex off the surface.** Offered A: name the level (`…and no
  neighbour has named it, in the underworld.` / `…, in the nexus.`); B: keep the number (`…, on level
  2.`). **Chosen: A.** B rejected because `level 0` is a name the game never uses while the control
  beside it says `nexus`. On the surface the sentence ends at `named it.` as today. Exact clauses:
  `, in the nexus` / `, in the underworld` / `, in the underdeep` / `, in the abyss`; a nameless
  level keeps `, on level 5`.
- **Q4 — hex labels in titles and lists.** Offered A: as today, `terrain (x,y) in Province`; B: as
  the report writes it, `cavern (7,53,underworld) in Deeps`. **Chosen: A.** B is a bead of its own if
  ever wanted; nothing in `hexLabelOf` changes.
- **Q5 — loading turn 1 with the nexus remembered.** Offered: stay on the nexus level with the empty
  nexus selected (the standing rule: a new turn never moves the player) — or move to the level of the

Not asked, decided by me as architecture: `z` stays the engine's own index; names live in the core

## Out of scope

- A three-part hex label (`(x,y,underworld)`) anywhere on screen (Q4 B).
- Migrating stored rows in SQLite or IndexedDB: the read-time repair in `resolve_known_map` covers
  the nexus; underworld rows written before this fix cannot be identified from the row (their
  terrain is `cavern`/`tunnels`/…) and are left as they are — a re-import of the turns that saw them
  writes the correct rows, and the mis-filed surface rows are overwritten only if the surface hex at
  that x,y is ever seen. Say so in the PR body.
- Any behaviour change for a report with no nexus and no underworld — the acceptance criterion says
  it parses exactly as before, and the surface's ids (`1:x,y`) do not change.
- Moving the player on a new turn (Q5).
- The `deep`/`very deep` and `N <name>` spellings are read but never written back in that spelling
  (`level_field` writes the base name for 2/3/4 and the number otherwise); no shipped ruleset prints
