   export.
8. **No smoke test in this bead.** The smoke suite drives the UI and never reaches the client
   directly (checked: nothing in `tests/smoke/` exposes it to the page), and there is no UI yet; the
   reload walk is ah-o1t.2's, and its plan names it.

## The test plan

- Rust: `cargo test --workspace` — the three new tests plus `schema_version_tracks_the_latest_migration`.
- Vitest: `pnpm --filter @atlantis/core-client test`, `pnpm --filter @atlantis/browser-core test`,
  `pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared test` — the tests named above.
- The full gate before the PR: `pnpm check` (the local gate `implement-bead` names), and the smoke
  suites run in CI as usual.

## User-facing decisions

None visible in this bead — no UI changes. The record's shape encodes decisions the navigator made
for the epic (quoted from `ah-o1t`'s design so nothing is re-decided later): **many notes per hex**
(hence `id`, not a per-region key); **a new note starts on the map** (`newHexNote` sets `onMap:
true`); **500 characters, multi-line** (`HEX_NOTE_MAX_CHARS`, newlines kept, no message on the
limit — the field simply stops); **stamped with the turn it was written on and unchanged by edits**
(`turn` set once); **stored in the game's own store like order drafts and included in a backup**
(the whole bead). Nothing else here is the player's.

## Out of scope

- Any UI: the region panel section (ah-o1t.2), the map layer and the Badges entry (ah-o1t.3), the
  palette action (ah-o1t.2).
- Notes on the desktop's game *export to file* beyond the existing backup JSON — there is no other
  export.
- Migrating notes between games, or importing notes from a report.
- A `getHexNote(id)` single read — the UI holds the list; nothing needs one.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test --workspace
pnpm --filter @atlantis/core-client test
pnpm --filter @atlantis/browser-core test
pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared test
pnpm check
```

Human check: none — Psylocke will mark it not needed only if nothing under `packages/` moved, which is
not the case here, but there is nothing to see: say in the PR that the visible half arrives with
ah-o1t.2 and ah-o1t.3.

## Known traps

- **`GAME_DATABASE_VERSION` must be bumped** (webStore.ts:19) or the new object store is never
  created in a browser that already has the game open, and every `putHexNote` fails with
  `NotFoundError`. `openGameDatabase`'s comment says what a bump costs; the `onblocked` handler at
  :249 fires if the game is open in another tab — say so in the PR description.
- **A backup written before this bead has no `hexNotes`.** Rust needs `#[serde(default)]` on that
  one field and the web reader `payload.hexNotes ?? []` — the merged-reports precedent did neither
  and would reject; do not copy it.
- **SQLite has no boolean.** `on_map` is `INTEGER`; the normaliser in core-client accepts `0|1` as
  well as `true|false` because the Tauri DTO sends a Rust `bool` and any future raw-row path would
  send an integer.
- **`created_at` must not move on upsert** — an edit is `ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE` and the update
  list must leave `created_at` out, or newest-first ordering reshuffles on every edit.
- **Two shells, one wire.** The Tauri `save_hex_note` command takes `note: HexNoteDto` — the
  `#[tauri::command(rename_all = "snake_case")]` renames the *argument*, the DTO's own
  `rename_all = "camelCase"` reads the *fields*; do not snake_case the note's fields in the adapter.
- **`crypto.randomUUID()`** exists in every runtime this app ships in (secure context / Tauri
  webview / Node ≥ 19 for vitest); `gameSession.ts:82` already relies on it.
- **`cargo check --workspace` after touching `main.rs`** — the desktop commands are behind
  `#[cfg(all(any(target_os …), feature = "desktop-runtime"))]`; a missing import compiles fine in
  tests and fails only in the desktop build.
acceptance_criteria: CoreClient can save, list and delete hex notes for an open game on both shells; a note survives an app restart and a report reload; a game backup exported after adding a note restores that note; the shared module validates and orders notes; every layer has tests.

title: Manual hex annotations
description:
Reporter (GitHub #261) wants to be able to attach manual, free-text annotations to individual hexes on the map — e.g. a note like "Build a castle here" — as a lightweight planning aid independent of game report data.

Each annotation should carry a visibility toggle: shown as an overlay on the map itself, or only surfaced in the region report frame for that hex (i.e. kept out of the map view but still reachable when looking at the region).

Open questions for planning: how annotations are created/edited (map click, region panel, dedicated UI), whether they persist across turns/report loads, whether they are scoped per-faction or per-user/browser profile, and how they interact with existing map overlays.
design:
## The interview (2026-08-15, navigator and Xavier) — the record every child plan quotes

Issue #261 (Puckohue): "I would like to be able to make manual annotations for hexes, i.e. 'Build a
castle here'. Ideally each annotation would have a checkbox indicating if it is to be visible on the
map or only in the region report frame." No further thread beyond Moira's acknowledgement and CREATED
comment. Mockup: `docs/ui/hex-notes.html` (PR #266), with the choices marked on it.

Split into three children, in build order: **ah-o1t.1** storage → **ah-o1t.2** region-panel editor →
**ah-o1t.3** map layer. Each child's plan carries the decisions it implements; the whole set is here.

1. **Where a note is written — A, the region panel only** (chosen). A `Notes` section at the foot of
   the region panel, after Structures, and on an unexplored hex too (the panel's `unknown` branch).
   Rejected: B, the same section plus a popover editor opened from the map pin (a second editor to
   keep in step; the panel is built either way). Right-click was never an option: it means "centre
   here" (ah-t2i).
2. **How a map-visible note is drawn — the pin, opening into a stack of tags** (chosen in round 2,
   variant a, after none of round 1's three as drawn). A paper-note glyph, warm paper yellow, in the
   hex's upper-right, screen-constant, with a count badge when the hex has more than one map-visible
   note; shown at mid and near zoom, hidden at far like unit marks. **Clicking the pin selects the
   hex and opens the tags**: one tag per map-visible note, newest on top, full text wrapped at about
   28 characters, at most four lines each before an ellipsis. **One stack open at a time**; a click
   anywhere else, Escape, or the pin again closes it; opening another pin closes the first; not
   remembered across reloads. **Keyboard: none on the map** — the panel is the keyboard path.
   Rejected: 1 pin only; 2 pin plus first line at near; 3 always-open sticky tag; round 2 b (newest
   note plus "+N more in the panel"); pin click that does not select; several stacks open; a
   shortcut to open the selected hex's tag.
3. **The map-wide switch — a Badges menu entry `Notes`** (chosen), twelfth, after Regions, on by
   default, persisted with the other badges. Rejected: a layer chip.
4. **Many notes per hex, newest first; a new note starts ON the map** (chosen). Rejected: new notes
   off the map; one note per hex.
5. **Storage — the game's own store, like order drafts** (chosen): SQLite on the desktop, IndexedDB
   on the web, through the core client, included in a game backup. Rejected: localStorage per game.
6. **Words, as drawn** (chosen verbatim): section heading `Notes` with the count; button
   `+ Add note`; per-note chip `Map` (lit = on the map); `Save` / `Cancel`; `Remove`, then in the
   same row `Remove this note?` with `Keep` / `Remove`; empty state `No notes on this hex.`; the
   turn stamp `turn 71` (the report's turn at save time, unchanged by later edits); Badges entry
   `Notes`; palette action `Add note to this hex`. At the panel's narrowest the button drops under
   the heading and Remove becomes `✕`.
7. **Length and shape — multi-line, up to 500 characters** (chosen): a textarea, newlines kept, input
   stops at 500 with no message; ⌘/Ctrl+Enter saves, Escape cancels, Save disabled while the text is
   empty or whitespace. Rejected: single line, 120 characters.
8. **Turn stamp — yes** (chosen), shown small in the row and as the tag's last line.

Planner's decisions recorded here so the children agree: notes are keyed by **game and region**
(`gameId`, `regionId` such as `1:7,53`), not by faction or turn, which is what makes them survive a
new turn and an ally's report; the map layer is **map-owned** (drawn once in `MapCanvas.tsx` beside
the region decorations, not a theme mark); the pin is the one mark on the map with a hit target.
acceptance_criteria:
A player can attach a free-text annotation to a hex.
Each annotation has a visibility setting: map-visible or region-report-only.
Annotations persist across application restarts / report reloads.
Annotations are visually distinguishable from game-generated map content.
close_reason: All children closed; last was ah-o1t.3, delivered in PR #276

title: Drag the units-in-hex pane to size it; the row-count setting is gone
description:
The "Units in hex" pane is sized by a row count rather than by dragging. Everywhere else in the
workspace a pane is resized by grabbing its edge — the region pane, and the unit/orders split — so
this one is the odd pane out, and the setting behind it is a number the navigator has to translate
into a height.

**The request:** give the pane the same drag handle the others have, and remove the row-count
setting entirely.

## What exists to copy

`PanelSplitter.tsx` and `RailSplitter.tsx` (`packages/shared/src/workspace/`) already implement the
drag mechanic used by the other panes, each with its own tests. This should be those, not a third
implementation.

## What comes out

Two settings in `packages/shared/src/settingsStore.ts`, and everything hanging off them:

- `unitListLimit` — the row count, defaulted from `DEFAULT_UNIT_LIST_LIMIT` and clamped by
  `clampUnitListLimit`;
- `unitListFixedSize` — whether that count is a fixed reservation or a ceiling.

Plus their UI: `UnitListLimitStepper.tsx` (the in-pane stepper), the Settings dialog controls, and
the persisted values. `UnitTableDock.tsx` is where the pane reads them.

**`unitListFixedSize` shipped today**, in PR #236 for `ah-3cs` — "option to keep the units-in-hex
pane a fixed number of rows tall", closed the same day. This bead removes it. That is the
navigator's call and not a mistake to be reconciled, but it should be said out loud: an implementer
finding a freshly-merged feature being deleted deserves to know it was deliberate, and Psylocke may
have `ah-3cs` queued for verification of behaviour that is about to stop existing.

## For the planner to settle with the navigator

- **Migration.** Somebody has a saved `unitListLimit` of 12 and `unitListFixedSize` on. Does the
  first run after this convert that into a pixel height, or does the pane start at a default and
  forget what they had?
- **What the drag bounds are.** A minimum height, and whether it may be dragged to nothing.
- **Whether the pane still snaps to whole rows** while dragging, or is free-form in pixels. Rows are
  what it renders, and half a row of unit is a real visual question.
- Whether the fixed/ceiling distinction survives in any form — with a dragged height the pane is
  always the height you dragged it to, which is what `unitListFixedSize` was asking for. If so, say
  so in the bead's close, because that is the answer to the issue `ah-3cs` came from (gh-212).

## Validation

Manual: drag the units-in-hex pane taller and shorter, confirm it behaves like the region and
unit/orders panes. Confirm no row-count control remains in the pane or in Settings, and that a
profile carrying the old settings still opens.
design:
## Context The "Units in hex" pane at the bottom of the map is the one pane sized by a number — the `unitListLimit` row count (1–16, default 12) with the `unitListFixedSize` toggle from ah-3cs (gh-212, shipped in v0.7.0) — where every other pane is sized by grabbing its edge (`RailSplitter` for the rails, `PanelSplitter` for the unit/orders split). This bead gives it the same drag handle and **removes both settings and their UI**: the in-pane `+`/`-` stepper, the "Units in hex list" slider and the "Fixed pane size" checkbox in Settings. That reversal of ah-3cs is the navigator's own (they filed gh-212), deliberate, and stated here so an implementer deleting a day-old feature knows it is meant. Psylocke has already verified ah-3cs; nothing is queued against it. **Settled with the navigator (mockup `docs/ui/units-pane-drag-resize.html`, PR #260; the whole interview under *User-facing decisions*):** the dragged height **is** the height (short lists and empty hexes leave blank pane below — what "Fixed pane size" did is now the only behaviour); free pixels, no snapping to rows; floor one row (5.5rem), ceiling **70% of the map's overlay column** (today's `max-h-[45vh]` goes); a fresh build starts at the default of twelve rows and the old settings are forgotten; the handle is named "Resize units pane". Everything else about the handle is inherited from ah-13o's grip: the always-visible pill, amber at a limit, Escape cancels, double-click and Enter reset, ↑/↓ nudge 1rem, hidden while the pane is folded, height persisted globally. **Architecture (planner's):** `PanelSplitter` is orders-specific in its names only, so it is **generalised** rather than copied — one horizontal splitter, two callers. The units height lives in `workspaceStore` as `unitsHeightRem: number | null`, exactly beside `ordersHeightRem`. The dock stops sizing itself: its slot has a height, the panel fills it (`CollapsiblePanel` is already `h-full`), the scroller is already `h-full`. `settingsStore` loses the two keys and everything hanging off them. ## Files to change, and what to reuse Everything is in `@atlantis/shared` plus the smoke tests. No Rust, no `core-client`, no shell code. Line numbers against main at `75b2985`. ### `packages/shared/src/workspace/panelLayout.ts` — the arithmetic (pure, tested without a browser) Add beside the orders constants (lines 35–40) and functions, same shapes: ```ts /** * The units-in-hex pane's default height and bounds, in rem. Chosen with the navigator in * `docs/ui/units-pane-drag-resize.html`: twelve rows by default (what the old row count gave), * one row as the floor, never more than seven tenths of the map column. * * 20.625rem = 330px: title bar 28 + body padding 16 + column header 22 + 12 rows × 22 (ROW_HEIGHT). * 5.5rem = 88px: the same with one row. */ export const UNITS_DEFAULT_REM = 20.625; export const UNITS_MIN_REM = 5.5; export const UNITS_MAX_REM = 60; // sanity ceiling for stored values only export const UNITS_CEILING_FRACTION = 0.7; /** null unless a finite number; otherwise clamped into [UNITS_MIN_REM, UNITS_MAX_REM]. */ export function clampUnitsHeight(value: unknown): number | null; /** * One drag or key step on the units pane, resolved against the map column: `hostRem` is the * overlay column's content height (Infinity when unmeasurable, leaving UNITS_MAX_REM). Ceiling is * min(UNITS_MAX_REM, hostRem * UNITS_CEILING_FRACTION); if that falls under UNITS_MIN_REM the floor * wins outright with atLimit true. */ export function dragUnitsHeight(startRem: number, deltaRem: number, hostRem: number): DragResult; /** The bottom slot's classes: STRIP when the pane is folded, otherwise pinned or custom. */ export function unitsSlotClass(collapsed: Collapsed, hasCustomHeight: boolean): string; // folded → STRIP ("flex-none") // pinned → "h-[20.625rem] max-h-[70%] min-h-[5.5rem] flex-none" (const PINNED_UNITS) // custom → "min-h-[5.5rem] flex-none" (const CUSTOM_UNITS) /** Inline style once a height is stored: the height, and the 70% clamp-to-fit for a short window. */ export function unitsSlotStyle( collapsed: Collapsed, unitsHeightRem: number | null ): { height: string; maxHeight: string } | null; // null when unitsHeightRem == null or collapsed.units; else { height: `${rem}rem`, maxHeight: "70%" } ``` `max-h-[70%]` / `maxHeight: "70%"` resolve against the overlay column's **content box** (it is `absolute inset-0`, so its height is definite), which is why `hostRem` below is measured as a content-box height too — otherwise the drag would stop at a value CSS then refuses. ### `packages/shared/src/workspace/PanelSplitter.tsx` — generalised, one component for both splits Rename the props so nothing in the file says "orders"; the orders caller and the units caller pass what differs: ```ts export type PanelSplitterProps = { /** The slot div below the handle; measured at gesture start, written to directly during a drag. */ slot: RefObject; /** The committed height, or null while the default applies. */ heightRem: number | null; /** What null means, for aria-valuenow and for the first keyboard step. */ defaultRem: number; /** aria-valuemin / aria-valuemax. */ minRem: number; maxRem: number; /** The clamp: dragOrdersHeight or dragUnitsHeight. */ drag: (startRem: number, deltaRem: number, hostRem: number) => DragResult; /** Accessible name and test id: "Resize orders panel" / "panel-splitter", "Resize units pane" / "units-splitter". */ label: string; testId: string; /** Called once per finished gesture: pointerup, one arrow press, or a reset (null). */ onCommit: (rem: number | null) => void; }; ``` - `railRem()` (lines 35–38) becomes `hostRem(slot)`: the slot's parent's **content-box** height in rem — `parent.clientHeight - paddingTop - paddingBottom` from `getComputedStyle`, `Infinity` when there is no parent. For the orders slot the parent (`AppShell.tsx:2926`, `relative flex min-h-0 flex-col gap-2.5`) has no padding, so its value is unchanged; for the units slot the parent is the overlay column (`AppShell.tsx:2901`, `p-2.5 pt-12`) and the padding matters. - Every `dragOrdersHeight(...)` call (lines 90, 145) → `drag(...)`; `ORDERS_DEFAULT_REM` (line 143, 161) → `defaultRem`; `ORDERS_MIN_REM`/`ORDERS_MAX_REM` (159–160) → `minRem`/`maxRem`; `aria-label` (155) → `label`; `data-testid` (157) → `testId`. The imports from `./panelLayout` shrink to `DragResult` and `SPLIT_STEP_REM`. Nothing about the pointer choreography, the dismiss layer, the selection guard, the `moved` gate or `gripClassName` changes. Doc comment (lines 51–60): "the drag handle above a slot in a column — the orders editor's, and the units-in-hex pane's". - **`packages/shared/src/workspace/PanelSplitter.test.tsx`** — the harness at lines 54–60 builds props by hand; update to the new names (`slot: NO_SLOT, heightRem, defaultRem: ORDERS_DEFAULT_REM, minRem: ORDERS_MIN_REM, maxRem: ORDERS_MAX_REM, drag: dragOrdersHeight, label: "Resize orders panel", testId: "panel-splitter", onCommit`). acceptance_criteria: The units-in-hex pane is resized by dragging a handle, using the same splitter component as the region and unit/orders panes. The unitListLimit and unitListFixedSize settings are gone, along with the in-pane stepper and their Settings controls. A profile saved with the old settings still loads. title: Order-check options cross the validation wire as one object
description: Refactor only, no behaviour change: the warn_on_unguarded_hex positional boolean that travels client -> adapter -> wasm/tauri -> core becomes a single serialized options value (a disabled-codes list), so ah-m9q.2 can add per-check toggles without growing six signatures per toggle. Planned as part of the ah-m9q split; see the parent for the discussion.
design:
## Context

`OrderCheckOptions` has exactly one field, and it crosses the client/core boundary as a **bare
positional boolean** through six signatures on two platforms. ah-m9q (this bead's parent) adds a
per-check toggle for every advisory order warning — eight distinct codes — and eight more
positional booleans is untenable. This bead is the refactor that makes the feature possible:
the option becomes **one value, a list of disabled advisory codes**, everywhere the wire runs.
**No behaviour change**: with the same settings, the same diagnostics come out.

It also gives the codes a home. `Finding.code` is a scattering of `&'static str` literals across
nine emission sites in `semantics.rs` with no registry — Rust-side constants and a client-side
union are created here so ah-m9q.2 (and its tests) have one list to agree on.

ah-m9q.2 is planned separately and builds on the seams named here. All line numbers are against
`origin/main` at `4414626`.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`

- Name the codes once, above `Finding` (~line 50):

  ```rust
  /// Every advisory code the semantic checks can emit, in one place.
  /// The settings UI and the client mirror this list; a new check adds its code here first.
  pub mod codes {
      pub const NOT_ENOUGH_SILVER: &str = "not-enough-silver";
      pub const NOT_ENOUGH_ITEMS: &str = "not-enough-items";
      pub const GUARD_DROPPED: &str = "guard-dropped";
      pub const HEX_UNGUARDED: &str = "hex-unguarded";
      pub const TAUGHT_NOT_HERE: &str = "taught-not-here";
      pub const TAUGHT_NOT_STUDYING: &str = "taught-not-studying";
      pub const TEACHER_CANNOT_TEACH: &str = "teacher-cannot-teach";
      pub const TEACHING_OVERSUBSCRIBED: &str = "teaching-oversubscribed";
      pub const ALL: [&str; 8] = [NOT_ENOUGH_SILVER, NOT_ENOUGH_ITEMS, GUARD_DROPPED,
          HEX_UNGUARDED, TAUGHT_NOT_HERE, TAUGHT_NOT_STUDYING, TEACHER_CANNOT_TEACH,
          TEACHING_OVERSUBSCRIBED];
  }
  ```

  and replace the nine literal emission sites (lines 667, 679, 721, 758, 763, 817, 827, 846,
  861, 931) with the constants. (`not-enough-silver` is emitted from two sites — `check_resources`
  and `report_shared_purse` — one constant, both sites.)

- `CheckOptions` (lines 38–47) becomes:

  ```rust
  #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  pub struct CheckOptions {
      /// Advisory codes not to emit. Unknown codes are ignored.
      pub disabled: std::collections::BTreeSet<String>,
  }
  impl CheckOptions {
      pub fn emits(&self, code: &str) -> bool { !self.disabled.contains(code) }
  }
  impl Default for CheckOptions {
      /// `hex-unguarded` starts disabled: most hexes are deliberately unguarded, and the
      /// wasm/tauri entry points fall back to this default when no options arrive.
      fn default() -> Self {
          Self { disabled: std::iter::once(codes::HEX_UNGUARDED.to_string()).collect() }
      }
  }
  ```

  The `Copy` derive goes (a set is not `Copy`); callers that copied now clone or borrow.
  The gate at line 761 (`options.warn_on_unguarded_hex`) becomes
  `options.emits(codes::HEX_UNGUARDED)`. **No other emission site is gated in this bead** —
  wiring `emits` through the remaining eight sites is ah-m9q.2's first increment, so this
  refactor stays observably identical.

- Test helper `check(...)` at 1063–1070 keeps passing `CheckOptions::default()`; the three guard
  tests that build `CheckOptions { warn_on_unguarded_hex: true }` (lines 1631–1652 area) now
  build `CheckOptions { disabled: BTreeSet::new() }` — "nothing disabled" is the new spelling of
  "warn about unguarded hexes".

### `crates/core/src/lib.rs`

`pub use orders::semantics::CheckOptions as OrderCheckOptions;` (line 118) stands unchanged.

### `crates/core/src/orders/mod.rs`

`validate_turn` (line 46) signature unchanged — it already takes `options` whole.

### `crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs`

`the_broad_guard_check_is_the_noisy_one_the_setting_holds_back` (line 188) builds its options at
199–201 — same respelling as the unit tests.

### The wire, wasm side

- `crates/core-wasm/src/lib.rs:673-682` — `validate_orders_state(..., warn_on_unguarded_hex:
  Option<bool>)` becomes `(..., disabled_codes: Option<Vec<String>>)`; build
  `CheckOptions { disabled: disabled_codes.map(Vec::into_iter).map(Iterator::collect)
  .unwrap_or_else(|| CheckOptions::default().disabled) }` — i.e. absent still means the default
  (hex-unguarded off), present replaces it wholesale. wasm-bindgen passes `Vec<String>` from a JS
  `string[]` directly.
- `packages/browser-core/src/webCoreAdapter.ts:586-596` — the adapter's
  `validateOrders(raw, ruleset, report, warnOnUnguardedHex: boolean)` parameter becomes
  `disabledCodes: readonly string[]`.

### The wire, tauri side

- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs:370-382` — `warn_on_unguarded_hex: Option<bool>` becomes
  `disabled_codes: Option<Vec<String>>`, same absent-means-default rule.
- `crates/core-tauri/src/lib.rs:622-630` — `command_validate_orders(..., bool)` takes
  `Vec<String>` (already-defaulted by the shell, mirroring today's `bool` after `unwrap_or`).
- `packages/core-client/src/index.ts:2226-2236` — the tauri adapter's `invoke` args:
  `warn_on_unguarded_hex` key becomes `disabled_codes` (snake_case, as the command declares).

### `packages/core-client/src/index.ts`

- `OrderCheckOptions` (lines 567–577) becomes:

  ```ts
  /** Advisory order-check codes, mirrored from crates/core semantics::codes::ALL. */
  export const ADVISORY_CHECK_CODES = [
    "not-enough-silver", "not-enough-items", "guard-dropped", "hex-unguarded",
    "taught-not-here", "taught-not-studying", "teacher-cannot-teach",
    "teaching-oversubscribed",
  ] as const;
  export type AdvisoryCheckCode = (typeof ADVISORY_CHECK_CODES)[number];

  /** Which of the checks that read the report to run. */
  export type OrderCheckOptions = {
    /** Advisory codes not to produce. Omitted = the default: everything except hex-unguarded. */
    disabledCodes?: readonly AdvisoryCheckCode[];
  };
  ```

- `CoreClient.validateOrders` (1797–1810): the unwrap at 1807
  (`options.warnOnUnguardedHex ?? false`) becomes
  `options.disabledCodes ?? ["hex-unguarded"]` — the client always sends an explicit list, so the
  three scattered `unwrap_or(false)` defaults stop being load-bearing (they remain only as the
  no-options fallback).
- The adapter interface declarations at 836–841 and 1173–1178 change their last parameter to
  `disabledCodes: readonly string[]`.

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx`

The two call sites build the list from the existing setting — **`warnOnUnguardedHex` stays the
stored setting in this bead**; only the wire changes:

- Line 2002–2003 (main validation effect) and 2132–2133 (orders-import effect):
  `{ disabledCodes: warnOnUnguardedHex ? [] : ["hex-unguarded"] }`.
- The effect dependency arrays (2022 and 2160–2172) keep `warnOnUnguardedHex` — same value, same
  re-validation trigger. Build the array inside the effect (or memoise) so the dep stays the
  boolean, not a fresh array identity.

`settingsStore.ts` is untouched. `SettingsDialog.tsx` is untouched. Migration of the stored
setting into a per-code record is ah-m9q.2's, not this bead's.

## Increments

1. **Rust: the codes module and the new `CheckOptions`.** Failing test first, in `semantics.rs`
   `mod tests`: `default_options_disable_only_the_broad_guard_check` — asserts
   `CheckOptions::default().emits(c)` is true for every code in `codes::ALL` except
   `codes::HEX_UNGUARDED`, and `emits("hex-unguarded")` is false. Then the module, the struct,
   the gate at 761, and the respelled existing tests (`cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core` green,
   including `validate_real_orders.rs`).
2. **The wasm wire.** Failing test in `packages/browser-core/src/webCoreAdapter.test.ts` (stub
   at lines 28–29/206 currently records `warnOnUnguardedHex`): the stub records `disabledCodes`
   and the adapter passes `["hex-unguarded"]` through untouched. Then the adapter and
   `core-wasm/src/lib.rs`.
3. **The tauri wire.** Failing tests in `packages/core-client/src/index.test.ts` — rewrite the
   two wire-contract tests: `"asks tauri to validate with the argument names its command
   declares"` (line 701; the asserted args object's `warn_on_unguarded_hex: true` becomes
   `disabled_codes: []`) and `"validates without a report, which is what the pane does before an
   import"` (line 731; `warn_on_unguarded_hex: false` becomes `disabled_codes:
   ["hex-unguarded"]`). Then `index.ts` (type, unwrap, adapter), `core-tauri/src/lib.rs`, and
   `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs`.
4. **AppShell call sites.** No new unit test carries this (the mapping is two expressions); the
   proof is the existing end-to-end behaviour: the smoke suite's
   `"a unit told to spend silver it has not got is warned about, without blocking export"`
   (`workspace.spec.ts:909`) and the `warnAboutUnguardedHexes` helper tests (`:960`, `:991`) must
   pass **unchanged** — they are the no-behaviour-change bar for the whole bead.

## The test plan

- Rust: `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core` — the new default-options test, the respelled guard
  tests, `validate_real_orders.rs` untouched in outcome.
- `packages/browser-core/src/webCoreAdapter.test.ts` — the recorded arg.
- `packages/core-client/src/index.test.ts` — the two rewritten wire-contract tests.
- Smoke: the three named specs above, **unchanged**, as the no-behaviour-change proof.
- Run: `pnpm run check` (covers cargo, unit and smoke suites) before the PR.

## User-facing decisions

None. This is a wire refactor with an explicit no-behaviour-change bar; every player-visible
choice (the tab, the toggles, wording, defaults) was made in the parent ah-m9q discussion and is
recorded in **ah-m9q.2's** plan, which builds on this bead.

## Out of scope

- Gating any check other than `hex-unguarded` (ah-m9q.2 wires `emits()` through the other eight
  sites).
- The Warnings settings tab, the settings-store record, the moved checkbox, migration of the
  stored `warnOnUnguardedHex` — all ah-m9q.2.
- The parser's `unknown-item` warning and every syntax diagnostic — never toggleable (parent
  decision).
- Any change to which diagnostics are produced, counted or displayed.

## Validation

- `pnpm run check` green.
- Human check: none needed beyond the suites — by design nothing observable changes. (Psylocke
  can skip this one; say so in the PR description.)

## Known traps

- **`CheckOptions` loses `Copy`.** The derive list at `semantics.rs:38` includes `Copy`; a
  `BTreeSet` cannot. `check_turn` and the call chain take it by value today — follow the compiler:
  clone at the few call sites or switch to `&CheckOptions`; either is fine, pick one and be
  consistent.
- **The two wire-contract tests in `index.test.ts` (701, 731) are the fence, not an obstacle.**
  They assert exact snake_case argument objects and must be rewritten in the same increment as
  the tauri signature — red first, then the signature, then green.
- **`rename_all = "snake_case"`** on the tauri command (`main.rs:370`): the invoke key is
  `disabled_codes`, not `disabledCodes`. The wasm path has no such rename.
- **Absent-vs-empty is meaningful**: `None`/omitted = the conservative default (hex-unguarded
  disabled); `Some([])`/`[]` = everything enabled. Do not collapse the two — the client always
  sends an explicit list precisely so the Rust default is a fallback, not policy.
- **Do not add per-code gates to the other eight emission sites yet** — with all-default settings
  the diagnostic output must be byte-identical before and after this bead; the smoke suite is the
  referee.
- **A dependent bead's plan cites this seam**: ah-m9q.2 builds against `codes::ALL`,
  `CheckOptions::emits`, `ADVISORY_CHECK_CODES` and `OrderCheckOptions.disabledCodes` exactly as
  named here — if a name must change during implementation, update ah-m9q.2's design field in the
  same session (`bd update ah-m9q.2 --design-file ...`), or the next builder inherits a stale
  promise.

title: Fleet list fits its window: For column readable, finishing marked by a glyph
description:
The fleet's agent list is wider than it needs to be, and the width it wastes costs the last column
entirely.

## Measured, in `emacs/cerebro.el`

`tabulated-list-format` is `Agent 14 · Role 13 · State 18 · Bead 10 · For 6`, plus one column of
`tabulated-list-padding`: **62 columns of table**. `cerebro-list-width` is also **62**.

That is the bug behind the third symptom. A window shows a truncated line by putting `$` in its
final column, so a table exactly as wide as its window loses one column to the marker: the header
reads `Fo`, and `48m` renders as `4$`. Nothing is wrong with the elapsed time — there is nowhere to
draw it.

## What can shrink, and what cannot

| Column | Now | Longest content | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Agent | 14 | 14 | glyph + space + `Nightcrawler` (12). At its floor. |
| Role | 13 | 13 | `orchestrator` (12) + padding. At its floor. |
| State | 18 | 7 | `working`. **Ten columns of nothing.** |
| Bead | 10 | 14 | see below |
| For | 6 | 4 | `1h03` |

**The Bead column is the one assumption in the request that does not hold.** Bead ids are not always
six characters: a child bead is `<parent>.<n>`, nested to any depth. In this repository's own
database today — 98 beads — 55 ids are 6 characters, 34 are 8, and the rest run to 14
(`ah-dzj.1.1.1.1`). The column is 10 because that is the width of `(external)`, which it shows for
an agent Emacs did not start, and even 10 truncates a fifth of the ids that could appear in it.

So the saving is roughly eleven columns from State and one from For: a 62-column table becomes about
51.

## For the planner to settle with the navigator

- **Does the window shrink with the table?** The bead panel below inherits `cerebro-list-width` and
  spends every column on bead titles, which are already truncated at 62. Narrowing the table without
  narrowing the window buys the panel eleven characters of title; narrowing both buys screen space
  for the detail window instead. These pull opposite ways and it is a taste question.
- **What to do about long bead ids.** Widen the column, truncate the id, or leave both and accept
  that a deep child bead is cut. Widening fights the compactness this bead is asking for.
- Whether `(external)` needs its own column at all, or could be a glyph, which would free the Bead
  column to be as narrow as the ids actually need.

## Validation

Manual: open the fleet view and confirm the `For` column shows a full elapsed time — `48m`, `1h03` —
with no `$` at the right edge, for a working implementer and for an interactive agent alike.
design:
## Context

The fleet view's agent table is 62 columns (`Agent 14 + Role 13 + State 18 + Bead 10 + For 6` plus
one column of `tabulated-list-padding`), and `cerebro-list-width` is also 62 — a table exactly as
wide as its window loses its last column to Emacs's `$` truncation marker, so the header reads `Fo`
and `48m` renders as `4$`.

One correction to the bead's measurements, found in planning: **State 18 is not "ten columns of
nothing"** — `cerebro--entry` appends `" finishing"` to the state of a stop-flagged in-flight agent
(`working finishing` = 17 chars), so 18 was sized to real content. The navigator chose to replace
the word with a glyph, which is where the real saving comes from.

Chosen outcome (settled with the navigator, ASCII previews in the question tool — no HTML mockup;
the surface is a terminal table and the previews showed it exactly):
`Agent 14 · Role 13 · State 10 · Bead 10 · For 5` + 1 padding = **53 columns**, window at **54**,
and the window shrinks with the table (the detail window gains the freed columns; the bead panel's
titles narrow with it, knowingly).

**This is the cerebro submodule** (`emacs/cerebro.el` in `https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro`,

title: Turn each advisory order warning on and off from its own settings tab
description:
The order checks that read the turn report — teaching, study, silver, guarding — are advisory rather
than syntax errors: they say what *could* be arranged better, not what is malformed. Which of them
are useful is a matter of how somebody plays. "This unit has 10 teaching slots free and could teach
unit 6857" is a gift to one player and noise to another, every turn, on every teacher.

**The request:** each advisory check gets its own on/off toggle, in a tab of its own in the settings
widget.

## What already exists

Every diagnostic carries a stable `code` (`OrderDiagnostic.code`, `packages/core-client/src/index.ts`),
so the code is the natural key for a toggle — no new identifier needs inventing.

There is already one such switch, and this generalises it: `OrderCheckOptions.warnOnUnguardedHex`
turns `hex-unguarded` on and off, off by default, "because most hexes are deliberately unguarded, so
this speaks about hex after hex". That is the same argument as this bead, made once for one check.
Whether the new tab absorbs it or sits beside it is a decision, not an assumption — see below.

The settings widget has four tabs today (`SETTINGS_TABS` in
`packages/shared/src/workspace/settingsTabs.ts`): Global, Per game, Snippets, About. They are an
ARIA tab list — one tab stop, arrows moving within it — so a fifth is an entry in that array plus
its panel, and `settingsTabs.test.ts` covers the navigation.

## The advisory checks, as they stand

All emitted from `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`:

| Code | About |
|---|---|
| `teacher-has-free-slots` | a teacher could teach somebody and is not |
| `teaching-oversubscribed` | more students than the teacher can take |
| `teacher-cannot-teach` | the unit cannot teach that skill |
| `taught-not-studying` | a unit is being taught and is not studying |
| `taught-not-here` | teacher and student are not in the same hex |
| `not-enough-silver` | the orders spend more than the unit has |
| `not-enough-items` | the orders move more than the unit holds |
| `guard-dropped` | a hex you were guarding no longer is |
| `hex-unguarded` | a hex holds your units and nothing guards it |

**Syntax and parse diagnostics are out of scope** — `unknown-command`, `unterminated-quote`,
`missing-faction` and the rest. Those say the orders will not run, and turning them off would hide a
broken turn rather than a suggestion.

## For the planner to settle with the navigator

- **Grouping.** Nine toggles in a flat list, or grouped (Teaching / Resources / Guarding)? The
  teaching family is five of the nine.
- **Where the setting lives.** Global, or per game? The widget has both, and playing two factions
  differently is plausible.
- **`warnOnUnguardedHex`.** Does the new tab replace it — one mechanism, off by default preserved —
  or does it stay as a separate control? Two switches for one check would be a bug in waiting.
- **Defaults.** Everything on except `hex-unguarded`, matching today, or something else.
- **What "off" means.** Not produced at all, or produced and not shown? It decides whether the
  toggle reaches the Rust checks or filters in the client, and whether an off check can still be
  counted somewhere ("3 hidden warnings").
- Whether a toggled-off check should still underline in the editor, given diagnostics drive the
  CodeMirror gutter through `orderLint.ts`.

## Validation

Manual: turn `teacher-has-free-slots` off with a report loaded that produces it; the warning
disappears from the orders editor and from wherever else warnings surface. Turn it back on; it
returns. Confirm a syntax error is unaffected by every toggle in the tab.
acceptance_criteria: The settings widget has a tab for order warnings. Each advisory check listed in the description has its own on/off toggle there. Turning one off stops its warnings appearing; turning it back on restores them. Syntax and parse diagnostics are unaffected by every toggle. The existing warnOnUnguardedHex control does not end up duplicated by the new one.
close_reason: All children closed; last was ah-m9q.2, delivered in PR #263 (retrospective for a stale-build false-failure reopen; the feature itself shipped in PR #255)

title: Left and right map panes resize by a grip on their inner edge
description:
The left and right panes sitting over the map have fixed widths. A wide map wants them narrower; a
long order wants them wider. The navigator cannot trade one for the other.

**The request:** make the width of the left and right panes changeable.

Related, and not the same thing: ah-13o made the split *between* the unit and orders panels
draggable (PR #233). That was the vertical division within one side. This is the horizontal width of
each pane against the map.

## For the planner to settle with the navigator

- How the width is changed: a draggable edge, a keybinding, a setting.
- Whether the two panes resize independently.
- Whether a chosen width persists across sessions, or resets each time.
- Minimum and maximum widths, and what happens to the map when a pane grows.

## Validation

Manual: widen the left pane, confirm the map re-lays out and nothing is clipped; repeat for the
right.
design:
## Context

The two panes floating over the map have fixed widths — `w-[19rem]` (left, the region panel) and
`w-[21rem]` (right, the unit/orders column) at `AppShell.tsx:2888` and `:2896` — so the navigator
cannot trade map for panes: a wide map wants them narrower, a long order wants them wider. ah-13o
(PR #233) already made the *vertical* split inside the right rail draggable via `PanelSplitter.tsx`;
this bead is its horizontal sibling: each rail's width becomes draggable at a grip on the rail's
inner edge, with the same gestures, persistence and reset semantics.

Every user-facing choice was settled with the navigator in a mockup discussion; the chosen mockup
is committed at `docs/ui/rail-resize.html` (merged in PR #244) and its "Decisions" paragraph
records the outcome. Open it before building.

Structural fact that shapes everything: the rails are **absolute overlays** on the map. The overlay
row (`AppShell.tsx:2887`, `flex min-h-0 flex-1 justify-between gap-2.5`) pushes the two rails to
opposite edges with **live map between them — there is no shared gap to house a splitter**, unlike
the ah-13o one. The handle therefore lives *inside* each rail, hanging off its inner edge. The map
does **not** re-lay out when a rail resizes (MapCanvas's ResizeObserver watches only the host), and
the navigator chose to keep that: no re-fit on release.

All line numbers below are against `origin/main` at commit `f44e917`; verify with
`git show origin/main:<path>` if the file has moved on.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/panelLayout.ts` — the arithmetic (extend, don't fork)

The module already holds the split constants (`ORDERS_DEFAULT_REM` etc., lines 35–40) and the
clamp/drag pair `clampOrdersHeight` (60) / `dragOrdersHeight` (83, returns
`DragResult = { rem, atLimit }`). Add the width family beside them:

```ts
export const RAIL_LEFT_DEFAULT_REM = 19;   // today's w-[19rem]
export const RAIL_RIGHT_DEFAULT_REM = 21;  // today's w-[21rem]
export const RAIL_MIN_REM = 12;            // chosen by the navigator
export const RAIL_MAX_REM = 45;            // chosen by the navigator

export type RailSide = "left" | "right";

/** null unless finite; otherwise clamped into [RAIL_MIN_REM, RAIL_MAX_REM]. */
export function clampRailWidth(value: unknown): number | null;

/**
 * Resolve a drag. deltaRem is positive when the rail grows (the component maps pointer
 * direction per side). Ceiling: min(RAIL_MAX_REM, hostRem / 2) — a rail may never take more
 * than half the window (chosen); if the host is unmeasurable (Infinity), RAIL_MAX_REM rules.
 */
export function dragRailWidth(startRem: number, deltaRem: number, hostRem: number): DragResult;

/** { width: "<n>rem" } for a stored width, null for the default (the class width applies). */
export function railWidthStyle(widthRem: number | null): { width: string } | null;
```

Reuse `DragResult` as exported today; follow `clampOrdersHeight`'s shape for the clamp (accepts
`unknown`, rejects non-finite to `null`).

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/RailSplitter.tsx` — new component, modelled on `PanelSplitter.tsx`

`PanelSplitter.tsx` is the pattern; copy its mechanics, rotated. Public surface:

```ts
export type RailSplitterProps = {
  side: RailSide;                            // decides drag/arrow direction and position
  rail: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>;       // the rail div; width written directly during drag
  widthRem: number | null;                   // committed width, null = default
  defaultRem: number;                        // RAIL_LEFT_DEFAULT_REM or RAIL_RIGHT_DEFAULT_REM
  label: string;                             // aria-label, see the agreed strings below
  onCommit: (rem: number | null) => void;    // once per finished gesture
};
export function RailSplitter(props: RailSplitterProps): JSX.Element;
```

Mechanics to copy from `PanelSplitter.tsx` **verbatim in spirit**:
- `remPx()` from computed root font size (its lines 21–27) — honours browser zoom.
- Pointer drag (63–138 there): left button only; measure `startRem` from the rail's rect and
  `hostRem` from `rail.current?.parentElement?.getBoundingClientRect().width / remPx()`
  (`Infinity` when unmeasurable, for DOM-free tests); `guardSelection()`
  (`workspace/selectionGuard.ts`) and `pushDismissLayer()` + capture-phase Escape
  (`dismissStack.ts`, gated by `isTopDismissLayer`) — both are load-bearing, see Known traps;
  write `rail.current.style.width = `${rem}rem`` directly during the drag, no React state;
  commit only if moved; `pointercancel`/Escape restore the starting width.
- Direction: growing drag is pointer moving **toward the map** — for `side: "left"`,
  `deltaRem = (clientX - startX) / remPx()`; for `side: "right"`, `(startX - clientX) / remPx()`.
- Keyboard (its 140–150): **arrows move the edge in screen direction** (chosen):
  for the left rail ArrowRight grows and ArrowLeft shrinks; for the right rail ArrowRight
  *shrinks* and ArrowLeft grows. Step `SPLIT_STEP_REM` from `widthRem ?? defaultRem`, commit
  immediately. Enter commits `null` (reset). Double-click commits `null`.
- Markup: `role="separator"`, `aria-orientation="vertical"`, `tabIndex={0}`,
  `aria-valuemin={RAIL_MIN_REM}`, `aria-valuemax={RAIL_MAX_REM}`,
  `aria-valuenow={widthRem ?? defaultRem}`, `data-testid={`rail-splitter-${side}`}`,
  `pointer-events-auto touch-none cursor-col-resize` (the overlay layer is `pointer-events-none`,
  so without the opt-in the handle is dead).
- Position: absolutely inside the rail — `absolute inset-y-0 -right-2.5 w-2.5` for the left rail,
  `-left-2.5` for the right — a 10px strip straddling the inner border, vertically centring a grip
  pill (`w-1 h-8 rounded-full bg-edge`, `group-hover:h-12 group-hover:bg-brass`, dragging
  `bg-brass h-12`, at-limit `bg-amber-400 h-12` — the vertical rotation of `gripClassName` at
  `PanelSplitter.tsx:41–50`), plus `focus-visible:outline focus-visible:outline-1
  focus-visible:outline-brass`. Because the handle is a child of the rail div, it does **not**
  widen the rail's own `getBoundingClientRect`, so the map insets are untouched.

### `packages/shared/src/workspaceStore.ts` — two persisted fields

Copy `ordersHeightRem`'s round trip exactly (its field at line 80-ish `ordersHeightRem: number |
null`, action `setOrdersHeight` at 270, `Persisted` at 200, `partialize` at 298, per-key `merge`
clamp at 318, reset in `resetWorkspaceStore`):

```ts
leftRailWidthRem: number | null;    // initial null = the 19rem default
rightRailWidthRem: number | null;   // initial null = the 21rem default
setRailWidth: (side: RailSide, rem: number | null) => void;  // clamps via clampRailWidth
```

Both fields join `Persisted`, `partialize`, and `merge` (each read through `clampRailWidth`, never
spread — the merge builds its object key by key, keep that), and are cleared in
`resetWorkspaceStore`. They do **not** reset on `openGame`/`closeGame`/`setLevel` — a layout
preference outlives the game, exactly like `ordersHeightRem`. Import `clampRailWidth` at runtime
alongside `clampOrdersHeight` (line 15's import, which carries a comment about the type-only
reverse import — keep that arrangement).

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx` — wiring

- Two new refs beside `ordersSlotRef` (line ~440): `leftRailRef`, `rightRailRef`.
- Store reads beside the existing ones (~510): both width fields and `setRailWidth`.
- Left rail div (2888): add `relative`, attach `leftRailRef`, spread
  `style={railWidthStyle(leftRailWidthRem) ?? undefined}`, keep `w-[19rem]` (the style overrides
  it when set), render `<RailSplitter side="left" rail={leftRailRef}
  widthRem={leftRailWidthRem} defaultRem={RAIL_LEFT_DEFAULT_REM}
  label="Resize region panel" onCommit={(rem) => setRailWidth("left", rem)} />` as its last child.
- Right rail div (2896): same with `right`, `w-[21rem]`, `RAIL_RIGHT_DEFAULT_REM`, and
  `label="Resize unit and orders panels"`.
- The rails keep their default `flex-shrink:1` — on a window too narrow for the stored widths they
  compress, which is today's behaviour and the chosen narrow-window answer.

### `packages/shared/src/navigationGuide.ts` — the help overlay

One new entry in `NAVIGATION_MOVES` under the `PANELS` group, next to `panelFold` (line 205).
`NavigationMove.keys` is `{ mac: string; other: string } | null` (line 27). The agreed words:

```ts
{
  id: "railResize",
  group: PANELS,
  description: "Resize a side pane",
  mouse: "Drag the pill on its inner edge",
  keys: { mac: "Tab to the pill, then ← / →", other: "Tab to the pill, then ← / →" }
}
```

The module's contract (its header comment): a mouse gesture in the guide must be exercised by the
smoke suite — increment 4's test satisfies it.

## Increments

1. **Arithmetic.** Failing tests first in `panelLayout.test.ts`, sibling describes to the height
   ones: `describe("clampRailWidth")` — `"treats non-finite input as no preference"` (null),
   `"clamps a finite value into the stored range"` ([12, 45]); `describe("dragRailWidth")` —
   `"resolves a plain move"`, `"clamps at the rail minimum"`, `"caps at half the host"`
   (hostRem 60 → ceiling 30), `"caps at the rail maximum on a wide host"` (hostRem 200 → 45),
   `"flags atLimit only when the raw value overshot"`; `describe("railWidthStyle")` — `"is null

2. **Store.** Failing test in `workspaceStore.test.ts`, a describe beside `"the orders panel's

3. **Component + wiring.** Failing test `RailSplitter.test.tsx`, same DOM-free style as

4. **Smoke + guide.** Failing browser test in `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts` near the ah-13o

   `"a rail drags at its edge pill and survives a reload"` — drag `rail-splitter-left` 100px
   toward the map, assert the left overlay's box width grew accordingly, reload, assert it stuck;
   double-click the pill, assert the width is back to the 19rem default. Then the
   `navigationGuide.ts` entry, with its existing tests (`navigationGuide.test.ts`,
   `ShortcutHelp.test.tsx`) updated if they pin the move count.

## The test plan

- `packages/shared/src/workspace/panelLayout.test.ts` — increment 1's arithmetic.
- `packages/shared/src/workspaceStore.test.ts` — increment 2's persistence lifecycle.
- `packages/shared/src/workspace/RailSplitter.test.tsx` — increment 3's markup/keyboard/reset,
  DOM-free like `PanelSplitter.test.tsx`.
- `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts` — increment 4's drag/reload/reset, Chromium and WebKit.
- `packages/shared/src/navigationGuide.test.ts` / `ShortcutHelp.test.tsx` — keep green after the

- Run: `pnpm -C packages/shared test`, `pnpm run test:smoke`, and `pnpm run check` before the PR.

## User-facing decisions

Mockup: `docs/ui/rail-resize.html` (PR #244; the "Decisions" paragraph in the file records all of
this). The interview, in full:

1. **Handle style**: always-visible vertical grip pill on each rail's inner edge (variant B) —
   **chosen** over a hover-reveal edge line (variant A, rejected as undiscoverable — the same
   trade the navigator declined for ah-13o).
2. **Independence**: each rail resizes independently — chosen over one linked width (rejected: a
   wide orders editor should not force a wide region pane).
3. **Map behaviour on release**: the view is left alone; hexes may sit under a widened pane until
   the next Zoom to fit — chosen over re-fitting on release (rejected: the view would jump on
   every resize). This matches what folding a panel does today.
4. **Persistence**: widths persist with the workspace layout and reset by double-click or Enter on
   the pill — chosen over session-only (identical lifecycle to `ordersHeightRem`).
5. **Limits**: **12rem minimum, 45rem maximum, never more than half the window width** — the
   navigator chose the looser 12–45 range over my recommended 14–40. At a limit the pill turns
   amber, like the ah-13o grip.
6. **Arrow keys move the edge in screen direction**: ArrowRight grows the left rail and shrinks
   the right rail — chosen over "ArrowRight always widens" (rejected: on the right rail the pane
   would grow leftward while pressing Right).
7. **Labels**, verbatim: left handle `"Resize region panel"`; right handle
   `"Resize unit and orders panels"` — chosen over side-named labels ("Resize left pane"),
   keeping ah-13o's content-named precedent (`"Resize orders panel"`).
8. **Help-overlay entry**, verbatim: description `"Resize a side pane"`, mouse
   `"Drag the pill on its inner edge"`, keys `"Tab to the pill, then ← / →"` (both platforms) —
   chosen as quoted; appending "; double-click resets" was offered and declined.

## Out of scope

- Any change to the vertical unit/orders split (`PanelSplitter.tsx`) beyond reading its pattern.
- Re-fitting or panning the map when a rail resizes (explicitly declined).
- Collapsing a whole rail to nothing, responsive breakpoints, or touch-specific affordances.
- The bottom dock (`UnitTableDock`) and top chips — full-width overlays, untouched.
- New `ShortcutId` chords — the handle is reached by Tab, not by a global shortcut.

## Validation

- `pnpm -C packages/shared test` green; `pnpm run test:smoke` green on Chromium and WebKit;
  `pnpm run check` before the PR.
- Human check: drag each pill — the pane follows live and the map behind does not move; release,
  reload — widths kept; double-click — back to defaults; Tab to a pill — brass outline, arrows
  step 1rem in the screen direction of the arrow, Enter resets; drag to 12rem — pill turns amber;
  narrow the window below the stored widths — rails compress, nothing clips into a scrollbar;
  press ⌘/ — the guide lists "Resize a side pane" under Panels and windows.

## Known traps

- **The overlay layer is `pointer-events-none`** (`AppShell.tsx:2886`); every interactive child
  must opt back in with `pointer-events-auto`. A handle without it renders and is silently dead —
  the panels (`CollapsiblePanel.tsx:68`) and `PanelSplitter` (its line ~162) both carry the class.
- **`guardSelection()` and `pushDismissLayer()` are not optional.** WebKit anchors a text
  selection on whatever a drag crosses (the guard suppresses it), and Escape must cancel the drag
  even with a dialog-dismiss handler registered — `PanelSplitter` uses a capture-phase `keydown`
  gated by `isTopDismissLayer`. Copy both, or the smoke suite's WebKit project will catch it.
- **Do not put the handle outside the rail div**: a sibling inside the `data-map-overlay` element
  would add its 10px to the map insets read by `readInsets()` (`MapCanvas.tsx`, queries
  `[data-map-overlay]` rects). As a child of the rail div it costs nothing.
- **The smoke test `"fitting the map puts every hex clear of the panes drawn over it"`**
  (`workspace.spec.ts:~2299`) recomputes insets live. It passes as long as nothing resizes a rail
  *between* the fit and the assertion — do not add a resize into that test, and if the new smoke
  test fits the map, fit *after* the resize.
- **`"the map under a folded panel can be clicked"`** (`workspace.spec.ts:~1339`) derives its
  click rectangle from the right rail's geometry; run it after your changes — a leftover stored
  width in the test profile would move the rectangle. Use the ah-13o test's `resetSplit` helper
  pattern (line ~1241) to clear stored layout before asserting.
- **Persistence merge never spreads**: `workspaceStore.ts`'s `merge` builds the state key by key
  precisely so a hostile/stale blob cannot land on an action; add the two fields the same way,
  each through `clampRailWidth`.
- **Line-number drift**: ah-sup merged into these same files hours before this plan; all numbers
  here are from `origin/main` at `f44e917`. Verify against your checkout before relying on one.
acceptance_criteria: The width of the left pane and the width of the right pane can each be changed by the navigator. The map re-lays out to the remaining space.

title: Selected hex gets a high-contrast double ring and lock-on pulse
description:
The currently selected hex is highlighted, but the highlight is easy to lose track of — it does not
stand out enough to answer "which one am I on?" at a glance.

**The request:** emphasise it more. The navigator suggested red.

## For the planner to settle with the navigator

- The treatment itself: colour, outline weight, fill, or something else. Red is a suggestion rather
  than a decision.
- Whatever is chosen has to stay distinct from the other things a hex can be showing — hover,
  reachable, occupied, enemy — so a colour already carrying a meaning is worse than a weak
  highlight, not better. Enumerate the existing hex states before picking.
- Whether the emphasis needs to survive a colour-blind reading, or the map already relies on colour
  alone elsewhere.

## Validation

Manual: select a hex in a crowded part of the map and confirm it is findable without hunting.
design:
## Context

The selected hex is marked today by a single brass ring (`stroke-brass`, 2.5px, screen-constant)
drawn in `MapCanvas.tsx` — and brass is the map's busiest colour family: the route line, the export
marquee and the battle chip all use it, so the ring is easy to lose on a busy map. The navigator
confirmed the problem and chose a replacement in a mockup-driven discussion (see *User-facing
decisions*): a high-contrast achromatic **double ring** (bright ring over a dark casing), plus a
one-shot **lock-on pulse** when the selection changes by user action.

The chosen mockup is committed at `docs/ui/selected-hex-emphasis.html` (merged in PR #242) — open
it before building; the CHOSEN markers in it record every decision.

This work is entirely in `packages/shared`; both shells pick it up for free. The map is pure SVG
and currently has **zero animation machinery** — this bead introduces the map's first `@keyframes`,
with a `prefers-reduced-motion` guard.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `packages/shared/src/theme.css`

Two new colour tokens, in the dark `@theme` block (lines 36–94) **and** the light
`:root[data-theme="light"]` block (lines 118–164) — `theme.test.ts:119` fails the build if the two
blocks' token sets differ, and `theme.test.ts:37` fails it if any `#rrggbb` literal appears in a
`.ts`/`.tsx` file, so the colours must live here and nowhere else:

```css
/* dark block */
--color-selection-ring: #f5f8fc;
--color-selection-casing: #0a0e13;
/* light block (inverted pairing — chosen by the navigator) */
--color-selection-ring: #1c2530;
--color-selection-casing: #f5f8fc;
```

Tailwind v4 derives `stroke-selection-ring` / `stroke-selection-casing` utilities from `@theme`
tokens automatically, exactly as `stroke-brass` is derived today.

Also here: the pulse keyframes and class, next to the existing shared map classes (`.map-label` at
line 171 onward):

```css
@keyframes map-selection-lockon {
  from { transform: scale(1.6); opacity: 0.35; }
  to   { transform: scale(1);   opacity: 1; }
}
.map-selection-pulse {
  animation: map-selection-lockon 0.3s ease-out;
  transform-box: fill-box;
  transform-origin: center;
}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .map-selection-pulse { animation: none; }
}
```

`transform-box: fill-box` is what makes `scale()` act about the polygon's own centre; without it
SVG scales about the viewport origin and the ring flies in from a corner.

### `packages/shared/src/workspaceStore.ts`

The store owns "which hex is selected" (`selectedRegionId`, line 57; `selectRegion` implemented at
lines 226–231, a no-op when the id is unchanged). Add a monotonic epoch that counts **user-initiated
selection changes**, which is what the pulse listens to:

```ts
// in WorkspaceState
selectionEpoch: number;                       // bumped by selectRegion, never by restore
restoreSelection: (regionId: string | null) => void;
```

- `selectionEpoch` initial value `0`; reset to `0` wherever `selectedRegionId` is reset today
  (`openGame` line 210, `closeGame` line 217, `setLevel` line 238, `resetWorkspaceStore` line 313).
- `selectRegion` keeps its no-op-when-unchanged branch (so re-clicking the selected hex does not
  pulse) and otherwise bumps `selectionEpoch` alongside setting `selectedRegionId`.
- `restoreSelection(regionId)` sets `selectedRegionId` (and clears `selectedUnitId` the same way
  `selectRegion` does with no default unit) **without** touching the epoch. The restore path in
  `AppShell.tsx` — the `selectRegion(saved.regionId)` call at line 1685, inside a `useCallback`
  whose dependency array at line 1688 lists `selectRegion` and must be updated with it — switches
  to `restoreSelection`. Every other caller stays on `selectRegion` — the
  navigator chose "any change pulses, restore does not", and callers outside the map (unit lists,
  region problems) are changes.
- `selectionEpoch` is **not** persisted (the `Persisted` set at ~line 187 is unchanged).

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/MapCanvas.tsx`

Replace the single selection polygon at lines 899–909 with a group. Structure — outer group keeps
the world-space translate, inner group carries the pulse animation, so the CSS `transform` never
clobbers the SVG `translate`:

```tsx
{selectedAt && (
  <g transform={translateAt(selectedAt)} pointerEvents="none" data-testid="map-selection-ring">
    <g key={selectionEpoch} className={selectionEpoch > 0 ? "map-selection-pulse" : undefined}>
      <polygon points={HEX_POINTS} fill="none" className="stroke-selection-casing"
               strokeWidth={7} strokeLinejoin="round" vectorEffect="non-scaling-stroke" />
      <polygon points={HEX_POINTS} fill="none" className="stroke-selection-ring"
               strokeWidth={3} strokeLinejoin="round" vectorEffect="non-scaling-stroke" />
    </g>
  </g>
)}
```

- `key={selectionEpoch}` remounts the inner group on every user selection, restarting the CSS
  animation — the standard React way to replay a one-shot animation; no `requestAnimationFrame`,
  no timers.
- `selectionEpoch === 0` means "nothing user-selected yet this game" (fresh open or restore), so
  the class is omitted and a restored selection renders the static ring only — exactly the chosen
  behaviour.
- `selectionEpoch` arrives as a new prop next to `selectedRegionId` (wired in `AppShell.tsx:2831-2852`
  where `MapCanvas` is mounted; read from the store at ~`AppShell.tsx:490` with the other selectors).
- Both strokes stay `vectorEffect="non-scaling-stroke"` — screen-constant at every zoom, as chosen.
- The z-order does not move: the group replaces the old polygon in place, so it stays above the
  route line, risk tint and `MarkLayer`, and below the focus ring (lines 917–929) and the hit layer.
  The focus ring is untouched — the navigator chose "draw both" when they coincide.
- `selectedAt` (memo at lines 667–670) is untouched; the ring still renders on unexplored ground.

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/MapCanvas.test.tsx`

The route-measuring test at lines 207–229 carries the comment "`stroke-brass` is also the selection
ring's class…" and works around it. After this change no polygon carries `stroke-brass`; simplify
the workaround and update the comment while touching the file.

### `docs/ui/hex-rendering.md`

The layer-stack prose at §7–8 (lines 206–212) describes the old single brass ring. Rewrite those
lines to describe the double ring, its tokens, and the pulse; keep the section numbering.

## Increments

1. **Store epoch.** Failing test first: in `packages/shared/src/workspaceStore.test.ts` (the file
   exists), `"selectRegion bumps selectionEpoch, restore
   and re-selection do not"` — asserts epoch starts at 0, `selectRegion("r1")` → 1,
   `selectRegion("r1")` again → still 1, `restoreSelection("r2")` → still 1, `setLevel` resets to 0.
   Then implement `selectionEpoch`/`restoreSelection` as above.
2. **Tokens + double ring (static).** Failing test: in `MapCanvas.test.tsx`, `"marks the selected
   hex with a casing and ring pair"` — renders with a selected region, finds
   `[data-testid="map-selection-ring"]`, asserts two polygons with classes
   `stroke-selection-casing` (width 7) and `stroke-selection-ring` (width 3), both with
   `vector-effect`. Add the tokens to both theme.css blocks (the existing `theme.test.ts` parity
   and no-hex-literal guards must stay green), swap the polygon for the group, wire the
   `selectionEpoch` prop through `AppShell`, simplify the route-measuring test's brass workaround.
3. **Pulse.** Failing test: `"pulses on user selection but not on a restored one"` — render with
   `selectionEpoch: 0`, assert no `map-selection-pulse` class; re-render with epoch 1, assert the
   class is present. Add the keyframes/class/reduced-motion block to theme.css, switch the restore
   call in `AppShell.tsx` to `restoreSelection`.
4. **Smoke + docs.** Failing browser test first (in `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts`, near the focus
   ring specs at 2561–2586): `"the selected hex is marked by the double ring"` — click a hex,
   expect `map-selection-ring` attached and its `transform` to match the clicked hex's; then switch
   the map theme and expect it still attached (the ring is theme-independent). Assert presence, not
   animation — WebKit timing makes animation asserts flaky. Update `docs/ui/hex-rendering.md`.

## The test plan

- `packages/shared/src/workspaceStore.test.ts` — increment 1's epoch semantics test.
- `packages/shared/src/MapCanvas.test.tsx` (lives in `workspace/`) — increment 2's structure test,
  increment 3's pulse-class test, plus the simplified route measurement.
- `packages/shared/src/theme.test.ts` — no new code; the existing parity (line 119) and
  no-hex-literal (line 37) guards must pass with the new tokens.
- `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts` — increment 4's browser test, both Chromium and WebKit projects.
- Suites to run: `pnpm -C packages/shared test` (vitest) for the unit suites, `pnpm run test:smoke`
  (root) for the browser suite, and `pnpm run check` before the PR — that is the CI gate.

## User-facing decisions

Mockup: `docs/ui/selected-hex-emphasis.html` (chosen options marked CHOSEN in the file; iterated in
this planning session with the navigator, merged as PR #242).

1. **Treatment — which mark?** Options shown over a busy neighbourhood (route line, risk tint,
   unit shields, focus ring adjacent): **A** white 3px ring over 7px dark casing; **B** crimson
   ring (the navigator's own opening suggestion); **C** `--color-select` blue wash at 20% + bright
   ring; **D** brass corner reticle. **Chosen: A.** B rejected because red already means monster
   units, high risk and battle in every theme; C rejected because the wash tints terrain and blue
   is foreign units; D rejected as a new visual language with too little ink at far zoom.
2. **Focus ring landing on the selected hex:** both marks drawn, dashed focus ring on top —
   **chosen** over suppressing the focus ring (rejected: the cursor would vanish exactly when it
   reaches the selection).
3. **Motion:** a **one-shot lock-on pulse** — ring starts ~1.6× and contracts to fit, ~300ms
   ease-out, opacity 0.35→1 — chosen over a static ring and over a two-flash blink (rejected as
   easier to miss and more nagging). Suppressed entirely under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
4. **Pulse trigger:** **any selection change by click or keyboard, but not the silent restore at
   app load** — chosen over "every change incl. restore" and over "click only" (rejected: keyboard
   jumps are exactly where the eye loses the map). Re-selecting the already-selected hex does not
   pulse (store no-op).
5. **Light theme:** **inverted pairing** — near-black ring over pale casing — chosen over keeping
   white-over-dark in both themes (rejected: on light parchment the white ring washes out).
6. **Zoom:** **screen-constant** stroke widths at every zoom, like today's ring — chosen over
   scaling with the map (rejected: nearly invisible zoomed out, which is the original complaint).

No new user-visible text of any kind — no labels, no messages.

## Out of scope

- Any change to the keyboard focus ring, the export marquee, route rendering or the risk tints.
- A hover state (none exists today, none is added).
- Per-theme variations of the selection mark — it stays theme-independent in `MapCanvas`, one
  treatment across all five themes.
- Persisting `selectionEpoch` or changing what `mapViewportStorage.ts` saves.
- Any change to `aria-pressed` selection semantics on the hit polygons.

## Validation

- `pnpm -C packages/shared test` — all green, including `theme.test.ts`.
- `pnpm run test:smoke` — the new spec green on Chromium **and** WebKit; `pnpm run check` before
  the PR.
- Human check: open the app, click a hex on busy terrain — white double ring with a ~300ms lock-on
  contraction; arrow the cursor onto it — dashed ring appears on top; switch to the light theme —
  dark ring over pale casing; reload the app — the remembered hex shows the ring with **no** pulse;
  with the OS reduced-motion setting on, no pulse ever.

## Known traps

- **`theme.test.ts` guards:** any `#rrggbb` in a `.ts`/`.tsx` under `packages/shared/src` fails the
  build (line 37), and a token present in only one of the dark/light blocks fails parity (line 119).
  Both new tokens go in both blocks of `theme.css`, nothing anywhere else.
- **CSS `transform` vs SVG `translate`:** putting `map-selection-pulse` on the element that carries
  `transform={translateAt(...)}` makes the animation override the placement and the ring animates
  at the world origin. Hence the two-group structure; keep it.
- **`transform-box: fill-box`** is required for `scale()` to centre on the hex; omitting it scales
  about the SVG viewport origin.
- **The route-measuring test** (`MapCanvas.test.tsx:207-229`) currently special-cases the selection
  ring sharing `stroke-brass`; after the swap that workaround is stale and should be simplified,
  not left asserting a class that no longer exists there.
- **WebKit smoke flakiness:** assert the ring's presence and transform, never animation timing —
  the existing focus-ring specs (workspace.spec.ts:2561–2586) are the pattern to copy. Also note
  WebKit's driver returns `""` for text it considers clipped; irrelevant here as long as the specs
  stick to attributes.
- **Restore path:** the saved-view restore in `AppShell.tsx` (line 1685, deps array line 1688) must
  move to `restoreSelection`, or every app launch pulses — the one behaviour the navigator explicitly
  declined. `setLevel` clears the selection (store line 238) and resets the epoch, so switching
  levels never pulses either.
acceptance_criteria: The selected hex is identifiable at a glance in a crowded part of the map. The chosen treatment does not collide with the colour or styling of any other hex state.

title: Units from older turns are shown as if they were still there
description:
# Summary

Units seen in an earlier turn are still shown as though they were there now. **Only units named in
the latest report should be visible anywhere in the workspace.** A unit the faction saw three turns
ago may have moved, disbanded or been killed; showing it on a hex the faction cannot currently see
tells the player something the report does not say, and they plan against it.

The one exception is the turn comparison, which exists precisely to say what is no longer there.

# Where it comes from

The map remembers regions across turns, and a remembered region carries the units that were standing
in it when it was last seen. Nothing filters them out again.

`hexMapModel.ts:292-310` builds a hex from each `StoredRegion` with `knowledge: "stale"` and keeps
`region: stored.region` whole — units included — then derives `ownUnitCount`/`foreignUnitCount` from
it via `countUnits`. So a hex last seen in turn 21, displayed in turn 25, carries turn 21's units.

Everything downstream then believes them:

- **`unitsForHex` (`hexMapModel.ts:352`)** returns `hex.region.units` without consulting
  `hex.knowledge`, so a stale hex lists its old occupants.
- **`UnitTableDock.tsx:75`** feeds exactly that into the units table.
- **`hexView.ts:315,330`** draws the own/foreign unit badges from the stale counts, so the map shows
  unit badges on hexes nobody is looking at.
- **`AppShell.tsx:531, 893, 1461`** pick an initially selected unit from `unitsForHex`, so the
  workspace can open with a unit from an old turn selected.

Remembering the *terrain*, the settlement and the exits is correct and is what makes routes longer
than one step possible — this bead does not touch that. It is the **units** inside a remembered
region that must not survive into the present.

# Scope

- A hex the current report does not describe shows **no units**: none in the units table, none in the
  units-in-hex pane, no unit badges on the map, no unit tooltips, and it is never the source of an
  initially selected unit.
- The same rule wherever else units are read — the fix should make the stale case unrepresentable
  rather than filtered at each call site, if that is reasonable. The implementer audits every reader
  of `region.units`; the list above is where the bug is known to surface, not a guarantee that it is
  the whole of it.
- Anything a player can act on — writing an order, planning a route — must be impossible against a
  unit that is not in the latest report. This is the part that matters most: an order written for a
  unit that is no longer there is rejected by the server, and the player finds out a turn later.
- **The turn comparison keeps working exactly as it does**, including reporting units that were in
  the older turn and are not in the newer one. That view is about two named turns and says which one
  each fact came from; it is the one place a departed unit belongs.

# Out of scope

- Remembered **terrain**, provinces, settlements, structures and exits. The map is meant to keep
  those, and the movement planner depends on it.
- How stale hexes are drawn otherwise — the dimming, the age shading, the "last seen turn N" label
  all stay as they are.
- The turn comparison's own behaviour, beyond proving it still works.
- Allied reports merged into the *same* turn (issue #53). Those are current, not stale, and are not
  what this is about.

# A question for the planner

Whether a stale hex should say *something* where the units would be — "not seen since turn 21" in the
units pane, rather than an empty list that looks like an empty hex. An empty pane and a genuinely
empty hex would then be indistinguishable, which is a smaller version of the same bug. That is
user-facing and the navigator's call.

# Known traps

- **`countUnits` is called for stale regions as well as current ones**, so fixing `unitsForHex`
  alone leaves the map badges wrong — the counts come from a different path.
- **`mergeAlsoSeen` (`hexMapModel.ts:148-172`) adds units from an ally's report into the current
  turn's hex.** Those are current and must survive; a fix that strips units by asking "is this from
  the stored map" will remove them too.
- **Fixtures and tests may encode the present behaviour.** `congestedFixture.ts` builds hexes with
  unit counts directly; a test that asserts a stale hex lists units is asserting this bug and should
  change with it.
- **The map's own fixtures are large.** Prefer a small hand-built case for the new tests over
  extending a fixture whose failure will be hard to read.

# Validation

- Unit tests: a hex present only in the stored map lists no units, contributes no badge counts, and
  is never chosen as the initial selection; a hex in the current report is unaffected; an ally's
  units merged into the current turn still appear.
- A turn-comparison test proving a unit present in the older turn and absent from the newer is still
  reported as gone.
- Manually, against two committed consecutive turns: load the later one, find a hex last seen
  earlier, and confirm it shows terrain but no units and no unit badges — then open the comparison
  and confirm the departed units are named there.
- `pnpm run ci` (or the repo's usual gate) green, including the smoke suites, which touch the units
  table and the map badges.
design:
## Context

Bug: hexes remembered from earlier turns still carry the units that were standing in them when last
seen, and the whole workspace displays them as current — the units table, the map's unit badges and
guard marks, tooltips, the opening selection, and the movement planner (`PlannerPanel.tsx:34`
`canPlan = Boolean(unit?.own)` arms on a stale own unit). A player plans against a unit that may
have moved, disbanded or died; an order written for it bounces off the server a turn later.

Root cause, one place: `buildHexMapModel` (`packages/shared/src/hexMapModel.ts:292-311`) builds each
stale hex with `region: stored.region` whole — units included — and `...countUnits(stored.region)`.
Everything downstream then believes the region: `unitsForHex` (:351-362, no knowledge check),
`UnitTableDock.tsx:75`, `buildHexView` (`mapThemes/hexView.ts:303-342`, reading `ownUnitCount`,
`foreignUnitCount`, `countMonsters(units)` and `guardOf(units)`), the selected-unit lookup
(`AppShell.tsx:629-632`), and the opening selection (`hexMapModel.ts:338-348`, `withOwnUnits` scans
stale hexes too).

The fix makes the state unrepresentable at the source: **a stale `HexNode`'s `region` carries an
empty `units` array**, so every reader — present and future — is right by construction. No
per-call-site filtering.

Decided with the navigator: the units pane on a stale hex says why it is empty (wording below), and
the map export keeps its dated stale units (out of scope).

## Files to change, and what to reuse

**1. `packages/shared/src/hexMapModel.ts`** — the stale branch only, :292-311. Replace the last two
fields of the object literal:

```ts
    const remembered = stored.region ? { ...stored.region, units: [] } : null;
    byKey.set(key, {
      // ...unchanged fields...
      settlementName: stored.region?.settlement?.name ?? null,
      region: remembered,
      ...countUnits(remembered)
    });
```

`countUnits` (:127-135) of an empty list yields zero counts, keeping the invariant that counts
derive from `region`. Everything else in the file is untouched, and three things deliberately so:

- **`withAlliesUnits` (:137-173) must keep reading `stored.region.units` raw** — it merges an
  ally's same-turn sighting into the *current* hex (guard: `stored.lastSeenTurn !== currentTurn`
  returns early), and it takes `stored` from `storedByKey`, not from the built hex. Strip there, or
  in `gameMemory.ts`'s `toStoredRegions`, and allied units die with the bug.
- **Structures, settlement, exits, terrain stay remembered** — `{ ...stored.region, units: [] }`
  keeps them; the movement planner and `tallyStructures` depend on it (bead's out-of-scope).
- **The opening selection needs no guard of its own**: `withOwnUnits` (:340) keys on
  `ownUnitCount > 0`, which is now always 0 for stale hexes.

**2. `packages/shared/src/workspace/UnitTableDock.tsx`** — the two strings the navigator settled:

- The empty state (:282-286): when `units.length === 0` and `hex` is stale
  (`hex.knowledge === "stale"`), render
