Suites: `pnpm -r run test` and **`pnpm run test:smoke`** — increment 4 has no unit test, so the smoke
walk is the only thing that proves the view travels and returns.

## User-facing decisions

All the navigator's, 2026-08-17, against
`file:///Users/henrikku/repos/atlantis-hud/docs/ui/ah-60m-trade-arrow.html` (mockup in the scratchpad;
commit it with the work if it is worth keeping).

1. **A straight line between the two ends** (S1), with one head for a one-way run and two for a
   circuit. *Rejected: S2, drawing the travel route the turns figure comes from* — it would say "this
   is the journey" and match the turns count, but the path is computed to count turns and is not
   carried on the answer today, so the core's trade result would have to grow. **The accepted cost,
   stated in the mockup: a straight line cuts across water a land unit cannot cross.**
2. **When an end is off screen, the map zooms out to fit both while hovering** (E3). *Rejected: E1,
   drawing it anyway and letting it leave the viewport* — honest and free, but the reader cannot see
   how far, which is half the question. *Rejected: E2, pinning the far end to the edge with the
   distance beside it* — it draws a marker where the hex is not.
3. **The view snaps back when the pointer leaves**, and the arrow vanishes with it. The whole gesture
   is undone when you look away. *Rejected: staying where the fit left it* (sweeping five rows leaves
   you somewhere you never chose, with no arrow to explain why); *rejected: hover previews and a click
   pins it* (the click already flies to the buying hex).
4. **A route whose ends are both on screen does not move the map at all.** *Rejected: always fitting* —
   consistent, but the map would move on nearly every hover, including zooming *in* on a short route.
5. **The travel animates**, like flying to a selected hex. *Rejected: jumping instantly* — no wasted
   moment, but more disorienting on exactly the long jump this feature is for.
6. **It sits outside the layer system.** No chip returns. *Rejected: bringing back the "Trade routes"
   chip* — `LayerChips.tsx:11` records that it once sat there with nothing behind it and was removed
   because a control that does nothing is worse than no control; this is transient feedback tied to an
   open popover, not a layer you switch on and leave on.

**Two things I settled rather than asked**, both worth a sentence at review:

- **Keyboard focus behaves as hover does.** Every row is already a `<button>`, so a keyboard reader
  tabs through this list; hover-only would give them nothing. Invisible to a mouse user.
- **The wrapped-map-edge question does not arise.** The bead asks what the arrow looks like across a
  wrapped edge; this map does not wrap — there is no wrapping anywhere in `hexMapModel.ts`, and
  `worldOf` is a plain projection. Nothing to design.

## Out of scope

- **Drawing the journey** rather than the straight line (S2), and anything that would put a path on
  `TradeRoute`.
- **A Trade routes layer chip.**
- **Changing what clicking a row does.**
- **The trade calculation itself**, its ordering, its worth figure or its turns count — ah-1j5's, and
  passed.
- **Showing an arrow for anything else** — a planned route, a unit's destination. The map has its own
  overlay for those.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run check:fast
pnpm run test:smoke
```

Then the navigator's own check, and what Psylocke will repeat: load `g3-f42-t82`, open the Trade
popover, and sweep the list. Each row draws its arrow; the (36,4)→(0,48) row zooms the map out to hold
both ends and animates there; moving the pointer off the list puts the map back exactly where it was
and takes the arrow with it. A short route draws its arrow and moves nothing.

## Known traps

- **Remember the view once per gesture, not once per row.** Sweeping from row to row must return to
  where the reader was before the *first* hover — storing the current viewport on every hover would
  make "back" mean "the previous row's fit", and the map would never find its way home.
- **The popover can close mid-hover.** Dismissing it must run the same clearing path as
  `onHoverRoute(null)`, or the arrow and the fitted view both survive a popover that is no longer
  there.
- **`fitTo` returns `null`** for an empty list or a zero-sized viewport (line 227). Treat that as "do
  not move", not as a reason to skip drawing the arrow.
- **`pointerEvents="none"` on the arrow group.** It spans most of the map at the setting this feature
  is for, and without it the reader cannot click a hex underneath it.
- **`AppShell` has no unit test** — this package runs vitest in Node with no DOM. Increment 4's proof
  is the smoke walk, and it is not optional.
- **Insets matter.** `visibleRect` and `fitTo` both take them, and the map has overlay insets
  (`useOverlayInsets.ts`) for the panes that sit over it — pass the same ones the map already uses, or
  a "fitted" route lands under a pane.

title: A shortfall says the orders spend the items, whatever spent them
description:
Found while verifying ah-dbb.2 (Psylocke, 2026-08-17, origin/main 0ed5814). The navigator passed the bead; this is the follow-up filed alongside that pass.

ah-dbb.2 made CAST charge the ledger, so a mage short of what its spell costs is now warned through the existing not-enough-silver / not-enough-items reporting. The arithmetic is right. The sentence explaining it is not, because that reporting only had words for giving and selling.

On the committed turn-71 template (fixture neworigins-3.0.0-g7-f95-t71.rep), four mages in hex 1:26,52 CAST earm with no plate armor in the hex's shared stock, and the warning reads:

    the units in this hex are short 4 plate armor between them: they can have 0 and
    their orders give away or sell 4

Nothing is given and nothing is sold - the armor is consumed by a cast. The cost being paid: a player who trusts the message goes looking through their orders for a GIVE or a SELL that was never written, and the one line that actually caused the shortfall is the line the message does not name. A warning that misdescribes its own cause spends the player's time instead of saving it, which is the opposite of what these checks exist for.

The fix is in how the not-enough-items / not-enough-silver message names what spent the resource: casting needs a word of its own alongside give and sell, and the message should pick the one that matches the orders it actually found. Worth checking whether not-enough-silver has the same gap for a cast paid in silver, and whether any other intent added since (BUILD, PRODUCE, STUDY) reaches this reporting with no word of its own either.
design:
## Context

Found by Psylocke while verifying ah-dbb.2 (2026-08-17). The navigator passed that bead; this is the
follow-up filed alongside the pass.

ah-dbb.2 made `CAST` charge the ledger, so a mage short of what its spell costs is now warned through
the existing not-enough-silver / not-enough-items reporting. **The arithmetic is right. The sentence
explaining it is not**, because that reporting only ever had words for giving and selling. On the
committed turn-71 template four mages CAST `earm` with no plate armor in the hex's shared stock, and
the warning reads:

```
the units in this hex are short 4 plate armor between them: they can have 0 and
their orders give away or sell 4
```

Nothing is given and nothing is sold — the armor is consumed by a cast. A player who trusts the
message goes looking through their orders for a GIVE or a SELL that was never written, and the one
line that actually caused the shortfall is the line the message does not name. A warning that
misdescribes its own cause spends the player's time instead of saving it, which is the opposite of
what these checks exist for.

**What can charge the ledger**, checked while planning rather than assumed — six call sites, in
`crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`'s `transfer`, `buy`, `sell`, `study` and `cast`:

| Order | Charges | The message says |
|---|---|---|
| GIVE | items | "give away or sell" |
| SELL | items | "give away or sell" |
| **CAST** | **items** | **"give away or sell" — wrong** |
| BUY | silver | "spend" |
| STUDY | silver | "spend" |

So the silver half has never had this problem: "spend" already covers both of its causes. Only the
item half names its causes, and now names them wrongly. The bead asks whether BUILD, PRODUCE or
STUDY reach this reporting with no word of their own — **they do not**: BUILD and PRODUCE charge
nothing, and STUDY charges silver, which says "spend".

## Files to change, and what to reuse

The fix the navigator chose is one word in two places, making the item half read exactly like the
silver half.

### `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`

Two `format!` strings, both `give away or sell` → `spend`:

- **The per-unit message** (`shortfall`'s item branch, in the `else` beside
  `codes::NOT_ENOUGH_SILVER`'s branch):

```rust
                        "short {short} {name}: this unit can have {} and its orders spend {}",
```

- **The pooled message** (the `let message = if tag == SILVER { … } else { … }` beside it):

```rust
                 {held} and their orders spend {}",
```

Find them by the phrase rather than by line number — this file has changed three times today and
moves under a plan:

```bash
grep -rn "give away or sell" crates/core/src crates/core/tests packages
```

Five hits at `ec82563`: the two messages, two test assertions, one integration-test assertion and one
TypeScript settings description. All five change.

**The comment above the pooled message says the quiet part** and should be corrected with the code:
*"so the message can say 'they can have X and their orders spend/give away Y' the way the per-unit one
does"* — after this bead both say `spend`, so the slash goes.

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.tsx`

The `not-enough-items` entry in `WARNING_GROUPS` describes when the check fires:

```ts
        description: "Orders spend more of an item than the unit or the hex holds."
```

was `"Orders give away or sell more of an item…"`. Its own neighbour two lines above already reads
`"Orders spend more silver than the unit or the hex holds."`, so this makes the pair identical but for
the noun. See *User-facing decisions* — this one is a consequence I took rather than one the navigator
was asked about.

### Nothing else

No new code, no new intent handling, no change to the arithmetic or to which findings are produced.
`charged_at` (which records the first order to draw on a tag, for the finding's line) is untouched:
with one verb for every cause there is nothing to look up.

## Increments

One.

RED: change the four test assertions first — `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`'s two,
`crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs`'s one, and the `SettingsDialog` description if a test
pins it. The suite then fails against the two messages still saying "give away or sell".
GREEN: the two `format!` strings and the settings description.

That order is the whole of the discipline here: it proves the tests actually pin the wording rather
than being edited to agree with whatever the code now says.

## The test plan

No new tests — the wording is already pinned in four places, which is why this is small.

| Assertion | File | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `finding.message.contains("give away or sell")` | `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` | Becomes `contains("spend")`. **Keep its message** — "a SELL also charges the item" — it is why the assertion is about the shared verb and not about GIVE |
| the pooled-message `assert_eq!` (`…and their orders give away or sell 30`) | same | Becomes `…and their orders spend 30` |
| `items.message` `assert_eq!` | `crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs` | Becomes `…they can have 0 and their orders spend 4`. **This is the bead's own reproduction** — the four mages casting `earm` on the committed turn-71 template — so it is the assertion that proves the fix |
| (existing) `renders one toggle per advisory code` | `packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.test.tsx` | Unchanged; only the description text moves |

Suites: `cargo test --workspace` and `pnpm -r run test`, both inside `pnpm run check:fast`. No browser
suite — nothing renders differently except one line of settings prose.

## User-facing decisions

**The wording is the navigator's**, chosen 2026-08-17 against
`file:///Users/henrikku/repos/atlantis-hud/docs/ui/ah-49h-shortfall-wording.html` (mockup in the
scratchpad; commit it with the work if it is worth keeping):

> **V1 — one verb, `spend`.** `…they can have 0 and their orders spend 4`

Always true whichever order caused it, and the same word the silver half of this very message already
uses, so the two finally read alike. It stops naming the wrong order rather than starting to name the
right one — which the navigator accepted explicitly.

*Rejected: V3, naming every kind of order responsible* (`give away or cast with 8`) — truthful in
every case and closest to the phrase being replaced, but it costs a joined list and reads long at
three verbs. *Rejected: V2, naming the order that drew on it first* — wrong whenever two kinds of
order share the blame, since it would name whichever the ledger happened to record first: a guess
wearing a fact's clothes. *Rejected by implication: `cast with` and `consume` as a CAST verb* — with
V1 no verb is named at all.

**One consequence I took rather than asked about**, and it is worth a sentence at review: the
Settings › Warnings description for **Overdrawn items** changes from *"Orders give away or sell more
of an item…"* to *"Orders spend more of an item…"*. It is the same word in the same spirit, it makes
the entry match its silver neighbour exactly, and leaving it would put the old wrong wording in the
one place a player goes to read what a check is for.

## Out of scope

- **Naming which order caused a shortfall**, in any form. That is V2/V3, and both were rejected.
- **The silver message.** It already says "spend" and is already right.
- **`charged_at`, and the line a finding sits on.** The finding still points at the first order that
  drew on the tag; only the sentence changes.
- **BUILD and PRODUCE.** Neither charges the ledger, so neither reaches this reporting — checked, not
  assumed.
- **Whether a CAST *should* charge the ledger at all.** ah-dbb.2 decided that and the navigator passed
  it.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run check:fast
```

And the reproduction from the bead, which `validate_real_orders.rs` runs for you: the four mages
casting `earm` on the committed turn-71 template now read *"…they can have 0 and their orders spend
4"*. Nothing to look at in the application beyond that line and the Settings entry.

## Known traps

- **`crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` moves under a plan** — three separate beads changed it
  today. Use the `grep` above; do not trust a line number in this or any other document about this
  file.
- **There are two messages, not one.** The per-unit shortfall and the pooled one are built in
  different branches a few dozen lines apart, and a fix to one alone passes most of the suite: the
  bead's own reproduction is the *pooled* message, and the unit test that names `give away or sell`
  is the *per-unit* one.
- **The pooled message is a wrapped string literal** (`\` continuation), so the phrase is split
  across a line boundary in the source and a naive search for the whole sentence misses it.
- **Change the assertions first.** If the messages are fixed first, the four assertions are then
  edited to agree with the code and nothing has been proved.
- **Do not "improve" the assertion comment** *"a SELL also charges the item"* in
  `semantics.rs`. It explains why that test asserts the shared verb rather than a GIVE-specific one,
  and it is more true after this bead, not less.

title: One merge call for a single report and for a batch
description:
Second child of ah-sgn. mergeTurn splits into the merge itself and the read-back that follows it, so batchImport stops calling client.mergeReport directly to avoid the read-back.

The divergence is deliberate today (review of ah-u4e.3, PR #313: a batch reads the map back once at the end, and a read-back failure after a landed merge must not mark the step failed) - so the fix is to split the function, never to make the batch call the whole of it.

Depends on ah-sgn.1 only to keep two beads out of the same files at once.
design:
## Context

Second child of the epic ah-sgn. **Read the epic's `design` field first.**

Merging an ally's report is done two ways. `AppShell.mergeReport` (line 1011) calls `mergeTurn`
(`gameMemory.ts:260`), which merges and then reads the map back. `walkBatch`
(`batchImport.ts:199`) calls `client.mergeReport` directly, on purpose, with eleven lines of comment
saying why: the walk reads the map back once at the end, so a read-back per merged step is wasted
work — **and worse, a read-back failure after a merge that itself succeeded would mark a landed step
as failed** (review of ah-u4e.3, PR #313).

That reasoning is right, and this bead does not undo it. What it removes is the shape it was
expressed in: a second call site composing the client by hand, so a change to how a merge lands has
to be made twice and was, in ah-u4e.3, made once — `tsc` found the other caller, and the review then
found the latent bug in it.

`gameMemory.ts` already has the pattern this wants: `commitTurn` (line 137) is "the half of
`rememberTurn` that writes", split out for exactly this reason — "thirty reports mean thirty commits
but only one map worth looking at". Merging simply never got the same treatment.

There is also a defect to fix while the seam is being cut, and the navigator has approved it:
**`mergeTurn` does its own three reads inline and lets them throw**, so a merge that reached the
database but whose sightings read failed is reported to the player in red as a failed merge — the
same class of bug the review caught on the batch side, in the one place it was not looked for. Its own
doc comment already claims otherwise ("Resolving the map afterwards is not held to that").

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `packages/shared/src/gameMemory.ts`

**One new exported function**, named for the symmetry that already exists — `commitTurn` is to
`rememberTurn` as `commitMerge` is to `mergeTurn`:

```ts
/**
 * Folds an ally's report into the viewer's map for this turn, and stops there.
 *
 * The half of [`mergeTurn`] that writes, split out for the same reason [`commitTurn`] is split out
 * of [`rememberTurn`]: a batch merges many reports and reads the map back once at the end, so a
 * read-back per merged step is work thrown away - and a read-back failure after a merge that itself
 * landed would mark a landed step as failed (review of ah-u4e.3, PR #313).
 *
 * Throws when the merge does not land. There is nothing to salvage: a status line saying the merge
 * worked over a database that was never written would be a lie.
 */
export async function commitMerge(
  client: CoreClient,
  game: OpenedGame,
  viewerFactionId: string,
  viewerTurnNumber: number,
  rawReport: string,
  rulesetJson: string | null,
  now: string
): Promise<ReportMergeResult> {
  return client.mergeReport(
    game.databasePath,
    game.manifest.metadata.gameId,
    viewerFactionId,
    viewerTurnNumber,
    rawReport,
    rulesetJson,
    now
  );
}
```

**`mergeTurn` keeps its signature and its `MergeOutcome`** and becomes the two halves, with the
read-back going through `readMemory` (line 178) rather than through a third hand-written copy of the
same three calls:

```ts
export async function mergeTurn(/* unchanged parameters */): Promise<MergeOutcome> {
  const result = await commitMerge(
    client, game, viewerFactionId, viewerTurnNumber, rawReport, rulesetJson, now
  );
  // The read half, and the same trade it makes everywhere else: the merge has landed, so a memory
  // or map failure now is a warning on a turn that is still on screen and still correct - not a
  // merge reported as failed after it was written (navigator, 2026-08-17).
  const memory = await readMemory(
    client, game, viewerFactionId, viewerTurnNumber, viewerRawReport, rulesetJson
  );
  return { ...memory, result };
}
```

`MemoryOutcome` is `KnownMemory & { merged, warning }` (line 74) and `MergeOutcome` is that plus
`result` (line 236), so `{ ...memory, result }` **is** a `MergeOutcome` — no new field, no reshaping.

`mergeTurn`'s doc comment (lines 246–259) needs its last paragraph rewritten: what throws is now the
merge alone, and the read half warns like every other read in the module. Keep the first two
paragraphs — where the regions land, and that nothing else about the workspace moves — word for word.

### `packages/shared/src/batchImport.ts`

The direct client call (lines 199–207) becomes:

```ts
        await commitMerge(
          client,
          game,
          viewerFactionId as string,
          step.turnNumber,
          source.text,
          rulesetText,
          now()
        );
```

**Keep the whole comment above it** (lines 190–198) — the `viewerFactionId as string` justification
and the read-back reasoning are both still exactly right — but rewrite its last sentence: it no longer
calls `client.mergeReport` "rather than `mergeTurn`", it calls `commitMerge`, which is the half that
writes, and the walk supplies the read half itself in `runBatch`'s `readMemory` call.

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx`

**No edit.** `mergeReport` already renders `outcome.warning` as an amber `warningStatus` and only a
thrown error as a red `failedStatus` (lines 1029–1034), which is precisely the behaviour the navigator
asked for. That is why this bead is small.

## Increments

1. **The write half.** RED: the two `commitMerge` tests below, in `packages/shared/src/gameMemory.test.ts`.
   GREEN: `commitMerge`, and `mergeTurn` calling it while keeping its own three reads for now.
2. **The read half, and the failure it changes.** RED: `a merge that landed is not reported as failed
   when the map cannot be read back` — today `mergeTurn` rejects, so the test fails.
   GREEN: `mergeTurn` composed of `commitMerge` and `readMemory`.
3. **The batch shares the write half.** RED: `merges through the same call the single-report path
   writes with` in `packages/shared/src/batchImport.test.ts`. GREEN: the `batchImport.ts` edit.

## The test plan

| Test | File | What it pins |
|---|---|---|
| `merges under the viewer's faction and turn, and stops there` | `gameMemory.test.ts` | `commitMerge` calls `client.mergeReport` with the seven arguments in order, and calls **neither** `loadRegionSightings` nor `loadMergedReports` nor `knownMap` |
| `throws when the merge does not land` | same | A rejected `mergeReport` rejects — the batch's `catch` depends on it to demote a step to a skip |
| `a merge that landed is not reported as failed when the map cannot be read back` | same | **The behaviour change**: `loadRegionSightings` rejects, `mergeTurn` still resolves, `result` is the merge's own result, and `warning` says `the turn could not be remembered: …` |
| (existing, line 319–389) `merging an ally's report into the turn on screen` | same | Unchanged assertions: what is merged, what comes back, and that an older report still rejects |
| `merges through the same call the single-report path writes with` | `batchImport.test.ts` | `client.mergeReport` still receives exactly what it received before (line 141's assertion, unchanged) |
| (existing) `does not read the map back after each merged step` | same | If no such test exists, **add it**: `loadRegionSightings` is called once by `runBatch`, never per merge step. This is ah-u4e.3's finding, and after this bead it is one line away from regressing |
| (existing, line 179) a merge step that will not land becomes a skip | same | The `catch` still sees a throw |

Suites: `pnpm -r run test`. The smoke suite is not required — no component changes — but
`tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts:771` ("merging leaves the orders and the selection where they were")
is the end-to-end net and CI runs it.

## User-facing decisions

One, taken by the navigator on 2026-08-17:

> **A merge that reached the database reports success**, with an amber warning if the map could not be
> read back afterwards — `the turn could not be remembered: …` — rather than the red
> `could not merge <file>: …` it shows today. A reload shows the merge either way, so the red message
> was misleading.

Rejected: keeping every failure red and narrowing this bead to the function split; doing it as a
separate bead.

Nothing else the player sees changes: not the words of `describeMerge`, not the "+1 merged" chip, not
the selection, the orders or the map. The warning text is `readMemory`'s existing string — do not
write a new one for this path.

## Out of scope

- **Which reports a batch merges at all**, the ceiling rule, and `chooseViewerFaction`. See the epic.
- **`rememberTurn`/`commitTurn`.** They are already split; leave them.
- **Making the batch read the map back per step.** That is the bug this bead is protecting, not
  fixing.
- **`AppShell.mergeReport`.** The comment above it warns that "it will be tempting to make this look
  more like `applyReport`; that temptation is the bug". Nothing here touches it.
- **The core's `command_merge_report`** and everything on the Rust side.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run check:fast
```

And the check a person makes: with a turn on screen, merge an ally's report for that same turn. The
status line says what `describeMerge` says, the "+1 merged" chip appears, and the orders, the selected
hex and the map's position are all exactly where they were.

## Known traps

- **The batch's `catch` turns a throw into a skip** (`batchImport.ts:210`), so `commitMerge` must keep
  throwing on a failed merge. If it were softened to return a warning like its read-half neighbours,
  every failed merge in a batch would be counted as a landed step.
- **`viewerFactionId as string`** in the batch's call is deliberate and its comment explains why
  (`planReportBatch` never raises a step unless `viewer.factionId` is non-null). Keep both.
- **`readMemory` swallows and warns; `commitMerge` throws.** That asymmetry is the whole design of
  this module — write failures are failures, read failures are warnings. Do not "tidy" it into one
  behaviour.
- **`ah-sgn.1` touches `batchImport.ts` too** (`prepareBatch` and `BatchCandidate`), which is the only
  reason this bead is blocked by it. Rebase on main after ah-sgn.1 merges rather than branching from
  an older tip.
- **`mergeTurn`'s parameter list stays as it is**, `viewerRawReport` last. It is the report already on
  screen, and it is what the map is resolved against — not the ally's report, which is `rawReport`.
  Swapping the two compiles perfectly and silently draws the ally's map.

title: A report is judged usable in one place, whether it arrives alone or in a batch
description:
First child of ah-sgn. One shared answer to 'can this report be imported at all', replacing the copy in decideReportLoad and the copy in planReportBatch.

The navigator settled the two behaviour differences this exposes (2026-08-17): a report naming no turn, and a report with no regions and no units, are both refused on the single-file path too, reported through the red import status line that already carries 'the report does not name its faction'.
design:
## Context

First child of the epic ah-sgn. **Read the epic's `design` field first** — it carries the navigator's
four decisions and, just as importantly, which parts of these two pipelines are *not* duplication and
must be left alone.

"Can this report be imported at all" is answered twice, and the two answers disagree:

| The report | One file at a time (`decideReportLoad`, `reportLoadDecision.ts:78`) | Twenty at a time (`planReportBatch`, `reportBatch.ts:128`) |
|---|---|---|
| Names no faction | `reject` (`REPORT_NAMES_NO_FACTION`) | skip, same constant, shared since ah-brd |
| Names no turn | **accepted** — becomes the working turn | skip, `"the report does not name its turn"` |
| No regions and no units | **accepted** — replaces a populated map | accepted |

The first row was already shared, and only because ah-brd (P1, found by Psylocke) had to thread a
`reject` case through five production files after the single-file path accepted a factionless report
and wiped the map, regions and orders on screen. Its second commit says outright: "this bead exists to
keep the single-file and batch paths from drifting apart". The other two rows are the same drift,
still there.

After this bead **one function** answers the question, both front doors call it, and the answers in
that table are identical — with rows two and three refused, as the navigator decided.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `packages/shared/src/reportLoadDecision.ts` — the one owner

Two new exported constants beside `REPORT_NAMES_NO_FACTION` (line 31), and one new function. The
strings are the navigator's, quoted exactly:

```ts
export const REPORT_NAMES_NO_TURN = "the report does not name its turn";
export const REPORT_HAS_NOTHING_IN_IT = "the report has no regions or units in it";

/** Whether a report can be imported at all, and why not when it cannot. */
export type ReportUsability = { ok: true } | { ok: false; reason: string };

/**
 * Whether this report can be imported at all - the one answer, for a file dropped on its own and
 * for one of twenty in a batch alike.
 *
 * The three conditions are the Rust core's own `meets_minimum_import_threshold`
 * (`crates/core/src/lib.rs:247`): a turn, a faction, and something in it. Kept in step with that
 * function by hand and by the test named in this bead's plan - the shells hold a `ParsedReport`
 * from `parseReportFull`, not the `ReportParseResult` that carries the core's flag, so reading the
 * flag would cost a second parse of every imported file.
 *
 * Order matters only for which reason the player is told first, and it goes from the most basic
 * fact outwards: who it is from, when it is from, what is in it.
 */
export function judgeReportUsable(report: ParsedReport): ReportUsability {
  if (report.header.factionId === null) {
    return { ok: false, reason: REPORT_NAMES_NO_FACTION };
  }
  if (report.header.turnNumber === null) {
    return { ok: false, reason: REPORT_NAMES_NO_TURN };
  }
  if (report.regions.length === 0) {
    return { ok: false, reason: REPORT_HAS_NOTHING_IN_IT };
  }
  return { ok: true };
}
```

`report.regions.length === 0` is the whole of the third condition: the core's rule is "no regions
**and** no units", and a unit only exists inside a region in `ParsedReport`
(`crates/core/src/report/mod.rs:53`, `units()` flat-maps the regions), so no regions implies no units.
Say that in a comment — the next reader will otherwise "fix" it into a second clause that can never
fire.

This module currently imports no types. Importing `ParsedReport` from `@atlantis/core-client` is
fine — `reportBatch.ts` beside it already imports from there — and it stays a plain module with no DOM.

**`decideReportLoad` loses its `reject` branch** (line 82–84) and its `reject` variant
(line 41). It becomes purely "load / storeOnly / ask": usability is judged before it is reached, and
two owners of one rule is the thing being removed. Its header comment gains a line saying where the
rule went.

### `packages/shared/src/reportLoad.ts`

`routeReport` (line 230) judges first, and keeps its own `ReportRoute`'s `reject` variant (line 221) —
that is the shape `AppShell` already handles:

```ts
  const usable = judgeReportUsable(report);
  if (!usable.ok) {
    return { kind: "reject", reason: usable.reason };
  }
```

directly above the existing `decideReportLoad` call, whose `decision.kind === "reject"` branch
(lines 241–243) then goes with it.

Nothing else changes. `AppShell.loadReport` (line 950) already throws on `kind: "reject"` so that
`runReported`'s `could not read <file>: …` prefix and red status apply — which is exactly the
presentation the navigator chose, so **there is no `AppShell` edit in this bead**.

### `packages/shared/src/reportBatch.ts` and `batchImport.ts`

`BatchCandidate` (`reportBatch.ts:17`) gains the verdict, computed where the full report is still to
hand:

```ts
export type BatchCandidate = {
  fileName: string;
  factionId: string | null;
  turnNumber: number | null;
  /** `judgeReportUsable`'s answer for this file. `{ ok: false }` for one that would not even parse. */
  usable: ReportUsability;
};
```

- `prepareBatch` (`batchImport.ts:52`) sets it: `usable: judgeReportUsable(report)` on the success
  path, and `usable: { ok: false, reason: REPORT_NAMES_NO_FACTION }` on the parse-failure path — that
  branch already sets `factionId: null` for the same reason, and its own `unreadable` entry is what
  the player is actually shown ("`could not be read: …` says what actually went wrong", line 73).
- `planReportBatch` (`reportBatch.ts:128`) replaces its first two skip branches (lines 141–155) with
  one:

```ts
    if (!candidate.usable.ok) {
      skipped.push({ index, fileName: candidate.fileName, reason: candidate.usable.reason });
      continue;
    }
```

  The third branch — "there is no faction of your own to import it into" (lines 156–164) — **stays**:
  that is about the workspace, not about the report, and it has no counterpart on the single-file
  path. `REPORT_NAMES_NO_FACTION`'s import goes if nothing else uses it.
- After the branch, `candidate.turnNumber` is still typed `number | null`. The existing
  `usable.push({ …, turnNumber: candidate.turnNumber, … })` needs a non-null assertion or a local
  narrowing; prefer narrowing by keeping a `const turnNumber = candidate.turnNumber; if (turnNumber === null) continue;`-free
  shape — the honest answer here is one `as number` with a comment saying `judgeReportUsable` has
  already refused a null turn, in the style of `batchImport.ts:191`'s `viewerFactionId as string`
  and its comment.

### Test fixtures

`BatchCandidate` gaining a required field means every test literal that builds one must set it. That
is deliberate — an optional field would let a caller forget the judgement, which is the defect. Expect
`reportBatch.test.ts` and `batchImport.test.ts` to need a small helper (`candidate({ … })`) if they do
not already have one.

## Increments

1. **The one function.** RED: the five `judgeReportUsable` tests below, in
   `packages/shared/src/reportLoadDecision.test.ts`. GREEN: the constants, the type and the function.
2. **The single-file door.** RED: rewrite `reportLoadDecision.test.ts`'s "rejects a report that names
   no faction, whatever is on screen" (line 101) as a test of `judgeReportUsable`, and add the two new
   route tests in `reportLoad.test.ts` beside "rejects a report with no faction and says why"
   (line 255). GREEN: `routeReport` judges first; `decideReportLoad` loses its `reject` branch and
   variant.
3. **The batch door.** RED: a `planReportBatch` test that an unusable candidate is skipped with the
   verdict's own reason. GREEN: `BatchCandidate.usable`, `prepareBatch` filling it, and the collapsed
   branch.

## The test plan

| Test | File | What it pins |
|---|---|---|
| `refuses a report that names no faction` | `reportLoadDecision.test.ts` | Reason is `REPORT_NAMES_NO_FACTION` |
| `refuses a report that names no turn` | same | Reason is `REPORT_NAMES_NO_TURN` — the behaviour change on the single-file path |
| `refuses a report with nothing in it` | same | Reason is `REPORT_HAS_NOTHING_IN_IT`, wording exact |
| `names the faction before the turn before the contents` | same | A report failing all three reports the faction — so the reason is stable rather than incidental |
| `accepts a report with a faction, a turn and one region` | same | The floor, and that one region with no units is enough |
| `refuses an unnumbered report rather than loading it` | `reportLoad.test.ts` | `routeReport` → `{ kind: "reject", reason: REPORT_NAMES_NO_TURN }`, whatever is on screen |
| `refuses an empty report rather than replacing what is on screen` | same | The map-wiping case from ah-brd, in its second form |
| (rewritten) `rejects a report with no faction and says why` | same | Still rejected, now via the shared judgement — pin it to the constant, as ah-brd's second commit did |
| `skips a report the shared judgement refuses, with its reason` | `reportBatch.test.ts` | One branch, the verdict's own words |
| `still skips a usable report when there is no faction of your own` | same | The third branch survived the collapse |
| (existing) every other `reportBatch.test.ts` / `batchImport.test.ts` case | unchanged assertions | The candidate's new field changed no batch behaviour |

Suites: `pnpm -r run test`. The smoke suite is not required — `AppShell` is untouched — but CI runs
it, and `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts`'s import tests are what would notice if the status line
stopped saying what it says.

## User-facing decisions

All four are the navigator's, taken 2026-08-17, and recorded **in full with their rejected
alternatives in the epic ah-sgn's `design` field**. In short:

- A report naming **no turn** is refused on both paths (today the single-file path accepts it).
- A report with **no regions and no units** is refused on both paths (today the single-file path
  accepts it and wipes a populated map), adopting the core's own
  `meets_minimum_import_threshold` rule.
- A refusal is the **existing red import status line** — `could not read turn-70.rep: <reason>` — and
  nothing on screen changes. **No dialog**, and never silent.
- The wording of the new reason, exactly: **`the report has no regions or units in it`**. Its two
  neighbours keep their words: `the report does not name its faction`, `the report does not name its
  turn`.

Do not re-open any of these, and do not invent a fourth reason string.

## Out of scope

- **The age and ownership rules.** `storeOnly` for an older report, `ask` for a foreign one, and the
  batch's own ceiling and `chooseViewerFaction` are deliberate policy differences between one file and
  twenty, explained at length in both module headers. Leave them, and leave those headers.
- **`mergeTurn` and the batch's merge step** — ah-sgn.2.
- **Reading `meetsMinimumImportThreshold` off the wire.** Considered and rejected while planning: the
  shells hold a `ParsedReport` from `parseReportFull`/`parseReportClassified`, not the
  `ReportParseResult` that carries the flag, so reading it would mean a second parse of every imported
  file or a new field on a persisted type. The TS function names the core function it mirrors instead.
- **Removing the unread flag from the wire.** It is part of a persisted shape; not this bead's
  argument.
- **`commitTurn`'s defensive faction check** (`gameMemory.ts:145`). It says it is unreachable and kept
  as defence for a future caller; that is still true and still right.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run check:fast
```

Then the check a person makes, and the one this bead is really for: drop a truncated report — a real
one with its header lines and nothing after them — onto a workspace showing a full turn. The status
line goes red and says `could not read <file>: the report has no regions or units in it`, and the map,
the regions and the orders on screen are exactly as they were.

## Known traps

- **`decideReportLoad` losing its `reject` variant is a type change with reach.** `routeReport` maps
  it, `reportLoad.test.ts` and `reportLoadDecision.test.ts` assert on it. Follow the compiler, and do
  not leave the variant behind "just in case" — an unreachable branch that used to be the rule is
  exactly what the next reader will copy.
- **`ReportBatchPlan`'s indices are the chosen files' indices**, and every skip carries one because a
  file name is not an identity (`reportBatch.ts:31–37`: two folders dragged together can hand over two
  files called `turn.rep`). Collapsing the two skip branches must not disturb `index`.
- **`prepareBatch`'s parse-failure branch already has its own reason** (`could not be read: …`, in
  `unreadable`), and that is what the player sees for such a file. The `usable` field it sets is only
  so the plan skips it; do not report both.
- **The core's rule and this function must be read together.** If `meets_minimum_import_threshold`
  (`crates/core/src/lib.rs:247`) ever gains a condition, this function is where it has to be repeated.
  The comment naming it is load-bearing — keep it, and keep the file:line.
- **Do not add a turn-number check to `decideReportLoad`'s `isOlderTurn`** (`reportLoadDecision.ts:60`).
  It answers false for an unnumbered report on purpose ("refusing to say which of two unknowns came
  first is more honest than guessing"), and now no unnumbered report ever reaches it anyway.

title: An Interface size setting scales the panes without touching the map
description:
Second half of ah-46p, and the visible feature. Depends on ah-46p.1, which puts the pane type on rem tokens - a multiplier cannot reach an absolute pixel.

A control in Settings' **Global** tab, since it is about this reader's eyes rather than about a game: a stepped scale (Small / Normal / Large / Larger) that multiplies the pane type tokens. The map is unaffected, which is the whole point - full-page zoom already scales both and is the unhelpful trade this bead exists to replace.

Still open for its own planning session: the exact steps and their multipliers, whether the setting is a slider or a select, what it is called and described, whether it persists per machine or per game, and what happens to a pane the reader has dragged narrow when the text grows inside it.
design: ## Context `ah-46p.1` merged this morning (PR #370, `fb1b2a1`): the panes' 67 hard-coded pixel sizes became three rem tokens in `packages/shared/src/theme.css:113-119`. ```css --text-pane-sm: 0.6875rem; /* 11px at a 16px root */ --text-pane: 0.75rem; /* 12px */ --text-pane-lg: 0.8125rem; /* 13px */ ``` So a reader who raises their **browser's** font size now sees the panes grow. This bead adds a control inside the app, for the reader who would rather not change their browser, or who wants the panes bigger and the rest of the web left alone. It is the second and last half of `ah-46p`. **The map is provably safe, and by design rather than by luck.** `theme.css:115-117` says it: *"The map sets its own sizes and is not on this scale."* Every piece of map text carries its own explicit size — SVG `fontSize` numbers (`MapCanvas.tsx:1192, 1218, 1228, 1250, 1253, 1262, 1270`) or `px` in the theme stylesheets (`theme.css:209-210`, `:277-279`, and the five `mapThemes/*/theme.css`) — and `MapCanvas.tsx` uses `text-pane` **zero** times. Nothing in the map inherits a font size, so scaling the three tokens cannot reach it. There is no `rem` or `em` anywhere in the map theme stylesheets. **All settings here are global.** `SettingsDialog.tsx:434-436` states it: *"Global in scope — 'per game' is not a settings scope today"*. The Per game tab changes the game's ruleset through a callback and nothing else. Interface size is a property of the reader's eyes, not of a game, so it belongs in the Global tab beside *Pane transparency*. **The hazard, and it is not a CSS problem.** The units dock is virtualised: every row must be a known, identical height for the scroll arithmetic to work, so each is pinned by an inline style (`UnitTableDock.tsx:508`) to `ROW_HEIGHT = 22` (`unitTable.ts:11`), and that same constant drives scroll offsets and the scroller's total height (`UnitTableDock.tsx:83, 128, 130, 134, 391`). Scaling only the type would put 22px text in a 22px box at 200%. The navigator chose to make the row height follow the scale (decision 2), which makes this a TypeScript change and not only a stylesheet one. ## Files to change, and what to reuse Line numbers are at `fb1b2a1`. ### `packages/shared/src/theme.css` — the multiplier Two edits. First, beside `--pane-transparency` in the plain `:root` block (`:302`) — **not** inside `@theme`: ```css /* What the Interface size setting multiplies the pane type scale by; 1 is 100%. Stamped on the root by `settingsStore`, exactly as `--pane-transparency` is, and defaulted here so the app renders correctly before the store has run and in any test that mounts a component alone. */ --ui-scale: 1; ``` Second, the three tokens inside `@theme` (`:117-119`) become products: ```css --text-pane-sm: calc(0.6875rem * var(--ui-scale, 1)); /* 11px at a 16px root, at 100% */ --text-pane: calc(0.75rem * var(--ui-scale, 1)); /* 12px */ --text-pane-lg: calc(0.8125rem * var(--ui-scale, 1)); /* 13px */ ``` Why this and not the alternative: - **The tokens stay in `rem`, so both dials still work and multiply.** The reader's browser preference sets the root, and this setting scales on top of it. That was the whole point of `ah-46p.1` and must not be undone. - **Scaling the tokens, rather than setting a root `font-size`, is what keeps the map and the layout still.** The rails are sized in `rem` — `RAIL_LEFT_DEFAULT_REM = 19`, `RAIL_RIGHT_DEFAULT_REM = 21`, `RAIL_MIN_REM = 12`, `RAIL_MAX_REM = 45` (`panelLayout.ts:119-122`), applied as `width: Nrem` (`:154-159`) — as are `ORDERS_*_REM` (`:35-39`), the units-pane heights (`:162-167`) and the map's own zoom buttons (`MapCanvas.tsx:1356`, `h-7 w-7`). A root `font-size` would move all of them. Redefining only the three tokens moves only type. - **The `, 1` fallback** means a component mounted without `theme.css` still gets the base size rather than an invalid `calc()`. - **`--ui-scale` goes outside `@theme`** because `@theme` is Tailwind's utility-generating namespace and this is not a utility. `--pane-transparency` is the precedent and lives in the plain block. Tailwind is **v4, CSS-first**: there is no `tailwind.config.*` and no `postcss.config.*` anywhere. `theme.css` is the whole configuration (`:1` `@import "tailwindcss"`, `:21-23` the `@source` lines, `:36-120` `@theme`). The `--text-*` namespace is what generates the `text-pane*` utilities, each compiling to `font-size: var(--text-pane*)` — a runtime `var()` reference, which is why putting a `calc()` in the token's value reaches every use. ### `packages/shared/src/settingsStore.ts` — the setting `paneTransparency` is the pattern to copy, and it has **six** parts. Miss the last one and the setting works until the page is reloaded. ```ts /** The Interface size setting's default, as a percentage. 100 means the panes are as designed. */ export const DEFAULT_INTERFACE_SIZE = 100; ``` beside `DEFAULT_PANE_TRANSPARENCY` (`:20`). ```ts /** * How much bigger the panes' type is than designed, as a percentage. The map is not on this * scale and never moves with it. */ interfaceSize: number; ``` on `SettingsState` beside `paneTransparency` (`:69`), with the action beside `setPaneTransparency` (`:101`): ```ts setInterfaceSize: (percent: number) => void; ``` The clamp, beside `clampTransparency` (`:149-157`) and in its shape: ```ts /** * 100% to 200%, in steps of 25. Rounded to a step rather than merely bounded, so a hand-edited * localStorage value or an older payload cannot land the slider between its stops. */ function clampInterfaceSize(percent: number): number { const numeric = Number(percent); if (!Number.isFinite(numeric)) { return DEFAULT_INTERFACE_SIZE; } const stepped = Math.round(numeric / 25) * 25; return Math.min(200, Math.max(100, stepped)); } ``` The DOM side effect, beside `applyPaneTransparency` (`:164-169`) and in its shape: ```ts /** Stamps the multiplier the pane type scale is expressed against. See `theme.css`'s `--ui-scale`. */ function applyInterfaceSize(percent: number) { if (typeof document === "undefined") { return; } document.documentElement.style.setProperty("--ui-scale", String(percent / 100)); } ``` The setter, beside `setPaneTransparency` (`:237-241`) and in its shape — clamp, apply, set. Then the four registration sites, each of which `paneTransparency` also appears in: `Persisted` (`:110-120`), `DEFAULTS` (`:208-217`), `partialize` (`:276-285`), `resetSettingsStore` (`:337-343`). **And `applyPersistedSettings` (`:295-334`), which is the one that is easy to forget.** Its own comment (`:297-299`) states the rule: *"Rehydration merges storage straight into state without the setter, so an out-of-range or string value must be reconciled in BOTH places here"* — the clamped value goes into the CSS **and** back into the store. It runs once before React mounts (`apps/web/src/main.tsx:12`, `apps/desktop/src/main.tsx:11`), which is what stops the panes flashing at the old size on load. Follow `paneTransparency`'s lines there exactly. A key absent from a saved payload needs no migration — zustand merges `DEFAULTS` — so nothing like the `warnOnUnguardedHex` → `advisoryChecks` rename (`:313-333`) is needed here. Persistence is `localStorage` under `"atlantis-hud-settings"` (`:274`), with an in-memory `Map` fallback (`:177-198`) so the store imports under Node. ### `packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.tsx` — the control Directly beneath the *Pane transparency* field (`:251-272`), in the Global tab, copying its markup: ```jsx ``` Two notes on that: - **The hint line ships**, worded exactly as above. It is the only place the reader is told the map stays put, which is the question the control raises. - **`data-testid="settings-interface-size"`, with the prefix.** The convention is inconsistent — most controls are `settings-*` (`settings-map-theme`, `settings-game-ruleset`, `settings-warning-`) but the neighbouring slider is a bare `pane-transparency`. Follow the majority; do not "fix" `pane-transparency` in this bead. ### `packages/shared/src/unitTable.ts` and `workspace/UnitTableDock.tsx` — the rows `ROW_HEIGHT = 22` (`unitTable.ts:11`) becomes the base rather than the answer. **Keep the name and the value** — `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts:16` imports it, and `panelLayout.ts:166` explains `UNITS_DEFAULT_REM` in terms of it. Add beside it: ```ts /** * How tall a row is at a given interface size, in whole pixels. * * Rounded, because the windowing arithmetic divides scroll offsets by this and a fractional height * makes the first visible row drift from the one the scroller is actually showing. The row's own * inline height and every offset computed from it must use this same number. */ export function rowHeightAt(interfaceSize: number): number { return Math.round((ROW_HEIGHT * interfaceSize) / 100); } ``` `windowRange` (`unitTable.ts:44`) **already takes `rowHeight` as a parameter** and needs no change — the pure maths was written scale-ready. Only its caller passes a constant today. In `UnitTableDock.tsx`, read the setting once and use the scaled height at all six sites: ```tsx const interfaceSize = useSettingsStore((state) => state.interfaceSize); const rowHeight = rowHeightAt(interfaceSize); ``` replacing `ROW_HEIGHT` at `:83` (into `windowRange`), `:128`, `:130`, `:134`, `:391` (`const height = rows * rowHeight`) and `:508` (`style={{ height: rowHeight }}`). Check the import at `:17` and swap `ROW_HEIGHT` for `rowHeightAt`. **All six must move together**: a scaled inline height with unscaled offsets puts the wrong rows under the pointer, which is worse than clipping. `--pane-transparency` is defined at `theme.css:302` and consumed by the one rule at `:296-308`; put `--ui-scale` beside it. For the store subscription in `UnitTableDock`, match how the file's siblings read `useSettingsStore` — the selector shape above is the usual zustand one. ### Nothing else changes No new pane widths, no rail changes, no map changes. See *Out of scope*. ## Increments **1 — The multiplier exists.** RED: a `theme.test.ts` case asserting `--ui-scale` is declared and that each `--text-pane*` token is a `calc()` naming it. GREEN by the two `theme.css` edits. `pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared exec vitest run src/theme.test.ts`. **2 — The setting exists and reaches the CSS.** RED: a `settingsStore` test — default 100, a set to 150 stamps `--ui-scale: 1.5`, a set to 137 clamps to 125, a set to 500 clamps to 200, a garbage value falls back to 100. GREEN by the store changes. **Include `applyPersistedSettings`**: a test that seeds `localStorage` with `{"interfaceSize": 999}`, calls it, and asserts both the CSS and the store read 200. **3 — The control.** RED: a `SettingsDialog.test.tsx` case for the slider's presence, its `min`/`max`/`step` and its value. GREEN by the JSX. `pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared exec vitest run src/workspace/SettingsDialog.test.tsx`. **4 — The rows follow.** RED: `unitTable.test.ts` for `rowHeightAt` — 100 → 22, 125 → 28 (27.5 rounded), 200 → 44. Then GREEN, and thread `rowHeight` through the six `UnitTableDock` sites. The existing `unitTable` windowing tests must stay green untouched; `windowRange` did not change. **5 — The smoke walk.** RED: extend `tests/smoke/settings.spec.ts` per the test plan. GREEN once the above is in. **6 — Gate.** `pnpm run check:fast`, then `pnpm run check` in full — this bead is a layout change and the browser suites are the ones that would catch a regression. Then *Validation*. ## The test plan ### Unit - **`packages/shared/src/theme.test.ts` — and one of `ah-46p.1`'s own guards MUST be edited, which is the trap in this bead.** Its regex at `:140` is ```js [...themeBlock.matchAll(/(--text-pane[\w-]*)\s*:\s*([\d.]+rem)/g)] ``` which requires the value to begin with a bare number. **I ran it: against `--text-pane-sm: calc(0.6875rem * var(--ui-scale, 1));` it matches zero times**, so `expect(sizes.get("--text-pane-sm")).toBeDefined()` (`:146`) fails. Do not weaken the guard to get past it — make it stronger, in two steps: 1. Let the regex reach inside an optional `calc(` while still capturing the **rem base**, so the `endsWith("rem")` loop at `:151-153` keeps biting: ```js [...themeBlock.matchAll(/(--text-pane[\w-]*)\s*:\s*(?:calc\(\s*)?([\d.]+rem)/g)] ``` 2. Add an assertion, in the same test, that each token is multiplied — otherwise step 1 has quietly made it possible to drop the multiplier and still pass: ```js // Each token must carry the Interface size multiplier, or the setting reaches nothing. for (const token of ["--text-pane-sm", "--text-pane", "--text-pane-lg"]) { const declared = themeBlock.match(new RegExp(`${token}\\s*:\\s*([^;]+);`))?.[1] ?? ""; expect(declared, `${token} is ${declared}`).toContain("var(--ui-scale"); } ``` Then add a case of your own: `--ui-scale` is declared with a default of `1` in the plain `:root` block. The other guard, `:185-187` (no absolute pane px anywhere), **stays green untouched** — a `calc()` is neither a `text-[Npx]` nor a `fontSize: "Npx"`. - **`packages/shared/src/settingsStore.test.ts`** — it exists; sit the five clamp cases and the two-places rehydration case beside `paneTransparency`'s own. - **`packages/shared/src/unitTable.test.ts`** (it exists) — `rowHeightAt` at 100/125/150/175/200 → 22/28/33/39/44. State the rounding in the test's name so the half-pixels are visibly deliberate. - **`packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.test.tsx`** — the slider renders with `data-testid="settings-interface-size"`, `min="100"`, `max="200"`, `step="25"`, and the default value; and the hint text is present verbatim. ### Smoke **`tests/smoke/settings.spec.ts:193-222` is the template** — it is the end-to-end walk for the neighbouring slider and does exactly what this one needs: default value, `toHaveValue`, the `min`/`max` attributes, survives a reload, and **resets to the default at the end so later tests inherit the expected look.** That last part is not optional: leave the app at 200% and every pixel-exact test after it fails. Add one walk, `"the panes grow when the interface size does"`: 1. Read the computed `font-size` of a pane element and of a map label. 2. Set the slider to 200%. 3. The pane's font size has doubled; **the map label's has not moved at all**. 4. A units-dock row's height has gone from 22 to 44, and its text is not clipped (`scrollHeight <= clientHeight` on the cell). 5. Reload; both survive. 6. Set it back to 100%. **`ah-46p.1` added the sibling walk** at `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts:3389-3414` (`"the panes grow when the reader's text size does"`), which injects `html { font-size: 20px }`. Read it before writing yours — it is the same shape from the other dial, and the two together prove the dials multiply rather than fight. ### The pixel-exact tests this threatens, and why they survive at the default `docs/retrospectives/ah-1uj.md` records that several pixel-exact smoke tests broke when header chips grew, and recommends a header height budget that **still does not exist**. This bead can grow the header the same way, so every one of these must be left at the default size: | test | assertion | holds at 100%? | |---|---|---| | `workspace.spec.ts:2299` | `toBeCloseTo(ROW_HEIGHT, 1)` over every unit row | **Yes** — `rowHeightAt(100)` is 22, and `ROW_HEIGHT` keeps its name and value | | `workspace.spec.ts:1347, 1557` | strip height `< 40` (`h-7` plus borders) | Yes — `h-7` is rem-based and the root does not move | | `workspace.spec.ts:3249, 3269` | narrow-window header wrap and panel fit | Yes | | `workspace.spec.ts:1373-1540` | the rail and panel drag walks, `toBeCloseTo(before, 0)` | Yes — no rem constant changes | | `orders-editor.spec.ts:233-259` | the 6px left-edge budget | Yes — CodeMirror's size is `var(--text-pane)`, which is unchanged at 100% | | `games.spec.ts:149`, `shortcuts.spec.ts:193-248` | no-overflow and fixed map corners | Yes | **Do not adjust any of them.** If one goes red, the default is not 100% or something scaled that should not have. ## User-facing decisions Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-17 against **`docs/ui/interface-size.html`** (PR #373, merged). Read it before starting — it carries the rejected options and the clipping hazard drawn at 200%. **1. A slider, 100% to 200%, in steps of 25%,** in the Global tab directly beneath *Pane transparency*, labelled `Interface size` with the current value shown as a percentage beside the label — exactly the shape of the control above it. *Rejected:* four named steps (`Normal` / `Large` / `Larger` / `Largest`) in the shape of the Dark/Light control. Only sensible values are reachable and each has a name, but four words stand for four numbers, `Largest` is a poor name for 200%, and it never tells the reader how much bigger they will get. **2. Row heights follow the text; pane widths do not.** The units dock's rows scale with the setting, so nothing clips at any offered size. The rails and panes keep the widths the player dragged. *Rejected:* scaling only the type, which is the smallest change and moves no smoke test, but clips in the units dock — the pane most likely to be read at length — and would force the range down to about 125%, which is most of the point gone. The reason widths stay is that the player already drags them and that choice is saved; a size setting silently overriding it would be worse than leaving it. **3. The default is 100%** — nothing changes for anybody until they ask. Mine, and it is what the epic's own description asks for ("Nothing changes unless asked for"). It is also what keeps every pixel-exact smoke test green. **4. The hint line ships, verbatim:** `Makes the panes, the header and the dialogs bigger. The map is not affected.` It is the only place the reader is told the map stays put, and that is the question the control raises. Mine; the navigator saw it in the mockup and did not object. **5. Global, not per game.** There is no per-game settings scope (`SettingsDialog.tsx:434-436`), and interface size is a property of the reader's eyes rather than of a game. Not a choice so much as the only option, and stated so nobody re-opens it. **6. Accepted, drawn in the mockup's table, and not to be re-opened:** the map never scales; the header, dialogs, command palette and the orders editor's text all do, because they read the same tokens; the Settings dialog itself scales as the slider moves, which is the right feedback; the reader's browser font-size preference still works and the two multiply; and the setting survives a reload and is applied before the first paint so there is no flash at the old size. ## Out of scope - **Pane and rail widths, and the units pane's default height.** Decision 2. `UNITS_DEFAULT_REM` (`panelLayout.ts:169`) is twelve 22px rows' worth of rem, computed by hand; at 200% a fresh install shows six rows in it until the player drags. Deliberately left — the alternative is overriding a saved width. - **A header height budget in the smoke suite.** `docs/retrospectives/ah-1uj.md` recommends one and this bead makes it more valuable, but it is a test-infrastructure bead of its own and nobody has filed it. Say so in the PR rather than adding it here. - **The `data-testid` inconsistency.** `pane-transparency` is bare where nearly everything else is `settings-*`. Left alone; renaming it would touch `settings.spec.ts` for no gain in this bead. - **Scaling the map.** The epic exists precisely because full-page zoom scales the map and that is the unhelpful trade. - **A separate control for the map's own text size.** Not asked for, not filed. - **The app shells' own type.** `theme.test.ts`'s no-absolute-px guard scans `packages/shared/src` only; whether `apps/web/src` or `apps/desktop/src` carry pane type of their own is unswept. If something in a shell does not scale with everything else, that is why — file it rather than fixing it here. ## Validation ```bash pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared exec vitest run src/theme.test.ts src/unitTable.test.ts src/workspace/SettingsDialog.test.tsx pnpm run check:fast pnpm run check # in full: this is a layout change, and the browser suites are the gate ``` **Look once, in the running app.** This is a visual bead and the screenshot is the point. 1. `pnpm --filter @atlantis/web dev`, load any fixture report — `neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t41.rep` is a big one with a full units dock. 2. Settings → Global. *Interface size* sits under *Pane transparency*, reads `100%`, and the hint says the map is not affected. 3. Drag it to `200%`. **Watch three things at once**: the panes and header grow; the Settings dialog you are dragging in grows with them; and **the map's hex labels do not move at all**. 4. Close Settings and read the units dock. Rows are twice as tall, nothing is clipped, and scrolling still lands on the row you clicked — that last one is the virtualisation arithmetic and it is what would break if any of the six `rowHeight` sites was missed. 5. Reload. It comes back at 200% **without a flash at the old size** — that is `applyPersistedSettings` running before React mounts. 6. Set it back to `100%` and confirm the app looks exactly as it did. 7. With the setting at 150%, also raise the browser's own font size. Both apply and the panes get larger still; that is the two dials multiplying, and is correct. ## Known traps - **Six sites for the row height, and they must move together.** `UnitTableDock.tsx:83, 128, 130, 134, 391, 508`. A scaled inline height with unscaled offsets does not clip — it puts the wrong row under the pointer, which is much harder to notice and much worse. - **`windowRange` already takes `rowHeight`** (`unitTable.ts:44`). Do not add a scale parameter to it; the pure maths is already right and its tests must stay untouched. - **Round the row height.** `22 * 1.25` is 27.5, and a fractional height makes the scroller drift from what it displays. - **Keep `ROW_HEIGHT`'s name and value.** `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts:16` imports it and `panelLayout.ts:166` explains a rem constant in terms of it. - **`applyPersistedSettings` is the sixth part of the store change**, and the one that is invisible until a reload. Its own comment names the both-places rule. - **Do not set a root `font-size`.** It would scale every rem in the app — the rails, the orders pane, the units-pane heights, the map's zoom buttons — and break the drag walks. Scale the tokens. - **`--ui-scale` goes outside the `@theme` block**, beside `--pane-transparency`. `@theme` is Tailwind's utility-generating namespace. - **`ah-46p.1`'s own guard rejects a `calc()`** and will go red the moment `theme.css` changes, in a file nothing else in this bead touches. `theme.test.ts:140`'s regex demands a bare number after the colon. The fix is in *The test plan* and it makes the guard stronger, not weaker — do not reach for `.skip` or delete an assertion. - **`theme.test.ts` also forbids absolute pane px** (`:185-187`), and that guard stays green. A `calc()` is fine; computing a pixel string in JS and stamping it as a font size is not. Never go near that. - **Reset the size at the end of any smoke test that changes it.** `settings.spec.ts:193-222` does this for the transparency slider, and the pixel-exact tests that follow depend on it. - **The default must stay 100%.** Every pixel-exact assertion in the suite holds only there, and `docs/retrospectives/ah-1uj.md` is the record of what it costs when the chrome grows unnoticed.

title: A three-step type scale in rem replaces 67 hard-coded pixel sizes
description:
First half of ah-46p. The panes set type in absolute pixels at 67 sites across 28 files - 31 `text-[10px]`, 19 `text-[11.5px]`, 13 `text-[11px]`, 2 `text-[10.5px]`, 1 each of `text-[9.5px]` and `text-[13px]` - and CSS `px` ignores the browser's font-size preference outright, so a reader who raises theirs sees no change at all.

Decided with the navigator on 2026-08-17 (mockup: docs/ui/pane-type-scale.html): six sizes become **three named rem tokens**, and the floor rises - the smallest pane text goes from 10px to 11px at a 16px root. That is visible to everyone, deliberately.

Nothing else changes: no setting, no control. ah-46p.2 adds the Interface size slider on top, and needs this first because a multiplier cannot reach an absolute pixel.
design:
## Context

The map is resolution-independent by construction — it is SVG, so the browser re-rasterises it at
device resolution. The panes over it are not: they set type in **absolute pixels at 67 sites across
28 files** in `packages/shared/src`, and CSS `px` ignores the browser's font-size preference
outright. A reader who raises their default sees no change at all, because all 67 sites override it.
On a 4K panel at 100% OS scaling — ordinary on Windows and Linux — 10px type is physically about half
the size it is on a 1080p screen, and the only escape is full-page zoom, which also zooms the map
that was perfectly legible.

Counted on `origin/main`, and the numbers below are what
`git grep -o 'text-\[[0-9.]*px\]' -- packages/shared/src | sed 's/.*://' | sort | uniq -c` returns:

| Class | Uses |
|---|---|
| `text-[10px]` | 31 |
| `text-[11.5px]` | 19 |
| `text-[11px]` | 13 |
| `text-[10.5px]` | 2 |
| `text-[9.5px]` | 1 |
| `text-[13px]` | 1 |

This bead replaces all 67 with **three named `rem` tokens**, and raises the floor. `ah-46p.2` then
adds an Interface size setting on top; it is blocked on this one, because a multiplier cannot reach
an absolute pixel.

The mockup the navigator chose from is `docs/ui/pane-type-scale.html`.

Branch from `origin/main`; line numbers are that tree.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### The scale — `packages/shared/src/theme.css`

Tailwind v4 generates a font-size utility from every `--text-*` key in the `@theme` block, so the
scale is declared once beside the colours (`:36-110`) and used as a class everywhere:

```css
  /* The panes' type scale. Three steps, in rem so the reader's own font-size preference reaches
     them - `px` does not, which is the whole of ah-46p. The map sets its own sizes and is not on
     this scale. */
  --text-pane-sm: 0.6875rem;   /* 11px at a 16px root */
  --text-pane: 0.75rem;        /* 12px */
  --text-pane-lg: 0.8125rem;   /* 13px */
```

Font sizes only — **do not add `--text-pane--line-height` companions.** The existing markup sets its
own leading with `leading-*` classes where it wants it, and giving these tokens a line-height would
silently re-space every pane in the same commit that changes the sizes, making a layout regression
impossible to attribute.

There is no `--text-*` token in the file today; these are the first. Note they go in the `@theme`
block **only** — unlike a colour, a size has no light-theme counterpart, and `theme.test.ts`'s guard
is specifically about `--color-*` tokens (`theme.test.ts:13`, `colorTokens`), so it neither requires
nor objects to these.

### The mapping — 67 sites, 28 files

| Today | Uses | Becomes |
|---|---|---|
| `text-[9.5px]`, `text-[10px]`, `text-[10.5px]` | 34 | `text-pane-sm` |
| `text-[11px]`, `text-[11.5px]` | 32 | `text-pane` |
| `text-[13px]` | 1 | `text-pane-lg` |

Mechanical, and the whole of it. Find every site with:

```bash
git grep -n 'text-\[[0-9.]*px\]' -- packages/shared/src
```

**The floor rises**: today's smallest pane text is 10px and becomes 11px at a default root. That is
visible to every reader and is the navigator's deliberate choice — see *User-facing decisions*. Do
not "preserve" it by mapping 10px to 0.625rem.

### The one site that is not a Tailwind class

`packages/shared/src/workspace/OrdersEditor.tsx` sets the editor's type inside an injected CodeMirror
theme rather than as a class: `"&": { height: "100%", fontSize: "11.5px", … }` (`:147`). It is pane
text read by the same eyes, so it moves too:

```ts
"&": { height: "100%", fontSize: "var(--text-pane)", color: "var(--color-ink)" },
```

Tailwind emits the `@theme` tokens on `:root` (`theme.css:124` says so in as many words), so a
`var()` in an injected style resolves exactly as it does for the colours that file already reads
this way. The file's own comment — *"Tokens, not hex literals: theme.test.ts's rule holds in spirit
for injected styles its component scan cannot see"* (`:144-145`) — is the precedent, and it applies
to sizes for the same reason.

That is a **decision I took rather than the navigator**: they settled that pane text scales, and the
orders editor is a pane. If the monospace editor should keep a fixed size while the panes around it
grow, that is a one-line reversal and worth asking about — but the default that follows from what was
agreed is that it scales.

### The guard — `packages/shared/src/theme.test.ts`

Add a case that the panes carry no absolute type any more, so this cannot come back a site at a time:

```ts
it("sets no pane type in absolute pixels", () => {
  // `px` ignores the reader's font-size preference, which is the whole of ah-46p. The three
  // `--text-pane*` tokens are the scale; a new `text-[13px]` is how 67 of them accumulated.
  expect(sourcesWithAbsoluteType()).toEqual([]);
});
```

reading the same `packages/shared/src` tree the file already reads `theme.css` from, and matching
`/text-\[[0-9.]+px\]/`. Report the offending file paths in the failure, not just a count — the
message is what tells the next author what to do.

## Increments

1. **The scale exists and is proven to reach the DOM.**
   RED: `theme.test.ts` — `the pane type scale is declared`, asserting `--text-pane-sm`, `--text-pane`
   and `--text-pane-lg` are all in the `@theme` block, in rem.
   GREEN: the three tokens.

2. **Nothing sets type in pixels.**
   RED: the `sets no pane type in absolute pixels` case, which fails with 28 file paths.
   GREEN: the mechanical replacement, one size at a time — the 34 smallest first, then the 32, then
   the single `13px`. Run `pnpm run lint` and `pnpm run typecheck` between them; a mistyped class name
   is not a type error in Tailwind, so the test above is the only thing that catches a typo in a
   class that silently does nothing.

3. **The editor moves with them.**
   RED: extend the guard to `OrdersEditor.tsx`'s injected theme, or assert directly that the file
   contains no `fontSize: "…px"`.
   GREEN: `var(--text-pane)`.

4. **Nothing is clipped.**
   RED: the smoke walk in *The test plan*.
   GREEN: whatever it turns up — see *Known traps* for the two places most likely to need a
   `min-h`/`min-w` nudge.

## The test plan

**Unit — `packages/shared/src/theme.test.ts`, `pnpm -r run test`.** The two cases above. They are
cheap and they are the whole regression story: a scale that exists, and nothing bypassing it.

**Component — none.** Every changed line is a class name; a component test asserting a class name
pins the implementation rather than the behaviour.

**Browser — `pnpm run test:smoke`.** The existing suite is the safety net for layout, and two of its
walks already measure boxes: `tests/smoke/orders-editor.spec.ts:169` pins the editor's left edge at
≤6px, and the units-pane drag walks measure heights. Run the whole suite; a type change that breaks
layout shows up there rather than in a unit test.

Add one walk, `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts`, that is the actual point of the bead:

> **the panes grow when the reader's text size does** — set the root font size to 20px
> (`page.addStyleTag({ content: "html { font-size: 20px }" })` before the app renders, or
> `document.documentElement.style.fontSize`), then assert a known pane's computed `font-size` is
> larger than at the default, and that the region panel's own bounding box has not overflowed its
> rail. That is one assertion for "rem reached it" and one for "and it still fits".

**By eye, and this is the case no test covers**: with the browser's default font size raised two
steps, walk the region panel, the unit panel, the unit table dock, the orders panel and the header —
nothing clipped, nothing overlapping, the rails still draggable.

**Suites:** `pnpm run check:fast` and `pnpm run test:smoke`.

## User-facing decisions

Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-17 over `docs/ui/pane-type-scale.html`, which draws the
same pane at today's sizes, ×1.15 and ×1.3.

**Q1 — how the reader gets control.** Chosen: **rem first, then a UI-scale setting**, as two beads.
The conversion alone already fixes the reported problem for anyone who has set a browser preference,
and rem is what makes a multiplier possible at all, so the first is half of the second either way.
Rejected: rem only (a reader who does not know the browser preference exists gets no help); one bead
doing both (28 files and the settings store at once).

**Q2 — the sizes themselves.** Chosen: **tidied — six sizes become three, and the floor rises to
11px** at a 16px root. Six sizes, three of them within half a pixel of each other, were carried
forward unexamined; a named three-step scale is what the next author needs, and 10px is small by any
measure. Rejected: a faithful translation (zero visual risk, six sizes preserved for the next person
to wonder about); tidying to three steps while keeping the 10px floor.

**Consequence the navigator accepted**: because the floor rises, this bead is *not* invisible. Every
reader's smallest pane text grows by a pixel, and the densest lists — the unit table, the market rows
— are where it shows.

**Taken by me, and flagged**: the orders editor's injected `fontSize: "11.5px"` moves onto the same
token, because it is pane text and the decision was that pane text scales.

## Out of scope

- **The Interface size setting.** `ah-46p.2`, blocked on this.
- **The map.** It sets its own sizes, is SVG, and already scales with the display. Nothing under
  `mapThemes/` or in `MapCanvas`'s SVG text is touched.
- **Line heights and spacing.** No `leading-*`, padding or gap changes: this bead moves font sizes
  and nothing else, so a layout regression has one possible cause.
- **The rails' widths.** They are already in rem (`RAIL_LEFT_DEFAULT_REM = 19`, `panelLayout.ts:35`)
  and grow with the root on their own; a reader who has dragged one keeps their width.
- **`apps/`.** The 67 sites are all in `packages/shared/src`; if the shells carry any of their own,
  they are a separate sweep and not part of the measured cost.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run check:fast
pnpm run test:smoke
```

Then by eye, at the browser's default and again two steps up:

- the region panel, unit panel, unit table dock, orders panel and header all readable and unclipped;
- the orders editor's monospace text grows with them;
- the rails still drag, and a narrow rail still shows its content;
- the map is unchanged at both sizes — that is the point of the bead.

## Known traps

- **A mistyped Tailwind class silently does nothing.** `text-pane-sm` and `text-pane-small` both
  compile; only one has a size. The `sets no pane type in absolute pixels` test catches a leftover
  `text-[10px]`, but nothing catches a typo in the new name, so read the diff — or grep for
  `text-pane` and count 67.
- **`--text-*` in `@theme` is what makes the utility exist.** Declaring the tokens under a plain
  `:root` gives working `var()` references and **no** `text-pane` class, which then falls back to
  inherited size and looks almost right.
- **Do not give the tokens line-height companions.** Tailwind v4 lets `--text-pane--line-height` ride
  along, and it would re-space every pane in the same commit as the size change.
- **`theme.test.ts` guards `--color-*` only** (`:13`). It will not notice a missing size token; the
  new cases are what do.
- **The two dense lists are where the extra pixel shows** — `UnitTableDock` (a virtualised table with
  its own row heights) and the market rows in `RegionPanel`. If a row clips, raise that container's
  `min-h`, do not shrink the type back.
- **The editor's own left-edge budget is pinned at ≤6px** by `tests/smoke/orders-editor.spec.ts:169`
  and is measured in px against a 2px line padding. Changing the editor's font size changes the
  text's box but not that padding; if the walk fails, read it before adjusting anything — the budget
  is a deliberate agreement (`docs/ui/orders-editor-left-edge.html`).

title: Refactoring: one script answers which closed beads are real work
description:
## The cost being paid
"Closed beads that are work, not bd's own audit records" is a query hand-written independently wherever the harness reads closed beads — the fleet view's bead partition in elisp, Psylocke's work list and first-pass check in verifier.md, Cerebro's shipped-count and merged-but-unverified queries in orchestrator.md — and each copy had to learn bd's `event` beads and its default-to-open listing on its own. The same defect was fixed twice in nineteen hours in two implementations: b0bbfaf (#6, 2026-08-15 01:22) taught the elisp panel to exclude event beads after three "State change: verification -> passed" records sat at the top of Verified as merged work; 7cea8fa (#26, ah-9gm, 20:54 the same day) fixed verifier.md and orchestrator.md after Psylocke's work list grew an event-bead chain "one link per pass, forever". A third fix the next day, 5ccc3b3 (#30): verifier.md's first-pass query lacked `--status closed` and read zero against 118 labelled beads — a trap agents/user-feedback.md had already documented for Moira ("`--all` is load-bearing"). Every reader of closed beads is a place the next bd quirk has to be discovered again.

## Evidence
- b0bbfaf "A bead panel under the agent list, and three fixes it turned up (#6)" — body: "It also holds bd's `event' beads … three of them were sitting at the top of Verified titled 'State change: verification -> passed'"
- 7cea8fa "fix(ah-9gm): closed-bead queries exclude bd's own audit event beads (#26)" — agents/orchestrator.md and agents/verifier.md
- 5ccc3b3 "fix(verifier): first-pass detection must query closed beads (#30)"
- .claude/cerebro @ bbfa374: emacs/cerebro.el:1520 (`(member (alist-get 'issue_type bead) '("epic" "event"))`); agents/verifier.md:123 (`select(.issue_type != "event")`), :152; agents/orchestrator.md:622-626, :649 (`--exclude-type epic,event`)

## Where
