title: The core finds every trade route in the known map and prices it
description:
First half of ah-1j5. No user interface: the core answers 'what trades are there', and ah-1j5.2 shows it.

What it answers, decided with the navigator on 2026-08-16 (the full interview is in this bead's design field, the mockup is docs/ui/trade-routes.html):

- A **hex pair**, carrying **every** good buyable in one and sellable dearer in the other - not one row per good.
- Both directions folded into one **circuit** where each way pays (the fixture corpus has exactly one: perfume out, chocolate back, worth $15,598 together).
- Worth = the smaller of what the seller has and what the buyer will take, times the margin. Ranked by that, most first.
- Distance as **three** numbers - on foot, riding, flying - each the month count of the cheapest route through known hexes, or absent where that mode cannot make it.
- Over the **known map**, remembered hexes included, each half carrying the turn it was seen in.

Measured before planning: a single turn's report almost never contains a route at all (the turn-71 smoke fixture has none), while one game's remembered turns yield seven. That is what makes the known map non-optional.
design:
## Context

Every region block a report prints carries what the hex sells and what it wants, with prices and
quantities. Finding a hex selling a good another will pay more for is arithmetic over data already
parsed — and today it is done by eye, across turns, by remembering where things were cheap.

This bead is the **core half**: it answers *what trades are there*, and shows nobody. `ah-1j5.2`
puts a counted `Trade` chip in the header and lists the answer.

**Two measurements taken before planning, which shaped the whole design.** Both are reproducible
from the committed fixtures:

- **A single turn's report almost never contains a route at all.** The turn-71 report the smoke
  tests use has seven goods for sale and thirteen wanted, with *no overlap*. Across the entire
  fixture corpus the best single report yields four routes and most yield none. A faction sees the
  markets of the handful of hexes it has units in, and that is all.
- **The remembered map is where the answer lives.** Game 3, faction 42 — turn 82 as the current
  report with turn 42 remembered — yields **seven hex pairs**, of which **one is reciprocal**: perfume
  out from `0,48` to `36,4`, chocolate back, worth $15,598 the circuit.

So the known map is not an enhancement here; without it the feature has nothing to show.

The interview is recorded under *User-facing decisions*; the mockup is `docs/ui/trade-routes.html`.
Branch from `origin/main`; every line number below is that tree.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### The finder — `crates/core/src/trade.rs` (new)

```rust
/// One good worth carrying from one hex to another.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct TradedGood {
    /// The item's tag, as both markets name it.
    pub tag: String,
    /// The seller's own spelling, which is what the region panel shows.
    pub name: String,
    pub buy_price: i64,
    pub sell_price: i64,
    /// The smaller of what the seller has and what the buyer will take.
    pub quantity: i64,
    /// `sell_price - buy_price`, per unit.
    pub margin: i64,
    /// The turn each half was last seen in, so a rumour can say so. `None` only when the report
    /// carries no turn number at all.
    pub buy_seen_turn: Option<u32>,
    pub sell_seen_turn: Option<u32>,
}

/// How long the journey takes, in months, for each way of travelling. `None` where the known map
/// offers that mode no route at all - water for a walker, or a gap in what has been seen.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct TravelTurns {
    pub walk: Option<u32>,
    pub ride: Option<u32>,
    pub fly: Option<u32>,
}

/// A pair of hexes worth trading between, and everything worth carrying either way.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct TradeRoute {
    /// Where the journey starts: the hex whose outbound leg is worth more.
    pub from: Coordinate,
    pub to: Coordinate,
    /// Goods bought at `from` and sold at `to`. Never empty.
    pub outbound: Vec<TradedGood>,
    /// Goods bought at `to` and sold at `from`. Empty unless the way back also pays, which is what
    /// makes this a circuit rather than a one-way trip.
    pub inbound: Vec<TradedGood>,
    /// Silver earned running the whole thing once: every good on both legs, quantity times margin.
    pub worth: i64,
    pub turns: TravelTurns,
}

/// Every trade worth making in the map the faction has seen, best first.
///
/// Both halves of every pair come from the known map, so a price seen forty turns ago is included
/// and says so through `buy_seen_turn`/`sell_seen_turn`. Nothing here judges whether a unit could
/// carry the goods: `quantity` is what the market allows, and the weight of it is the player's
/// problem (see this bead's *Out of scope*).
#[must_use]
pub fn trade_routes(
    report: &ParsedReport,
    remembered: &[RememberedRegion],
    ruleset: &Ruleset,
) -> Vec<TradeRoute>;
```

The body, in order:

1. **The markets.** `resolve_known_map(report, remembered)` (`crates/core/src/known_map.rs:189`)
   gives a `KnownMap` whose every `KnownMapHex` carries `region: Option<ReportRegion>`
   (`known_map.rs:70`) and `last_seen_turn: Option<u32>` (`:66`). That is where `for_sale`, `wanted`
   and the dates come from — a hex with `region: None` was only named by an exit and has no market.
   **`MapKnowledge` is the wrong structure for this**: `KnownHex` (`movement/graph.rs:135-155`)
   drops markets entirely, and reaching for it is the obvious wrong turn.
2. **The pairs.** For every ordered pair of hexes with a region, and every tag appearing in the
   seller's `for_sale` and the buyer's `wanted` where `sell_price > buy_price`, a `TradedGood`.
   `MarketItem` (`crates/core/src/report/model.rs:41-50`) carries `amount`, `name`, `tag` and
   `price`; `quantity` is `min(seller.amount, buyer.amount)` and `worth` accumulates
   `quantity * margin`. A pair with no good is not a route.
   Match tags case-insensitively and take `name` from the **seller's** market line: it is the
   spelling the region panel already shows, plural and all.
3. **The circuits.** After the ordered pairs exist, fold `(A, B)` and `(B, A)` into one route: the
   leg worth more becomes `outbound` and sets `from`, the other becomes `inbound`, and `worth` is
   the sum. This is a display fold with no new arithmetic — the journey is walked either way — and
   it is why `from` is defined as "where the journey starts" rather than by hex order.
4. **The distances.** Once per route, not per good: `MapKnowledge::from_remembered(report, remembered)`
   (as `movement/request.rs:88` builds it), then one route search per mode over
   `[MovementMode::Walk, MovementMode::Ride, MovementMode::Fly]`, each giving `Option<u32>` months.
   `MovementMode::Sail` is deliberately not among them: a fleet is a different question and the
   navigator asked for three numbers.
5. **The ranking.** By `worth`, descending. Ties by `from` then `to`, so the order is stable between
   runs — a list that reshuffles when nothing changed is worse than one in an arbitrary order.

### The seam this needs in the route planner — `crates/core/src/movement/plan.rs`

`plan_route` (`:124`) resolves a *unit's* mode and then does the part this bead needs: the two
`blocks` guards, `cheapest_path(map, ruleset, mode, origin, destination)` with its
`blocked_by_water` fallback, `split_into_months(points_per_month, origin, &steps)`, and the
flight-must-end-on-land rule. A trade route has no unit, so extract that part and call it from both:

```rust
/// The cheapest route between two hexes for one way of travelling, and how the months fall.
///
/// What `plan_route` does once it knows a unit's mode; `crate::trade` asks the same question of a
/// hypothetical traveller. Sharing it is what stops the two disagreeing about whether a flier may
/// end a month over water.
pub(crate) fn route_for_mode(
    map: &MapKnowledge,
    ruleset: &Ruleset,
    mode: MovementMode,
    origin: Coordinate,
    destination: Coordinate,
) -> Result<(Vec<RouteStep>, Vec<MonthLeg>), RouteProblem>;
```

`plan_route` keeps everything else it does — mode resolution, `AlreadyThere`, the `MoveStep` list and
the order string — and calls this in the middle. `trade.rs` calls it and keeps `months.len()`,
mapping any `Err` to `None`: for a distance column, *why* there is no route does not matter.

`ruleset.movement_points(mode)` (`crates/core/src/movement/rules.rs`) supplies the points per month
for each mode, exactly as `plan_route` does for a unit's own.

### The wire — the same eight files every core command crosses

`plan_route` is the precedent to copy at every step: it already takes a ruleset, a raw report and
`remembered_json`.

1. **`crates/core/src/lib.rs`** — `pub mod trade;` and a re-export of `trade_routes` beside the
   others at `:130`.
2. **`crates/core-wasm/src/lib.rs`**, modelled on `plan_route_state` (`:321`):

   ```rust
   #[wasm_bindgen]
   pub fn trade_routes_state(
       ruleset_json: String,
       raw_report: String,
       remembered_json: String,
   ) -> Result<JsValue, JsValue>
   ```

   resolving the ruleset and the report through `cache::with_global` and the remembered regions with
   `serde_json::from_str`, exactly as `plan_for_remembered_report` (`movement/request.rs:68-92`)
   does. Errors: an unusable ruleset or unreadable remembered regions reject; everything else is an
   empty list, because "no routes" is an answer and not a failure.
3. **`crates/core-tauri/src/lib.rs`** — `command_trade_routes(ruleset_json: &str, raw_report: &str, remembered_json: &str) -> Result<Vec<TradeRoute>, String>`
   with the `#[cfg_attr(feature = "tauri", tauri::command(rename_all = "snake_case", rename = "trade_routes"))]`
   attribute, added to the `pub use commands::{…}` list alphabetically.
4. **`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs`** — one more line in `generate_handler!`.
5. **`packages/core-client/src/index.ts`** —
   `tradeRoutes(rulesetJson: string, rawReport: string, rememberedJson: string): Promise<TradeRoute[]>`
   plus the three exported types mirroring the Rust ones.
6. **`packages/core-client/src/tauriCommands.ts`** —
   `tradeRoutes: ["trade_routes", "ruleset_json", "raw_report", "remembered_json"],`
7. **`packages/browser-core/src/webCoreAdapter.ts`** — the `CoreWasmModule` member and the adapter
   method.
8. **The two complete-by-construction fakes** — `packages/core-client/src/index.test.ts:30`
   (`fakeAdapter`) and `packages/browser-core/src/webCoreAdapter.test.ts:39` (`fakeWasm`).
9. **`tests/native/sweep.ts`** — a row:
   `{ command: "trade_routes", args: () => ({ ruleset_json: RULESET, raw_report: REPORT, remembered_json: "[]" }) }`.
10. **`scripts/tauriCommands.test.ts`** — `expect(renames.size).toBe(N)` goes up by one. **Take
    whatever number is on `main` when you branch and add one**: `ah-bai.1` bumps the same literal, so
    a number written here today would be wrong by the time this is built.

No UI: nothing in `packages/shared` changes, and `AppShell` does not call this yet. That is
`ah-1j5.2`.

## Increments

1. **A route is found.**
   RED: `crates/core/src/trade.rs`'s test module — `a_hex_selling_cheap_and_one_paying_more_is_a_route`,
   on a hand-built two-hex report (`region(...)` helpers as `semantics.rs`'s tests build them), one
   selling `SILK` at $60 with 20 in stock, the other wanting it at $300 for 15, expecting one route
   whose single good has `quantity: 15`, `margin: 240` and `worth: 3600`.
   GREEN: the types and steps 1-2 above, with `TravelTurns` all `None` for now.

2. **Nothing is a route when it should not be.**
   RED: `a_pair_that_does_not_pay_is_not_a_route` (sell price equal to and below the buy price),
   `a_hex_does_not_trade_with_itself`, and `a_hex_with_no_market_is_skipped`.
   GREEN: the guards.

3. **Remembered hexes count, and say how old they are.**
   RED: `a_remembered_market_is_used_and_dated` — turn 82 as the report with turn 42 remembered
   (see *The test plan* for the exact numbers), asserting the `49,3 → 0,48` chocolate route exists
   with `buy_seen_turn: Some(42)` and `sell_seen_turn: Some(82)`.
   GREEN: reading the markets from `resolve_known_map` rather than from the report alone.

4. **Both directions fold into a circuit.**
   RED: `a_pair_that_pays_both_ways_is_one_circuit` — the same fixture pair, expecting `0,48`/`36,4`
   to appear **once**, with `from` the richer leg's origin, a non-empty `inbound`, and
   `worth == 15_598`.
   GREEN: step 3.

5. **How far it is, per mode.**
   RED: `the_route_says_how_long_it_takes_each_way` — a small hand-built map where a walker's path
   exists and is longer than a flier's, expecting `walk: Some(..)`, `fly: Some(..)` with
   `fly < walk`; and `a_mode_with_no_route_says_so`, over water, expecting `walk: None`.
   GREEN: `route_for_mode` extracted in `plan.rs` and called three times.
   Guard the refactor first: before extracting, confirm `cargo test --workspace` is green, and
   after it, that `plan.rs`'s own tests still are. They are the proof the extraction changed
   nothing.

6. **The answer crosses to both shells.**
   RED: `packages/browser-core/src/webCoreAdapter.test.ts` — `adapter.tradeRoutes(...)` resolves to
   what the fake wasm returns.
   GREEN: the wire, items 1-10.

## The test plan

**Rust — `crates/core/src/trade.rs`'s test module, `cargo test --workspace`.** Most cases are
hand-built two- and three-hex reports, which is what makes the arithmetic legible; two are against
the committed fixtures, because the point of this feature is what it finds in a real map.

The fixture case, measured and reproducible: **`atlantis_hud_fixtures::G3_F42_T82` as the current
report, with every region of `G3_F42_T42` as `RememberedRegion { region, last_seen_turn: 42 }`.**
That yields exactly **seven ordered pairs**, one of them reciprocal, and therefore **six routes**
after folding:

| Route | Worth | Good |
|---|---|---|
| `36,4` ⇄ `0,48` (circuit) | $15,598 | chocolate out 41 × +$218, perfume back 36 × +$185 |
| `49,3` → `0,48` | $10,209 | chocolate 41 × +$249, bought on a turn-42 sighting |
| `0,48` → `25,9` | $5,868 | perfume 36 × +$163 |
| `25,9` → `49,3` | $5,103 | silk 21 × +$243, sold on a turn-42 sighting |
| `35,9` → `49,3` | $4,066 | silk 19 × +$214 |
| `0,48` → `40,0` | $1,105 | perfume 5 × +$221 |

| Test | Pins |
|---|---|
| `a_hex_selling_cheap_and_one_paying_more_is_a_route` | the arithmetic, on two hand-built hexes |
| `quantity_is_the_smaller_of_the_two_sides` | seller has 20, buyer wants 15 → 15; and the reverse |
| `a_pair_that_does_not_pay_is_not_a_route` | `sell == buy` and `sell < buy` both yield nothing |
| `a_hex_does_not_trade_with_itself` | a hex selling and wanting the same tag |
| `a_hex_with_no_market_is_skipped` | `region: None`, and a region with empty market lists |
| `several_goods_between_one_pair_are_one_route` | two tags tradeable between the same two hexes → one route, two `outbound` goods, `worth` their sum. **Hand-built: no pair in the corpus carries more than one good**, so the fixture cannot exercise this |
| `a_remembered_market_is_used_and_dated` | the `49,3 → 0,48` route, `buy_seen_turn: Some(42)` |
| `a_pair_that_pays_both_ways_is_one_circuit` | `36,4`/`0,48` once, `worth == 15_598`, `inbound` non-empty |
| `the_whole_known_map_answers` | the six routes above, in that order, from the two fixtures |
| `the_ranking_is_stable` | two routes of equal worth come back in a fixed order across runs |
| `the_route_says_how_long_it_takes_each_way` | `fly < walk` on a hand-built map |
| `a_mode_with_no_route_says_so` | `walk: None` across water, `fly: Some(..)` |

**`crates/core/src/movement/plan.rs`:** no new tests; its existing ones are the proof that extracting
`route_for_mode` changed nothing.

**TypeScript:** the two adapter tests only — this bead adds no shell behaviour.

**Suites:** `pnpm run check:fast`. No browser suite: nothing renders.

## User-facing decisions

Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-16 over three rounds; the mockup is
`docs/ui/trade-routes.html`. The decisions below shape what this bead computes; the ones about how
it is displayed live in `ah-1j5.2`.

**Q1 — how much of the arithmetic.** Chosen: **margin, quantity and distance** — and, at the
navigator's own extension, *a route is a hex pair carrying every good tradeable between those two
hexes*, not one row per good. Rejected: margin alone, which ranks the real data wrongly (a perfume
trade worth $1,105 above a chocolate one worth $8,938); and margin with quantity but no distance.

**Q2 — which hexes count.** Chosen: **everything remembered, each half dated**, so a route may rest
on a forty-turn-old price and says so. Rejected: this turn's report only (empty in most fixtures,
always empty in the smoke fixture); a staleness cutoff, which needs a number nobody can defend and
would hide the two best routes in the corpus.

**Q3 — distance for whom.** Chosen: **all three modes at once** — walking, riding and flying, each
its own month count, which the interface renders `14/7/4 turns on foot/riding/flying`. Rejected:
straight-line hex distance (says nothing about the ocean in between); the selected unit's own mode
(the whole list would change on every click, and say nothing with no unit selected).

**Q4 — both directions.** Chosen: **fold a reciprocal pair into one circuit**, worth the sum, since a
laden unit going both ways earns both margins on a journey it was making anyway. Rejected: one row
per direction.

**Q5 — carrying capacity.** Chosen: **not modelled.** The quantity the market allows is stated and
the player judges what their unit can haul. Rejected: capping quantity by a unit's capacity, which
needs a chosen unit and moves the number as you click around.

**Q6 — ranking.** Chosen: **by what the trade is worth, most first.** Rejected: reachable-first
(a huge margin with no known way sinks out of sight); margin per unit.

## Out of scope

- **Everything the player sees.** No chip, no panel, no map drawing: `ah-1j5.2`.
- **Carrying capacity and weight**, per Q5.
- **`MovementMode::Sail`.** The three modes the navigator named are walking, riding and flying; a
  fleet's journey is a different question with a different origin.
- **Whether the faction has a unit that could actually go.** The route is a fact about the map, not
  a plan for a unit.
- **Writing the orders.** No `BUY`/`SELL` is generated; the planner's "Apply to orders" is a
  different feature and is not being copied here.
- **Prices moving.** A remembered price is reported as it was seen, dated. Guessing how a market has
  drifted is not something the report supports.
- **Hexes named only by an exit.** They have no `region` and therefore no market; they are skipped
  rather than treated as empty markets.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run check:fast
```

There is nothing to look at in the running app — the answer reaches no interface until `ah-1j5.2`.
What stands in for an eyeball check is the fixture test `the_whole_known_map_answers`: its six routes
and their worths are in *The test plan* above, and they were measured from the committed fixtures
before this plan was written. If the implementation disagrees with that table, the implementation is
wrong.

## Known traps

- **`MapKnowledge`/`KnownHex` has no markets.** `graph.rs:135-155` keeps coordinate, terrain,
  province, visited, roads, structures and units — and drops `for_sale`, `wanted` and `products`.
  The markets come from `resolve_known_map`'s `KnownMapHex.region`; the pathing comes from
  `MapKnowledge`. This bead needs **both structures**, built from the same two inputs.
- **An empty market list is ambiguous** — `For Sale: none` and a hex that printed no market line at
  all are the same empty `Vec` (`crates/core/src/report/scan.rs:180-184`). Here that ambiguity is
  harmless: either way there is nothing to sell, and no route.
- **A market list is read whole or not at all** when reports are merged (`report/merge.rs:88-93`):
  a shorter list is a different observation, not a subset. Do not try to union two sightings of one
  hex's market.
- **`last_seen_turn` is `Option<u32>`** and is `None` when the current report carries no turn number.
  Carry the `None` through to the goods rather than defaulting it to zero, which would date every
  price to turn 0.
- **Route searches are the expensive part**: three per pair, each a search over the whole known map.
  Compute them once per route, after the goods are known and the pairs are folded — not per good,
  and not for pairs that turned out to carry nothing.
- **`plan_route`'s flight rule must not be lost in the extraction.** A flier may not end a month over
  water (`plan.rs`, `flight_must_end_on_land`), and that check belongs inside `route_for_mode` so the
  trade finder and the planner cannot disagree. Its own tests are what prove the refactor.
- **`scripts/tauriCommands.test.ts`'s `renames.size` literal is contended.** `ah-bai.1` bumps it too;
  read it off `main` at branch time rather than trusting a number written here.
- **`bd show --json` returns an array** if this plan is read back with `jq`: index `.[0]`.

title: Warn when cargo loaded this month overloads a fleet ordered to sail
description:
Follow-up to ah-j0e (navigator, 2026-08-16: scope B ships first, this is scope C). ah-j0e warns on a SAIL when the fleet is overloaded or short of sailors, counting the units aboard after this month's ENTER/LEAVE at their report weights. It does not re-weigh a unit for what it is GIVEn or TAKEs this month, so a Cog loaded by `GIVE 1234 500 GRAI` and then SAILed still passes silently — and that is the usual way a fleet gets overloaded.

**The request:** price this month's GIVE/TAKE (not BUY/SELL, which the server runs after movement) into each aboard unit's weight using the ruleset's item weights (`items[].weight`, men included), so the load the check compares against capacity is the load at sailing time. Accept on doubt: a moved item with no known weight, or a unit the silver/item ledger already doubts, silences the fleet's load check (its sailors are still judged). Same code (`fleet-overloaded`), same message, same toggle — only the number gets more accurate.

Reuse: the ledger in crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs (`Ledger`, `apply`, `transfer`) already tracks per-unit per-tag balances after transfers; weight_after = report weight + Σ_tag (balance − holding) × weight(tag). Read ah-j0e's plan first: it names the seam (`fleet_load` in the sailing check) this bead replaces.

title: A mage short of what its spell costs to cast is warned like any other shortfall
description: Second child of ah-dbb. CAST becomes an intent that charges the ledger with the ruleset's stated casting cost (once per cast; transmutation's source for the named output), so the existing not-enough-silver / not-enough-items reporting - pooled with the hex's sharing units by ah-j2w - warns at the CAST line. Blocked on the ruleset child and on ah-j2w. Plan in the design field.
design:
## Context

Second child of ah-dbb (navigator, 2026-08-16). Blocked on **ah-dbb.1** (the ruleset carries each
spell's casting cost as `SkillEntry.cast: Option<CastCost>` — read its plan for the shape) and on
**ah-j2w** (any unit's shortfall counts what sharing units in the hex hold; a mage is usually
supplied by its hex). Planned by Beast on 2026-08-16.

Today `CAST` is read as `Intent::MonthLong("CAST")` (`crates/core/src/orders/intents.rs:215`) and
`apply()` charges nothing for it (`semantics.rs:470`). A mage ordered to create a ring it cannot
pay 600 silver for, or to enchant swords it does not have, is not warned, and the turn runs
without the spell.

**After this bead**, a `CAST` charges the ledger with what the engine will consume — the stated
inputs once per cast; for transmutation the source of the named output, one per item or the
stated number — at the CAST line, and the existing shortfall reporting (per unit, or pooled for
the hex once ah-j2w is in) does the rest under `not-enough-silver` / `not-enough-items`. No new
code, message or toggle: the navigator chose "same codes and words as any shortfall".

Engine facts this stands on (Atlantis `spells.cpp`, verified 2026-08-16): `RunCreateArtifact`
consumes each input `amt` **once per cast** regardless of how many items the roll makes and
refuses the cast when it cannot ("Doesn't have sufficient … to create that"); `RunEnchant` makes as
many as it has inputs for and consumes one input per output (a mage with none makes none);
`RunTransmutation` consumes one source per output up to `2 × level`, or the stated number, erroring
only when a number was stated; `RunConstructGate` consumes 1000 silver before the roll. So "the
least a successful cast consumes" — one of each stated input, one source unit for an unnumbered
transmutation — is exact for artifacts and the gate, and the conservative bound for enchant and
transmute. All through the shared pool ah-j2w models.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `crates/core/src/orders/intents.rs`

- `Intent` (:20): replace nothing; **add**
  ```rust
  /// `CAST <spell> [arguments…]`. The month is spoken for (as `MonthLong` says), and the spell
  /// may consume what the ruleset says it costs; the arguments are kept for the one spell whose
  /// cost depends on them (transmutation names its output, and optionally a number).
  Cast { spell: String, arguments: Vec<String> },
  ```
- :213–215: `"CAST" => { let spell = arguments.first()?; Some(Intent::Cast { spell: spell.text.clone(), arguments: arguments[1..].iter().map(|t| t.text.clone()).collect() }) }`.
  (`arguments` here is the token slice the other arms use; `Token.text`/`.kind` as `STUDY` reads
  them at :175–184.) Delete the `MonthLong("CAST")` arm and its comment; keep the `MonthLong`
  variant for BUILD/PRODUCE/SAIL.
- Test in `mod tests`: `cast_keeps_the_spell_and_its_arguments`
  (`"unit 5\nCAST Transmutation 4 rootstone\n"` → `Intent::Cast { spell: "Transmutation", arguments: ["4","rootstone"] }`),
  and update the existing MonthLong test near :569 if it lists CAST.

### `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`

- `Ordered::is_busy` (:275–289, the "spends its month" predicate the teaching check reads) gains
  `| Intent::Cast { .. }` — a caster is still not a spare teacher.
- `apply()` (:470): `Intent::Cast { spell, arguments } => cast(ledger, actor, placed, spell, arguments, ruleset),`
  and remove `MonthLong(_)` from nothing (it stays for the others).
- New, beside `study` (:583):
  ```rust
  /// Charges what the ruleset says a cast consumes. A spell the ruleset does not know, or knows
  /// no cost for, charges nothing and doubts nothing: most spells cost nothing to cast, and a
  /// unit's other sums are still good.
  fn cast(ledger: &mut Ledger<'_>, actor: &Ordered<'_>, placed: &PlacedIntent, spell: &str, arguments: &[String], ruleset: Option<&Ruleset>) {
      let who = &actor.unit.unit_id;
      let Some(cost) = ruleset.and_then(|r| r.find_skill(spell)).and_then(|s| s.cast.as_ref()) else { return; };
      for input in &cost.costs {
          charge(ledger, who, &input.tag, input.amount, placed);     // `SILV` is the SILVER key
      }
      if cost.transmute.is_empty() { return; }
      // CAST Transmutation [number] <material>: the material is the *output*, the source is the
      // ruleset's business; an unnumbered cast makes what it can, so the least a successful one
      // consumes is one.
      let (number, material) = match arguments {
          [n, m] => match n.parse::<i64>() { Ok(n) if n > 0 => (n, m.as_str()), _ => return },
          [m] => (1, m.as_str()),
          _ => return,
      };
      let Some(output) = ruleset.and_then(|r| r.find_item(material)) else { return; };
      let Some(source) = cost.transmute.get(&output.tag.to_ascii_uppercase()) else { return; };
      charge(ledger, who, source, number, placed);
  }
  ```
  `charge` (:694) uppercases the tag and records `charged_at` so the finding points at the CAST
  line; `find_skill` (`rules.rs:575`) resolves `Create_Ring_Of_Invisibility` / `CRRI` / quoted
  names as `STUDY` already relies on; `find_item` (`rules.rs:551`) resolves `rootstone`/`ROOT`.
- No message changes: a short mage gets `short $400: this unit can have $200 and its orders spend $600`
  (per-unit silver, :749) or `short 1 sword: this unit can have 0 and its orders give away or sell 1`
  (per-unit item, ah-j2w's wording) — the "give away or sell" verb is slightly off for a cast; the
  navigator accepted the shared wording knowingly (see *User-facing decisions*).

### Tests (`semantics.rs::tests`, helpers `unit`, `with_silver`, `with_item`, `with_skill`, `sharing`, `region`, `check`, `codes`, `only`; `check` uses the committed ruleset, so the real cast costs apply — CRRI 600 silver, ESWO one SWOR, TRNS ROOT→STON, CGAT 1000, FIRE none)

New block `// --- what a spell costs to cast ---`:
- `a_mage_that_cannot_pay_for_the_artifact_it_casts_is_warned_about`: `with_silver(with_skill(unit("5"), "CRRI", 3), 200)`, `"unit 5\nCAST Create_Ring_Of_Invisibility\n"` → `only`, `not-enough-silver`, `unit_id == Some("5")`, `line == Some(2)`, message `"short $400: this unit can have $200 and its orders spend $600"`.
- `a_mage_that_can_pay_is_silent` (600 silver → `vec![]`).
- `the_stated_cost_is_charged_once_however_much_the_spell_makes` (CRPA at level 3 with 200 silver → `vec![]`; the engine charges 200 once, not 600).
- `an_enchanter_with_nothing_to_enchant_is_warned_about` (ESWO, no swords, `"CAST Enchant_Swords"` → `not-enough-items`, message contains `"1 sword"`); `an_enchanter_with_one_sword_is_silent`.
- `a_transmuter_names_its_output_and_is_charged_the_source` (`with_item(unit("5"), 3, "stone", "STON")`, `"CAST Transmutation 4 rootstone"` → `not-enough-items` short 1 stone; `"CAST Transmutation rootstone"` with 3 stone → `vec![]`; with no stone → short 1 stone).
- `constructing_a_gate_costs_a_thousand` (999 silver → short $1).
- `a_spell_with_no_stated_cost_charges_nothing` (`"CAST Fire"` on a penniless mage → `vec![]`; and `"CAST Fire\nSTUDY combat"` on a mage with $10 for 1 man → `vec![]` too, i.e. the mage is not doubted).
- `an_unknown_spell_charges_nothing` (`"CAST Super_Magic"` → `vec![]`).
- `a_mage_supplied_by_a_sharing_unit_in_the_hex_is_silent` (mage with 0 silver, `sharing(with_silver(unit("7"), 600))`, `"CAST Create_Ring_Of_Invisibility"` → `vec![]`) — this is ah-j2w's rule seen from the mage's side, the reason the family was ordered as it was.
- `a_caster_is_not_a_spare_teacher` — extend whatever test pins `MonthLong` for the teaching check (`grep -n MonthLong` in the teaching tests) with a `CAST` line, or add one asserting no `teacher-has-free-slots` for a casting mage.

### `packages/shared` — no change (codes and messages are the existing ones).

## Increments

1. **The intent.** RED: `cast_keeps_the_spell_and_its_arguments`. Add `Intent::Cast`, the arm,
   the month-long predicate; `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core intents`.
2. **Charging.** RED, one at a time: the artifact pair, `the_stated_cost_is_charged_once…`, the
   enchant pair, the transmutation test, the gate, the two no-cost tests. Add `cast()`;
   `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core semantics`.
3. **Pooling and teaching.** RED: `a_mage_supplied_by_a_sharing_unit_in_the_hex_is_silent` (goes
   green at once if ah-j2w is in — it is the pin), `a_caster_is_not_a_spare_teacher`.
4. **Gate.** `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --check`;
   `pnpm run check:fast`; `pnpm run check` once. PR
   `feat(ah-dbb.2): a mage short of what its spell costs is warned like any other shortfall`;
   `@copilot`; CI; squash. Close the parent ah-dbb with the last child (`implement-bead`).

## The test plan

- Rust `intents.rs::tests`: 1. `semantics.rs::tests`: 12 (increments 2–3). Pins: each cost class,
  once-per-cast, unknown/no-cost silence without doubt, the pool, the month.
- Suites: `cargo test --workspace`, `pnpm run check:fast`, `pnpm run check` once.

## User-facing decisions

Asked 2026-08-16 (Beast → navigator), for the family:

1. **Scope:** every spell with a stated cost — silver-cost creations and construct gate, the three
   enchant spells, transmutation. Rejected: silver-cost creations only.
2. **Reporting:** the same codes and words as any shortfall (`not-enough-silver` /
   `not-enough-items`), pointing at the CAST line. Rejected: a new toggle and a message naming the
   spell ("cannot pay for Create Magic Carpet: it needs $400 and this unit can have $200").
   Consequence accepted: an item cost reads "its orders give away or sell 1" for a cast.
3. **A spell the ruleset knows no cost for:** say nothing, and do not doubt the unit. Rejected: an
   informational note per unknown spell.
4. **Chance-based creations:** charge one item's cost, i.e. the stated cost once. (The question's
   gloss that level-count spells charge `level × cost` was mine and wrong: the engine's
   `RunCreateArtifact` consumes the stated inputs once per cast whatever it makes — recorded here
   so nobody "fixes" the once-per-cast rule toward the gloss.)

## Out of scope

- Naming the spell in the message, or a spell-specific toggle.
- The success chance, how many items a cast makes, skill-level prerequisites ("CAST: Skill level
  isn't that high") — the check reads only what is consumed.
- Reading costs from the report (a failed casting's message) — the ruleset is the source.
- Enchant/transmute upper bounds (`5 × level`, `2 × level`): the check charges the least a
  successful cast consumes; a mage with fewer inputs than the maximum makes fewer, which is not a
  fault.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core intents
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core semantics
cargo test --workspace
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --check
git grep -n 'MonthLong("CAST")' crates   # → nothing
pnpm run check:fast && pnpm run check
```

Human check (Psylocke): load a report with a mage (e.g. `g7f95t71`), write
`CAST Create_Ring_Of_Invisibility` on a unit with less than 600 silver in its hex → a
`not-enough-silver` warning on that line; give a sharing unit in the hex 600 silver → gone.

## Known traps

- **`Intent::Cast` must join `Ordered::is_busy` (`semantics.rs:275`)**, or a casting mage
  is offered as a spare teacher — the reason CAST was `MonthLong` in the first place.
- **The transmutation argument is the output**, not the source ("<material> is the resource you
  wish to create"); the map in `CastCost.transmute` is output → source. Charging the output tag
  would warn about rootstone nobody has.
- **`SILV` goes through `charge` like any tag** and lands under the `SILVER` key (`"SILV"`), so the
  silver message and the pooled purse pick it up with no special case — do not add one.
- **Do not doubt the caster** for an unknown spell or a spell without a cost; `Withdraw` doubts
  because its price is unknowable, a cost of nothing is known.
- **A number followed by nothing** (`CAST Transmutation 4`) is not a valid form; charge nothing.
- **The smoke suite rebuilds the web bundle with the service worker disabled**; run `pnpm run check`
  as one command.

title: The ruleset carries what each spell costs to cast, read from the game's data page
description: First of two children of ah-dbb. The data page states every casting cost in a fixed sentence (silver or items 'via magic at a cost of …', construct gate's 'the attempt costs 1000 silver', transmutation's 'N stone [STON] times the skill level into rootstone [ROOT]'); the scraper reads them into SkillEntry.cast on both sides of config/public/ruleset.json (TS packages/ruleset, Rust crates/core movement/rules.rs). No behaviour change yet. Plan in the design field.
design:
## Context

First of two children of ah-dbb (navigator, 2026-08-16: warn when a mage cannot pay for the spell
it is ordered to cast). Planned by Beast on 2026-08-16.

The bead's open question was *where spell costs come from*. Answer, established here: **the game's
data page states them**, in the same per-skill entries the scraper already reads study cost from
(`packages/ruleset/src/data.ts:307 parseSkillReference`, `tests/fixtures/ruleset/neworigins-data.html`).
Four phrasings cover every casting cost the committed page carries:

| Phrasing (level-1 entry unless said) | Skills | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `via magic at a cost of 600 silver [SILV].` | CRRI, CRCL, CRSF, CRTA, CRPA, CRRU, CRSS, CRMA, CPOR, CFSW, CRAG, CRWC, CRGC, CRSH, CRSO, CRCO, CRBX, CRHS, CRCN | silver, once per cast |
| `via magic at a cost of sword [SWOR].` (no number) | ESWO, EARM, ESHD | one item per item made; the least a successful cast consumes is one |
| `via magic at a cost of 75 floater hides [FLOA] and 75 ironwood [IRWD].` — on the **level 3** entry | SWIN | several inputs, joined by ` and ` |
| `the attempt costs 1000 silver.` | CGAT | silver, once per attempt |
| `may transmute 2 stone [STON] times the skill level into rootstone [ROOT] or 2 iron [IRON] times the skill level into mithril [MITH].` — level 1; level 2 adds `2 wood [WOOD] … into ironwood [IRWD]`, level 3 `2 furs [FUR] … into floater hide [FLOA]` | TRNS | output → source, one source per output made |

Everything else a mage can CAST (summons, lores, combat spells) states no cost, and the engine
charges none.

Verified in the engine (Atlantis `spells.cpp`, fetched 2026-08-16): `RunCreateArtifact` checks
`GetSharedNum(input) < amt` and consumes `amt` **once per cast** whatever the roll makes;
`RunEnchant` makes `min(5 × level, inputs available)` and consumes one input per output;
`RunTransmutation` consumes one source per output up to `2 × level` (or the stated number, and
errors "Can't create that many" only when a number was stated); `RunConstructGate` consumes 1000
before the roll. All through `GetSharedNum`/`ConsumeShared` — own holdings plus sharing units,
which ah-j2w models.

**This child carries the costs into the ruleset** — scraper, JSON, and the Rust reader — and
nothing else. ah-dbb.2 (blocked on this and on ah-j2w) charges them at the CAST line.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `packages/ruleset/src/data.ts`

Extend `SkillEntry` (:93):

```ts
/** One thing a cast consumes: an item tag and how many, silver being `SILV`. */
export type CastInput = { tag: string; amount: number };

/**
 * What CASTing the skill consumes, as the data page states it: `costs`, each taken once per cast
 * (an input with no number is one), and for transmutation the output tag → source tag it turns
 * into. `null` when the page states no cost - most spells.
 */
export type CastCost = { costs: CastInput[]; transmute: Record<string, string> };

export type SkillEntry = {
  tag: string;
  name: string;
  cost: number | null;
  maxLevel: number;
  cast: CastCost | null;
};
```

Patterns, beside `STUDY_COST` (:298):

```ts
/** "via magic at a cost of 600 silver [SILV]." / "… of sword [SWOR]." / "… of 75 floater hides [FLOA] and 75 ironwood [IRWD]." */
const CAST_COST = /via magic at a cost of ([^.]+)\./i;
/** One input inside the list above: an optional number, a name, the tag. */
const CAST_INPUT = /^(?:(\d+) )?[a-z][a-z ]* \[([A-Z0-9]{2,6})\]$/i;
/** "the attempt costs 1000 silver." (Construct Gate) */
const ATTEMPT_COST = /the attempt costs (\d+) silver/i;
/** "2 stone [STON] times the skill level into rootstone [ROOT]" - the source and what it becomes. */
const TRANSMUTE = /\d+ [a-z ]+ \[([A-Z0-9]{2,6})\] times the skill level into [a-z ]+ \[([A-Z0-9]{2,6})\]/gi;
```

`readCastCost(paragraph): CastCost | null`: `CAST_COST` match → split on ` and `, each through
`CAST_INPUT` → `{ tag, amount: n ?? 1 }` (an input that does not match the pattern throws
`RulesetScrapeError` naming the skill and the text — the page changed shape, and a silently
dropped cost is the failure this whole ruleset refuses); `ATTEMPT_COST` → `{ tag: "SILV", amount: n }`;
every `TRANSMUTE` match → `transmute[output] = source`. Return `null` when both are empty.

In `parseSkillReference`'s fold (:317–327): `cast: mergeCast(existing?.cast, readCastCost(paragraph))`
— costs are stated on **any** level (SWIN's are on level 3, TRNS adds outputs on levels 2 and 3),
so the fold unions: `costs` from whichever level states them (first stated wins, as `cost` does),
`transmute` merged across levels. Doc the fold accordingly (:303–306).

### `packages/ruleset/src/build.ts` — no shape change (`skills: SkillReference` carries the field);
the sanity check at :123 stays. Regenerate:

```bash
pnpm --filter @atlantis/ruleset scrape -- --rules tests/fixtures/ruleset/neworigins-rules.html --data tests/fixtures/ruleset/neworigins-data.html
```
which rewrites `config/public/ruleset.json` (every skill gains `"cast": null` or a block;
`source.fetchedAt` moves — that is expected, `committed.test.ts` compares the scrape's output).

### `crates/core/src/movement/rules.rs`

Beside `SkillEntry` (:272):

```rust
/// One thing a cast consumes: an item tag (`SILV` for silver) and how many.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase", deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct CastInput { pub tag: String, pub amount: i64 }

/// What CASTing a skill consumes, as the data page states it and as ah-dbb.2 charges it: `costs`
/// once per cast, and for transmutation the output tag → the source tag it is made from.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase", deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct CastCost { pub costs: Vec<CastInput>, pub transmute: BTreeMap<String, String> }
```
and on `SkillEntry`: `#[serde(default)] pub cast: Option<CastCost>,` — `default`, because a
ruleset file deployed before this field existed must still load (the same promise
`a_ruleset_without_a_skill_catalogue_still_loads` makes for the whole block; the shell serves
whatever file is deployed).

### Tests

- `packages/ruleset/src/data.test.ts`, in `describe("parseSkillReference")` (:355), one `it` per
  phrasing, each with a small hand-written `<pre>` entry in the shape the existing tests use:
  `"reads a silver casting cost"` (CRRI → `{costs:[{tag:"SILV",amount:600}],transmute:{}}`),
  `"reads an item cost with no number as one"` (ESWO → `[{tag:"SWOR",amount:1}]`),
  `"reads several inputs joined by and, stated on a later level"` (SWIN: level 1 entry without a
  cost, level 3 with → the fold keeps them),
  `"reads the attempt cost of construct gate"` (`[{tag:"SILV",amount:1000}]`),
  `"reads what transmutation turns into what, across levels"` (TRNS levels 1–3 → `{ROOT:"STON",MITH:"IRON",IRWD:"WOOD",FLOA:"FUR"}`),
  `"records no casting cost for a spell the page prices nowhere"` (FIRE → `cast: null`),
  `"fails loudly on a cost it cannot read"` (`at a cost of some things.` → throws).
- `packages/ruleset/src/build.test.ts:45–47`: add `expect(ruleset.skills.CRRI.cast).toEqual({ costs: [{ tag: "SILV", amount: 600 }], transmute: {} })` and `expect(ruleset.skills.FIRE.cast).toBeNull()`.
- `packages/ruleset/src/committed.test.ts`: unchanged; goes green once the JSON is regenerated.
- `crates/core/tests/movement_ruleset.rs`, after `reads_what_a_month_of_study_costs` (:326):
  `reads_what_a_cast_consumes` (CRRI silver 600; ESWO one SWOR; SWIN two inputs; CGAT 1000; TRNS
  transmute map has ROOT→STON and MITH→IRON; FIRE `cast.is_none()`), and
  `a_skill_entry_without_a_cast_block_still_loads` (strip `cast` from one skill in the JSON →
  loads, `cast == None`). Extend the `deny_unknown_fields` probe test (:405–) with the new depth:
  an unknown key inside `cast` fails to load.

## Increments

1. **Scraper.** RED: the seven `data.test.ts` tests. Add the types, patterns, `readCastCost`, the
   fold. `pnpm --filter @atlantis/ruleset test`.
2. **Regenerate the JSON.** Run the scrape; `build.test.ts` additions RED → green;
   `committed.test.ts` green. Inspect the diff of `config/public/ruleset.json`: 23 skills gain a
   block, the rest `"cast": null`.
3. **Rust reader.** RED: `reads_what_a_cast_consumes` (compile error, then a `deny_unknown_fields`
   failure on the regenerated file — which is the guard doing its job). Add the structs and field;
   `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test movement_ruleset`; the probe and the default test.
4. **Gate.** `pnpm run check:fast`; `pnpm run check` once (the web bundle ships the JSON). PR
   `feat(ah-dbb.1): the ruleset carries what a spell costs to cast`; `@copilot`; CI; squash.

## The test plan

- TS `data.test.ts`: 7 (increment 1). Pins every phrasing, the level fold, the loud failure.
- TS `build.test.ts` +2, `committed.test.ts` unchanged (proves the committed JSON is the scrape).
- Rust `movement_ruleset.rs`: +2 and the probe. Pins the reader, the old-file default, the
  unknown-key refusal.
- Suites: `pnpm --filter @atlantis/ruleset test`, `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core`, `pnpm run check:fast`, `pnpm run check` once.

## User-facing decisions

None in this child (data only). The navigator's decisions for the family are recorded on
ah-dbb.2; the one that shapes this file — every spell with a stated cost is in scope, others say
nothing — is why `cast` is `null` rather than an error for a costless spell.

## Out of scope

- Charging anything (ah-dbb.2). Displaying costs anywhere in the UI.
- Spell *outputs* (what is made, how many, the success chance) — the check only needs what is
  consumed. `TRANSMUTE`'s `2 … times the skill level` cap is not carried either.
- Skills whose cost is stated in a form the page does not use today; the loud failure covers a
  page that changes.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm --filter @atlantis/ruleset test
pnpm --filter @atlantis/ruleset scrape -- --rules tests/fixtures/ruleset/neworigins-rules.html --data tests/fixtures/ruleset/neworigins-data.html && git diff --stat config/public/ruleset.json
python3 -c "import json;r=json.load(open('config/public/ruleset.json'));print(sum(1 for s in r['skills'].values() if s['cast']))"   # → 23
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test movement_ruleset
pnpm run check:fast && pnpm run check
```

## Known traps

- **`deny_unknown_fields` on `SkillEntry` means the regenerated JSON will not load until the Rust
  field exists** — increments 2 and 3 land in one PR; do not merge the JSON alone.
- **The scrape rewrites `source.fetchedAt`**; that churn is expected and `committed.test.ts`
  ignores it (check how it compares before worrying).
- **`CAST_COST` must stop at the first `.`** — the sentence continues "To use this spell…";
  `[^.]+` does that. Names in the list carry no dots.
- **The transmutation source/output pairs on levels 2–3 are only in the fixture if the page had them**
  — the committed fixture does (checked 2026-08-16: WOOD→IRWD on level 2, FUR→FLOA on level 3).
- **`ItemKind`'s hand-written `Deserialize`** (:132) is the pattern for tolerant enums; `CastCost`
  is a plain struct and needs none of that.
- **The smoke suite rebuilds the web bundle with the service worker disabled**; run `pnpm run check`
  as one command.

title: Find the trade routes hiding in the map you have already seen
description:
Every region report lists what the hex sells and what it wants, with prices. Finding a hex selling
something for less than another will pay for it is arithmetic over data the client already holds —
and today it is done by eye, across turns, by remembering where things were cheap.

**The request:** find trade routes — a hex selling a good, and another buying the same good for
more.

## The data is already there

- `ReportRegion.for_sale` and `.wanted` are both `Vec<MarketItem>`, and `MarketItem` carries
  `amount`, `name`, `tag` and `price`. Both halves of a route, priced, per hex.
- `known_map` already holds hexes across turns with a `last_seen_turn` and a precedence between
  what was seen now and what is remembered.

So the naive version — every `for_sale` against every `wanted` of the same tag where the buy price
is higher — is a join over data in hand.

## What makes it useful rather than merely correct

The naive version will produce a long list of routes nobody can run. Three things separate a
finding from a suggestion:

- **Staleness.** A price seen forty turns ago is a rumour. `last_seen_turn` is already there to say
  how old each half of a pair is, and a route built from two old sightings should say so rather than
  present itself as fact.
- **Distance.** A margin of 20 silver a unit is worth nothing thirty hexes away. The movement code
  already computes routes and costs; a trade route without a travel time is half an answer.
- **Quantity.** `amount` bounds both ends: how much the seller has and how much the buyer will take.
  The profit is over the smaller of the two, not over the price difference.

Whether all three are in scope is the main sizing question. The margin-only version is small and
might be enough to be useful; each addition makes it more useful and larger.

## For the planner to settle with the navigator

- **How far the first version goes** — margin only, or margin with distance and quantity.
- **Where it appears.** A panel, a map overlay showing both ends, something in the orders editor
  where the buying and selling would be written. This decides most of the work and is a user-facing
  decision.
- **Whether it accounts for what the player can actually carry.** Weight and capacity are parsed and
  a route needs a unit able to haul the goods, but that couples this to movement and could easily
  double the bead.
- **Which hexes count.** Only what the faction has seen, presumably — but the known map holds hexes
  named by an exit without ever being visited, and those have no prices at all.

## Validation

With a report where one hex sells an item and another wants it for more, the route is found and its
margin stated correctly. A pair with the buy price at or below the sell price is not offered. Where
staleness, distance or quantity are in scope, each is reflected — a route from a forty-turn-old
sighting is marked as such, and the profit respects the smaller of the two amounts.
acceptance_criteria: The client can find pairs of hexes where one sells a good and another buys the same good at a higher price, and states the margin. Pairs with no margin are not offered. Whatever is decided about staleness, distance and quantity, the answer does not present a route the player cannot judge - an old sighting is marked as old, and a stated profit is not larger than the amounts on either end allow.

title: Warn when a GIVE or TAKE names a unit that is not in the hex
description:
Filed by the corpus investigation ah-v25.

## Evidence
`GIVE: Nonexistant target (N).` - 5 occurrences across 2 turns of 1 game in
tests/fixtures/reports/ (docs/order-checks/corpus-errors.generated.md). A GIVE or TAKE order named
a unit id that was not present anywhere in the report - most likely a typo or a unit that had
already left.

## What the check would need
From the report: every unit id the report shows, anywhere (own units and any visible foreign
units). From the orders: the target id of every GIVE/TAKE order (`orders::intents::Party::Unit`).

## What it must not do
Never blocking; accept on doubt (crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs:1-17). A target that could be
a new unit not yet numbered (`Party::New`) or a unit outside the hex the report does not show is not
this case and must not warn.

## Validation
A GIVE naming a unit id absent from the whole report warns. A GIVE naming a unit id the report shows
anywhere, or targeting NEW/a faction, stays silent.
design:
## Context

The engine refuses a gift whose target it cannot find, and tells the player a week later, in the
report's `Errors during turn:` section:

```
tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t82.rep:87
  City Guards (13303): GIVE: Nonexistant target (7233).
```

Five occurrences across two turns of the committed corpus, all faction 42
(`docs/order-checks/corpus-errors.generated.md`, and the classification row in
`docs/order-checks/README.md`). The goods stay put and the month is spent.

**Reading the five cases changed the shape of this bead, and the change was agreed with the
navigator on 2026-08-17.** The bead's title and description say to warn when the target is "not
visible in the report". Only **two** of the five are that. The other three name a unit that is alive
and well and standing in a different hex:

| fixture:line | giver, and its hex | target | the report shows the target |
|---|---|---|---|
| `t82.rep:87` | 13303, `mountain (36,4)` | 7233 | **nowhere** — it died between turn 42 and turn 82 |
| `t82.rep:88` | 13303, `mountain (36,4)` | 16585 | **nowhere** in any fixture |
| `t82.rep:89` | 8443, `forest (40,4)` | 15467 | own unit, alive, in `mountain (36,4)` |
| `t82.rep:90` | 4426, `mountain (35,5)` | 13304 | own unit, alive, in `tundra (35,7)` |
| `t40.rep:59` | 6111, `plain (39,7)` | 3247 | own unit, alive, in `forest (49,3)` |

So the test is **"is it in this hex"**, not "does it exist" — which is also what the rules say. "Two
units in different regions cannot normally interact"
(`tests/fixtures/ruleset/neworigins-rules.html:830`), and `GIVE` requires a target "which it is
able to see" (`:6236`). `TAKE` is the same order from the other end and needs the other unit in the
same region too (`:7370`).

**A report-based check is sound because of the turn order.** `GIVE`/`TAKE` run in phase 4, before
movement in phase 9 (`neworigins-rules.html:7775` against `:7843`), so the positions this report
prints are exactly the positions next turn's transfer resolves against.

**What lands.** One new advisory code, `give-target-not-here`, one new toggle in the existing
*Orders* group, and four message forms — two for `GIVE`, two for `TAKE`, differing in whether the
report knows the unit at all. A courier that has moved and a mistyped number are different mistakes
with different fixes, and the line says which one the player has.

**The nearest thing already built is `taught-not-here`** (`semantics.rs:971-981`,
`"unit {id} is not in this hex to be taught"`), which is the same shape of mistake for `TEACH`. The
navigator chose to match its sentence deliberately. Read that emission site before writing this one.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` — the code

```rust
    pub const GIVE_TARGET_NOT_HERE: Code = Code("give-target-not-here");
```

appended to `codes::ALL`, which becomes `[Code; 13]`. **Count what is there when you arrive** rather
than trusting this number.

`ALL`'s doc comment (`:80-83`) currently ends:

> …but a new entry still goes last: the generated TypeScript copies this order, and every entry
> added since `hex-unguarded` has kept new-last / grouped-last in step with each other.

**That last clause stops being true with this bead** and must be amended, or the next reader will
believe it and put their entry in the wrong group. This code goes **last in `ALL`** and **into the
existing *Orders* group**, which is fourth of five. Replace the clause with:

> …but a new entry still goes last: the generated TypeScript copies this order. Until
> `give-target-not-here` every entry had also been last in its tab group; that one joins the
> existing *Orders* group instead, so the two orders are no longer in step and nothing depends on
> their being so.

### `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` — where the report shows each unit

The check needs to look **outside** the hex, which no check here has done before. `check_turn`
already has the whole report (`report: &ParsedReport`, `:152`) and `ParsedReport` already has the
iterator (`crates/core/src/report/mod.rs:53`, `pub fn units(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &ReportUnit>`;
production precedent at `crates/core/src/movement/request.rs:95`). Build the lookup once, above the
region loop:

```rust
/// Where the report shows each unit, by unit number, across every region it covers.
///
/// Built once for the whole report rather than per hex, because the point of the lookup is to tell
/// a mistyped unit number from a real unit standing somewhere else, and only the second of those
/// is answerable from outside the hex. Every unit the report prints is in here, ours and any
/// foreign one we can see: a gift to another faction's unit standing in our hex is ordinary.
fn where_the_report_shows_each_unit(report: &ParsedReport) -> BTreeMap<&str, String> {
    let mut located = BTreeMap::new();
    for region in &report.regions {
        let label = region.label();
        for unit in &region.units {
            located.insert(unit.unit_id.as_str(), label.clone());
        }
    }
    located
}
```

`ReportRegion::label()` (`crates/core/src/report/model.rs:223`, over `region_label` at `:236`) is
`format!("{terrain} ({x},{y}) in {province}")` — `mountain (36,4) in Slounspifra`. It is the
report's own header wording and the label the interface already uses everywhere; do not build a
different one.

In `check_turn`, above `for region in &report.regions`:

```rust
    let located = where_the_report_shows_each_unit(report);
```

and inside the loop, after `check_forms`:

```rust
        check_transfer_targets(&hex, &located, &options, &mut findings);
```

### `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs` — the check

Next to `check_forms`:

```rust
/// Every GIVE and TAKE one of our units gives whose counterparty is a unit number: is that unit in
/// this hex to receive the goods, or to be taken from? The engine refuses the order outright when
/// it is not - `GIVE: Nonexistant target (N).` - and says so only once the turn has run. GIVE and
/// TAKE are phase 4, before anything moves in phase 9, so the hex the report prints a unit in is
/// the hex the transfer will look for it in.
///
/// The test is against every unit the report shows in this region, not against `hex.find`, which
/// sees only our own: giving to another faction's unit standing here is legal and ordinary.
///
/// A unit the report shows somewhere else has that region named, because a courier that has moved
/// and a mistyped number are different mistakes with different fixes. NEW, FACTION n NEW and unit
/// zero name nothing the report could show, and are passed over rather than guessed at.
fn check_transfer_targets(
    hex: &Hex<'_>,
    located: &BTreeMap<&str, String>,
    options: &CheckOptions,
    findings: &mut Vec<Finding>,
) {
    if !options.emits(codes::GIVE_TARGET_NOT_HERE) {
        return;
    }

    for ordered in &hex.units {
        for placed in ordered.intents {
            let (party, verb) = match &placed.intent {
                Intent::Give { to, .. } => (to, "given to"),
                Intent::Take { from, .. } => (from, "taken from"),
                _ => continue,
            };
            let Party::Unit(id) = party else { continue };
            if hex
                .region
                .units
                .iter()
                .any(|unit| &unit.unit_id == id)
            {
                continue;
            }

            let message = match located.get(id.as_str()) {
                Some(label) => format!(
                    "unit {id} is not in this hex to be {verb} - your report shows it in {label}"
                ),
                None => format!(
                    "unit {id} is not in this hex to be {verb}, and appears nowhere else in \
                     your report"
                ),
            };
            findings.push(ordered.finding(hex, codes::GIVE_TARGET_NOT_HERE, message, Some(placed)));
        }
    }
}
```

Everything it leans on is verified:

- `Intent::Give { to: Party, .. }` (`orders/intents.rs:20`) and `Intent::Take { from: Party, .. }`
  (`:26`). `Party` (`orders/forms.rs:43-52`) is `Unit(String) | New(String) | Foreign { .. } |
  Discard`; `read_party` (`forms.rs:55-91`) turns an all-zero token into `Discard` at `:87`, so
  `GIVE 0` can never look like a missing unit. `TEACH` is the only other intent naming a `Party`
  and is not this bead's business.
- `Hex::read` (`:220-231`) filters `units` to `unit.own`, so `hex.find` (`:233`) **cannot see a
  visible foreign unit in the same hex**. Using it here would warn about every legal gift to
  another faction. `hex.region.units` (`report/model.rs:217`) is the full list.
- `Ordered::finding(hex, code, message, at)` (`:340`) puts the finding on the order's own line.
- `Party`, `Intent` and `BTreeMap` are already imported (`:19-27`); `ParsedReport` is too (`:27`).

**The message is ASCII, deliberately.** The mockup drew an em dash; every one of the twelve existing
finding messages is pure ASCII, and this file's prose uses ` - ` where an em dash would go. Use the
hyphen. At panel size the two are indistinguishable, and the consistency is worth more.

### `packages/core-client/src/coreVocabulary.generated.ts`

Regenerate, do not hand-edit:

```bash
ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test generated_ts
```

The guard is `crates/core/tests/generated_ts.rs` (`:9` names the file, `:54` the env var, `:68` the
staleness message). `pnpm run check:generated` fails until this is run.

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.tsx`

`WARNING_GROUPS` (`:290`): the **existing** *Orders* group (`:352-360`) gains a second entry, after
`form-alias-reused`:

```ts
      {
        code: "give-target-not-here",
        title: "Gifts to units that are not here",
        description: "A GIVE or TAKE naming a unit the report does not show in that hex."
      }
```

No new group. `settingsStore.ts` needs no change: a new code defaults to on, and only
`hex-unguarded` is off by default (`CheckOptions::default()`, `semantics.rs:115-127`).

### `packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.test.tsx`

The hand-written `titles` list (`:50-62`) gains `"Gifts to units that are not here"`. Nothing else:
the same test already loops `ADVISORY_CHECK_CODES` for a toggle per code (`:68-71`) and for the
on-by-default assertion (`:78-84`), so both pick the new code up from the regenerated vocabulary
without being edited. The group headings assertion (`:41-45`) already expects `Orders`.

### `docs/order-checks/README.md`

The `Covered by` column already names `ah-djq` for this row. Nothing to change.

## Increments

Run `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core` throughout.

**1 — The code exists and can be silenced.** RED: the per-code fixture table in `semantics.rs`'s
tests (`:2569`) asserts `cases.len() == ALL.len()`, so adding the constant to `ALL` breaks it before
anything emits. Add the constant, amend `ALL`'s doc comment, add the fixture row (below), and write
`check_transfer_targets` far enough to emit on that row. Regenerate the vocabulary.

**2 — The four sentences.** RED: the four message tests below, one per form. GREEN by the `match` on
`located`.

**3 — What it must not say.** RED for `a_gift_to_a_foreign_unit_in_the_hex_is_silent`, which fails
if the implementation reached for `hex.find`; the `NEW` / `FACTION` / `unit 0` tests are **green on
arrival** and are there to stop a later change reaching past `Party::Unit`.

**4 — The Warnings tab.** RED: `SettingsDialog.test.tsx` with the title added. GREEN by the
`WARNING_GROUPS` entry.
`pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared exec vitest run src/workspace/SettingsDialog.test.tsx`.

**5 — Gate and look once.** `pnpm run check:fast`, then *Validation*.

## The test plan

Rust tests go in `semantics.rs`'s `mod tests`, in a new `--- transfer targets ---` section after
`--- FORM aliases ---`. Reuse `region`, `unit`, `with_item`, `with_silver`, `check`, `codes`,
`only`, `report`.

**Two fixture facts these tests need.** `region(units)` builds region `1:7,53`, `mountain (7,53)`,
province `Inhead` — so its label is `mountain (7,53) in Inhead`. A second region needs its
`region_id` and `coordinate` changed, exactly as `a_disabled_code_silences_both_its_emission_sites`

```rust
elsewhere.region_id = "1:8,53".to_string();
elsewhere.coordinate = Coordinate { x: 8, y: 53, z: 1 };
// label: "mountain (8,53) in Inhead"
```

Also: **stock every giver**, or `check_resources` adds a `not-enough-items` or `not-enough-silver`

```rust

                codes::GIVE_TARGET_NOT_HERE,

```

Check that fixture emits **only** the new code when nothing is disabled — unit 5 holds 1000 silver
and gives 500, so no shortfall.

**TypeScript:** `SettingsDialog.test.tsx` as edited.

### The whole-turn test, and the six gifts that make it the best test in this bead

`crates/core/tests/validate_real_orders.rs:91` (`the_committed_turn_has_no_semantic_problems_either`)
runs `check_turn` over turn 71 and asserts **zero findings**; `:168` re-asserts it fifty times. This
bead is the one most likely to break it, being the first check that fires on an ordinary `GIVE`.

**It has been checked, by hand, before this plan was written, and it stays green — but only if you
build the check as specified.** Turn 71's template (there is no separate orders file; it is sliced
out of the same `.rep` by `extract_orders_template`, `crates/core/src/report/orders.rs:66`) holds
136 `GIVE`/`TAKE` lines. 130 are `GIVE 0 …` discards, none is a `NEW` or `FACTION` target, there is
not a single `TURN` or `FORM` block in the file, and there are no `TAKE`s. That leaves **six**:

| template line | issuer | target | both in |
|---|---|---|---|
| 229 | 881 | 2396 | `ocean (26,52) in Atlantis Ocean` |
| 262 | 12878 | 2396 | same |
| 297 | 12879 | 2396 | same |
| 334 | 20 | 2396 | same |
| 419 | 12880 | 2396 | same |
| 455 | 12881 | 2396 | same |

**Unit 2396 is not ours.** It is `- Wistful Soldiers (2396), Wistful Thinking (27), …` — an allied
faction's unit, standing in the same hex, receiving mithril armour from six of our units. The
report's own events section records last turn's identical gifts landing (`:1593`,
`Six of Seven (881): Gives 10 mithril armor [MARM] to Wistful Soldiers (2396).`).

So this test is the real version of `a_gift_to_a_foreign_unit_in_the_hex_is_silent`:

- Build the check against `hex.region.units` as specified and it stays green.
- Reach for `hex.find` and **it goes red with six findings**, every one of them wrong.
- Scope the check to the *structure* rather than the hex and it also goes red: the six givers are
  all inside `Princess of the Dawn [1239]`, a Cloudship, while 2396 is inside `Frozen Tomb [194]`,
  a Galley. Gifts across structures within a hex are ordinary.

**Run it at the end of increment 1**, not at the gate — six findings on a real turn is the loudest
and earliest signal available that the lookup is wrong, and it costs one `cargo test` to get.

If it does go red for some *other* reason — a target this survey did not anticipate — the finding
may well be correct, and "turn 71 has a real order mistake in it" is the navigator's call, not
yours. Do not weaken the check and do not edit the assertion: escalate through the `human` queue.

## User-facing decisions

Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-17 over two rounds, against two mockups. The chosen one is
committed at **`docs/ui/give-target-not-here.html`** (PR #350, merged) and carries the evidence, the
rejected options and the four sentences in place. Read it before starting.

**1. The test is "is the target in this hex", not "does the target exist anywhere".** Catches all
five real corpus cases rather than two.
*Rejected:* the bead's own wording, "not visible in the report" — it cannot be a false positive, but
it is silent on three of the five confirmed engine refusals, which are the commoner kind. Also
rejected: one message covering both cases, which is the smallest thing to build but leaves the
player unable to tell a typo from a courier that has moved.

**2. Four sentences, exactly as follows. Assert them verbatim.**

```
unit 15467 is not in this hex to be given to - your report shows it in mountain (36,4) in Slounspifra
unit 16585 is not in this hex to be given to, and appears nowhere else in your report
unit 13304 is not in this hex to be taken from - your report shows it in tundra (35,7) in Bedba
unit 16585 is not in this hex to be taken from, and appears nowhere else in your report
```

Chosen to match `taught-not-here`'s existing `unit {id} is not in this hex to be taught` — the same
shape of mistake, the same sentence, a different ending. The navigator noted "to be given to" is
clumsy read alone and kept it anyway for that consistency.
*Rejected:* leading with the order — `GIVE names unit 15467, which is not in this hex - …` — which
reads better and tells the player which line to look at when a unit has a `GIVE` and a `TAKE`
adjacent, but breaks step with the only sibling check of this shape.
**One deviation from the mockup, mine, and the navigator may reverse it:** the mockup drew an em
dash and these use a hyphen, because every existing finding message is ASCII.

**3. The toggle** is `Gifts to units that are not here`, described
`A GIVE or TAKE naming a unit the report does not show in that hex.`, in the **existing** *Orders*
group beside *Reused FORM numbers*, **on by default**.
*Rejected:* a group of its own.

**4. Accepted, drawn in the mockup's table, and not to be re-opened:**

| case | behaviour |
|---|---|
| `GIVE 0` | silent — unit zero destroys goods (`rules:6268`) |
| `GIVE NEW 2` / `GIVE FACTION 15 NEW 2` | silent — no number the report could show |
| `TAKE FROM` | warned the same way, with its own two sentences |
| a visible foreign unit in the hex | silent — a legal, ordinary target |
| a gift of **silver** to an unlisted unit | **warned.** The rules do let silver go to anyone (`:6240`), which argues for exempting it — but three of the four confirmed errors are silver gifts, so exempting silver would gut the check |
| a **stealthed friendly** unit in your hex | warned, **wrongly**. The one accepted false positive: an unseen unit is not printed but may legally be given to (`:6236`), and nothing distinguishes that from a typo. Accepted because on the corpus this check fires about eight times across two turns and at least four are confirmed engine refusals |
| orders inside `TURN … ENDTURN` | never checked — see *Out of scope* |

## Out of scope

- **Orders inside `TURN … ENDTURN` blocks.** `read_intents` reads only depth-0 orders
  (`orders/intents.rs:147`, guarded on `depth == Depth::default()`), so no check in this module sees
  a repeating order. **31 of the corpus's cross-hex gifts sit in these blocks** — the deliberate
  caravan pattern, correctly left alone — and one of the five real errors does too, so this check
  catches four of the five in practice. Changing that is a change to every check at once and is not
  this bead's.
- **Units remembered from earlier turns.** `known_map.rs` is not reachable from `check_turn`'s
  signature, and `resolve_known_map` drops units from stale sightings anyway (`known_map.rs:255-262`),
  so it carries no earlier-turn unit ids. A unit that existed last turn and is gone this turn is
  correctly the "appears nowhere" case.
- **`TEACH`**, whose `Party` targets are already handled by `taught-not-here`.
- **Whether the target's faction has declared you Friendly** (`rules:6236`), which the report does
  not carry reliably, and **whether men may be given to another faction** (`:6244`). Different
  checks, different beads, neither filed.
- **Telling a stealthed unit from a typo.** Not possible from the report; see the accepted false
  positive above.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core
ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test generated_ts
pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared exec vitest run src/workspace/SettingsDialog.test.tsx
pnpm run check:fast
```

**Look once, against the real report that produced the evidence.**

1. `pnpm --filter @atlantis/web dev`, then load
   `tests/fixtures/reports/neworigins-3.0.0-g3-f42-t82.rep` with its own orders template.
2. Go to `forest (40,4) in Pla'ere` (report line 5200). Unit 8443 orders `@give 15467 all yew` at
   template line 7600, and 15467 is `Lone Rider 40,4` in `mountain (36,4) in Slounspifra`
   (report line 5040).
3. Expect on that line: `unit 15467 is not in this hex to be given to - your report shows it in
   mountain (36,4) in Slounspifra`.
4. Go to `mountain (36,4) in Slounspifra` (report line 5114). Unit 13303 orders
   `@GIVE 16585 500 SILV` at template line 7541. Expect:
   `unit 16585 is not in this hex to be given to, and appears nowhere else in your report`.
5. Compare against the report's own `Errors during turn:` at lines 87-90: **the four warnings should
   be the four errors the engine reported.** Three more may appear (`6109`, `6391`, `7783`, all
   giving to `16340`, a courier that had ridden away) — those are real too; the engine did not
   report them only because those gifts succeeded before the courier moved or were written
   differently. Note what you see rather than treating a fifth line as a bug.
6. Turn the toggle off in Settings → Warnings → Orders and confirm every line goes.

## Known traps

- **`hex.find` is own-units-only** (`Hex::read` filters on `unit.own`, `:220-231`). Using it here
  warns about every legal gift to another faction's unit standing in your hex. Two tests catch it:
  `a_gift_to_a_foreign_unit_in_the_hex_is_silent`, and — far more convincingly — turn 71, which
  gives mithril armour to an allied unit six times.
- **The test is the hex, not the structure.** Turn 71's six givers are aboard one ship and their
  target is aboard another in the same hex. A gift across structures within a hex is ordinary.
- **`report.regions` is the region report, not the whole file.** Unit ids also appear in the
  battle and events sections above it, before any region header. The parser does not put those in
  `regions`, so `where_the_report_shows_each_unit` is already right — but do not "improve" it into
  a scan of the raw text, which would give unit 2396 a null region and five spurious findings.
- **`ALL`'s length is a type** (`[Code; 12]` today), and its doc comment makes a claim about tab
  grouping that this bead falsifies. Count what is there, and amend the comment.
- **`ALL`'s doc comment is not the only thing that must move together.** A code added to `ALL`
  without a `WARNING_GROUPS` entry gives a settings tab missing a toggle, and
  `SettingsDialog.test.tsx:68-71` is the test that catches it.
- **The vocabulary is generated.** Hand-editing `coreVocabulary.generated.ts` passes locally and
  fails `check:generated`. Use the env var.
- **Messages are ASCII in this codebase** — twelve of twelve. The em dash in the mockup is a hyphen
  in the code.
- **`validate_real_orders.rs` asserts zero findings over turn 71.** This bead can genuinely break
  it, and if it does the finding is probably right. See *The test plan* — that goes to the navigator,
  not into a weakened check.
- **`GIVE 0` is `Party::Discard`, not `Party::Unit("0")`** (`forms.rs:87`). Matching on the
  `Party::Unit` variant is what keeps discards silent; do not compare id strings to `"0"`.
- **A giver that cannot afford its gift produces a second finding** from `check_resources`, and
  `only(...)` panics on the count. Stock every giver in every fixture.
- **The two-region fixture needs both `region_id` and `coordinate` changed**, not just one:
  `region_id` is what `Finding` carries and `coordinate` is what `label()` prints. `:2686-2692`
  shows the pattern.
