title: Warn when a STUDY order targets a skill already at its maximum level
description:
Filed by the corpus investigation ah-v25.

## Evidence
`STUDY: Maximum level for skill reached.` - 11 occurrences across 3 turns of 3 games in
tests/fixtures/reports/ (docs/order-checks/corpus-errors.generated.md). A unit was ordered to STUDY
a skill it had already studied to the ruleset's own maximum for that skill, and the month's silver
was spent for nothing.

## What the check would need
From the ruleset: each skill's `maxLevel` (`crates/core/src/movement/rules.rs` `SkillEntry`). From
the report: the unit's current level in the skill named by the order (`ReportUnit`/`Skill` in
`crates/core/src/report/model.rs`). From the orders: the STUDY intent and the skill it names
(already read by `orders::intents`).

## What it must not do
Never blocking; accept on doubt (crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs:1-17). If the unit's current
level cannot be determined (an estimated skill list, or a skill the report never showed this unit
studying), stay silent rather than warn.

## Validation
A STUDY order for a skill already at the ruleset's maxLevel for that skill warns. A STUDY order for
a skill below its maximum, or for a skill the unit has never studied, stays silent.
design:
## Context

The engine says `STUDY: Maximum level for skill reached.` — eleven times across three turns of three
games in the committed corpus (`docs/order-checks/corpus-errors.generated.md`). A unit was ordered to
study a skill it had already taken to the ruleset's maximum, and the month's silver bought nothing.

Everything the check needs is already parsed: the skill's ceiling from the ruleset
(`SkillEntry::max_level`), the unit's current level from the report (`ReportUnit::skills`), and the
STUDY order itself (`Intent::Study`). This bead is one more advisory check in `semantics.rs`,
alongside the twelve already there, and nothing else.

It is a **warning, never blocking**, and it is silent whenever it cannot be sure — the module's
accept-on-doubt policy (`crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs:14-17`): *"A false warning costs the
player their confidence in every other line on the screen."*

Branch from `origin/main`; line numbers below are that tree.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### The check — `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`

**The code**, added last to both lists (the comment at `:80-83` says so explicitly, and the generated
TypeScript copies the array's order):

```rust
    pub const STUDY_AT_MAXIMUM: Code = Code("study-at-maximum");
```

`ALL` becomes `[Code; 13]` with `STUDY_AT_MAXIMUM` appended — the array's length is in its type, so
forgetting it is a compile error rather than a silent omission.

**The check itself**, a new `fn check_studying(hex, ruleset, options, findings)` called from
`check_turn` (`:151`) in the per-hex loop beside its siblings at `:167-169`:

```rust
        check_resources(&hex, ruleset, &options, &mut findings);
        check_guard(&hex, &options, &mut findings);
        check_teaching(&hex, ruleset, &options, &mut findings);
        check_studying(&hex, ruleset, &options, &mut findings);   // new, after teaching
```

What it does, per own unit in the hex:

1. Nothing at all without a ruleset (`ruleset: Option<&Ruleset>` is `None` before one loads) — the
   ceiling is the ruleset's to state, and there is no ceiling to compare against without it.
2. Find the unit's `STUDY` order **with its line**. `Ordered::studies()` (`:312`) returns only the
   skill text and drops the `PlacedIntent`, and this finding must sit on the line that carries it —
   so iterate `self.intents` for `Intent::Study { skill }` and keep the `PlacedIntent`, exactly as
   `check_teaching` does for `Intent::Teach`. Add a sibling helper beside `studies()` rather than
   inlining the loop in the check:

   ```rust
   /// The unit's STUDY order and where it was written, for a finding that must sit on its line.
   /// `studies()` answers the same question without the placement, and several callers only want
   /// that.
   fn studies_placed(&self) -> Option<(&PlacedIntent, &str)>;
   ```

3. Resolve the skill with `Ruleset::find_skill` (`crates/core/src/movement/rules.rs:609`), which
   already matches a tag or a name and turns `_` into a space — so `STUDY obse`, `STUDY observation`
   and `STUDY magical_healing` all land. `None` → silent: a skill the catalogue does not know has no
   stated maximum, and guessing is exactly what accept-on-doubt forbids.
4. Find the unit's current level: `unit.skills` (`crates/core/src/report/model.rs:157`), each a
   `Skill { name, tag, level, points }` (`:111-116`), matched on `tag` case-insensitively against the
   resolved `SkillEntry::tag`. Match on the **resolved tag**, not on the order's text — that is the
   whole reason the skill is resolved first, and it is what makes `STUDY observation` match a report
   line that says `observation [OBSE] 5`.
5. No entry for that skill → silent. It means the unit has never studied it, so it is not at any
   maximum.
6. Warn only when `level >= max_level`. `>=` rather than `==`: a report from a game whose ceiling
   differs from the committed ruleset's could show a level above it, and that unit is even more
   certainly wasting the month.

The finding uses `Ordered`'s own `finding(…)` — the one `check_teaching` calls as
`teacher.finding(hex, code, message, Some(placed))` (`:973`), which fills in the region, the unit and
the line/column from the placed intent. `Hex::finding` (`:239`) is the other one, for findings that
belong to no unit; not this.

**The message, exactly:**

```rust
format!("this unit is already at {} {}, the highest the ruleset has", skill.name, level)
```

giving `this unit is already at observation 5, the highest the ruleset has`. The skill is named by
the **ruleset's name**, not by the tag the order was written with, which is what the item checks do
with item names. Lowercase, no trailing stop, addressed to the player — the voice of
`this hex is guarded now and will be guarded by nobody next turn`.

Guard the whole thing with `options.emits(codes::STUDY_AT_MAXIMUM)` as every other check does, so
the toggle in the settings tab actually turns it off.

### The generated vocabulary — regenerate, do not edit

`packages/core-client/src/coreVocabulary.generated.ts` carries `ADVISORY_CHECK_CODES` in
`codes::ALL`'s order and says at the top that it is generated. Regenerate it:

```bash
ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test generated_ts
```

### The settings tab — `packages/shared/src/workspace/SettingsDialog.tsx`

The Warnings tab groups checks by concern. The navigator's decision: **the existing `Teaching` group
is renamed `Studying/Teaching`** and the new check joins it — not a new group, and not the catch-all
`Orders` group. So, in the groups array (`:~300-375`):

- the heading string `"Teaching"` becomes `"Studying/Teaching"`;
- a new entry is added to that group, after the existing teaching entries:

```tsx
      {
        code: "study-at-maximum",
        title: "Study with nothing to learn",
        description: "A unit ordered to study a skill it has already taken to the ruleset's maximum."
      }
```

Both strings are the navigator's, quoted verbatim; do not reword them.

## Increments

1. **The check warns.**
   RED: `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`'s test module —
   `a_unit_at_the_ruleset_maximum_is_warned`, a hex with one own unit holding `observation [OBSE] 5`
   and orders `unit 5\nSTUDY OBSE\n`, expecting exactly one finding whose code is
   `codes::STUDY_AT_MAXIMUM` and whose message is
   `this unit is already at observation 5, the highest the ruleset has`. It does not compile: there
   is no such code.
   GREEN: the code, `ALL` at 13, `studies_placed`, `check_studying`, and its call in `check_turn`.

2. **It stays silent everywhere it cannot be sure.**
   RED: the four silence tests in *The test plan*, one at a time.
   GREEN: the `None` arms — no ruleset, no catalogue entry, no skill on the unit, level below the
   maximum.

3. **The toggle turns it off.**
   RED: `the_check_can_be_switched_off` — the same fixture with
   `CheckOptions { disabled: ["study-at-maximum"] }` expecting no findings. There is very likely an
   existing table-driven test that walks every code and asserts each can be disabled (the array at
   `semantics.rs:~2570` pairs each code with a fixture and orders); add a row to it rather than
   writing a new test, and let that table be the RED.
   GREEN: the `options.emits(...)` guard.

4. **The vocabulary and the tab.**
   RED: `pnpm run check:generated` fails — `coreVocabulary.generated.ts` no longer matches the core.
   GREEN: regenerate it with the command above, then add the settings entry and rename the heading.

## The test plan

**Rust — `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`'s test module, `cargo test --workspace`.** Its
helpers already exist: `ruleset()` (`:1320`), `report(regions)` (`:1409`), and the `unit(...)`
builders the other checks use. Build a unit with a skill list rather than reaching for a fixture —
the corpus's own eleven occurrences are across three games and are not what a unit test should
depend on.

| Test | Pins |
|---|---|
| `a_unit_at_the_ruleset_maximum_is_warned` | `observation [OBSE] 5` + `STUDY OBSE` → one finding, the exact message |
| `the_skill_may_be_named_or_tagged` | `STUDY observation` and `STUDY obse` both warn — `find_skill` resolves either |
| `a_skill_below_its_maximum_is_silent` | `observation [OBSE] 3` + `STUDY OBSE` → nothing |
| `a_skill_the_unit_has_never_studied_is_silent` | a unit with no `OBSE` entry → nothing |
| `a_skill_the_ruleset_does_not_know_is_silent` | `STUDY xyzzy` → nothing, no panic |
| `without_a_ruleset_nothing_is_said` | `ruleset: None` → nothing |
| `a_level_above_the_maximum_still_warns` | `observation [OBSE] 6` against a ceiling of 5 → warns |
| `the_finding_sits_on_the_study_line` | orders with a blank line and a `WORK` before the STUDY → the finding's `line` is the STUDY's, not the block's |
| the disable table at `:~2570` | a row for `study-at-maximum`, so the toggle is proven like every other |

**TypeScript:** none of its own. `coreVocabulary.generated.ts` is regenerated and
`pnpm run check:generated` is what proves it; the settings entry is data in a list the tab renders
from, with no branch of its own.

**Suites:** `pnpm run check:fast`, which covers `cargo test --workspace`, the package suites,
`check:generated`, typecheck and clippy. No browser suite is involved — this adds no interaction,
only a string in a list and a warning in an existing strip.

## User-facing decisions

Interviewed with the navigator on 2026-08-16 over `docs/ui/study-at-maximum.html`, which is
committed and carries the chosen state and the rejected variants.

**Q1 — the warning's wording.** Chosen: **`this unit is already at observation 5, the highest the
ruleset has`**. It states the fact and names the ceiling, and it says the ceiling is the *ruleset's*
— which matters, because another game's ruleset may stop somewhere else. Rejected: `observation stops
at level 5 and this unit is already there` (shortest, but silent about where the number comes from);
`already at observation 5, the ruleset's maximum: this month buys nothing` (names the cost, but is
the only one that editorialises).

**Q2 — where the toggle sits in the Warnings tab.** Chosen: **the existing `Teaching` group is
renamed `Studying/Teaching`** and this check joins it. Rejected: a new `Studying` group of its own
(the navigator preferred one group covering both halves of the same subject); the catch-all `Orders`
group, where the name says nothing about what the check is. The two study checks already in the
backlog — the quartermaster allowance (`ah-oq3`) and magic studied outside a building (`ah-a2k`) —
belong in this renamed group when they land.

**The toggle's own words**, quoted as agreed: title `Study with nothing to learn`, description
`A unit ordered to study a skill it has already taken to the ruleset's maximum.`

## Out of scope

- **Teaching that would take a unit past the maximum.** A taught unit gains levels faster, and a
  teacher pushing a pupil at the ceiling is a different check with a different message.
- **The other study checks in the backlog.** `ah-oq3` (quartermaster allowance) and `ah-a2k` (magic
  outside a building) are their own beads. This one only touches their future group's heading.
- **`STUDY [skill] [level]`'s level argument.** The grammar accepts it; this check ignores it and
  warns on the unit's current level against the ruleset's ceiling, which is true whatever target was
  written.
- **Telling the player what to study instead.** The warning names the problem, as every other one
  does.
- **A ruleset with no skill catalogue.** An older ruleset has an empty `skills` map, `find_skill`
  answers `None`, and the check is silent — which is correct and needs no special case.

## Validation

```bash
ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test generated_ts
pnpm run check:fast
```

Then by eye: load any turn, select a unit whose skill is at its maximum, order it to study that
skill, and check the warning appears in the orders panel's diagnostics strip with the exact wording
above and a warning-coloured mark in the editor's margin. Open Settings → Warnings and confirm the
group now reads **Studying/Teaching** and carries **Study with nothing to learn**, and that
unticking it makes the warning disappear.

## Known traps

- **`codes::ALL` has its length in its type** (`[Code; 12]` → `[Code; 13]`), and the generated
  TypeScript copies its order. Append; never insert. The comment at `semantics.rs:80-83` states the
  rule and why.
- **`coreVocabulary.generated.ts` is generated**, and `pnpm run check:generated` fails if it is
  hand-edited or left behind. Regenerate with
  `ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test generated_ts`.
- **`studies()` drops the placement**, so a finding built from it lands on no line and the editor
  cannot mark it. Take the `PlacedIntent`, as `check_teaching` does.
- **Match the report's skill on the resolved tag, not on the order's text.** `STUDY observation`
  against a report line reading `observation [OBSE] 5` only matches once `find_skill` has turned the
  order's word into `OBSE`.
- **Accept on doubt is the module's contract** (`semantics.rs:14-17`), and four separate silences
  here follow from it. A check that warns when it cannot be sure is worse than no check.
- **The renamed heading is a plain string in a list** and no test asserts it today; the eyeball step
  in *Validation* is what proves it, so do not skip it.

title: Warn when a mage cannot pay for the spell it is ordered to cast
description:
A spell that needs reagents is checked like any other order: not at all. A mage ordered to cast
something it cannot pay for produces no warning, and the turn runs without the spell.

**The request:** check that a mage holds what its spell requires — and count what it can reach, not
only what it carries.

## It depends on the item work

The reachability rules are the same ones the item shortfall bead establishes: a mage's own holdings,
plus what other units in the hex `GIVE` it this turn, plus what `sharing` units in the hex hold. A
mage is very often the unit that carries nothing and is kept supplied by the rest of its hex, so
without that this check would warn on almost every real casting.

That bead should land first. This one is the second consumer of the same "what can this unit
actually reach" question, and it is worth building it once.

## The part that is genuinely new

**Knowing what a spell costs.** Nothing in the codebase maps a spell to its reagents. That table has
to come from somewhere:

- the ruleset, if the shipped rulesets carry spell costs;
- a table written into the checker, which is accurate for the rules it was written against and
  silently wrong when a game uses others;
- the report itself, where a mage's skills and a failed casting may say more than is currently read.

Which of those is available decides whether this is a small bead or a large one, and it is the first
thing to establish.

## For the planner to settle with the navigator

- **Where spell requirements come from**, per above. If no source exists, this bead is really two:
  find or build the table, then check against it.
- **Which spells are in scope.** Starting with the ones that plainly consume something is cheaper
  than modelling every casting, and covers what a player actually gets wrong.
- **What a mage short of reagents should say** — the same shape as an item shortfall, or its own
  code, given the reader may not know a spell needs anything at all.
- Whether a spell the checker does not know about should say nothing (safe) or say it does not know
  (honest, and noisy if most spells are unknown).

## Validation

A mage ordered to cast a spell it has the reagents for: silent, including when the reagents arrive
by `GIVE` or from a sharing unit in the hex. The same mage with the reagents removed: warned. A
spell with no known requirements: whatever the navigator decides, consistently.
design: Epic — split by Beast on 2026-08-16 into ah-dbb.1 (the ruleset carries casting costs) and ah-dbb.2 (CAST charges them; blocked on ah-dbb.1 and ah-j2w). The children carry the plans; the navigator's decisions (scope: every spell with a stated cost; same codes and words as any shortfall; unknown spells say nothing; the stated cost once per cast) are recorded on ah-dbb.2.
acceptance_criteria: A mage ordered to cast a spell whose requirements it cannot meet is warned, counting its own holdings plus what it is given in the hex and what sharing units there hold. A mage that can pay is not warned. A spell whose requirements are unknown behaves as the navigator decided, and says so consistently.
close_reason: All children closed; last was ah-dbb.2, delivered in PR #343

title: The fleet view freezes Emacs while it waits for bd, gh and a process scan
description:
Moving up and down the agent list freezes Emacs for a few seconds at a time. The movement is not the
cause — it is when the navigator happens to be interacting, and Emacs is single-threaded, so
whatever the fleet view is doing on its timer stops everything, cursor included.

## Measured, against this repository

Everything the tick does runs through `call-process`, which blocks until the program exits:

| Runs | How often | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| `cerebro--system-args` — a scan of every process on the machine | every 5s | **75 ms** |
| `bd list --status open,in_progress,blocked,deferred,closed --json` | every 30s | **540 ms**, 1.8 MB of JSON |
| `sweep-claims.sh`, `sweep-epics.sh` | every 10 min | `bd` **and `gh`** — a network round trip |
| `prune-worktrees.sh` | on the watcher | `bd` and `gh` likewise |

Parsing is not the problem: 262 beads parse in 2 ms. It is the waiting.

**And 540 ms is the quiet case.** That figure was taken with the fleet idle. Four implementers run
`bd dolt pull`, `bd update` and `bd dolt push` throughout a bead against the same Dolt database, and
a `bd list` that queues behind them takes as long as they do. The freeze the navigator sees is
therefore worst exactly when the fleet is busiest — which is when they are most likely to be
watching the list.

The `gh` calls are the ones that can block longest and are the least bounded: a slow network, a rate
limit or a hung connection stalls Emacs for as long as it takes.

## What it is not

`cerebro--follow` on `post-command-hook` fires on every cursor move, and does call
`cerebro--show-detail` each time because the selected id changes. That path is buffer lookups and
`set-window-buffer` — cheap, and not what this is. It is worth confirming rather than assuming when
the fix is measured.

## The shape of a fix

Emacs can run a program without waiting: `make-process` with a sentinel, or `start-process` and a
filter, so the subprocess runs while the UI stays live and the panel updates when the answer
arrives. Everything here is a read whose result only refreshes a display — none of it needs to be
synchronous.

Cheaper measures that help without restructuring:

- **Ask `bd` for less.** The panel needs seven fields of twenty and does not need every closed bead's
  full description; 1.8 MB is mostly text nothing renders.
- **Do not scan every process every five seconds.** The scan exists to spot interactive agents
  started outside Emacs, which is a rare event polled at the rate of a state file.
- **Let the sweeps miss a beat.** They are ten-minutely housekeeping; nothing breaks if one is
  skipped because the last has not returned.

## For the planner to settle with the navigator

- **How far to go.** Making every subprocess asynchronous is the real answer and the largest change;
  narrowing the query and slowing the process scan may drop the freeze below what anyone notices.
- **What the panel shows while a refresh is in flight** — the previous contents, or a marker. Stale
  numbers that do not say they are stale have already caused one long debugging session here.
- Whether the tick should skip work entirely while the navigator is typing, which is a blunter
  instrument but a very direct answer to the reported symptom.

## Validation

With the fleet busy, hold a cursor key down in the agent list for a minute and confirm no pause is
perceptible. Confirm the panel still refreshes, the sweeps still run, and that a `bd` or `gh` that
never returns leaves the list responsive rather than freezing Emacs.
design:
## Context

**This is the cerebro submodule** (`https://github.com/rmstdope/cerebro`, mounted at
`.claude/cerebro`; `emacs/cerebro.el`, `emacs/cerebro-test.el`, `emacs/README.md`), delivered the
way ah-goz/ah-5pp were: a PR to cerebro, then a one-line submodule bump PR here. **Line numbers
below are against cerebro `origin/main` at `8d9bfef`** (2026-08-16, ah-goz merged). Fetch and cite
`origin/main`; the consumer pointer may still be behind it.

The fleet view freezes Emacs for seconds at a time. Emacs is single-threaded and everything the
five-second `cerebro--tick` (`cerebro.el:1871-1888`) does that leaves the process runs through
`call-process`, which blocks until the program exits:

| What | Where | How often | Measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bd list --status open,in_progress,blocked,deferred,closed --json` | `cerebro--gather-beads` :1398-1412 via `cerebro--bd-json` :1278-1291 | every 30 s (`cerebro-beads-refresh-seconds`) and on `g` | 440-540 ms idle, 1.95 MB; longer whenever implementers hold Dolt |
| `sweep-claims.sh --json`, `sweep-epics.sh --json` (`bd` **and `gh`**, a fetch) | `cerebro--gather-sweeps` :559-575 via `cerebro--run-script-json` :542-557 | every 600 s (`cerebro-sweep-refresh-seconds`), and once at panel creation :1704-1710 | unbounded: a slow network or a hung `gh` holds Emacs as long as it takes |
| `list-system-processes` + `process-attributes` over every pid | `cerebro--system-args` :940-944, called from `cerebro--revert` :1749-1770 | every 5 s | 75 ms |

Parsing is not it (262 beads in 2 ms); waiting is. The freeze is worst exactly when the fleet is
busiest, which is when the navigator is watching. `cerebro--follow` (:1890-1899, `post-command-hook`)
is buffer lookups and is not the cause; leave it alone.

**After this bead** the tick never blocks on a subprocess. One asynchronous runner
(`cerebro--run-async`, `make-process` + sentinel, one run in flight per key, killed after a
timeout) carries the `bd list` and the two sweep scripts; the panel keeps its rows while an answer
is out and says so in a header line — the navigator's choice, below; the process scan runs on a
thirty-second cadence; and `bd list` asks for `--brief` (1.95 MB → 199 KB — the same wall time, so
this is hygiene, not the fix). Keypress-driven calls — `bd show` for the detail (`cerebro--bd-text`
:1293-1305), `bd update` for a priority key (`cerebro--bd-set-priority`, around :1390) — stay
synchronous: a person pressed the key and is looking at the result. Deliberate; see *Out of scope*.

The panel's data flow becomes request → answer → draw, so `cerebro--gather-beads` and
`cerebro--gather-sweeps` (synchronous, return values) go, and every ERT test that stubs them stubs
the request functions instead — a mechanical rewrite listed under *Files to change*.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

Everything is in the cerebro repository. All new/changed functions in `emacs/cerebro.el`.

### 1. The runner (new, near `cerebro--run-script-json` :542)

```elisp
(defvar cerebro-subprocess-timeout-seconds 120
  "How long an asynchronous subprocess may run before it is killed and its
answer treated as none. Generous: the sweeps fetch from origin and talk to
`gh'; what this bounds is a hang, not a slow answer.")

(defvar cerebro--inflight nil
  "Runs still awaiting an answer: an alist of (KEY . PROCESS). One per KEY -
`cerebro--run-async' refuses a second while the first is out, so a slow
`bd' is waited for rather than stacked.")

(defun cerebro--run-async (key repo-root argv callback)
  "Run ARGV (program, then args) in REPO-ROOT without blocking Emacs.

CALLBACK is called exactly once, later, with the program's stdout as a
string when it exited zero and nil otherwise - non-zero exit, a signal, the
program missing, or `cerebro-subprocess-timeout-seconds' passing first, in
which case the process is killed. Returns `started', or `busy' when a run
under KEY is already in flight - then nothing is started and CALLBACK is
never called. Never signals.")
```

Implementation: `(if (assoc key cerebro--inflight) 'busy …)`; else `condition-case` around
`make-process` with `:name (format " *cerebro-%s*" key)`, `:buffer (generate-new-buffer …)`,
`:command argv`, `:noquery t`, `:connection-type 'pipe`, and **no `:stderr`** — stderr is merged
into the same buffer. That is deliberate and measured: `bd list … --json --brief`,
`sweep-claims.sh --json` and `sweep-epics.sh --json` each write 0 bytes to stderr on success (checked
2026-08-16 with `bash -c '… 2>&1 >/dev/null | wc -c'`), and on failure the non-zero exit already
makes the answer nil, so a separate stderr pipe process (which `:stderr BUFFER` would create, with
its own query-on-exit flag to manage) buys nothing. Say so in the docstring. `default-directory`
bound to `(file-name-as-directory repo-root)` around `make-process`. `:sentinel` — a closure that, when `(memq (process-status proc) '(exit signal))`:
removes KEY from `cerebro--inflight`, cancels the timeout timer stored with `(process-put proc
'cerebro-timeout …)`, takes `(with-current-buffer out (buffer-string))` if `(and (eq (process-status
proc) 'exit) (zerop (process-exit-status proc)))` else nil, kills the buffer, and calls
`(with-demoted-errors "cerebro: %S" (funcall callback output))`. The timeout: `(run-at-time
cerebro-subprocess-timeout-seconds nil (lambda () (when (process-live-p proc) (delete-process
proc))))` — deleting fires the sentinel with a signal status, so the nil path is one path. On a
`make-process` error (program missing): call `callback` with nil **synchronously** and return
`started` (the caller's contract — one callback — still holds).

```elisp
(defun cerebro--parse-json (text)
  "TEXT parsed as JSON the way the panel wants it (alists, lists, nil), or nil
when TEXT is nil or not JSON. What `cerebro--bd-json' used to do after
`call-process'; the parsing half survives, the blocking half does not.")
```
Same `json-parse-string` arguments as :1286-1288. **Delete `cerebro--bd-json` (:1278-1291)** — its
only caller was `cerebro--gather-beads` — and `cerebro--run-script-json` (:542-557), whose only
caller was `cerebro--gather-sweeps`. `cerebro--run-sweep-command` (:578-585, `x` on a finding) stays
synchronous and unchanged.

### 2. Beads: request, answer, draw (replaces `cerebro--gather-beads` :1398-1412 and rewrites `cerebro--beads-render` :1602-1626)

```elisp
(defconst cerebro--bd-list-argv
  '("bd" "list" "--status" "open,in_progress,blocked,deferred,closed" "--json" "--brief")
  "The one `bd' call the panel is drawn from. `--brief' drops the free-form
text nothing here renders (1.95 MB to 199 KB on this backlog); every status
by name and no `--exclude-type', as before - the partition is only complete
if the list it partitions is.")

(defun cerebro--request-beads (repo-root callback)
  "Ask `bd' for the panel's beads without blocking; CALLBACK gets the four
partition lists (see `cerebro--partition-beads') when the answer lands, or
nil when `bd' did not answer. Returns what `cerebro--run-async' returns.")
```
= `(cerebro--run-async 'beads repo-root cerebro--bd-list-argv (lambda (out) (funcall callback (and out (let ((parsed (cerebro--parse-json out))) (and parsed (cerebro--partition-beads parsed)))))))`.
(`cerebro--partition-beads` :1350-1396 is unchanged and stays pure.)

Panel state, all `defvar-local` beside `cerebro--sweep-findings` :1640:

```elisp
(defvar-local cerebro--beads nil            "The last partition `bd' answered with, or nil before the first.")
(defvar-local cerebro--beads-as-of nil      "`float-time' when `cerebro--beads' arrived, or nil.")
(defvar-local cerebro--beads-requested-at nil "`float-time' of the request now in flight, or nil when none is.")
(defvar-local cerebro--beads-failed-at nil  "`float-time' of the last request that got no answer, or nil once one has succeeded since.")
```

```elisp
(defun cerebro--panel-header (as-of requested-at failed-at)
  "Pure. The panel's header line: what the rows date from and what is going on.")
```
Exact strings, joined with ` · `: always `Beads`; `as of HH:MM:SS` when AS-OF (`format-time-string
"%H:%M:%S" (seconds-to-time as-of)`); `refreshing…` when REQUESTED-AT; `bd did not answer at
HH:MM:SS` when FAILED-AT. So: `Beads` / `Beads · as of 12:03:41` / `Beads · as of 12:03:41 ·
refreshing…` / `Beads · as of 12:03:41 · bd did not answer at 12:04:32` / `Beads · refreshing…`
(before the first answer). The failure clause is dropped by the next success. Propertize nothing.

```elisp
(defun cerebro--update-panel-header (buffer)
  "Set BUFFER's `header-line-format' from its panel state and redisplay it.")
;; (setq header-line-format (cerebro--panel-header cerebro--beads-as-of cerebro--beads-requested-at cerebro--beads-failed-at)) (force-mode-line-update)

(defun cerebro--draw-beads (buffer)
  "Draw BUFFER's rows from `cerebro--beads' and `cerebro--sweep-findings'.
The old body of `cerebro--beads-render' minus the `bd' call.")
;; cerebro--redraw with the same lambda as :1610-1626, `beads' = (or cerebro--beads (list nil nil nil nil)); the by-id mark restore unchanged.

(defun cerebro--beads-render (buffer)
  "Refresh BUFFER: draw what is known now, ask `bd' for what is current, and
draw again when it answers. Never blocks. A request already out is left to
finish rather than joined by a second (`cerebro--run-async' says `busy').")
```
Body: `(cerebro--draw-beads buffer)`; then `(pcase (cerebro--request-beads root (lambda (beads) (when (buffer-live-p buffer) (with-current-buffer buffer (setq cerebro--beads-requested-at nil) (if beads (setq cerebro--beads beads cerebro--beads-as-of (float-time) cerebro--beads-failed-at nil) (setq cerebro--beads-failed-at (float-time)))) (cerebro--draw-beads buffer) (cerebro--update-panel-header buffer)))) ('started (setq cerebro--beads-requested-at (float-time))))` — then `(cerebro--update-panel-header buffer)`. On `busy` nothing changes (the header already says refreshing). The first draw is what keeps `cerebro--setup-layout`'s contract (its test counts renders); with `cerebro--beads` nil it draws four `(none)` sections, exactly as an unanswered panel looks today.

`cerebro--beads-revert` (`g`, :1628-1630) unchanged: it calls `cerebro--beads-render`.

### 3. Sweeps (replaces `cerebro--gather-sweeps` :559-575; rewrites `cerebro--sweep` :1645-1653)

```elisp
(defun cerebro--request-sweeps (repo-root callback)
  "Run the claims and epics sweep scripts without blocking, one after the
other; CALLBACK gets the (LABEL . FINDING) list when both have answered, or
nil when either did not. Returns `busy' if a sweep is already out.")
```
Chain: `(cerebro--run-async 'sweep-claims root (list (expand-file-name (cerebro--script "sweep-claims.sh") root) "--json") (lambda (claims-out) (if (null claims-out) (funcall callback nil) (cerebro--run-async 'sweep-epics root (list … "sweep-epics.sh" …) (lambda (epics-out) (funcall callback (and epics-out (cerebro--findings-from root (cerebro--parse-json claims-out) (cerebro--parse-json epics-out)))))))))` — where `cerebro--findings-from (repo-root claims epics)` is the pure-ish body of today's :562-575 (`live-names`, `now`, the two `mapcar`s), computed **at answer time**, so `live-names` describes the fleet when the findings are shown. A nil parse of a non-nil output (garbage) counts as no answer.

```elisp
(defun cerebro--sweep (buffer)
  "Re-run the sweeps for BUFFER without blocking; when they answer, keep the
findings and redraw. A sweep that does not answer leaves the last findings
standing - ten-minutely housekeeping may miss a beat, and an empty Sweeps
section would say the fleet is clean when the script simply failed.")
```
Body: `(cerebro--request-sweeps root (lambda (findings-or-nil) (when (buffer-live-p buffer) (with-current-buffer buffer (when findings-or-nil-was-an-answer …)))))` — **careful**: an answered sweep with *no* findings must clear the section, while an unanswered one must keep it. So `cerebro--request-sweeps` calls back with `(list findings)` on an answer (a one-element list, possibly `(nil)`) and with `nil` on no answer; `cerebro--sweep` does `(when answer (setq cerebro--sweep-findings (car answer)))` then `(cerebro--draw-beads buffer)`. State this in both docstrings.

`cerebro--refresh-panel-when-due` (:1852-1869): the sweep no longer renders the beads, so drop the
"skip the plain render when swept" coupling — `(when swept (setq cerebro--swept-at seconds) (cerebro--sweep panel))` and `(when render-due (setq cerebro--beads-rendered-at seconds) (cerebro--beads-render panel))`, independently; rewrite its docstring (the reason it gave — avoiding a second `bd` call — no longer exists, since a sweep costs no `bd list`).

`cerebro--beads-buffer` (:1693-1712): the "once immediately, in the foreground" sweep becomes the same
`(cerebro--sweep buffer)` call, now non-blocking; reword the comment (:1704-1709) — it still runs at
creation so the section is not empty for ten minutes, but it no longer holds `M-x cerebro` open on
`gh`. Keep the `with-demoted-errors`.

### 4. The process scan cadence (`cerebro--system-args` :940-944, `cerebro--revert` :1749-1770)

```elisp
(defvar cerebro-system-scan-seconds 30
  "How often the process list is scanned for interactive agents started
outside Emacs. A rare event, polled at the rate of a state file; the scan
itself is 75 ms of blocking work and was on the five-second tick.")
(defvar-local cerebro--system-args-cache nil
  "(ARGS . SCANNED-AT) from the last scan, per fleet buffer.")

(defun cerebro--cached-system-args (&optional now)
  "`cerebro--system-args', rescanned only when `cerebro-system-scan-seconds' have passed.")
```
`cerebro--revert` calls `(cerebro--cached-system-args)` instead of `(cerebro--system-args)`.
`cerebro--system-args` itself stays as the impure primitive — the existing test stub at
`cerebro-test.el:278` keeps working because the wrapper calls it, and because the cache is
buffer-local to a fleet buffer each test creates fresh. Uses `cerebro--due-p` (:1848-1850).

### 5. Docs

- `emacs/README.md:132-135`: replace the paragraph with: "It refreshes every
  `cerebro-beads-refresh-seconds` (30) and on `g`, without ever holding Emacs: `bd` is asked in the
  background and the rows stay put until it answers. The header line above the panel says what the
  rows date from (`Beads · as of 12:03:41`), that a refresh is out (`· refreshing…`), and when `bd`
  did not answer — absent, unconfigured, mid-write, or past
  `cerebro-subprocess-timeout-seconds` — (`· bd did not answer at 12:04:32`), rather than showing
  numbers that do not say they are stale. The sweeps run the same way on their ten-minute cadence,
  and a sweep that does not answer leaves the last findings standing."
- `cerebro--tick`'s docstring (:1872-1879): add one sentence — "Nothing here waits on a subprocess:
  the panel and the sweeps request and draw when answered (ah-9dv); the process scan is the one
  blocking read left and runs every `cerebro-system-scan-seconds`."

### 6. Tests (`emacs/cerebro-test.el`) — new and rewritten

New (names as given; place near the `bd-json` test :1464 and the render tests :1600-1760):

## The test plan

  byte-compile step must stay warning-free (`make-process` keywords and `process-put` are fine on 28).
- The five real-process tests use `sh`, `printf`, `sleep` only — present on the CI runners and on
  macOS.
- atlantis-hud: the bump PR's normal CI.

## User-facing decisions

Nothing a player sees; the fleet view is the navigator's own instrument, and two things about how
it behaves were theirs (asked 2026-08-16, ASCII previews in the question):

- **What the panel shows while a refresh is in flight.** Offered: (A) keep the rows exactly as they
  were and add a header line saying what they date from and that a refresh is running —
  `Beads · as of 12:03:41 · refreshing…`, idle `Beads · as of 12:03:41`, on failure
  `Beads · as of 12:03:41 · bd did not answer at 12:04:32`; (B) keep the rows with no indicator; (C)
  clear the panel to `(refreshing…)` until the answer lands. **Chosen: A.** B rejected because stale
  numbers that do not say they are stale already cost a debugging session; C because it flickers
  every thirty seconds and loses the mark. The strings above are the strings.
- **Skip the tick while typing.** Offered: no — with every subprocess asynchronous the tick is
  milliseconds of file reads and there is nothing left to skip; or yes, defer the tick to the next
  idle moment after a keypress. **Chosen: no.**
- **How far to go** (the bead's first question) I decided as architecture and stated when asking:
  asynchronous `bd list` and sweeps, a slower synchronous process scan, keypress-driven `bd` calls
  left synchronous.

## Out of scope

- `cerebro--bd-text` (`bd show` for RET), `cerebro--bd-set-priority` (`bd update` on a digit),
  `cerebro--run-sweep-command` (`x`), `cerebro--fleet` (one `roster` call, cached): all on a keypress,
  all left synchronous. If one of them ever hangs it hangs in front of the person who pressed the
  key, which is a different bug.
- The prune watcher (already a `make-process`, :1805) and `cerebro--supervise` (vterm start/stop,
  no subprocess wait).
- Any change to what the panel lists or how sections are ordered; `cerebro--partition-beads` and
  `cerebro--bead-panel` are untouched.
- Deferring the tick on keypress (rejected above); parallelising the two sweep scripts (sequential
  is fine at a ten-minute cadence and keeps one callback).
- Running the bash test suites in cerebro CI (ah-30t).

## Validation

In the cerebro clone:

```bash
emacs --batch -L emacs -f batch-byte-compile emacs/cerebro.el          # no warnings
emacs --batch -L emacs -l cerebro-test -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit  # all pass, both Emacs versions in CI
grep -n "call-process" emacs/cerebro.el   # only: cerebro--run-sweep-command, cerebro--bd-text, cerebro--bd-set-priority, cerebro--fleet's roster read
```

By hand, in the consumer after the bump, with the fleet busy (three implementers running): `M-x
cerebro`, hold `<down>`/`<up>` in the agent list for a minute — no perceptible pause; the header
line over the bead panel reads `Beads · as of HH:MM:SS`, flips to `· refreshing…` briefly every
thirty seconds and settles again; `g` in the panel does the same; the Sweeps section fills within
a minute of opening. Then, in a shell, `mv "$(command -v bd)"{,.off}` (or otherwise make `bd` fail)
for a minute: the rows stay, the header says `bd did not answer at …`, Emacs never stalls; restore
`bd` and the clause clears on the next answer.

## Known traps

- **Never branch inside `.claude/cerebro`** of the shared checkout — agents' skills and agent files
  are symlinks into it. Clone cerebro elsewhere (e.g. `/tmp/cerebro-ah-9dv`) for the PR; the bump PR
  is from a worktree under `.cerebro/worktrees/` and will likely be `BEHIND` — the merge-state check
  in `implement-bead`.
- **A sentinel runs at an arbitrary point in Emacs's event loop.** Every callback must guard on
  `(buffer-live-p buffer)` before `with-current-buffer` — the panel may have been killed while `bd`
  was out — and must never assume the current buffer or window; draw through `cerebro--redraw`,
  which already checks liveness and pushes point to every window (:1715-1735).
- **`with-timeout` and `accept-process-output` in tests**: batch Emacs runs sentinels only while
  waiting, so the real-process tests need the `accept-process-output` loop; do not `sleep-for` and
  hope. Bound the wait (5 s) so a broken runner fails the test rather than hanging CI.
- **The timeout timer must be cancelled on normal exit**, or a later run under a different process
  object could be killed by a stale timer — store it with `process-put` and `cancel-timer` in the
  sentinel. Conversely, `delete-process` on timeout must reach the sentinel: it does (status
  `signal`), which is why the nil path is one path.
- **An answered-empty sweep is not a failed sweep.** `cerebro--request-sweeps` distinguishes them by
  calling back `(list findings)` versus `nil`; collapse the two and either a failed `gh` blanks the
  Sweeps section or a genuinely clean fleet keeps showing stale findings.
- **`header-line-format` is buffer-local by nature**; set it in the panel buffer, never globally, and
  call `force-mode-line-update` after changing it or the header lags until the next redisplay.
- **The tests that count renders** (`setup-layout-redraws-a-panel-that-already-existed`) stub
  `cerebro--beads-render`; keep that name as the entry point, or the count breaks for the wrong reason.
- **`--brief` exists on the fleet machine's `bd`** (`bd list --help`); it changes nothing the panel
  reads (`status`, `issue_type`, `priority`, `id`, `updated_at`, `labels`, `title` — grep of
  `alist-get '` in `cerebro.el`). If a future field is needed from the free text, drop `--brief`
  rather than fetching twice.
acceptance_criteria: Interacting with the fleet view stays responsive while its refreshes, panel queries and sweeps are running, including when the fleet is busy and bd is contended. A subprocess that is slow or never returns does not freeze Emacs. The list, the bead panel and the sweeps still show the same information they do today.

title: Rename the open game in place from the picker's This game tab
description:
A game is named once, when it is created, and never again. The name is shown in the game picker's
**This game** panel as plain text (`GamePicker.tsx`, the `Name` row of the settings panel) and again
in the settings dialog (`SettingsDialog.tsx`, `presentation.gameName`) — read-only in both places.

A name is chosen before the player has played a turn, which is exactly when they know least about
what to call it. Typos, placeholders and second thoughts are all permanent.

**The request:** let the name be changed from the **This game** panel.

## What exists

`newGameManifest` (`packages/shared/src/gameSession.ts`) is where a name is currently accepted, and
it already carries the rule a rename must obey:

    const trimmed = gameName.trim();
    if (trimmed === "") throw new Error("a game needs a name");

So trimming, and the refusal of an empty name, are settled — a rename should reuse that judgement
rather than restate it, or the two will drift and one path will accept what the other rejects.

The name lives in `manifest.metadata.gameName`, alongside `gameId` and `rulesetId`. `gameId` is the
identity; the name is a label on it, which is what makes renaming safe: nothing keys off it.

## For the planner to settle with the navigator

- **Where the edit happens.** In place in the `Name` row of the **This game** panel, or a small
  dialog. In place is fewer clicks and needs a save/cancel affordance that the row does not have
  today.
- **What an empty or whitespace name does.** Refusing is consistent with creation; the question is
  whether the field refuses on save with a message, or simply reverts to the old name.
- **Duplicate names.** Two games may already share a name — nothing prevents it at creation, since
  `gameId` is the identity. Renaming makes duplicates easy to create by accident. Either that is
  fine and the picker must stay usable when two rows read the same, or a rename warns.
- **Does anything outside the manifest carry the name?** Exported files and backups may embed it,
  and a rename does not travel to a file already written. Worth naming in the bead's close so nobody
  reports it as a bug later.

## Validation

Rename a game from the **This game** panel: the picker, the settings dialog and any other place the
name appears all show the new one, and it survives closing and reopening the app. Try an empty name
and a name of only spaces, and confirm the behaviour matches what creation does. Confirm the game's
reports, orders and history are untouched — only the label changed.

""; const duplicate = renaming !== null && trimmedDraft !== "" && trimmedDraft !== currentGame?.metadata.gameName && games.some((g) => g.metadata.gameId !== currentGameId && g.metadata.gameName === trimmedDraft) ? trimmedDraft : null; const cancel = () => { setRenaming(null); setRenameError(null); renameLinkRef.current?.focus(); }; const save = async () => { if (renaming === null || !currentGame) return; let name: string; try { name = gameNameOf(renaming); } catch (error) { setRenameError(describeError(error)); return; } if (name === currentGame.metadata.gameName) { cancel(); return; } // nothing to write if (await onRename(name)) { cancel(); } // else: the field stays open; the picker's error line says why }; ``` `useEffect(() => { if (renaming !== null) renameInputRef.current?.select(); }, [renaming !== null])` — select-all on open, so typing replaces (the mockup's "text selected"); guard the dependency so it runs once per open, not per keystroke (use a `renaming !== null` boolean, or a `useRef` flag). - While `renaming !== null`, the *Export game backup…* and *Import game backup…* buttons are `disabled` (add `|| renaming !== null` to their `disabled`), and the *Ruleset* row is unchanged. - `text-warn` is the shell's amber: `packages/shared/src/theme.css:66` defines `--color-warn: #d9a441` (`:158` the light-theme value), which Tailwind exposes as `text-warn`; grep `packages/shared/src/workspace` for an existing `text-warn` use and copy its form. - Escape: the input's `onKeyDown` cancels the edit and calls `event.stopPropagation()`; React dispatches from the root container, which is *below* `document` in the native bubble path, so the picker's `document` keydown listener (:46-52) never sees that Escape and the picker stays open. A second Escape (field closed) closes the picker as today. Say this in a comment on the handler. - Component doc comment (:6-15): one sentence — the name can be changed in place from *This game*, and the same rule as creation decides what a name may be. ### 7. Smoke — `tests/smoke/games.spec.ts` Four tests, using `clearGames`/`createGame`; a helper `openThisGameTab(page)` = click `game-indicator`, click `game-picker-tab-settings`: - `"a game can be renamed in place from the This game tab"`: create `Backup gmae`; open the tab; click `rename-game`; the input is focused (`toBeFocused()`) and its value is `Backup gmae`; `fill("Backup game")`; press `Enter`; expect `game-rename-input` count 0, the tab's Name row to contain `Backup game`, `game-indicator` to contain `Backup game`, `rename-game` focused; `page.reload()`; expect `game-indicator` to contain `Backup game` (it persisted). - `"an empty name is refused, with the words creation uses"`: `fill(" ")`, `Enter`; expect `game-rename-error` to contain `a game needs a name`, the input still visible with value ` `, `game-indicator` still the old name; then click `game-rename-cancel`; input gone; `rename-game` focused. - `"Escape cancels the rename and leaves the picker open"`: type a new name, press `Escape`; input gone, `game-picker` visible, Name row still the old name; press `Escape` again; `game-picker` count 0. - `"renaming to another game's name only warns"`: two games (`Alpha`, `Beta`, Beta open); rename Beta to `Alpha`; before Enter expect `game-rename-warning` to contain `Another game is already called “Alpha”.`; Enter; the header reads `Alpha`; the Games tab lists two `Alpha` rows (`[data-testid^="game-row-"]` count 2, both containing `Alpha`). ## Increments 1. RED (Rust): the persistence tests, then the core-tauri tests. GREEN: `set_game_name`, `command_set_game_name`, the `main.rs` wrapper + handler + the sweep row (one commit). `cargo test --workspace`, clippy, fmt. 2. RED: `index.test.ts` (client contract) and `webCoreAdapter.test.ts` (store rename). GREEN: the client and adapter methods. `pnpm --filter @atlantis/core-client test && pnpm --filter @atlantis/browser-core test`. 3. RED: `gameSession.test.ts` `gameNameOf`; `gameActions.test.ts` `renameGame`; `workspaceStore.test.ts` `updateGameName`. GREEN: the three. 4. `AppShell.tsx` (generic `runGameAction`, handler, prop) and `GamePicker.tsx` (the edit). Typecheck. 5. RED: the four smoke tests. GREEN is increment 4; run `pnpm run test:smoke tests/smoke/games.spec.ts` locally (both projects). 6. `pnpm run check:fast`; PR `feat(ah-lkw): rename a game in place from the This game tab`; `@copilot`; CI (watch `native` — the sweep row); squash. Close the bead. ## The test plan - Rust: `core-persistence` (+2), `core-tauri` (+2), workspace clippy/fmt. - Unit: `core-client/index.test.ts` (+1), `browser-core/webCoreAdapter.test.ts` (+2), `gameSession.test.ts` (+2), `gameActions.test.ts` (+3), `workspaceStore.test.ts` (+1); the whole shared suite green. - Browser: `tests/smoke/games.spec.ts` (+4), both projects; the rest of the suite unchanged and green. - Native: CI's `native` job with `set_game_name` in the sweep. ## User-facing decisions Interview 2026-08-16; mockup `docs/ui/rename-game.html` (PR #301) draws the three homes, the chosen one mid-edit, and the states. 1. **Where.** A — in place: a brass `Rename` link after the name on the *This game* tab's Name row, which opens a field in that row with `Save` / `Cancel` under it. Rejected: B, a `Rename game…` button in the export/import stack opening an inline form (a rarely used third line, name shown twice); C, an always-editable Name field saved on blur (no Cancel, empty must revert silently, a click to select text risks a save). 2. **Empty or whitespace name on Save.** Refused with `a game needs a name` under the field, in red; the field stays open with the bad value. Rejected: reverting silently. 3. **Duplicate name.** Warn while typing — `Another game is already called “”.` in the amber the shell uses for warnings — and still allow Save; creation allows duplicates and the id is the identity. Rejected: no warning; refusing duplicates. 4. **Keys and focus.** Enter saves; Escape cancels the edit only (the picker stays open; a second Escape closes it as today); focus lands in the field with the text selected; after Save or Cancel focus returns to `Rename`. Rejected: Escape closing the whole picker. 5. **Words.** Link `Rename`; buttons `Save` / `Cancel`; `Saving…` (disabled) while the core writes; the two lines quoted above. Rejected: link `Edit`; buttons `Rename` / `Cancel`. 6. **A refusal from the core** (disk, locked database) shows in the picker's existing bottom error line, like every other action's failure; the field stays open with the typed name so Save can be retried. Rejected: routing it under the field. 7. **Unchanged name** (equal after trimming): Save closes the field without writing. Rejected: writing anyway. 8. Not asked, decided here: export/import buttons are disabled while the field is open (as drawn on A′); Cancel is disabled while saving; the Games tab has no rename (the bead names *This game*). ## Out of scope - Renaming from the Games tab, the header chip, or the Settings dialog (it keeps showing the name, read-only, and follows a rename). - Refusing duplicate names at creation or rename. - Renaming a game that is not the open one. - Files already exported: a backup or map export written under the old name keeps it (say so in the close reason, as the bead asks). - Validating the name in the core: the rule stays in `gameSession.ts`, once. ## Validation ```bash cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace pnpm run typecheck && pnpm run test pnpm run test:smoke tests/smoke/games.spec.ts pnpm run check:fast grep -n "set_game_name" apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs tests/native/sweep.ts # wrapper and sweep row, both present ``` Human (Psylocke): rename the open game on the desktop app; the chip, the Games row, Settings and a fresh backup's file name all read the new name after a restart; an empty name is refused under the field; Escape cancels without closing the picker. ## Known traps - **Register and sweep in the same commit.** `main.rs`'s `generate_handler!` and `tests/native/ sweep.ts` — the five-times slip; if `pnpm run test:tooling` has a lockstep check (ah-ga6), run it. - **`rename_all = "snake_case"` on the Tauri command** and `{ game_id, game_name }` in the invoke — the client-side keys are snake_case (`index.ts:2008-2013`), and a camelCase key fails at runtime only on the desktop, which no local suite drives. - **The Escape order.** The picker's Escape handler is a `document` listener (`GamePicker.tsx:46-52`). The input's `onKeyDown` must call `stopPropagation()` on the *React* event, which stops the native event before it reaches `document` (React listens on the root container). Do not "fix" the picker handler with a `renaming` check instead — the effect's closure would go stale or re-register on every keystroke. - **`autoFocus` + `select()`.** `autoFocus` focuses; selecting the text is a separate `select()` in an effect that must run once per open, not on every render while typing (or every keystroke re-selects and the next key replaces the whole name). - **`runGameAction` generic.** Widening `work` to `() => Promise` changes nothing for existing callers, but the handler must compare `done === true`, not `Boolean(done)` — `runReported` resolves `undefined` on failure and `true` on success only because the work returns `true`. - **No jsdom.** The picker's clicks and focus are smoke-tested only; `renderToStaticMarkup` cannot see focus or `select()`. - **The amber is `text-warn`** (`theme.css:66`), not `text-warning` — Tailwind will silently accept an unknown class and render the line in the default ink. - **Rebase risk: ah-c0m touches the same tab** (`GamePicker.tsx` *This game*: the small print, an import confirmation, and `AppShell.tsx`'s `importGameBackup`). Whichever lands second rebases; the Name row (this bead) and the import block (ah-c0m) are different parts of the same `div`, so the conflict is textual, not semantic.
acceptance_criteria: A game's name can be changed from the This game panel in the game picker. The new name appears everywhere the old one did and persists across a restart. An empty or whitespace-only name is refused, consistently with how creating a game refuses one. The game's identity, reports, orders and history are unaffected by a rename.

Also fixed a related bug found during implementation: three AppShell.tsx effects (ruleset fetch, hex-notes load, turn restore) were keyed on the whole game object rather than the fields they read, so a rename triggered a spurious ruleset refetch/turn re-parse and busy flip that stole UI focus. Fixed with a gameEpoch counter bumped only by enterGame. See docs/retrospectives/ah-lkw.md. title: Implementers check a pushed head can merge before waiting on its CI
description:
An implementer waiting for CI after a rebase/force-push can waste a wait cycle polling , whose state can be stale, when the real problem is that the branch is CONFLICTING against main and GitHub never ran (or won't meaningfully complete) a fresh check run against that head.

Observed on ah-k6i.5 (PR #285, 2026-08-15): after rebasing and force-pushing, `gh pr view --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus` already showed `DIRTY`/`CONFLICTING`, but the implementer went straight into the *Waiting, without ending your run* CI-poll loop from `implement-bead` anyway, reading stale/cached check state. The navigator had to interrupt and point out the conflict. A second rebase then surfaced a real conflict against a sibling bead's PR (ah-k6i.3) that had also touched AppShell.tsx, which was resolved correctly — but the wasted poll cycle itself was never caught by the process.
design:
## Context

On ah-k6i.5 (PR #285, 2026-08-15) the implementer rebased, force-pushed, and went straight into the
CI wait — while `gh pr view --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus` already said `CONFLICTING` / `DIRTY`.
The check state it polled described an older head, and nothing in `implement-bead` told it to look at
the merge state first; the navigator had to interrupt. The gap is in the skill, not in any code:
`.claude/skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md`'s *Merging* section (line 515 on `main` `b701e08`) shows how
to catch a `BEHIND` branch up and how to resolve a 422, but the CI wait that follows every push is
entered on faith. This bead adds the check, in the words below, so the loop is never entered against
a head that cannot merge. Documentation only; no application code, no test code.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

One file: `.claude/skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md`. Three edits, all text; nothing else moves.

**Edit 1 — *Merging* (currently :515-563).** Insert the following block *after* the paragraph that
ends "`# back to --phase ci, and wait for CI`" (the 422 fallback, :538-545) and *before* the paragraph
beginning "An update (or a resolved rebase) that brings in commits touching nothing" (:547):

````markdown
**Before waiting on CI after any push that could have raced main** — an `update-branch`, a rebase and
force-push, a fix pushed onto a head that sat through a review — check that the head can merge at all:

```bash
until state="$(gh pr view <n> --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus -q '"\(.mergeable) \(.mergeStateStatus)"')" \
      && [ "${state%% *}" != "UNKNOWN" ]; do sleep 5; done
echo "$state"
```

`mergeable` reads `UNKNOWN` for a few seconds after every push while GitHub recomputes it, which is
what the poll is for. Then:

- `CONFLICTING DIRTY` — the head cannot merge, and whatever `gh pr checks` would show you next
  describes an older head or a run GitHub will not meaningfully finish. **Do not enter the CI wait.**
  Go to the local rebase above (`--phase rebase`), resolve, `git push --force-with-lease`, and run
  this check again.
- `MERGEABLE BEHIND` — catch up with `update-branch` as above, and check again once it lands.
- anything else (`MERGEABLE CLEAN`, `MERGEABLE BLOCKED`, `MERGEABLE UNSTABLE`) — the head is worth
  waiting on: `--phase ci`, and wait per *Waiting, without ending your run*.

Observed on ah-k6i.5 (PR #285, 2026-08-15): after a rebase and force-push the PR already read
`CONFLICTING`/`DIRTY`, and the implementer polled check state for a head that would never merge until
the navigator interrupted. Twenty seconds of `gh pr view` is what that wait cost.
````

**Edit 2 — the CI wait after the review (currently :490-495).** The sentence "and wait for CI as
*Waiting, without ending your run* describes." becomes:

> and wait for CI as *Waiting, without ending your run* describes — after first checking the head can
> merge, per *Merging*'s merge-state check, if anything was pushed since the PR opened.

**Edit 3 — *Traps this repository has already paid for* (currently :625+).** Add one bullet, after
"**A stale lease is not an abandoned agent**":

> - **A CI wait against a conflicted head.** After a rebase, a force-push or an `update-branch`,
>   `gh pr view --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus` can already say `CONFLICTING`/`DIRTY` while the
>   check state you are about to poll still describes the previous head. Look at the merge state
>   before the checks — *Merging* has the loop. Cost once on ah-k6i.5.

Nothing is renumbered by hand: the `:NNN` line references above are for finding the places, and are
not written into the file.

## Increments

1. Make the three edits. There is no failing test to open this increment: the artefact is prose in a
   skill file, and the repository has no lint that reads it (`pnpm run check:fast` does not touch
   `.claude/skills/`). The RED here is the reading in *Validation*.
2. `pnpm run check:fast` (unchanged, but it is the gate before every PR). PR
   `docs(ah-yvf): implement-bead checks the merge state before waiting on CI after a push`,
   `@copilot`, CI, squash. This is a change to a skill, so it is **not** the docs-only mockup
   exception — the Copilot review is required as for any bead. Close the bead.

## The test plan

None. Documentation only; no suite exercises skill text. The two checks that stand in for tests are in
*Validation*.

## User-facing decisions

None. Nothing a player sees; the reader is an implementer session.

## Out of scope

- Any change to `beads-workflow`, `plan-bead`, `CLAUDE.md`, or `.claude/agents/implementer.md`.
- A merge queue in front of main (ah-jcr) — that would make this check unnecessary one day; today it is
  unranked, and this bead is the cheap fix in the meantime.
- Automating the check into a script under `.claude/cerebro/scripts/` (that directory is a submodule
  and is Cerebro's).

## Validation

```bash
grep -n "Before waiting on CI after any push" .claude/skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md      # edit 1 present, once
grep -n "merge-state check" .claude/skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md                         # edit 2 present, once
grep -n "A CI wait against a conflicted head" .claude/skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md      # edit 3 present, once
bash -n <(sed -n '/^until state=/,/^echo "\$state"/p' .claude/skills/implement-bead/SKILL.md)   # the loop parses
gh pr view <any open PR> --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus -q '"\(.mergeable) \(.mergeStateStatus)"'  # the query works
pnpm run check:fast
```

Read the *Merging* section top to bottom once as an implementer about to rebase, and confirm the order
of operations is unambiguous: push → merge-state check → (resolve | catch up | wait on CI).

## Known traps

- **Do not touch the fenced-code nesting.** The block in edit 1 contains a ```` ```bash ```` fence
  inside a Markdown list of prose; the four-backtick fence in this plan is only how the plan quotes it —
  in the skill file it is a plain ```` ```bash ```` block between paragraphs, like the ones already in
  *Merging*.
- **`gh pr view -q` with a template string.** The `-q '"\(.mergeable) \(.mergeStateStatus)"'` form is
  jq string interpolation and needs the outer single quotes exactly as written; `--jq` and `-q` are the
  same flag.
- **`.claude/skills/` is tracked; `.claude/cerebro/` is a submodule.** The edit is to the former. If
  `git status` shows `.claude/cerebro` modified, that is an unrelated submodule pointer and must not go
  into this PR.
acceptance_criteria: `implement-bead`'s *Merging* section (or *Waiting, without ending your run*) is updated so that, after any push that could have raced main (a rebase, an `update-branch` call), the implementer checks `gh pr view --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus` for `CONFLICTING`/`DIRTY` BEFORE entering the CI-poll loop — and if conflicting, resolves the conflict (or re-syncs) first rather than polling checks. The change is a documentation/skill edit, not application code.
notes: Filed from a navigator conversation during ah-k6i.5's implementation (Cyclops), not from Bishop's sweep — this is a process gap in the implementer skill itself, not a codebase smell.
close_reason: Delivered in atlantis-hud PR #299 (bringing in rmstdope/cerebro#33)

title: The map on screen is derived from the core's known map, not rebuilt in TypeScript
description: Third slice of ah-u4e. gameMemory's outcomes (rememberTurn, readMemory, restoreLatestTurn, mergeTurn) carry the core-built known map alongside the remembered regions; buildHexMapModel becomes a synchronous conversion of that model into HexNodes (labels, knowledge word, ages, unit counts) with every precedence rule deleted from hexMapModel.ts; the smoke suite and the map tests must not change what they see.
design:
## Context

Third and last slice of **ah-u4e**. **ah-u4e.1 has merged** (#297, `6388e88`): the precedence rules
for the accumulated map live once, in `crates/core/src/known_map.rs` (`resolve_known_map(current,
remembered) -> KnownMap`, `KnownMapHex { coordinate, terrain, province, knowledge: Current|Stale|Named,
last_seen_turn, region }`, hexes sorted by `(z, y, x)`, module doc = the specification), and the
planner derives `MapKnowledge` from it. **ah-u4e.2 is planned and being built** (blocks this; read
its plan with `bd show ah-u4e.2 --json`): it carries that resolution across the boundary as one
command — `CoreClient.knownMap(rawReport: string, rulesetJson: string | null, remembered:
RememberedRegion[]): Promise<KnownMap>` on both shells, with `KnownMap`, `KnownMapHex` and
`HexKnowledge` exported from `@atlantis/core-client`. **Verify those names against what .2 actually
merged before writing a line** — the seam is a promise until then.

This slice makes the screen consume it. Today `packages/shared/src/hexMapModel.ts`
`buildHexMapModel(parsed, storedRegions)` (:253-365 on `origin/main` `6388e88`) re-derives every rule
in TypeScript — namings oldest first, the report's namings win, a stored sighting overwrites a naming,
same-turn ally sightings are current, `withAlliesUnits` — from `StoredRegion`s that `gameMemory.ts`
`toStoredRegions` flattens out of the core's `RememberedRegion`s. After this bead:

- **The screen's map is the core's `KnownMap`, converted.** `buildHexMapModel(known: KnownMap):
  HexMapModel` is a synchronous, rule-free conversion of `KnownMapHex` into `HexNode` (label, age,
  settlement name, unit counts, region id). Every precedence rule, `withAlliesUnits`, `namedFromExit`,
  `namingsOldestFirst`, `nodeFromRegion`, `StoredRegion` and `toStoredRegions` are deleted.
- **The known map arrives with the memory it was resolved from.** Every place the shell reads the
  remembered regions back (`rememberTurn`/`readMemory`, `mergeTurn`, `restoreLatestTurn`, and
  `loadTurn` on top of them) also asks the core for the known map, and hands both to the shell as one
  value, so a render never shows a new report over an old map or the reverse.
- **The opening selection is read from the report alone**, which is all it ever depended on: the hex
  the player has units in, else the first visited hex, in `(z, y, x)` order.
- **One addition to core**, small and stated: `KnownMapHex` gains `settlement: Option<Settlement>`.
  Today's `namedFromExit` (:208-223) carries `exit.settlement?.name` for a hex known only by name, and
  the map draws it (`workspace/mapThemes/hexView.ts:277`) and the region panel shows it
  (`workspace/RegionPanel.tsx:87-90`); .1's struct dropped it, and without it a named town would lose
  its label — a visible change the epic promised not to make.

**No player-visible change.** The smoke suite and the map tests must see exactly what they see
today. The only behaviour that moves is the one .1 already moved (a same-turn ally's units, which the
screen already showed).

Verified on `origin/main` `6388e88` (line numbers below are against it):
- `hexMapModel.ts`: `HexKnowledge` :17, `HexNode` :19-35, `HexMapModel` :37-42
  (`initialSelectedRegionId` :41), `StoredRegion` :46-54, `countUnits` :127-135, `withAlliesUnits`
  :156-173, `nodeFromRegion` :175-195, `namedFromExit` :208-223, `namingsOldestFirst` :238-240,
  `buildHexMapModel` :253-365, `unitsForHex` :370-380, `hexLabelOf` :96-102, `regionIdOf` :86-88.
- `gameMemory.ts`: `toStoredRegions` :35-45, `MemoryOutcome` :48-67, `rememberTurn` :81-97,
  `readMemory` :150-166, `MergeOutcome` :199-206, `mergeTurn` :221-248, `RestoredTurn` :251-263,
  `restoreLatestTurn` :281-324 (`remembered`/`warning` at :299-306).
- `reportLoad.ts`: `LoadedTurn.remembered` :57, `loadTurn` :80-122 (`remembered: memory.remembered`
  :109), `openingSelection` :131-146 (uses `buildHexMapModel(report)`), imports :33.
- `workspace/AppShell.tsx`: `EMPTY` :163-168, `remembered` state :245, `storedRegions` :431,
  `rememberedJson` :435, `model` :436-439, `setRemembered` at :796 (`applyLoadedTurn`), :964
  (`mergeReport`), :1058 (batch merge-only path), :1249 (restore effect), :1320 (`enterGame`);
  `buildHexMapModel(restored.parsed)` :1273-1277; `openingSelection(loaded.parsed)` :812;
  `rulesetText` :261; the restore effect calls `restoreLatestTurn(client, game,
  reportParser(client, ruleset))` :1234; the merge-only batch path reads `readMemory(client, game,
  viewerFactionId, parsed?.header.turnNumber ?? null)` :1057, the finished-batch path
  `readMemory(client, game, viewerFactionId as string, walk.finish.step.turnNumber)` :1044-1049 with
  `walk.finish.source.text` to hand.
- `crates/core/src/known_map.rs`: `KnownMapHex` :54-67, rule 1 :147-155, rule 2 :171-179, rule 3
  :200-212, rule 4 :234-242; `crates/core/src/report/model.rs`: `Exit.settlement: Option<Settlement>`
  :68, `ReportRegion.settlement` :151. `crates/core/tests/known_map.rs` (its `report_at_turn` /
  `at` helpers :9-33). `core-client` `SettlementInfo = { name: string; size: string }` :112,
  `RememberedRegion` :242 (arrives as-is from the wire, cast at :1942 — no normaliser).
- `region_id` is always `coordinate.id()` = `"z:x,y"` (`report/region.rs:65`, `write.rs:489`), which
  is `regionIdOf` in TS — so a `HexNode.regionId` can be derived from the coordinate for every hex.
- Consumers of `HexNode` that stay untouched: `hexView.ts`, `RegionPanel.tsx`, `UnitTableDock.tsx`,
  `changesView.ts` (uses `hexLabelOf`), `congestedFixture.ts` (builds `HexNode`s by hand).
- Tests: `hexMapModel.test.ts` (612 lines; the "map knowledge", "opening selection" and "a hex an
  ally also saw this turn" describes are the rule tests, :192-503 and :529-593; "hex geometry",
  "addressing a hex", "unit ordering", "abbreviateDirection" stay), `gameMemory.test.ts` (fake
  `client()` :63-70; "handing remembered regions to the map" :456+), `reportLoad.test.ts`
  (`openingSelection` :224-243).

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### 1. Core: `crates/core/src/known_map.rs` (+ `crates/core/tests/known_map.rs`)

```rust
pub struct KnownMapHex {
    // ...existing fields...
    /// The settlement the hex contains, when its description names one - for a `Named` hex the
    /// exit's `contains X [kind]`, for a visited one the region's. The screen labels the hex with it.
    pub settlement: Option<Settlement>,
}
```

Set it in all four rules: rule 1 and 2 `exit.settlement.clone()`; rule 3 `entry.region.settlement.clone()`;
rule 4 `resolved.settlement.clone()`. `Settlement` is `crate::report::model::Settlement` (serde
camelCase, `{ name, size }` — the same shape `SettlementInfo` reads on the TS side). New test in
`crates/core/tests/known_map.rs`, in its `report_at_turn` style:
`a_named_hex_keeps_the_settlement_its_exit_names` — an exit line
`Southeast : plain (2,2) in Nowhere, contains Foo [village].` yields a `Named` hex at `(2,2)` whose
`settlement` is `Some(Settlement { name: "Foo", .. })`; and `a_visited_hex_carries_its_own_settlement`
(a region line `contains Inholm [city]`, as `report/region.rs:290`).

The wire type in `packages/core-client/src/index.ts` (**created by .2 — find `KnownMapHex` there**)

### 2. `packages/shared/src/hexMapModel.ts` — the conversion

```ts
import type { Coordinate, HexKnowledge, KnownMap, KnownMapHex, ReportRegion, ReportUnit } from "@atlantis/core-client";

/** Owned by core since ah-u4e.1; re-exported so the map's consumers keep importing it from here. */
export type { HexKnowledge };

export type HexNode = { /* unchanged, all 13 fields */ };

export type HexMapModel = {
  hexes: HexNode[];
  levels: number[];
  currentTurn: number | null;
  // `initialSelectedRegionId` is gone: the opening selection is the report's alone (reportLoad.ts).
};

/**
 * The map as the screen draws it, converted from the core's resolution. No rule lives here any
 * more: which hex is current, stale or named, whose units count, and which naming won are all
 * `known_map::resolve_known_map`'s (crates/core/src/known_map.rs, module doc). This turns each
 * resolved hex into a `HexNode` and nothing else. The core hands the hexes sorted by level, row,
 * column, and that order is kept.
 */
export function buildHexMapModel(known: KnownMap): HexMapModel;

/** One resolved hex as the screen draws it. Exported for the tests. */
export function hexNodeOf(hex: KnownMapHex, currentTurn: number | null): HexNode;

/** Own units first, then by name - one of 92 being yours should not be buried. */
export function sortUnitsForDisplay(units: ReportUnit[]): ReportUnit[];
```

### 4. `packages/shared/src/gameMemory.ts` — the map arrives with the memory

```ts
import type { KnownMap } from "@atlantis/core-client";

/** What the shell holds about the world beyond the report: the remembered regions (for the planner and the map export, as the core keeps them) and the known map the core resolved from them (for the screen). Set together, always. */
export type KnownMemory = { remembered: RememberedRegion[]; knownMap: KnownMap | null };
export const EMPTY_MEMORY: KnownMemory = { remembered: [], knownMap: null };

/**
 * Resolves the map the screen draws. Never throws: a map that will not resolve with the memory is
 * resolved from the report alone (what today's shell drew when the memory could not be read), and
 * one that will not resolve at all is `null` - the map is empty, and the units panel, which reads
 * the report, still works. The warning names the first failure.
 */
export async function knownMapFor(
  client: Pick<CoreClient, "knownMap">, rawReport: string, rulesetJson: string | null, remembered: RememberedRegion[]
): Promise<{ knownMap: KnownMap | null; warning: string | null }>;
// try knownMap(raw, ruleset, remembered) → { knownMap, warning: null }
// catch e1 → try knownMap(raw, ruleset, []) → { knownMap, warning: `the remembered map could not be drawn: ${detail(e1)}` }
// catch e2 → { knownMap: null, warning: `the map could not be drawn: ${detail(e2)}` }
```

## Increments

1. RED (Rust): the two settlement tests in `crates/core/tests/known_map.rs`. GREEN: the field, set in
   four places. `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core`, clippy, fmt. Add `settlement` to the core-client
