title: Game backup export and import share one codec in the core on both platforms
description: Child 1 of ah-8m0 (Bishop: the store's rules are written twice). The backup document — its format tag, version bounds, field set, defaults for a turn's timestamps and the checks on a remembered region's payload — is encoded and decoded in crates/core-persistence (Rust, serde) and again in packages/browser-core/src/webCoreAdapter.ts (parseBackupJson, exportGame, importGame). This child moves the codec into the core (one Rust module, exported through core-wasm), and both stores call it: the desktop's export_game/import_game become SELECT→encode / decode→INSERT and the web's become getAll→encode / decode→put. Plan in the design field.

title: One builder per report type in tests, so a new field edits no test file
description: Third pass of ah-164. TypeScript: typed builders (parsedReport, region, unit, battle, parseResult) exported from @atlantis/core-client and used by the test files that today each carry their own copy of a whole-report literal. Rust: Default derives on the report family so in-crate test builders use ..Default::default(). Blocked by the generated types, which the builders are typed against.
design:
## Context

Third and last pass under epic `ah-164` (report types cross to TypeScript once). **Blocked by
`ah-164.2`**, which is being built as this is written: it deletes the hand-written report types in
`packages/core-client/src/index.ts` and re-exports ts-rs–generated ones from
`packages/core-client/src/generated/*.ts` (`ParsedReport`, `ReportHeaderInfo`, `ReportRegion`,
`ReportUnit`, `Battle`, `BattleUnit`, `Coordinate`, …). Read its plan first (`bd show ah-164.2
--json`); every type name below is the name that plan exports, and `packages/core-client/src/generated/`
must exist in your checkout before increment 1 — if it does not, `ah-164.2` has not merged and this
bead is not ready.

**The cost being paid.** After `ah-164.2` a Rust field crosses to TypeScript in one edit — and then
breaks every test file that spells a whole report, region, unit or battle as a literal, because the
generated type is complete and the literal is not. Bishop measured the ripple at three files
(`6af62de` battles, `923c711` faction status: `gameMemory.test.ts`, `hexMapModel.test.ts`,
`orderDraft.test.ts`, one line each); a survey on 2026-08-16 counted the set that would break today:

- whole `ParsedReport` (with all 14 `ReportHeaderInfo` fields): `packages/shared/src/batchImport.test.ts:5–28`,
  `gameMemory.test.ts:40–62`, `orderDraft.test.ts:11–33`, `ordersImport.test.ts:93–116`,
  `reportLoad.test.ts:67–90`, `turnDiff.test.ts:64–86`, `workspace/changesView.test.ts:63–85`;
- whole `ReportRegion`: `gameMemory.test.ts:18–39`, `hexMapModel.test.ts:42–67`, `reportLoad.test.ts:45–65`,
  `turnDiff.test.ts:41–62`, `workspace/changesView.test.ts:40–61`, `workspace/UnitTableDock.test.tsx:14–35`,
  `workspace/RegionPanel.test.tsx:37–56` (inside `HEX`), `workspace/mapThemes/hexView.test.ts:47–68`,
  `packages/core-client/src/index.test.ts:1169–1189` (`REMEMBERED`; note the stale `tax: null` key);
- whole `ReportUnit` (seven near-identical 21-line helpers): `hexMapModel.test.ts:21–40`,
  `reportLoad.test.ts:23–41`, `turnDiff.test.ts:8–28`, `unitComposition.test.ts:5–25`,
  `unitTable.test.ts:16–36`, `unitTooltip.test.ts:5–25`, `unitPreview.test.ts:5–27`,
  `workspace/changesView.test.ts:18–38`, `workspace/UnitTableDock.test.tsx:59–79`,
  `workspace/mapThemes/hexView.test.ts:25–45`, `workspace/mapThemes/congestedFixture.ts:25–43`;
- whole `Battle`/`BattleUnit`: `workspace/battles.test.ts:12–48`, `workspace/BattlesDialog.test.tsx:8–92, 198–214`.

`turnDiff.test.ts:6–86` and `changesView.test.ts:16–85` are byte-identical apart from `foreignUnit`.
Three of the report helpers (`batchImport`, `ordersImport`, `reportLoad`) end in
`as unknown as ParsedReport`, so today they would not even fail — they would silently hand the code
a report missing the field. `Battle.assassination` was declared optional in TypeScript
(`index.ts:554`, "so the existing literals would not break") while Rust has it required
(`crates/core/src/report/battle.rs:132`); ts-rs generates it required, which is right, and the
builder is what makes that cheap.

On the Rust side the integration tests under `crates/core/tests/` build reports by parsing text
(`parse_report_full`), so they never ripple. Three `#[cfg(test)]` modules spell whole literals:
`crates/core/src/report/merge.rs:280–321` (`region()`, `unit()`), `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs:1084–1128`
(`region()`, `unit()`) and `crates/core/src/movement/mode.rs:412–431` (`sample_unit()`).
`ReportHeader` (`crates/core/src/report/header.rs:34`) already derives `Default`, which is why
`report_of()` at `merge.rs:368` and `report()` at `semantics.rs:1162` already use
`..Default::default()` for the header and did not ripple on `923c711`.

**Decision.** TypeScript: one module of typed builders in `@atlantis/core-client`
(`packages/core-client/src/builders.ts`), re-exported from the package root, one function per type
that tests spell out today — `aReportUnit`, `aReportRegion`, `aReportHeaderInfo`, `aParsedReport`,
`aBattle`, `aBattleUnit` — each `(overrides: Partial<T> = {}) => T`, returning a complete,
self-consistent value. Every test file above is migrated to them, and no test file may spell a
complete literal of those six types afterwards. Rust: `Default` on the whole report family under
`crates/core/src/report/`, hand-written for `ReportUnit` so `men_estimated` defaults to `true` as
its doc comment says, and the three test modules trimmed to `..Default::default()`.

Rejected: a separate `@atlantis/test-builders` package or a `@atlantis/fixtures` home — `fixtures`
already exists on both sides and means "the committed `.rep` files"; putting builders there gives it
a dependency on `core-client` while `core-client`'s own tests want the builders, a cycle for
nothing. A `@atlantis/core-client/testing` subpath — the package has no `exports` map and adding
one to carry a second entry is more surface than six pure functions in the root. The functions are
side-effect-free and unused by any app, so the web bundle tree-shakes them out.

The naming rule, so nobody has to invent a name for the next one: **`a` + the exact type name**,
`aReportUnit` for `ReportUnit`. It reads as English in a test (`aReportUnit({ own: false })`), it
cannot collide with a local `unit`/`region` a file keeps as a wrapper, and it says which type
without looking it up.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `packages/core-client/src/builders.ts` — new

The whole file. Types come from `./generated/…` directly (the files `ah-164.2` writes; `index.ts`
imports its own uses the same way) rather than from `./index`, so the module `index.ts` re-exports
does not import `index.ts` back. All imports are `import type`, so nothing runs at load.

```ts
/**
 * Builders for the report model, for tests anywhere in the workspace.
 *
 * Each returns a complete, self-consistent value with every field set, and takes a shallow
 * `Partial<T>` of overrides — a test names only the fields it is about, and a field added to the
 * Rust model (and so to the generated types) is set once here and in no test file (ah-164.3).
 *
 * The defaults describe one small world, the same one the turn-diff tests already used: faction 95
 * "Borg TNG", turn 71 (December, Year 6), the mountain at (7,53) in Inhead, and a one-man unit
 * called Scouts standing in it. A test that asserts on one of these values passes it explicitly
 * all the same — the defaults are a convenience, not a contract.
 *
 * Overrides are spread last and shallowly: `aReportRegion({ units: [u] })` has exactly `[u]`,
 * and nested values are built with the nested builder, `aParsedReport({ header: aReportHeaderInfo({ … }) })`.
 * Naming rule: `a` + the exact type name.
 */
import type { Battle } from "./generated/Battle";
import type { BattleUnit } from "./generated/BattleUnit";
import type { Coordinate } from "./generated/Coordinate";
import type { ParsedReport } from "./generated/ParsedReport";
import type { ReportHeaderInfo } from "./generated/ReportHeaderInfo";
import type { ReportRegion } from "./generated/ReportRegion";
import type { ReportUnit } from "./generated/ReportUnit";

/** The mountain at (7,53) on the surface, where the default unit stands. */
const DEFAULT_COORDINATE: Coordinate = { x: 7, y: 53, z: 1 };

/** `z:x,y` — the spelling of Rust `Coordinate::id` and of `hexMapModel.regionIdOf`. */
function regionIdOf(coordinate: Coordinate): string {
  return `${coordinate.z}:${coordinate.x},${coordinate.y}`;
}

export function aReportUnit(overrides: Partial<ReportUnit> = {}): ReportUnit {
  return {
    unitId: "1",
    name: "Scouts",
    regionId: regionIdOf(DEFAULT_COORDINATE),
    factionId: "95",
    factionName: "Borg TNG",
    own: true,
    onGuard: false,
    flags: [],
    items: [],
    skills: [],
    men: 1,
    menEstimated: false,
    menByRace: [],
    weight: null,
    capacity: null,
    structureId: null,
    ...overrides
  };
}

/** `regionId` follows `coordinate` unless both are given. */
export function aReportRegion(overrides: Partial<ReportRegion> = {}): ReportRegion {
  const coordinate = overrides.coordinate ?? DEFAULT_COORDINATE;
  return {
    regionId: regionIdOf(coordinate),
    coordinate,
    terrain: "mountain",
    province: "Inhead",
    settlement: null,
    population: null,
    race: null,
    taxBase: null,
    wages: null,
    maxWages: null,
    entertainment: null,
    products: [],
    wanted: [],
    forSale: [],
    exits: [],
    structures: [],
    units: [],
    ...overrides
  };
}

export function aReportHeaderInfo(overrides: Partial<ReportHeaderInfo> = {}): ReportHeaderInfo {
  return {
    factionId: "95",
    factionName: "Borg TNG",
    factionTypes: [],
    month: "December",
    year: 6,
    turnNumber: 71,
    engineVersion: null,
    ruleset: null,
    rulesetVersion: null,
    unclaimedSilver: null,
    errors: [],
    events: [],
    factionStatus: { entries: [], unparsed: [] },
    attitudes: { defaultAttitude: null, levels: [] },
    ...overrides
  };
}

export function aParsedReport(overrides: Partial<ParsedReport> = {}): ParsedReport {
  return {
    header: aReportHeaderInfo(),
    regions: [],
    battles: [],
    ordersTemplate: null,
    ...overrides
  };
}

export function aBattleUnit(overrides: Partial<BattleUnit> = {}): BattleUnit {
  return {
    name: "Scouts",
    id: "1",
    faction: { name: "Borg TNG", id: "95" },
    flags: [],
    body: "1 man",
    ...overrides
  };
}

/**
 * The turn-71 fixture's first battle (`AA Tomb's Guards (7280) attacks Pirates (14789) in ocean
 * (25,55)`), with empty rosters, rounds and casualties — the two battle tests already start from it.
 */
export function aBattle(overrides: Partial<Battle> = {}): Battle {
  return {
    headline: "AA Tomb's Guards (7280) attacks Pirates (14789) in ocean (25,55) in Atlantis Ocean!",
    attacker: { name: "AA Tomb's Guards", id: "7280" },
    defender: { name: "Pirates", id: "14789" },
    terrain: "ocean",
    coordinate: { x: 25, y: 55, z: 1 },
    province: "Atlantis Ocean",
    attackers: [],
    defenders: [],
    rounds: [],
    statistics: [],
    casualties: [],
    damagedUnits: [],
    spoils: null,
    lineStart: 10,
    lineEnd: 200,
    assassination: false,
    ...overrides
  };
}
```

If a generated type has a field this file does not list, `pnpm run typecheck` says so at the return
statement — that is the mechanism working, not a mistake in the plan; add the field with its
neutral default here and nowhere else. If a generated file's name differs from the import above
(`ah-164.2` renames some: `ReportHeaderInfo`, `RegionExit`, `SettlementInfo`, `StructureInfo`,
`SkillInfo`), read `packages/core-client/src/generated/` and use the name that is there.

### `packages/core-client/src/index.ts`

One line, next to the `export type { … } from "./generated/…"` block `ah-164.2` added:

```ts
export { aBattle, aBattleUnit, aParsedReport, aReportHeaderInfo, aReportRegion, aReportUnit } from "./builders";
```

Nothing else in the file changes.

### `packages/core-client/src/builders.test.ts` — new

The pins are listed under *The test plan*. Import from `"./builders"`.

### The migrations — every file named in *Context*, and no other

For each file: delete the local exhaustive helper (or literal), replace its uses with the builder,
and re-run that file's tests before moving to the next
(`pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared exec vitest run src/<file>` from the repo root; for core-client,
`--filter @atlantis/core-client`). Rules that decide every case:

1. **A value the file's tests assert on is passed as an override, whatever the builder default is.**
   The compiler cannot catch a test that expected `"Borg"` and now gets `"Borg TNG"`; the failing
   test can, which is why each file is run before the next is touched.
2. **A local wrapper may stay when the file calls it many times with its own defaults**, as long as
   it lists only the fields that file cares about — that is the shape that makes the migration
   readable, not a way round it. E.g. `hexMapModel.test.ts:21`'s positional
   `unit(unitId, own, name = unitId)` becomes
   `const unit = (unitId: string, own: boolean, name = unitId): ReportUnit => aReportUnit({ unitId, own, name });`
   and `gameMemory.test.ts:40`'s `report(factionId)` becomes
   `aParsedReport({ header: aReportHeaderInfo({ factionId, factionName: "Borg", month: "January" }) })` — with
   whatever values that file's assertions actually read.
3. **The `as unknown as ParsedReport` casts go** (`batchImport.test.ts:28`, `ordersImport.test.ts:116`,
   `reportLoad.test.ts:90`); with the builders they type-check without a cast, and a type error that
   appears when the cast is removed is a real gap to fix with a builder, never by putting the cast
   back. `reportLoad.test.ts:67`'s `regions: unknown[]` becomes `regions: ReportRegion[]`.
4. **Nested literals go too.** `RegionPanel.test.tsx:37–56`'s `region:` inside `HEX` becomes
   `region: aReportRegion({ regionId: "1:7,53", coordinate: …, terrain: "mountain", province: "Inholm", settlement: { name: "Inholm", size: "city" }, population: 8500, race: "highelf", taxBase: 1200, wages: "$14", maxWages: 16, entertainment: 200 })`;
   `BattlesDialog.test.tsx`'s `FIRST` (`:8–74`), `SECOND` (`:77–92`) and the assassination battle
   (`:198–214`) become `aBattle({ … })` with `attackers: [aBattleUnit({ … }), …]` — keep every
   roster entry, round and casualty those tests draw, since the dialog's markup assertions read them.
   `index.test.ts:1169–1189`'s `REMEMBERED` region becomes `aReportRegion({ coordinate: { x: 2, y: 2, z: 1 }, terrain: "plain", province: "Nowhere" })`
   (`regionId` follows; the stale `tax: null` key disappears with it).
5. **`congestedFixture.ts:25–43`** is a fixture module, not a test, but it is the same literal — its
   `unit()` becomes a wrapper over `aReportUnit` with `unitId: "900", name: "Walker", regionId: "", factionId: "17", factionName: "Own"`.
6. **A helper that becomes unused is deleted** — `eslint` runs with `--max-warnings=0` and
   `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars` is an error (`eslint.config.mjs:22`).
7. **`turnDiff.test.ts` and `changesView.test.ts` first**: their helpers *are* the builder defaults
   (`unit()`, `region()`, `report()` at `turnDiff.test.ts:8–86`), so `unit` → `aReportUnit`,
   `foreignUnit(o)` → `aReportUnit({ unitId: "999", name: "Raiders", factionId: "32", factionName: "Elder Tree Forests", own: false, ...o })`,
   `region(coordinate, o)` → `aReportRegion({ coordinate, ...o })`, `report(regions, turnNumber = 71)` →
   `aParsedReport({ header: aReportHeaderInfo({ turnNumber }), regions })`. Both files' tests must
   pass unchanged; if one does not, a builder default is wrong — fix the builder, since these two
   files defined the defaults.

Left alone, deliberately: `comparisonActions.test.ts:14, 90` (`{ header: { turnNumber } } as unknown as ParsedReport`,
a two-key stub that reads as one), `browser-core/src/webCoreAdapter.test.ts:16–20, 967` (a fake wasm
returning untyped shapes), every `FactionStatus`/`DeclaredAttitudes`/`Combatant`/`Casualty`/`StructureInfo`
literal (two to five fields — a literal is clearer than a builder; `hexView.test.ts:21`'s and
`congestedFixture.ts:22`'s `structure(kind)` stay), and every `at(x, y, z = 1)` coordinate helper
(three fields, never gains one).

### Rust — `crates/core/src/report/{mod,model,header,battle,orders}.rs`

Add `Default` to the derive list of every type here that lacks it (verified 2026-08-16):
`ParsedReport` (`mod.rs:39`); `Coordinate` (`model.rs:14`), `ItemAmount` (`:31`), `MarketItem` (`:40`),
`Settlement` (`:50`), `Exit` (`:62`), `Structure` (`:73`), `Skill` (`:86`), `ReportRegion` (`:145`);
`FactionStatusEntry` (`header.rs:68`), `AttitudeLevel` (`:86`), `FactionRef` (`:94`);
`Combatant` (`battle.rs:60`), `BattleUnit` (`:72`), `Casualty` (`:86`), `Battle` (`:108`);
`UnitOrders` (`orders.rs:25`), `OrdersTemplate` (`:49`). Every field on all of them is
`String`/`Option`/`Vec`/integer/`bool`/another type on this list, so the derive compiles as-is.
`ReportHeader`, `FactionStatus`, `DeclaredAttitudes` and `BattleRound` already have it.

`ReportUnit` (`model.rs:99`) gets a **hand-written** impl, because its doc comment on `men_estimated`
says the field "Defaults to true" (the serde default at `model.rs:129`, `estimated_until_classified`),
and a derived `Default` would say `false` and make that comment a lie:

```rust
/// A unit nobody has described yet: no people, nothing carried, and — like every payload written
/// before classification existed — an estimate rather than a count. Tests build from this with
/// struct update; production never does.
impl Default for ReportUnit {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            unit_id: String::new(),
            name: String::new(),
            region_id: String::new(),
            faction_id: None,
            faction_name: None,
            own: false,
            on_guard: false,
            flags: Vec::new(),
            items: Vec::new(),
            skills: Vec::new(),
            men: 0,
            men_estimated: true,
            men_by_race: Vec::new(),
            weight: None,
            capacity: None,
            structure_id: None,
        }
    }
}
```

(`clippy::derivable_impls` does not fire: one field is not its type's default.) `model.rs` has no
test module today — add `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { use super::*; … }` at the end of the file for the
two pins under *The test plan*.

Then the three test modules. The rule that keeps behaviour identical: **delete a field from a
literal only when the value it sets is exactly what `Default` yields** (`Vec::new()`, `None`,
`false`, `0`, `String::new()`/`"".to_string()`, and for `ReportUnit`, `men_estimated: true`); keep
every other field, and end the literal with `..Default::default()`. Sites: `merge.rs:281–300`
(`region()`) and `:303–321` (`unit()`); `semantics.rs:1085–1103` (`region()`), `:1107–1127`
(`unit()`), `:1163–1168` (`report()`, where `battles: Vec::new(), orders_template: None` go);
`mode.rs:413–430` (`sample_unit()`, where `men_estimated: true` is now the default and goes too).
`known_map.rs:258` and `semantics.rs:1275, 1286` already use struct update and are untouched.

Production literals stay complete on purpose — `crates/core/src/orders/effects.rs:383–401` builds a
forming unit and must decide every field, and so do the parser sites (`report/unit.rs:132`,
`report/region.rs:64`, `report/battle.rs:214`). A new field breaking those is a decision being
asked for, which is what a compiler error is for.

### `docs/implementation-plan.md`

Add a section `## Report builders in tests` immediately after `## Generated bindings` (which
`ah-164.2` adds before `## Operating rules for all work packages`; if it is not there, put this one
before `## Operating rules …` instead). Three short paragraphs: the six builders in
`@atlantis/core-client` and the naming rule; the rule that no test file spells a complete literal
of those types (a wrapper over a builder is fine); and the Rust side — the report family derives
`Default`, `ReportUnit::default()` is estimated, and a test literal ends in `..Default::default()`.
One line on the payoff: a field added to a Rust report type is a Rust edit, a `git add` of the
