title: Refactoring: road scaling and fog damping become shared rules; a theme declares only its style
description:
## The cost being paid
Rules that are not "paint" — how road width scales with zoom, how unsurveyed ground is dimmed and rimmed per knowledge state — live inside each of the five ~400–500-line themes as near-identical code (the five RoadLayers differ only in class name, width constant, dash and reach fraction), so one rule change is five edits plus five test edits, and a rule applied wrongly in one theme is invisible to that theme's own suite. Two commits paid it; the second needed a review round and a new registry-wide net. docs/ui/map-themes.md documents "a theme is only the paint" as the chosen split — filed for the navigator's judgement, since the split is deliberate and the cost is real.

## Evidence
- 23abc9e fix(ah-ebv): let roads shrink with the map (#144) — 15 files: the identical edit in all five mapThemes/*/index.tsx (drop vectorEffect="non-scaling-stroke", width from radii()) plus five theme tests; bead ah-ebv notes: "screenshots of all five themes"
- a1fcafa feat(ah-rgp): make the terrain of undiscovered hexes visible (#143) — 19 files, all five index.tsx + five tests for one concept; commit body: "Two things review caught that no theme's own suite could see. Every theme damped its stale wash and left the named one whole … All five now damp both alike, and a registry-wide test checks the gap for every theme at once"
- e65d01f feat(ah-prh) touched all six theme test files

## Where
packages/shared/src/workspace/mapThemes/{beveledTile,cartographersTable,emblemAndDots,miniatureWorld,tacticalHud}/index.tsx (RoadLayer at :203, :200, :156, :240, :171) and their *.test.tsx; mapThemes/hexView.ts, mapHexView.ts

## What a refactoring would change
Lift the cross-cutting rules (stroke scaling, fog damping per knowledge state, rim) into the theme registry or a shared layer that takes theme parameters (width, dash, reach, colours), leaving each theme with only what differs — so a rule is one edit and the registry-wide test is the only test that needs to know it.

Filed by Bishop, weekly sweep of 2026-08-15 (first sweep, whole of origin/main), range e60bbbd..150ba17.
design:
## Context

Two rules that are not paint live inside each of the five map themes as near-identical code, and
each rule change has cost five edits plus five test edits, with a review round to catch the theme
that got it wrong (Bishop's evidence: ah-ebv, 15 files, the identical road-width edit in all five
`index.tsx`; ah-rgp, 19 files, and review found "every theme damped its stale wash and left the
named one whole"). All line numbers are against `main` at `837f0b7` (2026-08-16); everything is
under `packages/shared/src/workspace/mapThemes/` unless a path says otherwise.

1. **Roads.** The five `RoadLayer`s (`beveledTile/index.tsx:200-229`, `cartographersTable/index.tsx:196-237`,
   `emblemAndDots/index.tsx:153-182`, `miniatureWorld/index.tsx:237-265`, `tacticalHud/index.tsx:168-196`)
   are one component five times: the same badge-off short-circuit, the same `<g pointerEvents="none">`,
   the same `views.flatMap → view.roads.map → ROAD_VECTORS[direction]` walk, the same spoke from
   `view.at` along the bearing. What differs is a *style*: class name(s), width as a `radii(...)`
   fraction, reach along the spoke (0.87, or 0.83 for Beveled Tile whose tile is inset from the
   lattice), dash, linecap, opacity — and Cartographer's Table draws two strokes per road (a casing
   and a lighter dashed line) where the others draw one.
2. **Fog damping.** Every theme scales the shared fade before painting its wash —
   `dimOpacity` (`beveledTile:66-68`, ×0.72), `washOpacity` (`cartographersTable:86-88`, ×0.62),
   `dimOpacity` (`emblemAndDots:66-68`, ×0.7), an inline `Number((view.fogOpacity * 0.8).toFixed(3))`
   (`miniatureWorld:207`), `dimOpacity` (`tacticalHud:64-66`, ×0.8) — and the rule the registry test
   `index.test.tsx:164-222` exists to enforce is that a theme damps **both** faded states by the same
   factor. Nothing structural stops a theme damping one and not the other; ah-rgp's review caught
   exactly that in every theme.

After this bead:

- **One shared road layer, `mapThemes/roadLayer.tsx`.** `roadLayer(style)` builds a `RoadLayer`
  from a `RoadStyle` — the reach and an ordered list of strokes. It owns the width rule (fractions
  of `HEX_RADIUS` through `radii`, never `vector-effect`), the spoke geometry, the badge-off
  short-circuit and the pointer-events group. Each theme keeps a `ROAD_STYLE` of three to seven
  lines and sets `RoadLayer: roadLayer(ROAD_STYLE)`. Same classes, same numbers, same DOM order —
  the one visible-to-tests difference is that every road is now wrapped in a `<g>` (Cartographer's
  Table already was) and the layer's group carries `data-layer="roads"`.
- **One fog-damping rule, applied where the fade is made.** A theme *declares* how much it damps —
  `fogDamping` on its `MapTheme` — and `buildHexViews` applies it to every faded state alike, so
  `view.fogOpacity` arrives already damped and a theme paints it as it is. A theme can no longer
  damp stale and not named, because a theme no longer damps at all. The registry-wide test stops
  checking arithmetic each theme might have got wrong and instead pins that every theme paints the
  fade it was handed, unchanged, for both states.

Rendered output is numerically identical to today (same widths, same reach, same opacities to three
decimals) — this is a refactoring, and the theme suites are the net. `docs/ui/map-themes.md` calls
the split "a theme is only the paint"; this bead makes that truer, not different, and the doc is
updated to say where the two rules now live.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### New: `mapThemes/roadLayer.tsx`

```ts
import type { ComponentType } from "react";
import { HEX_RADIUS } from "../mapViewport";
import { radii } from "./geometry";
import { ROAD_VECTORS } from "./hexView";
import type { LayerProps } from "./mapTheme";

/** One stroke of a road, in the theme's own class. Widths are fractions of the hex radius. */
export type RoadStroke = {
  className: string;
  /** Stroke width as a fraction of `HEX_RADIUS` — `radii(width)` is applied here, never `vector-effect`. */
  width: number;
  /** SVG `stroke-dasharray`, in user units, or absent for a solid line. */
  dash?: string;
  linecap?: "round";
  opacity?: number;
};

/** How a theme draws its roads: how far along the spoke, and which strokes, first underneath. */
export type RoadStyle = {
  /** Where the spoke ends, as a fraction of `HEX_RADIUS` along the bearing (0.87 is the edge midpoint). */
  reach: number;
  strokes: readonly RoadStroke[];
};

/**
 * The road layer every theme draws through. Owns what is not paint: the spoke from the hex centre
 * along `ROAD_VECTORS[direction]`, the width rule (user units, so a road shrinks with its hex — see
 * ah-ebv), the badge-off short-circuit and the pointer-events group. Returns null when no view has
 * a road, exactly as each theme's own layer did.
 */
export function roadLayer(style: RoadStyle): ComponentType<LayerProps>;
```

The component: `if (!views.some((view) => view.roads.length > 0)) return null;` then
`<g pointerEvents="none" data-layer="roads">` containing, for each view and each direction, a
`<g key={`${view.key}-${direction}`}>` holding one `<line>` per stroke in order, with
`x1={view.at.x} y1={view.at.y} x2={view.at.x + bearing.x * HEX_RADIUS * style.reach}
y2={view.at.y + bearing.y * HEX_RADIUS * style.reach}`, `className`, `strokeWidth={radii(stroke.width)}`,
and `strokeDasharray`/`strokeLinecap`/`opacity` only when the stroke sets them (React omits an
`undefined` attribute, so a solid, butt-capped, fully opaque road serialises exactly as it does
today). Give the component a display name (`RoadLayer`) so a React error names it.

### The five themes — `RoadLayer`

Each `index.tsx`: delete the width constant(s) and the `RoadLayer` function; add, at the same
place, `const ROAD_STYLE: RoadStyle = …` and set `RoadLayer: roadLayer(ROAD_STYLE)` in the theme
object (`beveledTile:407`, `cartographersTable:495`, `emblemAndDots:359`, `miniatureWorld:478`,
`tacticalHud:425`). Keep each layer's one-line doc comment as the comment over its style. Import
`{ roadLayer, type RoadStyle } from "../roadLayer"`; drop `HEX_RADIUS` and `radii` from the imports
where nothing else uses them (check — `radii` is used elsewhere in every theme's marks; `HEX_RADIUS`
may not be). The styles, transcribed from today's code:

```ts
// beveledTile — "Roads as pale inlays across the tile's face."
{ reach: 0.83, strokes: [{ className: "bt-road", width: 0.222, linecap: "round", opacity: 0.9 }] }
// cartographersTable — "Roads as the surveyor's convention: a brown casing with a lighter dashed line over it."
{ reach: 0.87, strokes: [
  { className: "ct-road", width: 0.222, linecap: "round" },
  { className: "ct-road-dash", width: 0.078, dash: "3 3" } ] }
// emblemAndDots — "Roads as pale spokes: present, but never competing with the medallion."
{ reach: 0.87, strokes: [{ className: "ed-road", width: 0.189, linecap: "round", opacity: 0.85 }] }
// miniatureWorld — "Roads as tan paths trodden across the board."
{ reach: 0.87, strokes: [{ className: "mw-path", width: 0.278, linecap: "round" }] }
// tacticalHud — "Roads as a thin luminous lattice, dashed so they read as routing rather than as terrain."
{ reach: 0.87, strokes: [{ className: "hud-road", width: 0.111, dash: "5 3" }] }
```

(Beveled Tile's 0.83 is deliberate — its tile is inset from the lattice, `beveledTile.test.tsx:78`
— and stays.)

### Fog: `mapTheme.ts`, `hexView.ts`, `MapCanvas.tsx`, the five themes

`mapTheme.ts` — add to `MapTheme`, after `label`:

```ts
  /**
   * How much of the shared fade this theme lets through, 0 < n <= 1. `buildHexViews` scales
   * `fogOpacity` by it for every faded state alike — a hex known only by name and a stale sighting
   * both — so a theme paints `view.fogOpacity` as it arrives and never damps it itself. Declared
   * here, applied there: the theme owns the number, the shared code owns the rule that both states
   * get the same one (ah-rgp's review found every theme damping one and not the other).
   */
  fogDamping: number;
```

`hexView.ts`:
- `HexViewOptions` (:172-176) gains `fogDamping?: number;` documented "the theme's `MapTheme.fogDamping`;
  1 when absent, so a caller that is not drawing through a theme (tests, tools) gets the shared
  fade whole".
- New export, next to `buildHexView`:
  ```ts
  /** The shared fade scaled by a theme's damping, to three decimals — the one place this arithmetic lives. */
  export function dampFog(fogOpacity: number, damping: number): number {
    return Number((fogOpacity * damping).toFixed(3));
  }
  ```
- `buildHexView` (:307-346): `fogOpacity: dampFog(paint.fogOpacity, options.fogDamping ?? 1)`.
  Rounding at damping 1 changes nothing: every value `hexPaint` produces (`0`, `0.4`,
  `0.30 + 0.02n` capped at `0.62`, `mapHexView.ts:73-78,117`) already has three decimals or fewer.
- The `HexView.fogOpacity` doc (:84) → "How far this hex has faded, already scaled by the theme's
  `fogDamping`: paint it as it arrives, for a named hex and a stale one alike."

`MapCanvas.tsx` (`packages/shared/src/workspace/MapCanvas.tsx:254-258`): `viewOptions` becomes
`{ showStaleness, showTextures, badges, fogDamping: theme.fogDamping }` with `theme.fogDamping`
added to the memo's dependency list. Nothing else in the file changes.

The five themes: delete the damping function and paint `view.fogOpacity` directly —
- `beveledTile/index.tsx`: delete `dimOpacity` :59-68 (keep the comment's substance in one sentence
  over the wash: "Damped by `fogDamping` before it arrives, whichever state it is in"), :164
  `opacity={dimOpacity(view)}` → `opacity={view.fogOpacity}`. Add `fogDamping: 0.72` to the theme
  object.
- `cartographersTable/index.tsx`: delete `washOpacity` :86-88 and trim its comment :71-85 to the
  two sentences that are still true (the wash only tints; unsurveyed ground is the lightest thing on
  the sheet and the rim names the state); :135 and :158 → `opacity={view.fogOpacity}`.
  `fogDamping: 0.62`.
- `emblemAndDots/index.tsx`: delete `dimOpacity` :57-68 (same treatment of the comment); :138 →
  `opacity={view.fogOpacity}`. `fogDamping: 0.7`.
- `miniatureWorld/index.tsx`: :207 → `opacity={view.fogOpacity}`, comment :203-206 shortened to
  say the wash sits over the primer and arrives damped. `fogDamping: 0.8`.
- `tacticalHud/index.tsx`: delete `dimOpacity` :55-66 (its comment's first sentence — proportional
  to the fade rather than fixed — stays over the wash); :142 → `opacity={view.fogOpacity}`; comment
  :138-141 shortened. `fogDamping: 0.8`.
- Any `HexView` import that was only there for the deleted function's signature goes with it
  (`beveledTile`, `emblemAndDots` type their `dimOpacity(view: HexView)`; check whether `HexView` is
  still used elsewhere in the file before removing the import).

### Tests

**New `mapThemes/roadLayer.test.tsx`** — renders `roadLayer(style)` over `buildHexViews([CONGESTED_CENTRE], …)`
(two roads on the centre hex; helpers as `beveledTile.test.tsx:23-35`):
- `draws one spoke per road, from the centre to reach along the bearing` — one `<g>` per road, `x2`
  equals `at.x + ROAD_VECTORS[direction].x * HEX_RADIUS * reach` to 2 decimals.
- `draws every stroke of a road in order, first underneath` — a two-stroke style yields two `<line>`
  per road, first with the first class.
- `gives a stroke its width in hex units, never a screen-pixel effect` — `stroke-width` equals
  `radii(width)`, `vector-effect` absent.
- `writes dash, linecap and opacity only when the style sets them` — a bare stroke serialises with
  none of the three attributes; a full one with all three.
- `draws nothing when the roads badge is off` (`allBadges(true, { roads: false })`).
- `keeps pointer events off the roads, and names its layer` — the outer `<g>` has
  `pointer-events="none"` and `data-layer="roads"`.

**`index.test.tsx`** — extend `describe("every shipped theme")` (:127-152):
- `%s draws its roads through the shared road layer` — `theme.RoadLayer` over
  `buildHexViews([CONGESTED_CENTRE], all-on)` contains `data-layer="roads"`, contains no
  `vector-effect`, and every `stroke-width` parses to a number below `HEX_RADIUS`. (RED until each
  theme is switched; the marker is what tells a shared layer from a hand-rolled one.)
- `%s declares a fog damping in (0, 1]`.

Rewrite `describe("what every theme owes the three knowledge states")` (:164-222). Keep
`opacitiesOf` and `render`; replace the one test with:
- `%s paints the fade it is handed, unchanged, for named and stale alike` — render the named view
  with `fogOpacity: 0.5` and the stale view with `fogOpacity: 0.5`; the first `unsurveyed|unpainted`
  opacity and the first `stale` opacity are both `toBeCloseTo(0.5, 3)`. This is what makes a private
  damping impossible to reintroduce unnoticed.
- `%s keeps unsurveyed ground comfortably lighter than the oldest sighting` —
  `dampFog(FADE_LIMIT, theme.fogDamping) - dampFog(NAMED_FOG_OPACITY, theme.fogDamping)` is
  `toBeGreaterThan(0.05)`; and the rim assertions exactly as today (`named` contains
  `data-rim="unsurveyed"`, `ancient` does not) on views built with those two damped values.
- Update the describe's doc comment (:154-163) to say what changed: the fade is damped once, in
  `buildHexViews`, so the registry test's job is now to see that no theme damps again.
- The `dummy` theme (:28-40) gets `fogDamping: 1`.

**`hexView.test.ts`** — in `describe("what a hex shows, prepared for whichever theme draws it")` (:103):
- `scales the fade by the theme's damping, named and stale alike` — `buildHexView` of a stale hex
  (age 8 → 0.46) and of a named hex with `fogDamping: 0.5` gives `0.23` and `0.2`; with the option
  absent gives `0.46` and `0.4`; a current hex stays `0` either way.
- `dampFog rounds to three decimals` — `dampFog(0.62, 0.62)` is `0.384`.

**`packages/shared/src/workspace/MapCanvas.test.tsx`** — `probe()` (:18-33) gets `fogDamping: 0.5`
and its `TerrainLayer` also stamps `data-fog={props.views[0]?.fogOpacity ?? "none"}`; new test in
`describe("what the map hands a theme")` (:130): `hands a theme the fade already damped by its own
factor` — the stale bucket's mark reads `data-fog="0.23"` (CONGESTED_HEXES' one stale hex is eight
turns old, `congestedFixture.ts:172-178`: `0.46 × 0.5`).

**Theme suites** — three tests asserted a theme's own arithmetic and now assert the shared rule's
result instead; everything else in the five files passes untouched (checked: the road tests count
`<line ` and read `stroke-width`, both unchanged; the "≤ 0.5" and "deepens with age" fog tests are
relative or built through `draw`, which at damping 1 gives the raw 0.4):
- `cartographersTable.test.tsx:335-347` (`keeps the terrain readable under an old sighting`): build
  `ancient` as `viewWith({ knowledge: "stale", fogOpacity: dampFog(FADE_LIMIT, cartographersTable.fogDamping), hatched: true })`
  and `recent` with `dampFog(0.3, cartographersTable.fogDamping)`; assertions unchanged (`≤ 0.45`,
  recent < ancient). Import `dampFog` from `../hexView` and `FADE_LIMIT` from `../../mapHexView`.
- `miniatureWorld.test.tsx:292-306` (`washes a named hex proportionally…`): replace
  `expect(washOf(0.75)).toBeCloseTo(0.6)` with `expect(miniatureWorld.fogDamping).toBe(0.8)`; keep
  the relative assertion. Retitle "declares its damping, and paints the fade it is handed".
- `tacticalHud.test.tsx:322-334` (`dims a named hex proportionally…`): the same — the
  `toBeCloseTo(0.6)` becomes `expect(tacticalHud.fogDamping).toBe(0.8)`, relative assertion kept.
- Update the two describe doc comments above them (:284-291, :314-319) — the damping is declared,
  not performed, by the theme.

### Docs

- `docs/ui/map-themes.md`: the "Roads are the theme's because…" paragraph (:23-27) → roads are still
  the theme's, drawn through `roadLayer(style)` from `mapThemes/roadLayer.tsx`, which applies the
  width rule (`radii`, never `vector-effect`) for every theme; a `RoadStyle` is reach plus strokes.
  The two damping paragraphs (:84-97, "The same reasoning is why a theme damps…" through "…none of
  them could see this.") → a theme declares `fogDamping` on its `MapTheme`; `buildHexViews` applies
  it to every faded state alike, so `view.fogOpacity` arrives damped and is painted as-is; the
  registry test now checks that no theme damps again. Keep the history (Cartographer's Table at
  0.400 against 0.384) as the reason. The contract block (:112-124) gains `fogDamping: number;`
  with a one-line comment, and `RoadLayer`'s comment says "usually `roadLayer(style)`". Step 1 of
  "Adding a theme" lists `ROAD_STYLE` and `fogDamping` among what `index.tsx` holds.
- `docs/ui/hex-rendering.md:108-110` ("Each theme damps them by its own factor before painting")
  → "Each theme declares a damping factor and `buildHexViews` applies it before any theme paints".
  :124-131 (Roads): add that the spoke is drawn by the shared `roadLayer` and that Beveled Tile's
  reach is 0.83R because its tile is inset.

## Increments

Branch `ah-txl-shared-road-layer-and-fog-rule` from `origin/main`, in a worktree under
`.cerebro/worktrees/ah-txl`. Unit suite: `pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared test` runs `vitest run` in
`packages/shared` (`packages/shared/package.json:21`); `pnpm run check:fast` at the root runs it with
lint, typecheck and the Rust gates.

1. **The shared road layer.** RED: `roadLayer.test.tsx` (module missing). GREEN: `roadLayer.tsx`.
   Commit.
2. **Themes draw through it.** RED: `%s draws its roads through the shared road layer` in
   `index.test.tsx` fails for all five (no `data-layer="roads"`). GREEN: the five `ROAD_STYLE`s and
   `RoadLayer: roadLayer(ROAD_STYLE)`; every existing road test in the five theme suites still
   green. Commit.
3. **The fade is damped once.** RED: the `hexView.test.ts` pair (`fogDamping` unknown / `dampFog`
   missing), then the MapCanvas test (`data-fog` reads `0.46`), then `%s declares a fog damping` and
   `%s paints the fade it is handed, unchanged` in `index.test.tsx` (themes still damp: 0.5 comes out
   as 0.36/0.31/0.35/0.4/0.4). GREEN in that order: `hexView.ts`, `MapCanvas.tsx` + `probe`,
   `mapTheme.ts` + `fogDamping` on the five themes and `dummy`, then remove the five private
   dampings — at which point the three theme tests named above go RED and are rewritten as
   specified. `pnpm run check:fast` (typecheck will name any `MapTheme` literal missing
   `fogDamping`). Commit.
4. **Docs.** The two `docs/ui/*.md` edits and the shortened comments in the five themes. Commit.
5. PR, `@copilot`, CI, squash — the ordinary `implement-bead` flow.

## The test plan

- New: `mapThemes/roadLayer.test.tsx` (six tests above); `index.test.tsx` two new registry-wide
  tests plus the rewritten knowledge-states pair; `hexView.test.ts` two; `MapCanvas.test.tsx` one.
- Changed: `cartographersTable.test.tsx`, `miniatureWorld.test.tsx`, `tacticalHud.test.tsx` — one
  test each, as specified.
- Unchanged and still green: everything else in the five theme suites, `mapHexView.test.ts`,
  `theme.test.ts` (no hex literals arrive — `roadLayer.tsx` has no colours).
- Suites to run: `pnpm run check:fast`. The browser suites are CI's; nothing here changes what
  they see.

## User-facing decisions

None — no pixel changes. Numerically identical widths, reach, dashes, opacities; every class name
kept so every `theme.css` rule still lands. (Verified in planning by reading all five layers and the
five damping sites; the registry tests in increment 3 are what prove it at build time.)

## Out of scope

- **The unsurveyed rim.** Bishop lists it with the two rules above, but the five rims are genuinely
  different paint (a separate polygon in Cartographer's Table and Miniature World, a dash on the
  tile's own outline in Emblem & Dots and Tactical HUD, one of two rims in Beveled Tile), and the
  rule — a named hex carries `data-rim="unsurveyed"` and a stale one does not — is already pinned
  registry-wide. Nothing to lift without inventing a shape.
- Changing any theme's chosen width, reach, dash, opacity or damping factor.
- Moving `RoadLayer` off the `MapTheme` contract (a theme may still hand-roll one; the registry
  test would then fail on the marker, which is the point).
- `hexView.ts`'s other fields, the badge toggles, `MapCanvas` beyond the one option.
- The other nine `Refactoring:` beads.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run check:fast
grep -rn "vector-effect\|vectorEffect" packages/shared/src/workspace/mapThemes/   # nothing outside tests
grep -rn "toFixed(3)" packages/shared/src/workspace/mapThemes/*/index.tsx          # nothing: the fade arithmetic left the themes
grep -n "fogDamping" packages/shared/src/workspace/mapThemes/*/index.tsx           # exactly five hits, one per theme
grep -c "function RoadLayer" packages/shared/src/workspace/mapThemes/*/index.tsx   # 0 for every theme
```

By hand (Psylocke may treat this as not player-visible; if she looks): switch through the five
themes on a report with roads and stale hexes — roads, dashes and the faded washes look as they did.

## Known traps

- **`theme.test.ts` fails the build on a hex colour literal in `.ts`/`.tsx`** — `roadLayer.tsx`
  must carry classes only, no `stroke=`; colours stay in each `theme.css`.
- **`renderToStaticMarkup` writes attributes in JSX order and omits `undefined` ones.** The theme
  road tests read `/stroke-width="([\d.]+)"/` from the first match, and Cartographer's by class
  (`widthOf("ct-road")`, `:226-246`) — keep `strokeWidth` on the `<line>`, not on the wrapping `<g>`.
- **`opacity`, `strokeDasharray`, `strokeLinecap` must be absent, not `undefined`-valued, when the
  style does not set them** — React handles `undefined` by omitting; do not pass `null` or `""`.
- **`toFixed(3)` then `Number(...)`** is the exact rounding every theme used; keep it in `dampFog`
  so the registry gap numbers stay what they were (0.384 for Cartographer's ancient wash).
- **`fogDamping` optional on `HexViewOptions`, required on `MapTheme`.** Making the option
  required would touch every `buildHexViews` call in five test files for no gain; making the theme
  field optional would let a new theme forget it and ship undamped. Typecheck finds every
  `MapTheme` literal (`probe`, `dummy`, the five themes).
- **`MapCanvas`'s `viewOptions` memo** — add `theme.fogDamping` to its dependency array, or a theme
  switch keeps the previous theme's damping until something else changes.
- **Beveled Tile's reach is 0.83, not 0.87** — its road tests do not pin the length, but its inset
  tile does (`beveledTile.test.tsx:78`); a helpful "normalisation" to 0.87 would draw roads over the
  seam.
- **Never branch in the main checkout**; worktree under `.cerebro/worktrees/`, `pnpm install` there
  as `implement-bead` says.

title: Refactoring: the orders editor is never handed its own text back
description:
## The cost being paid
The unit editor is a controlled value that round-trips through the faction document, and the round trip is lossy and asynchronous (a block cannot hold a trailing blank line, so read(write(doc,u,text)) !== text; the value prop lags the edits). Three compensating pure functions plus an echo queue exist to make the editor ignore its own text coming back, and the same "editor mishandles its own text handed back" defect was fixed three times in three days — once visible only as a CI flake. All the compensators are still live.

## Evidence
- 9420c54 fix(#37): make the orders panel usable (#40) — "a newline typed at the end of a block was swallowed … pressing Enter was undone by the answer coming back"; added draftAfterDocumentChange and the trailing-blank drop in writeUnitOrders
- 949c6a6 feat(orders): end a saved unit draft with a trailing newline — added draftAfterSave with caret bookkeeping
- 279bffd feat(#89) sub-commits "fix(#89): the editor never applies echoes of its own text, however stale" (echo queue; "visible only as a CI flake, because only CI machines were slow enough") and "fix(#89): a late restore no longer wipes orders typed after an import"; minimalChange replaced the caret bookkeeping
- Today: draftAfterDocumentChange, draftAfterSave, minimalChange each used from OrdersPanel.tsx/OrdersEditor.tsx (5 + 2 references)

## Where
packages/shared/src/ordersDocument.ts (writeUnitOrders :112, withoutTrailingBlankLines); packages/shared/src/orderEditor.ts:76–104; packages/shared/src/editorReconcile.ts; packages/shared/src/workspace/OrdersPanel.tsx:101–121; packages/shared/src/workspace/OrdersEditor.tsx (pendingEchoes)

## What a refactoring would change
Make the editor the owner of its unit's text while it is focused — the document is written from the editor, never read back into it until the unit changes — or make the round trip lossless (blocks keep trailing blank lines) so the compensators can go.

Filed by Bishop, weekly sweep of 2026-08-15 (first sweep, whole of origin/main), range e60bbbd..150ba17.
design:
## Context

The orders editor is a controlled value that round-trips through the faction document, and the
round trip is lossy and asynchronous. Every keystroke goes `OrdersEditor.onChange` →
`OrdersPanel.setDraft` + `onChange(unitId, text)` → `AppShell.onOrdersChange` →
`writeUnitOrders` (which drops trailing blank lines, `ordersDocument.ts:101-118`) →
`setOrdersDocument` → re-render → `OrdersPanel` reads the block back → an effect hands it to
`draft` → `value` prop → `OrdersEditor` decides whether to apply it. Three compensating pieces
exist so the editor ignores its own text coming back:

- `draftAfterDocumentChange` (`orderEditor.ts:76-92`) — keeps the draft when the document agrees
  with it "about everything a block can express" (the trailing blank line typed by Enter);
- `pendingEchoes` (`OrdersEditor.tsx:77-84,129-133,208-209,223-232,242-244`) — a bounded queue of
  every text the editor emitted and has not heard back, because `value` lags the editor by however
  many commits React is behind, and splicing a lagging echo in rewound the editor (a CI-only flake,
  #89);
- `minimalChange` (`editorReconcile.ts`) — the smallest splice, so an external text keeps the
  caret (this one stays: it is the right tool for a genuine external update, and the after-save
  tidy relies on it).

Plus the panel's `draft`/`draftUnit` state and its two effects (`OrdersPanel.tsx:87-121`), and
`draftAfterSave` (`orderEditor.ts:94-105`), the tidy that ends a saved draft with a newline.

The same defect — the editor mishandles its own text handed back — was fixed three times in three
days (9420c54, 949c6a6, 279bffd). All the compensators are live. All line numbers are against
`main` at `837f0b7`; paths under `packages/shared/src/` unless said otherwise.

**After this bead the editor is never handed its own text back.** While a unit is on screen the
editor owns that unit's text: it writes the document (through the panel and `AppShell`, exactly as
now) and reads nothing back from it. What it *is* told about is a write that did not come from it —
an import, a restore, a game switch, a report load, a route from the planner — and it hears of that
through one number, `externalRevision`, which `AppShell` bumps on every non-editor write and never
on an editor write. When that number changes the editor takes the block from the document (as a
minimal splice, caret preserved); when it does not, the block is not looked at. `draftAfterDocumentChange`
goes, `pendingEchoes` goes, the panel's draft state and both effects go. `writeUnitOrders` still
drops trailing blank lines — that is a document rule (the block boundary cannot hold them,
`findUnitBlocks` :48-79 winds back over blanks), and nothing reads them back into the editor any
more, so no compensator is needed for it. The save tidy stays as behaviour (the navigator asked for
it, 949c6a6, and `tests/smoke/persistence.spec.ts:216-253` (`a saved draft gains its missing trailing newline without moving the cursor`) pins it with the caret staying put) but
becomes an editor-side transaction on a `savedAt` prop rather than a second controlled write.

Behaviour is preserved end to end; the smoke suite is the net (`tests/smoke/orders-editor.spec.ts`,
`persistence.spec.ts:195-330`, `workspace.spec.ts:301-334,836-878,1861-1900`). There is no jsdom in
this repository (`BadgeMenu.test.tsx:9-11`), so the React changes are gated by those specs and by
`check:fast`; the one pure function that goes takes its unit tests with it.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `orderEditor.ts`

- Delete `draftAfterDocumentChange` (:76-92) and the `withoutTrailingBlankLines` import (:2) if
  nothing else in the file uses it (nothing does today — `findUnitBlocks` stays imported for
  `diagnosticsForUnit`).
- Keep `draftAfterSave` (:94-105) unchanged; it is now called by `OrdersEditor`.
- Add, next to it, the vocabulary the shell and the panel share:

```ts
/**
 * Who wrote the orders document.
 *
 * The editor owns the selected unit's text while it is on screen: it writes the document and is
 * never handed its own text back - a round trip through React lags the editor by however many
 * commits it is behind, and applying a lagging copy rewound the text under the player (#89). What
 * the editor must be handed is a write from anywhere else - an import, a restore, a route from the
 * planner - and `AppShell` counts those in `externalRevision`, which is the one signal the editor
 * reloads on. An editor write leaves that number alone.
 */
export type OrdersOrigin = "editor" | "external";
```

### `workspace/AppShell.tsx`

- Next to `const [ordersDocument, setOrdersDocument] = useState("")` (:252):
  ```ts
  /** How many writes to the document did not come from the editor. See `OrdersOrigin`. */
  const [externalOrdersRevision, setExternalOrdersRevision] = useState(0);
  ```
  and, after them, the only place the document is written from now on:
  ```ts
  /**
   * Every write to the orders document says who made it. An external write also moves
   * `externalOrdersRevision`, which is what tells the editor to take the block again; the editor's
   * own writes do not, so it is never handed its own text back.
   */
  const writeOrdersDocument = useCallback(
    (origin: OrdersOrigin, update: string | ((document: string) => string)) => {
      setOrdersDocument(update);
      if (origin === "external") {
        setExternalOrdersRevision((revision) => revision + 1);
      }
    },
    []
  );
  ```
  React 19 batches the two state updates in every context (event handler, `await` continuation,
  timer), so a render always sees the new document and the new revision together.
- Replace every other `setOrdersDocument(` in the file with `writeOrdersDocument(<origin>, …)` —
  six sites, and after the change the raw setter appears exactly once, inside the wrapper:
  - :834 `setOrdersDocument(loaded.orders)` (report load) → `"external"`;
  - :1304 `setOrdersDocument(restored.orders)` (restore) → `"external"`;
  - :1373 `setOrdersDocument("")` (game switch) → `"external"`;
  - :1789-1793 `onOrdersChange` → `writeOrdersDocument("editor", (document) => { const next = writeUnitOrders(document, unitId, orders); writer.markDirty(game, draftKey, next); return next; })`;
  - :1833 `setOrdersDocument(pending.text)` (import) → `"external"`;
  - :1877-1885 `applyRoute` → `writeOrdersDocument("external", (document) => { … })` with the same body.
  `useCallback` dependency arrays that listed nothing for the setter need `writeOrdersDocument`
  added where the callback is memoised (`onOrdersChange` :1786-1795, `applyRoute` :1875-1887,
  `replaceOrdersImport` :1807 and its dependency list ending around :1858) — the lint rule will name each.
- `<OrdersPanel …>` (:2675-2686): add `externalRevision={externalOrdersRevision}`.
- Import `OrdersOrigin` through the existing `from "../orderEditor"` import (:69).

### `workspace/OrdersPanel.tsx`

- Props: add `externalRevision: number;` documented "moves when the document was written by
  something other than the editor — see `OrdersOrigin`; the editor reloads its block on it and on
  nothing else".
- Delete `draft`, `draftUnit`, the synchronous unit-switch block and both effects (:87-121), and the
  imports of `draftAfterDocumentChange`, `draftAfterSave`, `useEffect`, `useState` (keep `useMemo`).
  Keep `block`, `lock`, everything from :123 down.
- The editor call becomes:
  ```tsx
  <OrdersEditor
    ref={editorRef}
    unitId={unit?.unitId ?? ""}
    text={block ?? ""}
    externalRevision={externalRevision}
    savedAt={save.kind === "saved" ? save.at : null}
    ariaLabel={`Orders for unit ${unit?.unitId ?? ""}`}
    problems={problems}
    commands={commands}
    snippets={snippets}
    onChange={(text) => {
      if (unit) {
        onChange(unit.unitId, text);
      }
    }}
  />
  ```
  Update the header comment of the file/props to say the panel no longer holds a draft: the
  document is what it shows, and the editor is what edits it.

### `workspace/OrdersEditor.tsx`

Props (:27-39): replace `value: string` with

```ts
  /**
   * The unit's block as the document holds it. Read when the editor is created for a unit and
   * again whenever `externalRevision` moves; ignored otherwise - between those moments the
   * editor's own text is the truth and the document is a step behind it.
   */
  text: string;
  /** Moves when something other than this editor wrote the document. See `OrdersOrigin`. */
  externalRevision: number;
  /**
   * When the document last landed on disk, or null. A landed save ends the shown text with the
   * newline an orders file ends with (`draftAfterSave`) - in the editor only, never written back.
   */
  savedAt: string | null;
```

Body:
- Delete `pendingEchoes` (:77-84), the push/bound in the update listener (:129-133), the reset
  (:208-209), and the whole echo branch of the value effect (:223-232, :242-244).
- `latest` (:87-88) carries `text` instead of `value`; `EditorState.create({ doc: latest.current.text, … })`.
- The external effect replaces :216-246:
  ```ts
  // A write from outside - an import, a restore, a route from the planner - and only that: the
  // editor's own writes never come back through here (see OrdersOrigin), so there is no echo to
  // tell from a real change and nothing to rewind. Applied as the smallest splice so the caret
  // stays where the player put it; kept out of the undo history because the player did not do it.
  useEffect(() => {
    const editor = view.current;
    if (!editor) {
      return;
    }
    const change = minimalChange(editor.state.doc.toString(), latest.current.text);
    if (change) {
      editor.dispatch({
        changes: change,
        annotations: [External.of(true), Transaction.addToHistory.of(false)]
      });
    }
  }, [externalRevision, unitId]);
  ```
  `text` is deliberately **not** a dependency and is read through `latest` — with it in the list
  the effect would run on every keystroke and splice the block (which cannot hold the trailing
  blank line just typed) back in, which is the original Enter bug. On mount and on a unit switch
  the splice is null (the editor was just created from the same text). On the same commit as an
  external write, `latest.current.text` is the fresh block because `AppShell` sets both states
  together.
- The save tidy, a new effect after the one above:
  ```ts
  // Once a save has landed - and when a saved unit is browsed to - the shown text ends with the
  // newline an orders file ends with. In the editor only: the block boundary neither holds nor
  // needs it, so the document is not written (External, and not history either). An append at the
  // end never moves a caret that is anywhere else - what persistence.spec pins.
  useEffect(() => {
    const editor = view.current;
    if (!editor || savedAt === null) {
      return;
    }
    const current = editor.state.doc.toString();
    const tidy = draftAfterSave(current);
    if (tidy !== current) {
      editor.dispatch({
        changes: { from: current.length, to: current.length, insert: "\n" },
        annotations: [External.of(true), Transaction.addToHistory.of(false)]
      });
    }
  }, [savedAt, unitId]);
  ```
  Import `draftAfterSave` from `"../orderEditor"`. `unitId` is in the list so a saved unit browsed
  to is tidied too, as the panel's `[save, draft]` effect did (`OrdersPanel.tsx:108-121`).
- The header comment (:59-70) is rewritten: the document flows in as `text` and is read at
  creation and on `externalRevision`; edits flow out through `onChange`; the editor is never handed
  its own text back, so there is no reconciliation of echoes — only a genuine external update, as a
  minimal splice.

### Tests

- `orderEditor.test.ts`: delete the `draftAfterDocumentChange` block (:93-131, comment included)
  and its import (:9). `draftAfterSave`'s tests (:133-143) stay.
- `editorReconcile.test.ts`, `ordersDocument.test.ts`: unchanged.
- No new unit test — there is nothing pure left to pin that is not already pinned; the contract
  lives in the smoke specs named under *The test plan*.

## Increments

Branch `ah-vfr-editor-owns-its-text` from `origin/main`, worktree under `.cerebro/worktrees/ah-vfr`.
This is a refactoring under an existing net, so each increment names the tests that must stay
green rather than a new failing one; run them, do not assume them.

1. **The origin.** `OrdersOrigin` in `orderEditor.ts`; `externalOrdersRevision` and
   `writeOrdersDocument` in `AppShell`; the six call sites; the prop passed to `OrdersPanel` (which
   accepts and ignores it for now). Gate: `pnpm run check:fast`. No behaviour changes.
2. **The editor owns its text.** `OrdersEditor` props and effects as above; `OrdersPanel` loses its
   draft state and forwards `text`/`externalRevision`/`savedAt`. Gate: `check:fast`, then the four
   smoke specs locally, web project only:
   `SMOKE_PROJECT=web pnpm exec playwright test --project=web tests/smoke/orders-editor.spec.ts tests/smoke/persistence.spec.ts tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts`
   (see traps for the server reuse and the `--` rule). Every test in them green — in particular
   `a new line can be opened at the end of a unit's orders`, `a planned route can be written into
   the unit's orders`, `an orders file imports through the confirm prompt`, `typing can be undone
   and redone`, `undo cannot resurrect another unit's orders`, and persistence's save-tidy-with-caret
   test (`:216-253`) and `a slow ruleset fetch cannot wipe orders typed after an import` (`:265`).
3. **The compensator goes.** Delete `draftAfterDocumentChange` and its tests. `check:fast`. Commit.
4. PR, `@copilot`, CI (all shells — the desktop and native jobs run the same specs), squash.

## The test plan

- Unit: `orderEditor.test.ts` minus the deleted block; the rest of `packages/shared` unchanged and
  green; lint (`eslint --max-warnings=0`) clean, which is what enforces the dependency arrays.
- Browser (CI's, and run locally by choice in increment 2): `tests/smoke/orders-editor.spec.ts`
  (all), `tests/smoke/persistence.spec.ts` (all; the tidy-and-caret and late-restore tests are the
  ones this bead can break), `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts` (`301-334` import, `861-878` Enter at
  end, `1861-1900` route insertion, `836-859` selection fills the editor).
- The full `pnpm run check` by choice before the PR: this is exactly the "you suspect a smoke
  regression" case `implement-bead` reserves it for.

## User-facing decisions

None. Every observable behaviour is kept: Enter opens a line at the end; a saved draft ends with a
newline and the caret stays; a planned route, an import, a restore reach the editor; undo is
per-unit. One corner is knowingly different and accepted by the planner: an external write whose
block equals the editor's text *except* for a trailing blank line the player has opened (an import
of the identical document while a line stands open) now closes that line, where
`draftAfterDocumentChange` used to keep it. Nothing the player does reaches that corner on purpose.

## Out of scope

- Making the round trip lossless (blocks keeping trailing blank lines) — Bishop's other option. It
  changes `findUnitBlocks`'s projection, and with the editor no longer reading the document back it
  buys nothing.
- `minimalChange` and `draftAfterSave` — kept, both still doing a real job.
- The autosave, the writer, validation, diagnostics, completion, snippets, the shortcut layer.
- Adding jsdom to test the components.
- The other `Refactoring:` beads.

## Validation

```bash
pnpm run check:fast
grep -n "setOrdersDocument(" packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx        # exactly one hit, inside writeOrdersDocument
grep -rn "draftAfterDocumentChange\|pendingEchoes" packages/shared/src         # nothing
grep -n "useState\|useEffect" packages/shared/src/workspace/OrdersPanel.tsx    # neither imported
SMOKE_PROJECT=web pnpm exec playwright test --project=web tests/smoke/orders-editor.spec.ts tests/smoke/persistence.spec.ts tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts
```

By hand, if wanted: type at the end of a unit's orders, press Enter, type — the line opens; wait
for "saved" — the text gains a trailing empty line and the caret does not move; arm the planner and
apply a route — it appears in the editor; import an orders file — the editor shows the imported
block; switch units and back — the text is that unit's.

## Known traps

- **`text` must not be a dependency of the external effect.** With it, every keystroke splices the
  block back in and Enter stops working — the bug of 9420c54, reintroduced. Read it through
  `latest.current`; the ESLint hooks rule does not object to a ref read.
- **Both AppShell states move in one call.** `writeOrdersDocument` is the only writer; a stray
  `setOrdersDocument` for an external write leaves the editor showing stale text with no error
  anywhere. The validation grep is the guard.
- **The tidy dispatch is `External` and `addToHistory: false`**, like every non-player change:
  otherwise it echoes into `onChange` (a document write on save, which the smoke test's "untouched
  until the save lands" comment is about) and Ctrl+Z can undo a newline the player never typed.
- **`unitId` stays in the tidy effect's dependencies** — dropping it loses "a saved draft the moment
  it is browsed to" (`OrdersPanel.tsx:108-121` today).
- **The layout effect creates the editor before either passive effect runs**, so on a unit switch
  the external effect finds a fresh editor holding `text` and splices nothing; keep the creation in
  `useLayoutEffect` (as now) and the two reloads in `useEffect`.
- **Local smoke run**: without `CI=1` Playwright reuses a running preview server, including a
  stale one — kill any leftover `vite preview` first (`implement-bead`, "A leftover preview
  server"). Do not write `pnpm run test:smoke -- --project=web` (the `--` becomes a positional
  filter that matches nothing); the direct `pnpm exec playwright test --project=web …` above is the
  form.
- **A "flake" in `persistence.spec.ts` after this change is not a flake until reproduced** — the
  editor tests were the ones only slow CI machines caught before; a red there is the first thing to
  read, not re-run.
- **Never branch in the main checkout**; worktree under `.cerebro/worktrees/`, `pnpm install` there.

title: Header messages get their own tone and stop posing as import warnings
description:
## The cost being paid
ImportStatus — a per-import record {regionCount, unitCount, message, failed, warning} — is the shell's only way to put a line in front of the player, and AppHeader hangs two hidden rules on it (a message is visible only when failed || warning; failed also hides the turn-messages chip). So every unrelated message must claim to be an import warning to be seen: 18 setStatus sites in AppShell, 15 of them with regionCount: 0, unitCount: 0. Two beads in two days paid for it — one message shipped invisible (zero width) until review, and a comparison-load failure had to be encoded as a warning with a comment explaining why it must not be "failed".

## Evidence
- ba79edb fix(ah-kc7), second commit: the "stored for history" message "was in the DOM but had zero width, invisible to a real player" because warning: false; "Fixed by following applyReport's own established idiom: a message here is always a warning, which is what earns the line its room back"
- 9cb908b fix(ah-6l2): "puts a warning on the status line (not `failed`, which is the working turn's own load-failure state and would otherwise hide its messages chip - see the new comment on the callback)"; the comment at AppShell.tsx:2394–2399
- AppShell.tsx :973, :1049–1051 comments; AppHeader.tsx :5–16 (ImportStatus), :384–395 (visibility rule), :417 (chip gate)

## Where
packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx (setStatus sites); packages/shared/src/workspace/AppHeader.tsx

## What a refactoring would change
A status-line message type of its own (text, severity, optional counts) separate from the import result, with the header's visibility decided by severity rather than by an import flag, so a non-import message needs no lie and the messages chip is not hidden by a state that describes another turn.

Filed by Bishop, weekly sweep of 2026-08-15 (first sweep, whole of origin/main), range e60bbbd..150ba17.
design: ## Context The header's status line is typed as `ImportStatus` (`packages/shared/src/workspace/AppHeader.tsx:6-16`): the counts of the last import plus two flags, `failed` and `warning`. It is the shell's only way to put a line of text in front of the player, and `AppHeader` hangs two hidden rules on it — the line takes visible room only when `failed || warning` (`AppHeader.tsx:382-388`, otherwise `sr-only`), and `failed` also withholds the turn-messages chip (`AppHeader.tsx:417`). So every message that is not an import has had to pose as one: 18 `setStatus` sites in `AppShell.tsx`, 15 of them with `regionCount: 0, unitCount: 0`. Two beads paid for it inside two days — ah-kc7's "stored for history" line shipped at zero width until review because `warning` was false, and ah-6l2 had to encode a comparison-load failure as a *warning* so it would not hide the messages chip — and two more messages ship invisible today without anyone having noticed: "orders imported: N units" (`AppShell.tsx:1878-1884`, which ah-470's plan meant to be seen) and the merge line "merged 3 regions from Borg (73), turn 71 — 2 new to your map" (`AppShell.tsx:1021-1027`, unless the merge also produced a warning). Filed by Bishop (weekly sweep 2026-08-15). This plan replaces `ImportStatus` with a status line that carries a **tone**, and lets the header decide visibility and colour from the tone alone. The navigator chose what changes for the player (see *User-facing decisions*): notices become visible with a dim grey dot, the comparison failures become honest failures, "stored for history" drops from amber to a notice, and a failure no longer hides the turn-messages chip. Everything else the player sees — the line's position, its wrapping, `sr-only` for the routine counts, "no report loaded", a message persisting until the next replaces it — is unchanged. ## Files to change, and what to reuse All in `packages/shared`. No core, no `core-client`, no shell-specific code: the status line is a shared-workspace concern and both shells render `AppHeader`. ### `packages/shared/src/workspace/shellStatus.ts` — the type moves here, and grows a tone Today it holds `failedStatus` / `warningStatus` and imports `ImportStatus` from `AppHeader`. It becomes the owner of the type. Replace the whole file with this surface (keep the file name — 3 importers, 1 test, and the name is still right): ```ts /** * A line the header says to the player, and how loudly. * * `routine` is written for screen readers and the suites and takes no visible room - the counts of * a loaded turn, "restored turn 71". `notice` is worth a glance and nothing went wrong. `warning` is * a turn that is fine but something around it was not. `failure` is something that did not happen. * The header decides visibility and colour from the tone and from nothing else - see AppHeader. */ export type StatusTone = "routine" | "notice" | "warning" | "failure"; export type StatusLine = { text: string; tone: StatusTone; }; export function routineStatus(text: string): StatusLine; // { text, tone: "routine" } export function noticeStatus(text: string): StatusLine; // { text, tone: "notice" } export function warningStatus(text: string): StatusLine; // { text, tone: "warning" } export function failedStatus(text: string): StatusLine; // { text, tone: "failure" } /** The routine line for a loaded turn: "11 regions · 42 units", singular when 1. */ export function countsStatus(regionCount: number, unitCount: number): StatusLine; ``` `countsStatus` produces exactly the string `AppHeader.tsx:401` builds today: `` `${regionCount} region${regionCount === 1 ? "" : "s"} · ${unitCount} unit${unitCount === 1 ? "" : "s"}` `` — the smoke suite reads "11 regions", "1 region ·", "units" from it (`tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts:107,115,1578`, `desktop-shell.spec.ts:79`), so the separator is ` · ` (space, U+00B7, space), unchanged. Delete `ImportStatus` from `AppHeader.tsx` (`:6-16`) — nothing else defines the shape. `regionCount` and `unitCount` disappear as fields: they were only ever read to build the routine string, and every non-load site set them to 0. ### `packages/shared/src/workspace/AppHeader.tsx` — visibility and colour from the tone - `import type { StatusLine } from "./shellStatus";` and `status: StatusLine | null` (`:69`). - The status `` (`:381-405`): keep the testid, the `sr-only` fallback, the "no report loaded" text and its `text-ink-dim` span exactly. Replace the flag logic: ```tsx const visible = status !== null && status.tone !== "routine"; const DOT_CLASS: Record, string> = { notice: "bg-ink-dim", warning: "bg-warn", failure: "bg-danger" }; … {status ? ( <> {visible ? ( ]}`} /> ) : null} {status.text} ) : ( no report loaded )} ``` (Write the narrowing however TypeScript is happiest — a small `dotClass(tone)` function with a `switch` returning `null` for `routine` is fine; the point is the three class names above, verbatim. `bg-ink-dim` is a real utility: `--color-ink-dim` is a Tailwind v4 theme token in `packages/shared/src/theme.css:51`, alongside `--color-warn:66` and `--color-danger:67`.) - Rewrite the comment above it (`:373-380`) to say the rule is now the tone, not the import flags — three or four lines, no history lesson. - The chip gate (`:417`): `{chipLabel && status && !status.failed ? (` → `{chipLabel ? (`. Delete the "Withheld while an import is failed" paragraph of the comment above it (`:414-416`) and replace with one line: the chip counts the turn on screen, and stays whatever the status line says. - `chipLabel` is null when there are no messages (`describeTurnMessages`, `turnMessages.ts:99-106`), which is the case whenever no turn is loaded, so dropping `status &&` changes nothing there. ### `packages/shared/src/reportLoad.ts` — build tones, not flags - `import type { StatusLine } from "./workspace/shellStatus";` replaces the `ImportStatus` import (`:31`); extend the existing `warningStatus` import (`:36`) with `countsStatus, noticeStatus`. - `LoadedTurn.status: StatusLine` (`:65`); its doc comment: "The routine counts, or the remember/draft warning if there was one." - `loadTurn` (`:120-127`): `status: message !== null ? warningStatus(message) : countsStatus(report.regions.length, unitCount)`. Delete the "A message here is always a warning" comment. - `storeOlderTurn` (`:198-203`): returns `warning !== null ? warningStatus(warning) : noticeStatus(`turn ${report.header.turnNumber} stored for history; still showing turn ${currentTurn}.`)`. The string is unchanged (`workspace.spec.ts:148` reads "stored for history"). ### `packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx` — the 18 sites - `:89` `import { AppHeader, type ImportStatus } from "./AppHeader";` → `import { AppHeader } from "./AppHeader";` - `:162` → `import { failedStatus, noticeStatus, routineStatus, warningStatus } from "./shellStatus";` - `:273` `useState(null)` → `useState(null)` (add `type StatusLine` to the `:162` import). - Unchanged, because they already go through the helpers: `:856` (`loaded.status`), `:905`, `:929`, `:932`, `:969`, `:987`, `:1029`, `:1046`, `:1128`, `:1165`, `:1181`, `:1376`, `:1405` (`null`), `:1666`, `:1854`, `:1887`. - `:1021-1027` (merge) → `setStatus(outcome.warning !== null ? warningStatus(outcome.warning) : noticeStatus(describeMerge(outcome.result)));` — `describeMerge` is already imported there; the string it builds is unchanged. - `:1338-1348` (restore) → delete the `unitCount` reduce (`:1338-1341`, now unused) and write `setStatus(restored.warning !== null ? warningStatus(restored.warning) : routineStatus(`restored turn ${restored.turnNumber}`));` — routine, because the navigator kept "restored turn N" hidden (see *User-facing decisions*). - `:1878-1884` (orders imported) → `setStatus(noticeStatus(`orders imported: ${pending.unitCount} unit${pending.unitCount === 1 ? "" : "s"}`));` - `:2099` and `:2130` (comparison failures) → `failedStatus(message)` instead of `warningStatus(message)`. Delete the paragraph of the doc comment above `handleSelectComparisonTurn` that begins "A comparison failure is reported as a `warning`, not `failed`" (`:2121-2124`) — with the chip no longer gated on failure the reason is gone; the rest of that comment stays. `grep -n "withholds the turn-messages chip\|not .failed" AppShell.tsx` must then hit nothing. - `grep -n "regionCount\|unitCount: 0\|failed: \|warning: " AppShell.tsx` must then hit nothing status-related (a `unitCount` on `pending`/`ordersImportSummary` is a different thing and stays). ### Tests - `packages/shared/src/workspace/shellStatus.test.ts` — rewrite for the five constructors. - `packages/shared/src/workspace/AppHeader.test.tsx` — a new `describe("AppHeader status line")` using the existing `draw()` (`:6-52`); `status={…}` and `messages={…}` are already props it takes. - `packages/shared/src/reportLoad.test.ts` — the six expectations at `:155-161`, `:172-173`, `:183`, `:223`, `:283-289`, `:299` move to the new shape (below). - `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts:225-226` — one added assertion that the merge line is visible. ## Increments Branch `ah-9gk-status-line-tones` from `origin/main`, worktree under `.cerebro/worktrees/ah-9gk`. The type change is one refactor across five files, so **the branch typechecks again at the end of increment 4, not before** — run each increment's own vitest file for RED/GREEN (`pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared exec vitest run src/workspace/shellStatus.test.ts` etc.) and `pnpm run check:fast` from increment 4 onward. One commit per increment. 1. **The type and its constructors.** RED: rewrite `shellStatus.test.ts` first — `describe("status line constructors")` with one `it` per constructor asserting `toEqual({ text: "x", tone: "…" })`, plus `countsStatus(11, 42)` → `{ text: "11 regions · 42 units", tone: "routine" }` and `countsStatus(1, 1)` → `"1 region · 1 unit"`. It fails to import. GREEN: the new `shellStatus.ts`. Commit `refactor(ah-9gk): the status line is a text and a tone`. 2. **The header renders by tone.** RED: in `AppHeader.test.tsx`, `describe("AppHeader status line")`: - `"a routine status is written but takes no room"` — `draw({ status: routineStatus("11 regions · 42 units") })`; the `import-status` span's class contains `sr-only`, markup contains `11 regions · 42 units`, and contains no `rounded-full` dot inside that span. - `"a notice is visible with a dim dot"` — `noticeStatus("orders imported: 3 units")`; class does not contain `sr-only`; markup contains `bg-ink-dim`. - `"a warning is visible with an amber dot"` — `bg-warn`. - `"a failure is visible with a red dot and leaves the messages chip in place"` — `draw({ status: failedStatus("could not read x.rep: no faction header"), messages: { errors: ["e"], events: [] } })`; markup contains `bg-danger` **and** `data-testid="turn-messages-chip"`. - `"no status says no report loaded"` — `draw()` (status null) contains `no report loaded` and `sr-only`. Match with a regex over the static markup the way `AppHeader wrapping` does (`:62-64`). All five fail (import of `routineStatus` etc. is fine after increment 1; the assertions fail on the old flags). GREEN: the `AppHeader.tsx` edits above. Commit `refactor(ah-9gk): the header shows a status line by its tone, and never hides the chip for it`. 3. **reportLoad builds tones.** RED: update the six `reportLoad.test.ts` expectations — `:155` → `toEqual({ text: "2 regions · 2 units", tone: "routine" })`; `:172-173` → `expect(loaded.status.text).toContain("disk is full"); expect(loaded.status.tone).toBe("warning")`; `:183` → `.text`; `:223` → `expect(loaded.status.tone).toBe("routine")`; `:283` → `toEqual({ text: "turn 71 stored for history; still showing turn 71.", tone: "notice" })`; `:299` → `expect(status.text).toContain("disk is full")` and add `expect(status.tone).toBe("warning")`. GREEN: the `reportLoad.ts` edits. Commit `refactor(ah-9gk): loading and storing a turn report a tone`. 4. **AppShell's sites, and the smoke proof.** RED: `pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared typecheck` is red (`ImportStatus` no longer exists) — that is the RED for the shell; and in `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts` after `:226` add `await expect.poll(async () => (await page.getByTestId("import-status").boundingBox())?.width ?? 0).toBeGreaterThan(1);` with a one-line comment "a merge is worth a glance: the line takes room, as stored-for-history does at :150" — red today (the merge line is `sr-only`). GREEN: the AppShell edits; `pnpm run check:fast` green. Commit `refactor(ah-9gk): every shell message says its tone instead of posing as an import`. 5. **PR**, Copilot review requested on open, every comment answered, squash. Close the bead after merge. ## The test plan - Unit (`pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared test`): `shellStatus.test.ts` (7 cases: five constructors, two `countsStatus` pluralisations); `AppHeader.test.tsx` new describe (5 cases above); `reportLoad.test.ts` (six updated expectations). Everything else in the shared suite unchanged. - Browser (`pnpm run test:smoke`, CI): the whole suite is the regression net here — ~50 assertions read `import-status` by text and two by bounding box (`workspace.spec.ts:150` stored-for-history visible, `:434-436` routine counts hidden, `:445` warning visible). All must stay green with no string changed; the one added assertion (`:226`) pins the merge notice visible. - Native (`tests/native`, CI): `importStatusText()` in `helpers.ts:157-161` reads `textContent`; unaffected. - Suites to run locally: `pnpm run check:fast`. Smoke and native run in CI. ## User-facing decisions Mockup: `docs/ui/status-line-tones.html` (merged in PR #319; the scratch copy was `.cerebro/scratch/xavier/ah-9gk-status-line.html`). Interview 2026-08-16, three questions, all answered after the navigator confirmed opening the page. **Q1 — a visible "notice" tone, and how it looks.** Options: **A** notice with a dim grey dot (`bg-ink-dim`), same weight as a warning — *chosen*; B notice with the success green (rejected: "stored for history; still showing turn 71" is not a success, and green pulls the eye to a line that mostly does not need it); C no notice tier, notices `sr-only` like the counts (rejected: "orders imported: N units" would stay invisible, and "stored for history" would have to stay a warning to be seen — the lie the bead is about). Routine counts and "restored turn N" stay hidden in every variant: decided 2026-08-11 in 7eafbc5 "drop routine chatter from the title bar", not re-opened. **Q2 — the tone table.** Chosen *as proposed*: | Message (verbatim, as it ships) | Was | Now | |---|---|---| | `11 regions · 42 units` | hidden | **routine** (hidden) | | `restored turn 71` | hidden | **routine** (hidden) | | `orders imported: 3 units` | hidden by accident | **notice** | | `merged 3 regions from Borg (73), turn 71 — 2 new to your map` | hidden by accident | **notice** | | `turn 70 stored for history; still showing turn 71.` | warning | **notice** | | `the turn could not be remembered: …` / `the remembered map could not be read: …` / `…could not be drawn: …` | warning | **warning** | | `could not list the turns to compare: …` / `could not load turn 70 for comparison: …` | warning | **failure** | | `could not read x.rep: …` / `could not merge …` / `could not import …` / `could not plan a route: …` / `the last turn could not be restored: …` / `there is no open game to store it in` / `could not start the import` | failure | **failure** | Rejected alternatives offered: keep the comparison failures amber; keep "stored for history" amber. Both declined. **Q3 — does a failure hide the turn-messages chip.** **3-i never** — *chosen*: the chip always counts the turn on screen, one rule. Rejected: 3-ii hide only for a failed *report* load (a second flag on the message, the hidden rule the bead names); 3-iii any failure hides it (today; the comparison failures would have to stay warnings). Not asked, unchanged: the line's place in the header and its wrapping (one flex item, wraps with the rest); a message stays until the next replaces it (no timers); `no report loaded` when there is no turn; no keyboard or focus behaviour (the line is not interactive). ## Out of scope - The 45-prop `AppHeader` and its hand-built test object, the popover dismiss duplication — ah-9r0. - Any new message, any reworded message, timers or auto-dismiss, a message history/log. - Turning `ordersImportSummary` (the dialog for a dirty orders import) into a status line — it is a dialog by ah-470's decision and stays one. - Changing what `runReported` (`shellAction.ts`) does with its `prefix` — the strings it builds are unchanged and just flow into `failedStatus`. ## Validation - `pnpm run check:fast` green. - `pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared exec vitest run src/workspace/shellStatus.test.ts src/workspace/AppHeader.test.tsx src/reportLoad.test.ts` — 18 or more passing, none skipped. - `grep -rn "ImportStatus" packages tests apps --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx | grep -v node_modules | grep -v dist` prints nothing. - CI smoke and native green; the added `workspace.spec.ts:226` bounding-box assertion passes. - By eye, once, in `pnpm --filter @atlantis/web dev` (or the smoke run's screenshots): load turn 71, merge the ally report — the merge line shows with a grey dot; drop a junk file — a red line appears **and** the "1 error · N events" chip stays beside it. That last one is the only visible behaviour change a player could notice, and Psylocke will look for it. ## Known traps - **Do not touch a single status string.** ~50 smoke assertions match on `import-status` text (`"11 regions"`, `"restored turn 71"`, `"stored for history"`, `"merged 3 regions from Borg (73)"`, `"could not"`, `"cannot be remembered"`, `"faction 73"`…). The refactor changes tone and shape, never text; `countsStatus` must reproduce ` · ` exactly. - **`sr-only` must stay for routine and for null** — `workspace.spec.ts:434-436` asserts the routine status has a bounding box of width ≤ 1 or none, and `tests/native/helpers.ts:157-161` explains WebKitWebDriver answers `""` for text it considers invisible, which is why the native suite reads `textContent`. Do not switch `sr-only` to `hidden` and do not remove the span when routine. - **The chip gate is the one behaviour change** — after this, `import-status` red and `turn-messages-chip` present at the same time is correct. Nothing in the smoke suite asserts the chip absent on failure (checked at planning time: `grep -rn turn-messages-chip tests/` hits only the three chip tests at `workspace.spec.ts:2314-2352`), so no test needs deleting. - **`AppHeader.test.tsx`'s `draw()` hand-builds all 45 props** — add no new prop to `AppHeader`; this bead only changes the type of `status`, so `draw()` needs no edit beyond the new describe. - **`renderToStaticMarkup` escapes `·`?** It does not (it is a plain character), but it does escape `—` no more than the browser would; match text with `toContain("11 regions · 42 units")` on the markup and it works — the existing test at `:62-64` matches raw markup the same way. - **The comparison-failure sites also `setTurnPickerOpen(false)`** (`:2100`, `:2131`) — keep that; only the constructor changes. - **A `warning`/`failure` from `runReported`'s `onFail` is a string already prefixed** ("could not read x.rep: …") — do not prefix again in `failedStatus`.

title: Header popovers share one dismiss rule and one open-at-a-time state
description:
## The cost being paid
Every header chip is wired as an (open flag in AppShell, toggle prop, panel-node prop) triple through a 45-prop AppHeader whose only unit test hand-builds all 45, and each of the eight popovers hand-rolls the same dismiss effect (Escape + pointerdown outside `panelRef.current.parentElement`) and the same chrome, seven of them bypassing dismissLayer.ts. One PR needed a third commit purely to survive a rebase; the planner named the duplication and declined it; every plan since carries the DOM-nesting trap; changing one popover rule touched 8 of 14 files.

## Evidence
- eb59982 feat(ah-vp3.2) third commit: "test(ah-vp3.2): rebase - AppHeader.test.tsx gains the long-export props. main picked up onExportOrdersLong/canExportLong (#183) while this PR sat in review; the hand-built props object here needed them too"
- bead ah-vp3.2 design: "none of the five header popovers use [useEscapeToDismiss] — they each hand-roll Escape and outside-press … Extracting the five-way duplication into a shared usePopoverDismiss is tempting and is out of scope"; "Two popovers sharing one parent means pressing the merged chip counts as inside the faction panel and fails to dismiss it"
- bead ah-jg6.3 design: TurnPicker "copied structurally from GamePicker.tsx (its dismissal effect at :46-71 …)"; "the new turn-chip wrapper must be a sibling of, never shared with…"
- beads ah-470, ah-jg6.4, ah-cp8 designs: "AppHeader.test.tsx's draw() breaks on any new prop … prefer keeping all new state inside AppShell"; "hand-builds the full ~30-prop object, so any new AppHeader prop breaks that file"; "merging or re-parenting them breaks outside-press dismissal"
- 1f5be7e feat(ah-cp8): 14 files, 8 of them panels and their tests, for one popover max-height rule

## Where
packages/shared/src/workspace/AppHeader.tsx (AppHeaderProps :34–146; :277, :332–335); packages/shared/src/workspace/AppHeader.test.tsx (draw() :6–52); packages/shared/src/workspace/AppShell.tsx (12 *Open useStates :427–475); GamePicker.tsx, TurnPicker.tsx, MergedFactionsPanel.tsx, FactionPanel.tsx, ProblemsPanel.tsx, TurnMessagesPanel.tsx, ExportMenu.tsx, BadgeMenu.tsx; dismissLayer.ts

## What a refactoring would change
One popover primitive (chrome + dismiss through dismissLayer, keyed by the popover's own element rather than its parent) used by all eight, and chips declared as a list (id, label, panel) the header renders and AppShell owns one open-chip state for — so a new chip is one entry and the header test builds one small object.

Filed by Bishop, weekly sweep of 2026-08-15 (first sweep, whole of origin/main), range e60bbbd..150ba17.
design:
## Context Eight popovers hang off chips in this workspace — seven in the header (`GamePicker`, `TurnPicker`, `MergedFactionsPanel`, `FactionPanel`, `ProblemsPanel`, `TurnMessagesPanel`, `ExportMenu`) and one over the map (`BadgeMenu`, from `LayerChips.tsx`). Each hand-rolls the same dismiss effect (Escape on `document`, `pointerdown` outside `panelRef.current.parentElement`) and the same frame (`absolute left-0 top-full z-20 mt-1 w-… rounded border border-edge bg-panel-raised … shadow-lg`, `role="dialog"`, `onDragOver` stop), and each header chip is wired through `AppHeader` as an (open flag, toggle callback, panel node) triple owned by `AppShell` — six such flags (`AppShell.tsx:312,351,352,365,366,382`) plus `AppHeader`'s own `exportOpen` (`AppHeader.tsx:207`). Bishop's evidence (weekly sweep 2026-08-15): one popover rule change touched 8 of 14 files (1f5be7e, ah-cp8); every plan since ah-vp3.2 carries the "two popovers must not share a parent" trap; a PR needed a third commit only because `AppHeader.test.tsx`'s hand-built 45-prop object broke on a rebase; ah-vp3.2's plan named the five-way duplication and declined it. When this lands: **one primitive** — `usePopoverDismiss` + `PopoverFrame` + `ChipPopover` in `packages/shared/src/workspace/popover.tsx` — is the only place a popover's dismissal and chrome are written; the eight panels are content; the header holds its chips in **one open-at-a-time state** (`openPopover: HeaderPopoverId | null`) that `AppShell` owns, and `AppHeader` loses twelve props. Nothing a player sees changes, with one deliberate harmonisation recorded under *User-facing decisions* (the badge menu stops behaving differently from the other seven). **Blocked by ah-9gk** (planned; small): it edits `AppHeader.tsx`'s status span and the chip gate at `:417`, and this plan is written against those lines *after* ah-9gk — the status prop is `StatusLine | null` and the messages chip is `{chipLabel ? … : null}` with no `status` test. If you find `status.failed` still in `AppHeader.tsx`, ah-9gk has not merged: stop and wait for it. Bishop's second suggestion — chips declared as a data list the header maps over — is **not** done here; see *Out of scope* for why. ## Files to change, and what to reuse Everything is in `packages/shared/src/workspace/`. No core, no `core-client`, no shell code. ### New: `popover.tsx` — the primitive ```ts import type { ReactNode, RefObject } from "react"; /** Which edge of its chip a popover hangs from. */ export type PopoverAlign = "left" | "right"; /** * Escape and a press elsewhere close the popover - while it is open, and only then. * * `wrapperRef` is the element holding BOTH the chip and the panel: a press on the chip must not * count as "elsewhere", or the pointerdown dismisses and the chip's own click reopens, leaving a * control that can only ever open (tests/smoke/games.spec.ts:78-89). Escape is heard on `document` * in the BUBBLE phase, deliberately not through dismissLayer.ts's capture-phase stack: a text field * inside a popover (the game rename, GamePicker.tsx:258-265) must get Escape first and be able to * stop it, and the cycling chords in AppShell stand down behind `hasOpenDismissLayers()` - a * popover beside the map is not an overlay the player cannot see through. Listeners are added on * open and removed on close; `onDismiss` is read through a ref so a fresh lambda each render * re-registers nothing. */ export function usePopoverDismiss( wrapperRef: RefObject, open: boolean, onDismiss: () => void ): void; /** * The frame every popover shares: anchored under its chip, raised, bordered, and never a drop * target (the header accepts dropped reports; a panel floating off it must not become a second, * invisible one - the reason every header panel already stops `dragover`). `width`, `padding` and * `textSize` are Tailwind class literals passed whole (see Known traps). */ export function PopoverFrame(props: { testId: string; label: string; // aria-label align: PopoverAlign; // "left" → left-0, "right" → right-0 width: string; // "w-72" | "w-80" | "w-[28rem]" | "w-44" | "w-40" padding?: string; // "p-2" | "p-1" | undefined (no padding class) textSize?: string; // default "text-[11.5px]"; BadgeMenu passes "text-[11px]" children: ReactNode; }): JSX.Element; // renders: //
e.stopPropagation()} // className={`absolute ${align === "left" ? "left-0" : "right-0"} top-full z-20 mt-1 ${width} // rounded border border-edge bg-panel-raised ${padding ?? ""} ${textSize ?? "text-[11.5px]"} // whitespace-normal shadow-lg`}>{children}
// Class order as today's panels have it, so a diff of the rendered markup is a no-op apart from // whitespace: absolute, left/right, top-full, z-20, mt-1, width, rounded, border, border-edge, // bg-panel-raised, [padding], text size, whitespace-normal, shadow-lg. (BadgeMenu today lacks // whitespace-normal; gaining it changes nothing visible - its labels are single words.) /** * A chip and the popover that hangs off it, in the `relative` wrapper the popover positions * against, with dismissal wired once. `children` is the chip (a button); `panel` renders only * while `open`. */ export function ChipPopover(props: { open: boolean; onDismiss: () => void; panel: ReactNode; children: ReactNode; className?: string; // extra classes on the wrapper; AppHeader's chips today use "relative" only }): JSX.Element; // renders {children}{open ? panel : null} // and calls usePopoverDismiss(wrapperRef, open, onDismiss). ``` `ChipPopover` renders a `` because every header wrapper today is a `` (`AppHeader.tsx:257,280,337,354,418,450,529,557` — game, turn, faction, merged, messages, problems, export, settings; the settings one wraps a dialog trigger and stays a plain span — see traps). `LayerChips.tsx:58` uses a `
`; a `span` there is fine inside its flex row, but if the row's layout shifts (it will not — the wrapper carries no size of its own) pass `className="inline-block"`. ### New: `popover.test.tsx` `renderToStaticMarkup` only — the repository has no jsdom (`BadgeMenu.test.tsx:9-11` says so), so the hook's listeners are the smoke suite's to prove; what is unit-checkable is markup: - `PopoverFrame` — `"carries the popover chrome, anchored left"`: markup contains `data-testid="x"`, `role="dialog"`, `aria-label="X"`, and the class string contains each of `absolute`, `left-0`, `top-full`, `z-20`, `mt-1`, `w-72`, `bg-panel-raised`, `shadow-lg`, `whitespace-normal`; `"anchored right"`: `right-0` and not `left-0`; `"padding and text size are optional"`: with `padding: "p-1", textSize: "text-[11px]"` both appear; without, `text-[11.5px]` appears and no `p-` class does. - `ChipPopover` — `"renders the chip and, only when open, the panel"`: closed markup contains the chip text and not the panel text; open markup contains both; the wrapper class contains `relative`. ### `AppHeader.tsx` — one open state, chips wrapped once - New exported type, in `AppHeader.tsx` next to `TurnMessages`: ```ts /** The header's popovers, at most one of which is open. Dialogs (settings, battles, changes) are not popovers and keep their own flags. */ export type HeaderPopoverId = "games" | "turns" | "merged" | "faction" | "messages" | "problems" | "export"; ``` - Props removed (12): `pickerOpen`, `onTogglePicker`, `turnPickerOpen`, `onToggleTurnPicker`, `mergedOpen`, `onToggleMerged`, `factionOpen`, `onFactionToggle`, `messagesOpen`, `onToggleMessages`, `problemsOpen`, `onToggleProblems`. Props added (2): ```ts openPopover: HeaderPopoverId | null; /** Opens the named popover (closing whichever was open), or closes all with null. */ onOpenPopover: (id: HeaderPopoverId | null) => void; ``` Kept as they are: every `*Panel`/`picker`/`turnPicker` node prop, `battlesOpen`/`onToggleBattles`, `changesOpen`/`onToggleChanges`, `settingsOpen`/`onToggleSettings`/`settings` (dialogs), and all the rest. - Delete the local `exportOpen` state (`:199-207`) and its comment; the export menu is `openPopover === "export"`. - Inside the component: `const toggle = (id: HeaderPopoverId) => onOpenPopover(openPopover === id ? null : id);` and `const close = () => onOpenPopover(null);`. - Each of the seven chips becomes ```tsx ``` replacing the `…{xOpen ? panel : null}` pair. Button markup, testids, `aria-haspopup`, classes, labels: unchanged, byte for byte. Ids: game indicator → `"games"`, turn chip → `"turns"`, merged chip → `"merged"`, faction chip → `"faction"`, messages chip → `"messages"`, problems chip → `"problems"`, export button → `"export"`. - `onStopComparing` (`AppShell.tsx:2413-2416`) is unchanged as a prop; it is AppShell's. - Delete the per-chip "its own `relative` wrapper, sibling to…" comments (`:275-278` and the matching ones at the faction and merged chips) — the wrapper is now the primitive's, and the sibling rule is stated once in `ChipPopover`'s doc. ### `AppShell.tsx` — six flags become one - Delete `pickerOpen` (`:312`), `messagesOpen` (`:351`), `problemsOpen` (`:352`), `mergedOpen` (`:365`), `factionOpen` (`:366`), `turnPickerOpen` (`:382`) and their setters. Add, where `:312` was: ```ts /** Which header popover is open - one at a time, by construction. Dialogs keep their own flags. */ const [openPopover, setOpenPopover] = useState(null); /** Closes the named popover if it is the open one, and touches nothing otherwise. */ const closePopover = useCallback( (id: HeaderPopoverId) => setOpenPopover((open) => (open === id ? null : open)), [] ); ``` - The open handler, replacing `handleOpenTurnPicker` (`:2078-2107`) and the inline messages toggle (`:2444-2452`): ```ts const handleOpenPopover = useCallback( (id: HeaderPopoverId | null) => { if (id === "messages") { // Opening lands on the list that has something in it (unchanged rule, was inline in the toggle). setMessagesTab(messages && messages.errors.length > 0 ? "errors" : "events"); } setOpenPopover(id); if (id === "turns") { void loadTurnSummaries(); } }, [messages, loadTurnSummaries] ); ``` where `loadTurnSummaries` is `handleOpenTurnPicker`'s fetch half, verbatim, minus the toggle: guard `if (!game || !parsed?.header.factionId) return;`, the `runReported(listComparableTurns…)` call with the same failure lambda but `closePopover("turns")` instead of `setTurnPickerOpen(false)`, and `setTurnSummaries(summaries)` on success. Keep the doc comment's reasoning (fetch only on the way open; a failed listing closes the picker — ah-k6i.1).
