Commit `refactor(ah-9r0): the header's popovers are one open-at-a-time state the shell owns`. 3. **Dismissal moves into the wrapper.** RED: none unit-testable (no jsdom); the RED is behavioural and the smoke tests named above are the check. GREEN: `AppHeader.tsx` wraps the seven chips in `ChipPopover` (with `onDismiss={close}`), `LayerChips.tsx` wraps the badges button, and all eight panels lose `panelRef` + the effect (+ `useEscapeToDismiss` in BadgeMenu); `GamePicker`, `TurnPicker`, `BadgeMenu` lose the `onDismiss` prop; `TurnPicker.test.tsx` / `BadgeMenu.test.tsx` drop it. Run `pnpm exec playwright test tests/smoke/games.spec.ts tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts -g "picker|faction view|messages panel|Escape|elsewhere|outside"` locally, green. Commit `refactor(ah-9r0): every popover dismisses through the one wrapper`. 4. **Chrome moves into the frame.** RED: `grep -ln 'className="absolute left-0 top-full\|className="absolute right-0 top-full' *.tsx` lists the eight panels; GREEN: it lists none — each panel's outer div is `PopoverFrame` with the props in the table; the four panel tests still green; `pnpm run check:fast` green. Commit `refactor(ah-9r0): the eight popovers share one frame`. 5. PR, Copilot on open, every comment answered, squash. Close after merge. ## The test plan - Unit: `popover.test.tsx` (6), `AppHeader.test.tsx` (existing 5 + 2 new), `TurnPicker.test.tsx`, `BadgeMenu.test.tsx`, `MergedFactionsPanel.test.tsx`, `FactionPanel.test.tsx`, `ProblemsPanel.test.tsx`, `TurnMessagesPanel.test.tsx` — all green, no `.skip`. - Smoke (CI, and locally at increment 3): `games.spec.ts` "the indicator closes the picker as well as opening it", "the picker still goes away on Escape and on a press elsewhere", "Escape cancels the rename and leaves the picker open"; `workspace.spec.ts` "the faction view closes on Escape", "the faction view closes on an outside press", "the turn messages panel closes on Escape", and every test that opens the export menu, the problems panel, the merged panel or the badge menu. Whole suite green in CI. - Native (CI): unchanged. - `pnpm run check:fast` locally before the PR. ## User-facing decisions None asked of the navigator — this is a refactoring and every string, testid, class and behaviour of the seven header popovers is preserved. Two planner calls, recorded so they are not re-opened: - **The badge menu now dismisses like the other seven** (bubble-phase Escape, no dismiss-stack layer). Today it alone uses `useEscapeToDismiss`, so today alone among the eight it (a) takes Escape in the capture phase and (b) makes the cycling shortcuts stand down while it is open (`AppShell.tsx:738`, `hasOpenDismissLayers()`). After this, shortcuts keep working with the badge menu open, as they do with every other popover open. Harmonising to the majority, not a new rule. - **A game switch closes every header popover** (`AppShell.tsx:1417/1421` → `setOpenPopover(null)`), where today it closed only the merged panel and the turn picker. The others could not be open during a switch in practice (the switch happens from the game picker, which is the one open), so this is a guard, not a change. ## Out of scope - **Chips as a declared list** the header maps over. The seven chips are heterogeneous — the game indicator carries the name and a busy state, the turn chip a compare pair, the merged chip a count-gated visibility, the messages chip an error-vs-event colour — and a `{id, label, panel}` list would either grow a per-chip `render` field (a list of JSX, i.e. what the header already is) or lose those differences. The cost Bishop measured (14 files for one rule; 45 props) is paid by the primitive and the single state; the list is not needed to pay it. Not planned as a child. - Moving `battlesOpen` / `changesOpen` / `settingsOpen` into `openPopover` — those are dialogs (modal, centred, `useEscapeToDismiss`), not popovers. - Popovers joining the dismiss stack (see the doc on `usePopoverDismiss` for why not). - Any change to a popover's width, alignment, padding, text size or contents. - `AppHeader.test.tsx`'s `draw()` still hand-builds the props; it shrinks by ten and that is all. ## Validation - `pnpm run check:fast` green. - `grep -n "parentElement" packages/shared/src/workspace/*.tsx` prints only `RailSplitter.tsx:42` and `PanelSplitter.tsx:45` (the eight `panelRef.current?.parentElement` lookups are gone). - `grep -ln "pointerdown" packages/shared/src/workspace/*.tsx` prints `popover.tsx`, `MapCanvas.tsx` and `SettingsDialog.tsx` only — the eight panels are gone from that list, and `AppHeader.tsx` with them (its only mention was the wrapper comment this plan deletes); the other two use it for something else and are left alone. - `grep -n "useState(false)" packages/shared/src/workspace/AppHeader.tsx` prints nothing. - CI smoke green; the named dismissal tests in particular. - By eye once: open the game picker, press the indicator again — it closes; open it, click the map — it closes; open the faction chip then the merged chip — the first closes as the second opens; open the badge menu, press a unit-cycling shortcut — the selection moves and the menu stays. ## Known traps - **Blocked by ah-9gk.** Same file (`AppHeader.tsx`), and this plan's line numbers for the chip wrappers assume ah-9gk's status span and chip gate are in. Do not start until ah-9gk is closed. - **`wrapperRef` must hold the chip and the panel and nothing else that should count as "elsewhere".** The trap ah-vp3.2 recorded — the merged chip nested inside the faction chip's wrapper, so a press on the merged chip counted as inside the faction panel — is exactly what `ChipPopover` prevents *if* each chip gets its own `ChipPopover`. Today (`AppHeader.tsx:332-370`) the faction chip's `relative` span (`:337`) and the merged chip's (`:354`) are siblings inside one outer ``; keep that: two `ChipPopover`s, siblings, never one inside the other's wrapper. - **Tailwind class literals**: `PopoverFrame` interpolates `width`/`padding`/`textSize` into `className`, which is fine only because every value is written whole at a call site (`width="w-[28rem]"`) — Tailwind's scanner reads source text, not runtime strings (`primitives.tsx:5-12` explains the same rule for `POPOVER_BODY_MAX_H`). Never build a class from pieces (`w-[${n}rem]`). - **The rename field's Escape** (`GamePicker.tsx:258-265`) relies on the picker's Escape listener being a bubble-phase `document` listener that a React `stopPropagation` can stop. Keep `usePopoverDismiss` in the bubble phase; do not "improve" it onto `useEscapeToDismiss`'s capture path — `games.spec.ts:234-249` will fail if you do. - **`onDismiss` identity**: read it through a ref inside the hook (`latest.current = onDismiss` on every render, as `dismissLayer.ts:13-14` does) and key the effect on `[open]` only; otherwise a new lambda each render re-adds two document listeners per render, harmless but noisy, and a stale closure is one refactor away. - **`ChipPopover` renders `panel` only when `open`** — the panels rely on mount/unmount for their own state (`GamePicker`'s tab reset, `TurnMessagesPanel`'s scroll). Never render the panel hidden. - **`aria-expanded` on each chip must keep tracking its own popover** (`openPopover === id`), and the export button's `data-testid="export-menu"` and its panel's `export-menu-panel` are read by `tests/smoke/*` — unchanged. - **`handleOpenPopover` must set the state before it fetches** for `"turns"`: the picker opens immediately with the last summaries and refreshes, exactly as `handleOpenTurnPicker` did (`setTurnPickerOpen(opening)` before the await). A failed listing closes it (`closePopover("turns")`). - **AppShell's palette entry `Switch game`** (`:767`) opens the picker without a chip press; with one state that now also closes any other popover — intended. - **The header unit tests render with `renderToStaticMarkup`**: hooks with effects (`usePopoverDismiss`) do not run there, so `draw({ openPopover: "faction" })` renders the panel without touching `document`. If a test throws on `document`, the hook is doing work at render time — it must not.

title: Each report fixture is named once per language, with a test that keeps the names and the files in step
description:
## The cost being paid
The committed report fixtures are referenced by string literal in every test that uses them — Rust include_str! paths, TS imports, smoke specs — with no per-language fixture module, so renaming or replacing one is a repo-wide edit. It has been paid once already, and the next rename or replacement pays the same: today `neworigins-3.0.0-g7-f95-t71.rep` is named in 37 files on origin/main (33 of them code or tests). crates/core has no shared test-support module either: `const TURN_71 … include_str!`, `fn at()`, `fn ruleset()` are declared per test file (fixture path in 18 files under crates/, ruleset path in 16).

## Evidence
- b4357da "chore(ah-dyi): name each committed report fixture by its game too" (in 8909402 test(ah-dyi), PR #164): "updates the 43 references to them across 30 files" — stat shows 34 files changed, 43 insertions, 43 deletions; kept as its own commit "so it rebases cleanly against the two other planned beads (ah-vp3.1, ah-1is.1) also editing parse_real_reports.rs"
- 8379f5f "chore(ah-dyi): rewrap fixture const lines the rename pushed over width" — 11 more files
- git grep -l neworigins-3.0.0-g7-f95-t71.rep origin/main | wc -l = 37

## Where
crates/core/tests/*.rs (13 files), crates/core/src/{cache.rs,lib.rs,movement/request.rs,orders/mod.rs,report/sighting.rs}, crates/core-tauri/src/lib.rs, tests/smoke/*.spec.ts, tests/native/*.spec.ts, packages/browser-core/src/*.test.ts, packages/shared/src/ordersDocument.test.ts, packages/ruleset/src/capacity.test.ts

## What a refactoring would change
A fixture module per language — a Rust tests/common (or a `fixtures` module in the crate) exporting the constants and helpers, and a TS `tests/fixtures/reports/index.ts` — so a fixture is named once per language and a rename is two edits.

Filed by Bishop, weekly sweep of 2026-08-15 (first sweep, whole of origin/main), range e60bbbd..150ba17.
design:
## Context

The committed report fixtures (`tests/fixtures/reports/*.rep`, 25 files + a README) are named by
string literal wherever a test reads one: Rust `include_str!("../../../tests/fixtures/reports/…")` in
13 integration test files under `crates/core/tests/`, five `crates/core/src/*` unit-test modules and
`crates/core-tauri/src/lib.rs`; TypeScript `new URL("../../../tests/fixtures/reports/…", import.meta.url)`
in package tests and `join(__dirname, "..", "fixtures", "reports", "…")` in ten smoke specs and two
native specs. `neworigins-3.0.0-g7-f95-t71.rep` alone is named in 33 code files on `origin/main`
`6388e88`; the ah-dyi rename (b4357da + 8379f5f) touched 34 files and then 11 more to rewrap lines.
`crates/core` also has no shared test support: `fn at()` and `fn ruleset()` are declared per test file
(11 copies).

This bead names each fixture **once per language** — a Rust crate `atlantis-hud-fixtures` and a
workspace package `@atlantis/fixtures` — and adds, in each, a **lockstep test that fails when a
`.rep` file exists without a name or a name without a file**, so a rename or a new fixture is two
edits and cannot be half-done. Every reference then goes through the module. No behaviour changes
anywhere; every existing test stays green with the same fixture text. Documentation that quotes a
file name (`docs/ui/*.html`, `tests/fixtures/reports/README.md`) is not code and is left alone.

Verified on `origin/main` `6388e88`:
- Rust: `Cargo.toml` `members` :2-8; `crates/core/Cargo.toml` `name = "atlantis-hud-core"`,
  `[dev-dependencies] serde_json`; `crates/core-tauri/Cargo.toml:7` depends on core by path;
  `include_str!` sites: `crates/core/src/cache.rs:152-153` (report + `config/public/ruleset.json`),
  `crates/core/src/lib.rs`, `movement/request.rs`, `orders/mod.rs`, `report/sighting.rs`,
  `crates/core-tauri/src/lib.rs:1187,1206,1262` (ruleset) and `:1387` (report);
  `crates/core/tests/{export_map,merge_reports,movement_graph,movement_orders,movement_plan,movement_risk,movement_trace,orders_preview,parse_real_reports,unit_composition,unwrap_real_report,validate_real_orders,known_map}.rs`
  (`movement_graph.rs:13-15` two reports; `movement_plan.rs:35-37` `fn ruleset()`;
  `movement_graph.rs:17-19` `fn at()`).
- TS: `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (`apps/*`, `packages/*`); `packages/browser-core/src/parseReportFull.test.ts:15`,
  `turnDiff.fixtures.test.ts`, `packages/shared/src/ordersDocument.test.ts:249`,
  `packages/ruleset/src/capacity.test.ts` (`new URL(…, import.meta.url)` + `readFileSync`);
  `tests/smoke/{backup,desktop-shell,games,map-export,orders-editor,persistence,settings,shortcuts,workspace}.spec.ts`
  and `tests/native/{sweep.ts,workspace.spec.ts}` (`join(__dirname, "..", "fixtures", "reports", …)`,
  e.g. `workspace.spec.ts:27-63` seven files); package `tsconfig.json`s are `composite` with
  `include: ["src"]` (a relative import of a `.ts` outside `src` fails typecheck with TS6307 —
  hence a workspace package, not a shared file); `tsconfig.tooling.json:7` includes
  `tests/native/sweep.ts`; the smoke specs are transpiled by Playwright and typechecked by nothing
  (`typecheck` = `pnpm -r run typecheck && typecheck:tooling && cargo check`).

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### Rust: new crate `crates/fixtures` (`atlantis-hud-fixtures`), a workspace member

`Cargo.toml`: `[package] name = "atlantis-hud-fixtures"`, no dependencies. `src/lib.rs`:

```rust
//! The committed report fixtures, named once. Every test in the workspace that reads a fixture
//! reads it from here, so renaming or replacing one is an edit to this file and to the file on
//! disk - and `every_fixture_on_disk_is_named_here` fails when the two disagree (ah-v2l).

/// One committed report: its file name under `tests/fixtures/reports/`, and its text.
pub struct Report { pub file: &'static str, pub text: &'static str }

macro_rules! report {
    ($file:literal) => { Report { file: $file, text: include_str!(concat!("../../../tests/fixtures/reports/", $file)) } };
}

pub const G2_F42_T0: Report = report!("neworigins-3.0.0-g2-f42-t0.rep");
// … one `pub const` per file, `G<game>_F<faction>_T<turn>`, in the directory's order …
pub const G8_F73_T71: Report = report!("neworigins-3.0.0-g8-f73-t71.rep");

/// Every fixture, for the lockstep test and for anything that walks them all (`parse_real_reports`).
pub const ALL: &[&Report] = &[&G2_F42_T0, /* … */ &G8_F73_T71];

/// The shipped ruleset, `config/public/ruleset.json`, which the tests parse against.
pub const RULESET_JSON: &str = include_str!("../../../config/public/ruleset.json");
```

`#[cfg(test)]` in the same file: `every_fixture_on_disk_is_named_here` — `std::fs::read_dir(concat!(
env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/../../tests/fixtures/reports"))`, collect the `.rep` names, compare as
sorted sets with `ALL.iter().map(|r| r.file)` (both directions), and `names_follow_the_file` — each
const's `file` parses to the `G_F_T` numbers its name says (guards a copy-paste of the wrong literal
under a right name).

Add `"crates/fixtures"` to the workspace `members`. `crates/core/Cargo.toml` and
`crates/core-tauri/Cargo.toml`: `[dev-dependencies] atlantis-hud-fixtures = { path = "../fixtures" }`
(dev only — the wasm and desktop builds never see the text).

Then every Rust site: `const TURN_71: &str = include_str!(…)` → `use atlantis_hud_fixtures::G7_F95_T71;`
and `G7_F95_T71.text` where the const was used (or keep a local `const TURN_71: &str = G7_F95_T71.text;`
where a file names it many times — `const` items can read another const's field); `RULESET` →
`atlantis_hud_fixtures::RULESET_JSON`. `parse_real_reports.rs`, if it lists the fixtures by hand,
walks `ALL` instead. **Also** a `crates/core/tests/common/mod.rs` with `pub fn at(x: i32, y: i32) ->
Coordinate` and `pub fn ruleset() -> Ruleset` (`Ruleset::from_json(RULESET_JSON).expect(…)`), and
`mod common;` in each test file that had its own copy (11 files) — the standard integration-test
idiom; the unit-test modules under `src/` keep their tiny helpers (they cannot see `tests/common`).

### TypeScript: new package `packages/fixtures` (`@atlantis/fixtures`)

`package.json` (`"name": "@atlantis/fixtures"`, `"private": true`, `"type": "module"`, `"main":
"src/index.ts"`, `scripts.test = "vitest run"`, `scripts.typecheck = "tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json"`,
devDependency `@types/node`), `tsconfig.json` like `packages/ruleset`'s (`composite`, `include:
["src"]`), `src/index.ts`:

```ts
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

/** The committed report fixtures by key, `g<game>f<faction>t<turn>` → file name under tests/fixtures/reports/. */
export const REPORTS = {
  g2f42t0: "neworigins-3.0.0-g2-f42-t0.rep",
  // … one entry per file …
  g8f73t71: "neworigins-3.0.0-g8-f73-t71.rep"
} as const;
export type ReportKey = keyof typeof REPORTS;

/** Absolute path of a fixture on disk - for `setInputFiles` and the like. */
export function reportPath(key: ReportKey): string;   // fileURLToPath(new URL(`../../../tests/fixtures/reports/${REPORTS[key]}`, import.meta.url))
/** A fixture's text. */
export function readReport(key: ReportKey): string;   // readFileSync(reportPath(key), "utf8")
/** The shipped ruleset, config/public/ruleset.json. */
export const RULESET_PATH: string;
export function readRuleset(): string;
```

`src/index.test.ts` (vitest, node): `every fixture on disk is named here` — `readdirSync` the
directory, filter `.rep`, sorted-equal to `Object.values(REPORTS)` sorted; `every key reads its
file` — `readReport(key)` starts with `Atlantis Report For:` for each key; `keys follow the file` —
`/^g(\d+)f(\d+)t(\d+)$/` matches `neworigins-3.0.0-g$1-f$2-t$3.rep`.

Consumers: root `package.json` `devDependencies` gets `"@atlantis/fixtures": "workspace:*"` (the
smoke and native specs import from the root's `node_modules`); `packages/browser-core`,
`packages/shared`, `packages/ruleset` `devDependencies` likewise. Every `new URL(…rep…)` /
`join(__dirname, …rep…)` becomes `readReport("g7f95t71")` (or `reportPath` where a path is what is
needed — `setInputFiles` in `tests/smoke/backup.spec.ts` uses an in-memory buffer today, so
`readReport` there too; check each). `config/public/ruleset.json` reads in tests → `readRuleset()`.
`pnpm install` after the package.json edits (the lockfile changes; commit it).

Root `pnpm -r run typecheck` picks the new package up (`packages/*`), and so does the root
`pnpm test` (`scripts/runSuites.ts:24-28` runs `pnpm -r run test` for the packages leg) — as long as
the package has a `test` script, its lockstep test is in the gate with no further wiring.

### Documentation

`tests/fixtures/reports/README.md`: one paragraph at the top — a fixture is named in
`crates/fixtures/src/lib.rs` and `packages/fixtures/src/index.ts`, and both have a test that fails
when this directory and the names disagree; adding a fixture is: drop the file here, add the two
names, run both tests.

## Increments

1. RED (Rust): `every_fixture_on_disk_is_named_here` with an empty `ALL`. GREEN: the crate with all
   25 consts; workspace member; `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-fixtures`.
2. Rust consumers: the two dev-dependencies; replace every `include_str!` of a report or the ruleset
   in `crates/core` (src + tests) and `crates/core-tauri`; `tests/common/mod.rs` with `at`/`ruleset`
   and the 11 files on it. `cargo test --workspace`, clippy, fmt. `grep -rn "fixtures/reports/" crates/
   --include=*.rs` must show only `crates/fixtures/src/lib.rs`.
3. RED (TS): `packages/fixtures/src/index.test.ts` with an empty `REPORTS`. GREEN: the package with
   all 25 keys; `pnpm install`; `pnpm --filter @atlantis/fixtures test`.
4. TS consumers: the four devDependencies; every package test, smoke spec and native spec through
   `readReport`/`reportPath`/`readRuleset`. `pnpm run typecheck && pnpm run test`; `pnpm run
   test:smoke` locally (both projects — this touches every spec's setup) — a green run here is what
   proves the text still arrives.
5. README paragraph; `pnpm run check:fast`; PR `refactor(ah-v2l): the report fixtures are named once
   per language, with a lockstep test`; `@copilot`; CI (watch `native` — `tests/native/*` and
   `package.json` changed, so it runs); squash. Close the bead.

## The test plan

- Rust: the fixtures crate's two tests; the whole workspace suite unchanged and green.
- TS: `packages/fixtures` (3 tests); every package suite; the smoke suite on both projects; the
  native suite in CI.
- `git grep -n "neworigins-3.0.0-g" -- crates packages tests ':!tests/fixtures' ':!crates/fixtures' ':!packages/fixtures'`
  prints nothing.

## User-facing decisions

None. Test infrastructure only.

## Out of scope

- Renaming any fixture, or adding one.
- The `docs/ui/*.html` mockups and `.beads/issues.jsonl` that quote a file name.
- Sharing `at()`/`ruleset()` with the unit-test modules under `crates/core/src/` (they cannot see
  `tests/common`; three-line helpers stay).
- A fixture *ruleset* directory: `config/public/ruleset.json` is the shipped file and stays where the
  app serves it from; the modules only name it.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-fixtures && cargo test --workspace && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --check
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm --filter @atlantis/fixtures test && pnpm run typecheck && pnpm run test
pnpm run test:smoke
git grep -n "fixtures/reports/\|neworigins-3.0.0-g" -- crates packages tests ':!tests/fixtures/reports' ':!crates/fixtures' ':!packages/fixtures'   # nothing
pnpm run check:fast
```

Human: none.

## Known traps

- **`include_str!` paths are relative to the *source file*, not the crate root**: from
  `crates/fixtures/src/lib.rs` the reports are `../../../tests/fixtures/reports/`. `concat!` inside
  `include_str!` works with literals only — the macro above keeps them literal.
- **`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`** lints the new crate and the test
  `common` module: an unused helper in `common/mod.rs` (a test file that pulls `mod common;` but uses
  only `at`) warns `dead_code` per test binary — put `#![allow(dead_code)]` at the top of
  `common/mod.rs` with a one-line reason (the standard idiom), not on each function.
- **The wasm and desktop builds must not grow**: dev-dependencies only; `cargo build -p
  atlantis-hud-core-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` should not compile the fixtures crate at
  all (check `cargo tree -p atlantis-hud-core-wasm -e normal | grep fixtures` is empty).
- **`composite` TS projects and `include: ["src"]`**: the reason for a package rather than a shared
  file; a package test importing `@atlantis/fixtures` resolves through `node_modules`, so `pnpm
  install` must run before `typecheck` — CI does; a local `check:fast` on a stale install fails with
  "cannot find module".
- **`import.meta.url` under vitest and under Playwright** both point at the source file, so
  `reportPath` resolves the same way in both; `__dirname` is not used (ESM).
- **`tests/native/sweep.ts` is typechecked by `tsconfig.tooling.json`** — that project must be able
  to see `@atlantis/fixtures` (root devDependency covers it; if `tsc -p tsconfig.tooling.json`
  cannot resolve it, add `"paths"` there rather than a relative import).
- **Rebase risk**: every smoke spec changes its first lines; any bead touching a smoke spec (ah-c0m's
  `backup.spec.ts`, ah-lkw's `games.spec.ts`, ah-u4e.3's runs) will conflict textually at the
  imports — trivial, but expect `BEHIND` and a rebase before merge.

title: Report types cross to TypeScript once: one casing, generated types, one test builder
description:
## The cost being paid
Each core type is re-declared and hand-mapped three times on its way to the shell — core → core-tauri *Dto (field-by-field, camelCase) → core-wasm *Dto (serde flatten of the un-renamed core struct, so snake_case) → core-client *WireShape with every field in both spellings and a normalize* function — and ParsedReport/ReportHeader have no generated TS type and no builder on either side, so adding one field means the mirror plus every test that spells out a whole report literal. The two Rust copies disagree on casing, and two agents have already misread the stored payload the same way.

## Evidence
- 6af62de feat(ah-1is.1): parse the battles of the turn report — 11 files, of which index.ts (+62 mirror), gameMemory.test.ts / hexMapModel.test.ts / orderDraft.test.ts (+1 line `battles: []` each), merge.rs and orders/semantics.rs (`battles: Vec::new()`) carried nothing but the ripple; bead ah-1is.1 design "Known traps": "TypeScript cannot catch it, because the mirror is hand-written… The field simply reads undefined"
- 923c711 feat(ah-vp3.1): parse faction status and declared attitudes — 7 files, index.ts +35 and the same three test files ripple only
- f917be8 feat(#82): two fields on one diagnostic → crates/core/src/lib.rs, core-tauri (+52), core-wasm (+57), core-client (+140)
- crates/core/src/report/mod.rs:34: "ReportHeader is the type mirrored by hand in TypeScript"
- Casing misread twice: 18d7e30's persistence round-trip fixture is camelCase (`{"turnHeader":{"turnNumber":12,…}}`, still at crates/core-persistence/src/lib.rs:2829) which the crate's own peek cannot read; 855a40f "fix(ah-jg6.1): read the season through both casings the hydrator emits" (in 9120935) — the browser season peek "silently read null in production" until Copilot caught it; core-persistence/src/lib.rs:1163–1169 carries a paragraph explaining the same surprise; every core-client normaliser reads `payload.gameId ?? payload.game_id`

## Where
crates/core/src/lib.rs (ReportParseResult :185, no rename_all); crates/core/src/report/{mod,header,model}.rs; crates/core-tauri/src/lib.rs (*Dto :21–415); crates/core-wasm/src/lib.rs (DTOs; ReportParseResultDto #[serde(flatten)] :275); packages/core-client/src/index.ts (*WireShape :649–840, normalize*); packages/shared/src/{gameMemory,hexMapModel,orderDraft,turnDiff}.test.ts and workspace/{BattlesDialog.test.tsx,changesView.test.ts} (whole-report literals)

## What a refactoring would change
One casing decided in core (rename_all on the core types), one DTO layer instead of two disagreeing ones, TS types generated from the Rust definitions (ts-rs/typeshare or wasm-bindgen's own typing) so a new field is one edit and no *WireShape needs both spellings, and a report builder for tests so a new field does not touch six test files.

Filed by Bishop, weekly sweep of 2026-08-15 (first sweep, whole of origin/main), range e60bbbd..150ba17.

title: Committed ruleset.json is checked against the scraper and read strictly by the core
description:
## The cost being paid
The ruleset schema is hand-mirrored in the TS scraper's types, the core's serde structs, and the prose "Shape" section of the contract doc, with the committed JSON as a fourth artefact regenerated or hand-edited in step; nothing derives one from another and nothing checks the doc copy. Every field added has touched all of them — 4, 6 and 8 schema files in three commits — and a plan had to sequence increments to keep the mirrors compatible. The doc has drifted on main today.

## Evidence
- d09a573 feat(ah-2vy.1): scrape the sailing skill a ship requires into the ruleset — one optional integer, 4 files (data.ts, data.test.ts, crates/core/src/movement/rules.rs, config/public/ruleset.json); bead ah-2vy.1 design §Increments: "The Rust field first, so the two sides cannot land out of step in the wrong order"
- 962fbe4 feat(ah-2vy.2): the sailing rule — rules.ts (+51), rules.test.ts, rules.rs (+91), crates/core/tests/movement_ruleset.rs, docs/ruleset-contract.md, config/public/ruleset.json: 6 schema files; ruleset.json was hand-edited (source.fetchedAt still d09a573's 2026-08-13T16:50:41Z while movement.sailing was added 2026-08-14), against the file's own source.note
- f917be8 feat(#82): the skills block — build.ts, build.test.ts, data.ts, data.test.ts, rules.rs, movement_ruleset.rs, ruleset-contract.md, ruleset.json: 8 files
- docs/ruleset-contract.md §"Shape of config/public/ruleset.json" today: movement listed as movementPoints, terrainCosts, road, ocean (no sailing); item optionals as combat, cargoCapacity, capacityCondition (no sailingSkill) — while config/public/ruleset.json carries both; §"Where the numbers come from" omits the sailing rule and skill

## Where
packages/ruleset/src/{rules,data,build}.ts; crates/core/src/movement/rules.rs; docs/ruleset-contract.md; config/public/ruleset.json

## What a refactoring would change
One schema source (a JSON Schema the TS types and serde structs are both generated from or validated against), the doc's Shape section generated from it or dropped in favour of it, and the committed JSON always produced by the scraper (a check that source.fetchedAt moves when content moves).

Filed by Bishop, weekly sweep of 2026-08-15 (first sweep, whole of origin/main), range e60bbbd..150ba17.
design:
## Context

Bishop's weekly sweep (2026-08-15) found the ruleset's shape spelled in four artefacts with nothing
deriving one from another and nothing checking the doc: the scraper's TypeScript types
(`packages/ruleset/src/{rules,data,build}.ts`), the core's serde structs
(`crates/core/src/movement/rules.rs`), the prose "Shape" section of `docs/ruleset-contract.md`, and
the committed `config/public/ruleset.json`. Two of the four have drifted on main today, and this
session confirmed both:

- **The committed JSON is not what the scraper produces.** Running the scraper against the
  committed HTML fixtures (`tests/fixtures/ruleset/neworigins-{rules,data}.html`, which is exactly
  what `source.rulesUrl`/`dataUrl` in the committed file say it was last built from) and diffing
  everything but `source`: the `movement.sailing` block sits in a different position (hand-inserted,
  962fbe4) and `provenance.sailing` reads `"…one movement point. A coastal region … ocean region."`
  in the file but `"…one movement point A coastal region … ocean region"` from the scraper —
  `rules.ts:289` joins the two sentences with a bare space, and whoever hand-edited the file added
  the punctuation. `source.fetchedAt` still says 2026-08-13 while the block was added on 08-14.
- **`docs/ruleset-contract.md` §"Shape of `config/public/ruleset.json`"** (`:45–67`) lists
  `movement` as `movementPoints, terrainCosts, road, ocean` (no `sailing`) and the item optionals as
  `combat, cargoCapacity, capacityCondition` (no `sailingSkill`); §"Where the numbers come from"
  (`:7–17`) names neither the sailing rule nor the sailing skill.

**The design here is deliberately not code generation.** The JSON *is* the contract — the scraper
writes it, the shell fetches it and hands the text to the core, and nobody else reads it
(`packages/ruleset`'s types are imported by nothing outside that package; the shell passes
`rulesetJson` through as a string). So the cheapest honest "one source" is to make both ends strict
about that one file and prove, in tests that already run, that the file is what the scraper wrote:

1. **A vitest test in `packages/ruleset` proves the committed JSON equals `buildRuleset(fixtures)`.**
   A hand edit, a stale file after a scraper change, or a scraper change after which nobody
   regenerated all fail it, with "regenerate with: …" in the message.
2. **`deny_unknown_fields` on every ruleset struct in core** (eight of seventeen have it today), so a
   field the scraper adds that the core does not know fails
   `crates/core/tests/movement_ruleset.rs`, which already parses the committed file. A field the core
   adds that the scraper does not write already fails there as a missing field.
3. **The doc stops describing the shape field by field** and instead names the two typed sources
   and the two tests that hold them together, plus a short "adding a field" checklist. The two
   places where its prose is *wrong* today (§Where the numbers come from, §Shape) are corrected by
   the same edit.
4. **The scraper's sailing provenance joins its two sentences with `". "`** so regenerating the file
   changes only what the hand edit changed, not the meaning of a provenance string.

`ts-rs`/`schemars` were considered and rejected: they would remove one type declaration per field
from the scraper's TS while adding a crate, an export that runs as a side effect of every
`cargo test` (and maps `i64` to `bigint` unless an env var says otherwise), and a per-type file
layout — for a schema whose only two consumers are the two files above. If `ah-164` later brings a
generator in for the report types, this bead's tests still hold and can be replaced then.

What changes for the player: nothing. `config/public/ruleset.json` is regenerated, which moves
`source.fetchedAt`, reorders `movement`'s keys and drops one full stop from a provenance sentence
that no interface displays (`grep provenance packages/shared/src` finds nothing).

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `packages/ruleset/src/rules.ts:289` — the provenance join

```ts
      sailing: `${sentence(sailingCost)}. ${sentence(coastal)}`
```

(`sentence()` at `:151` trims and collapses whitespace and strips nothing else; the page's sentences
carry no trailing full stop in the extracted text, so this reads "…one movement point. A coastal
region is defined as…", which is what the committed file already says apart from its final stop.)

### `packages/ruleset/src/committed.test.ts` — new: the committed file is the scraper's output

```ts
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { buildRuleset, type Ruleset } from "./build";

const read = (relative: string) =>
  readFileSync(fileURLToPath(new URL(`../../../${relative}`, import.meta.url)), "utf8");

const RULES_HTML = read("tests/fixtures/ruleset/neworigins-rules.html");
const DATA_HTML = read("tests/fixtures/ruleset/neworigins-data.html");
const COMMITTED = JSON.parse(read("config/public/ruleset.json")) as Ruleset;

const REGENERATE =
  "pnpm --filter @atlantis/ruleset scrape -- " +
  "--rules tests/fixtures/ruleset/neworigins-rules.html --data tests/fixtures/ruleset/neworigins-data.html";

/**
 * The shell serves `config/public/ruleset.json` and the core reads it, so the file is the contract
 * between the scraper and everything else. This holds it equal to what the scraper writes from the
 * committed fixture pages, with the committed file's own `source` fed back in so nothing but the
 * scraped content is compared. A hand edit, or a scraper change nobody regenerated after, fails here.
 */
describe("the committed ruleset", () => {
  it("is exactly what the scraper produces from the committed fixture pages", () => {
    const built = buildRuleset({
      rulesHtml: RULES_HTML,
      dataHtml: DATA_HTML,
      rulesUrl: COMMITTED.source.rulesUrl,
      dataUrl: COMMITTED.source.dataUrl,
      fetchedAt: COMMITTED.source.fetchedAt
    });

    // toEqual, not toStrictEqual: an optional the scraper leaves `undefined` is a key the file does
    // not have, and key order is not part of the contract.
    expect(built, `config/public/ruleset.json is not the scraper's output; regenerate it with:\n  ${REGENERATE}`)
      .toEqual(COMMITTED);
  });
});
```

`fixture()` in `build.test.ts:6` is the pattern being copied; the `Ruleset` type is already exported
from `build.ts:46`. `vitest`'s `expect(value, message)` form carries the hint into the failure. The
package's tsconfig already has `types: ["node"]`.

### `config/public/ruleset.json` — regenerated, not edited

Run the `REGENERATE` command above after the `rules.ts` change. Commit the result. Expected diff
against today's file: `source.fetchedAt` moves to now; `movement.sailing` moves to after
`movement.ocean` (the scraper's key order, `rules.ts:279`); `provenance.sailing` loses its final
full stop; nothing else. If anything else moves, stop — the scraper and the file disagree about
content, and that is a finding to put in the PR rather than paper over.

### `crates/core/src/movement/rules.rs` — strict everywhere

Add `deny_unknown_fields` to the `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` attribute of each struct that
lacks it: `Provenance` (`:94`), `ItemCapacity` (`:147`), `SelfMobility` (`:157`), `MonsterCombat`
(`:167`), `ItemEntry` (`:176`), `RiskThresholds` (`:197`), `RulesetSource` (`:207`), `Gap` (`:220`),
`SkillEntry` (`:270`). Enums (`MovementMode`, `ItemKind`) are unit-variant string enums and take
none. `Ruleset` (`:282`), `Gaps` (`:232`) and the movement structs already have it. `#[serde(default)]`
on the optional item fields and on `skills` stays — `deny_unknown_fields` and `default` compose;
the inline-JSON unit tests at `rules.rs:591+` (e.g. `a_ruleset_written_before_this_field_existed_still_loads`,
`:702`) carry no extra keys and keep passing.

Update the module doc at `rules.rs:1–4`: it says "Mirrors `config/ruleset.json`" — make it
"Reads `config/public/ruleset.json`, which `packages/ruleset` writes; every struct here refuses a
key it does not know, so a field the scraper adds without a home here fails
`tests/movement_ruleset.rs`."

### `crates/core/tests/movement_ruleset.rs` — the strictness test

Alongside `loads_the_committed_ruleset` (`:14`), using `RULESET` (`:9`) and `RulesetError` (already
imported, `:7`):

```rust
/// Every struct in the file refuses a key it does not know, so a field the scraper starts writing
/// cannot be silently dropped on the way into the core - the file that carries it fails to load
/// until the core has a home for it. Probed at each depth the file has, since `deny_unknown_fields`
/// is per struct and one forgotten struct is a hole.
#[test]
fn an_unknown_key_anywhere_in_the_file_is_refused() {
    let json: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(RULESET).expect("the committed file is JSON");
    let probes: [&[&str]; 6] = [
        &["source"],
        &["movement", "provenance"],
        &["risk"],
        &["gaps", "weather"],
        &["items", "HORS"],
        &["skills", "COMB"],
    ];
    for path in probes {
        let mut value = json.clone();
        let mut node = &mut value;
        for key in path {
            node = node.get_mut(*key).unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{path:?} exists in the file"));
        }
        node["notAField"] = serde_json::json!(1);
        let error = Ruleset::from_json(&value.to_string()).expect_err(&format!("{path:?} must refuse an unknown key"));
        assert!(matches!(error, RulesetError::Malformed(ref detail) if detail.contains("notAField")), "{error}");
    }
    // And the file as committed still loads - the probes above must not have been the reason.
    Ruleset::from_json(RULESET).expect("the committed file loads");
}
```

`serde_json` is a dev-dependency of the crate already (`crates/core/Cargo.toml`). `items.HORS` and
`skills.COMB` both exist in the committed file (checked 2026-08-16); `HORS` is what
`build.test.ts:32` asserts on too.

### `docs/ruleset-contract.md`

- §"Where the numbers come from" (`:7–17`): the rules row's *Provides* gains "the sailing rule";
  the data row's *Provides* gains "the sailing skill a ship requires".
- §"Shape of `config/public/ruleset.json`" (`:45–67`, up to but not including "### Two things that
  are easy to get wrong", which stays): replace the bullet list with:

  > The shape is declared twice, once on each side of the file, and two tests hold the three together:
  >
  > - **Writing side:** `packages/ruleset/src/build.ts` (`Ruleset`), `rules.ts` (`MovementRules`) and
  >   `data.ts` (`ItemEntry`, `SkillEntry`). The scraper can only write what these types have.
  > - **Reading side:** `crates/core/src/movement/rules.rs` (`Ruleset` and its structs). Every struct
  >   is `deny_unknown_fields`, so the core refuses a file carrying a key it has no home for, and a
  >   field the core requires that the file lacks fails the same parse.
  > - **The file itself** is proven equal to the scraper's output from the committed fixture pages by
  >   `packages/ruleset/src/committed.test.ts`, and proven readable by
  >   `crates/core/tests/movement_ruleset.rs`. Both run in `pnpm test`.
  >
  > Two things the field lists do not say for themselves: `ocean.terrain` is the water terrain's name
  > read out of the rule's own sentence rather than assumed to be `ocean`; and `skills.*.cost` is
  > **null** for a skill the page prices nowhere (annihilation), never zero — zero would say studying it
  > is free. `skills` is its own block rather than merged into `items` because ten tags mean one thing
  > as a skill and another as an item (`FISH`, `HERB`).
  >
  > **Adding a field** touches exactly: the scraper (`rules.ts` or `data.ts`, and its test), the core
  > (`rules.rs`, and `tests/movement_ruleset.rs`), and the file — regenerated, never edited:
  >
  > ```
  > pnpm --filter @atlantis/ruleset scrape -- \
  >   --rules tests/fixtures/ruleset/neworigins-rules.html \
  >   --data  tests/fixtures/ruleset/neworigins-data.html
  > ```
  >
  > All in one change: the two tests above fail until every side agrees, so there is no order to get
  > wrong.

  The `risk` sentence ("**not scraped**, and says so on its face") and the `skills` cost paragraph are
  the two pieces of today's prose that are not shape and survive into the replacement above; the rest
  is field lists that `rules.rs` states better and checks.
- §"Running it" (`:19–31`): after "Either argument may be a local file instead of a URL", add one
  sentence: "The committed file is built from the fixture pages under `tests/fixtures/ruleset/`, and
  `packages/ruleset/src/committed.test.ts` fails if it is not — regenerate rather than edit."

### Layering

Nothing crosses a layer. The TS test lives in `packages/ruleset` because that is where `buildRuleset`
is; the Rust test lives with the crate that reads the file. Neither needs the other.

## Increments

1. **Sailing provenance join.** RED: in `packages/ruleset/src/rules.test.ts` at `:176`
   ("records the sentences the sailing rule came from"), add
   `expect(rules.provenance.sailing).toContain("one movement point. A coastal region")`. GREEN: the
   one-character change at `rules.ts:289`. `pnpm --filter @atlantis/ruleset test`.

2. **The committed file is the scraper's output.** RED: `committed.test.ts` as above; it fails
   today on `movement.provenance.sailing`'s final full stop and (only if `toEqual` cared, which it
   does not) key order. GREEN: run the `REGENERATE` command, check the diff is exactly what *Files to
   change* says, commit the JSON. Run `pnpm --filter @atlantis/ruleset test` again: green.

3. **The core refuses unknown keys everywhere.** RED: `an_unknown_key_anywhere_in_the_file_is_refused`
   fails on the first probe (`source` — `RulesetSource` has no `deny_unknown_fields` today). GREEN:
   the nine attribute additions and the module-doc line. `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core`.

4. **The doc.** No test; the three edits above. Read the section back once as somebody adding a
   field tomorrow.

## The test plan

- `packages/ruleset/src/rules.test.ts` — one added `toContain`.
- `packages/ruleset/src/committed.test.ts` — `is exactly what the scraper produces from the committed fixture pages`.
- `crates/core/tests/movement_ruleset.rs` — `an_unknown_key_anywhere_in_the_file_is_refused`; every
  existing test there still passes against the regenerated file (they assert numbers and
  `contains` on provenance, none of which the regeneration moves).
- Suites: `pnpm --filter @atlantis/ruleset test`, `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core`, then
  `pnpm run check:fast`. No browser suite is affected; the smoke suite serves the regenerated file
  and reads only its numbers.

## User-facing decisions

None. No interface, wording or behaviour changes; the regenerated file differs from today's in
`source.fetchedAt`, key order and one full stop in a provenance string nothing displays.

## Out of scope

- Generating either side's types from a schema (`ts-rs`, `schemars`, JSON Schema) — see *Context*
  for why; revisit under `ah-164` if a generator arrives for the report types.
- Making the scraper's live-site run part of any test or CI step — the doc's "never in CI" stands;
  the new test is offline against committed fixtures.
- Refreshing `tests/fixtures/ruleset/*.html` from the live pages.
- Dropping `#[serde(default)]` from `Ruleset.skills` (kept for rulesets generated before study
  costs were scraped, `rules.rs:289–292`).
- The other three refactoring beads from the same sweep (`ah-164`, `ah-p1p`, `ah-8m0`, `ah-wxk`).

## Validation

```bash
pnpm --filter @atlantis/ruleset test
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test movement_ruleset
pnpm run check:fast
git diff --stat config/public/ruleset.json      # one file, small diff, as described above
```

## Known traps

- **Regenerate the JSON after the `rules.ts` change, not before**, or `committed.test.ts` goes green
  against a file that still carries the unpunctuated join and then red on the next regeneration.
- **`toEqual`, never `toStrictEqual`**, for the reason in the test's comment — the scraper leaves
  `combat`/`cargoCapacity`/`capacityCondition`/`sailingSkill` `undefined` on 162 of 171 items and
  `JSON.stringify` drops them, so a strict compare fails on every one.
- **`pnpm --filter @atlantis/ruleset scrape` runs from the package directory**; the fixture paths in
  `REGENERATE` are repository-relative and the CLI resolves them against the repository root
  (`cli.ts:47–58`), so use them exactly as written, from anywhere.
- **`deny_unknown_fields` is per struct.** Missing one is invisible until a field lands in exactly
  that struct — which is why the Rust test probes six depths rather than the root.
- **`apps/web/dist/ruleset.json` and `apps/desktop/dist/ruleset.json` are build outputs and
  git-ignored**; do not commit them and do not be alarmed that they differ from `config/public/`.

title: Advisory codes and movement words come from core; a SAIL order counts as leaving
description:
## The cost being paid
Lists that core owns — the order vocabulary, the advisory check codes, the movement-order words — are re-typed in TypeScript with no test holding the two equal, and the drift has already been paid for twice: once when the shell's copy of the order vocabulary had "already drifted, and one of them was wrong" (four orders that do not exist, END missing, so correct FORM blocks reported an error), and again the same day a new hand copy was created (ADVISORY_CHECK_CODES) when a code turned out to be missing from both lists. A third mirror was touched in four files for one word and still missed a fifth reader.

## Evidence
- 3abf381 feat(#80): "The shell's hand-copied copy of the vocabulary is deleted in favour of a new orderCommands call - the two had already drifted, and one of them was wrong" — the served-from-core precedent, order_commands()
- 171f13a refactor(ah-m9q.1): creates ADVISORY_CHECK_CODES "mirrored from crates/core semantics::codes::ALL"; 581dabc feat(ah-m9q.2), same day: teacher-has-free-slots "was emitted as a bare string literal and missing from both the Rust and TypeScript code lists - a gap in ah-m9q.1 this bead's own wording table depends on closing"; bead ah-m9q.1 design counts eight codes, bead ah-m9q lists nine
- 962fbe4 feat(ah-2vy.2): SAIL added as a movement word in crates/core/src/movement/orders.rs (parse_move + render_sail), packages/shared/src/ordersDocument.ts (regex (move|advance|sail)), PlannerPanel.tsx (routeAsOrder), AppShell.tsx — and not in crates/core/src/orders/intents.rs:234, which still files SAIL as MonthLong, so semantics::leaves_the_hex says a unit ordered SAIL stays while the trace draws it leaving
- No test compares codes::ALL with ADVISORY_CHECK_CODES (grep of packages/*/src and crates/core-wasm|core-tauri: no reference)

## Where
crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs (pub mod codes, Finding.code as any &'static str); packages/core-client/src/index.ts (ADVISORY_CHECK_CODES :568–578); crates/core/src/movement/orders.rs; packages/shared/src/ordersDocument.ts:244; packages/shared/src/workspace/PlannerPanel.tsx:134; packages/shared/src/hexMapModel.ts:394 (DIRECTION_SHORTHAND)

## What a refactoring would change
Serve every such list from core the way order_commands() already is (or generate the TS constant from the Rust one in the build), tie Finding.code to the registry so a bare literal cannot be emitted, and give the movement-order words one reader.

design:
## Context

Bishop's weekly sweep (2026-08-15) found three lists that the Rust core owns and TypeScript re-types
by hand, with nothing holding the copies equal:

1. **The advisory order-check codes.** `crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs:41–62` (`pub mod codes`,
   nine `&str` consts and `ALL: [&str; 9]`) is mirrored in
   `packages/core-client/src/index.ts:601–614` (`ADVISORY_CHECK_CODES … as const`,
   `AdvisoryCheckCode`). No test compares them. `ah-m9q.2` found `teacher-has-free-slots` emitted as
   a bare literal and missing from *both* lists — which is possible because `Finding.code` is
   `&'static str` (`semantics.rs:96`) and anything can be written there.
2. **The movement-order words.** MOVE/ADVANCE/SAIL are spelled by `parse_move`
   (`crates/core/src/movement/orders.rs:59–61`), by the intents reader
   (`crates/core/src/orders/intents.rs:210,214`), by the TS regex `MOVEMENT_ORDER_LINE`
   (`packages/shared/src/ordersDocument.ts:244`) and by the TS writer `routeAsOrder`
   (`packages/shared/src/workspace/PlannerPanel.tsx:135–139`, mode → `"SAIL"`/`"MOVE"`). The two
   Rust readers already disagree: `intents.rs:210` files `SAIL` as `Intent::MonthLong("SAIL")`, so
   `semantics::leaves_the_hex` (`semantics.rs:221`) says a unit ordered `SAIL N` stays put — while
   the order tracer (`crates/core/src/movement/request.rs:203`, via `parse_move`) draws it leaving.
   A guard unit ordered `SAIL N` today gets no `guard-dropped` warning; ordered `MOVE N` it does.
3. **`render_move`/`render_sail`** (`movement/orders.rs:100–110`) exist in core and have no
   production caller — the shell writes the order itself in `routeAsOrder`.

What changes when this lands:

- `Finding.code` is a `Code` newtype that only `codes::*` can construct, so a bare literal cannot
  be emitted.
- `packages/core-client/src/coreVocabulary.generated.ts` carries `ADVISORY_CHECK_CODES` and
  `MOVEMENT_ORDER_COMMANDS`, **written by a Rust test from the core's constants and checked fresh
  on every `cargo test`**. `@atlantis/core-client`'s public exports do not change (the file is
  re-exported from `index.ts`); the hand-written copy is deleted.
- Core has one list of movement words (`MOVEMENT_ORDER_COMMANDS`) with one predicate
  (`is_movement_command`) that `parse_move` and the intents reader both use, so `SAIL <route>` reads
  as a move everywhere. A bare `SAIL` (no route — a form of its own, `grammar.rs:328–330`) stays a
  month-long order, as today.
- `RoutePlan` carries the order text (`order: "MOVE SE SE"` / `"SAIL N"`), rendered in core by the
  existing `render_move`/`render_sail`; `routeAsOrder` in TS is deleted and `PlannerPanel` shows
  `plan.order`.
- `ordersDocument.ts` builds its movement-line regex from `MOVEMENT_ORDER_COMMANDS`.

Behaviour that changes for the player (decided here as the resolution of an inconsistency, not a
question — the tracer already treats SAIL as departure): a guarding unit ordered `SAIL <dirs>` now
receives the same `guard-dropped`/`hex-unguarded` advisories as one ordered `MOVE`, and is no longer
offered as a teacher or counted present for the teaching checks. Everything else is invisible.

Bishop's "Where" list also names `DIRECTION_SHORTHAND` (`packages/shared/src/hexMapModel.ts:229`);
see *Out of scope* for why it stays.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### Rust — `crates/core`

**`crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs`** — the `Code` newtype, replacing the `&str` consts:

```rust
/// An advisory check's code, as the shell, the settings and the diagnostics know it.
///
/// Constructible only through the constants in [`codes`]: the field is private and `codes` is the
/// one child module, so a finding cannot be emitted under a code that is not in `codes::ALL`. That
/// is the guarantee `ah-m9q.2` had to add by hand when `teacher-has-free-slots` shipped as a bare
/// literal missing from both this list and the shell's copy.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
pub struct Code(&'static str);

impl Code {
    /// The kebab-case string that crosses the wire and is stored in the settings.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        self.0
    }
}

impl std::fmt::Display for Code {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.write_str(self.0)
    }
}

pub mod codes {
    use super::Code;
    pub const NOT_ENOUGH_SILVER: Code = Code("not-enough-silver");
    pub const NOT_ENOUGH_ITEMS: Code = Code("not-enough-items");
    pub const GUARD_DROPPED: Code = Code("guard-dropped");
    pub const HEX_UNGUARDED: Code = Code("hex-unguarded");
    pub const TAUGHT_NOT_HERE: Code = Code("taught-not-here");
    pub const TAUGHT_NOT_STUDYING: Code = Code("taught-not-studying");
    pub const TEACHER_CANNOT_TEACH: Code = Code("teacher-cannot-teach");
    pub const TEACHING_OVERSUBSCRIBED: Code = Code("teaching-oversubscribed");
    pub const TEACHER_HAS_FREE_SLOTS: Code = Code("teacher-has-free-slots");
    /// Every code, in the order the settings tab lists them. The generated TypeScript copies this order.
    pub const ALL: [Code; 9] = [ /* same order as today */ ];
}
```

The `codes` module must stay a child of the module that declares `Code` (it already is —
`semantics.rs:41`), because that is what lets it see the private field while nothing else can.

Then, mechanically:
- `Finding.code: Code` (`:96`), both `finding(...)` helpers take `code: Code` (`:201`, `:297`).
- `CheckOptions::emits(&self, code: Code) -> bool { !self.disabled.contains(code.as_str()) }`
  (`:74`). `disabled` stays `BTreeSet<String>` — it is filled from the wire with strings and
  "unknown codes are ignored" (`:67`) is unchanged.
- `Default for CheckOptions` (`:88`): `codes::HEX_UNGUARDED.as_str().to_string()`.
- Every emit site already passes `codes::X` (`:712–1013`) — they compile unchanged.
- **`crates/core/src/orders/mod.rs:73`** `into_diagnostic`: `code: finding.code.as_str().to_string()`.
- Tests in `semantics.rs`: `codes(&findings)` helper (`:1154`) becomes
  `.map(|finding| finding.code.as_str())` so it still returns `Vec<&str>` and its callers do not
  change; the fourteen `assert_eq!(finding.code, "…")` sites (`:1206` … `:1965`) become
  `assert_eq!(finding.code.as_str(), "…")`; `disabling(code: Code)` (`:1997`) inserts
  `code.as_str().to_string()`; the fixture table at `:2019` is `Vec<(Code, Vec<ReportRegion>, &str)>`
  and `:1712`'s `code == codes::HEX_UNGUARDED` compiles as is (`PartialEq` derived).

**`crates/core/src/movement/orders.rs`** — the one list of movement words:

```rust
/// The order words that move a unit across the map. `parse_move` reads exactly these; the intents
/// reader files exactly these as movement; the shell's generated vocabulary carries exactly these.
pub const MOVEMENT_ORDER_COMMANDS: [&str; 3] = ["MOVE", "ADVANCE", "SAIL"];

/// Whether `word` (a bare command token, no `@`) is one of [`MOVEMENT_ORDER_COMMANDS`], any case.
#[must_use]
pub fn is_movement_command(word: &str) -> bool {
    MOVEMENT_ORDER_COMMANDS.iter().any(|command| command.eq_ignore_ascii_case(word))
}
```

`parse_move` (`:59–63`) replaces its three `eq_ignore_ascii_case` tests with
`if !is_movement_command(command) { return None; }`. The comment above it about ADVANCE and SAIL
stays. `render_move`/`render_sail` are unchanged.

**`crates/core/src/orders/intents.rs:208–216`** — SAIL with a route is a move; bare SAIL is not:

```rust
        "BUILD" => Some(Intent::MonthLong("BUILD")),
        "PRODUCE" => Some(Intent::MonthLong("PRODUCE")),
        // A bare SAIL — the form the turn 71 template uses — spends the month but names no step this
        // reader can follow. With a route it is a move like any other, and is read below.
        "SAIL" if arguments.is_empty() => Some(Intent::MonthLong("SAIL")),
        "CAST" => Some(Intent::MonthLong("CAST")),
        word if crate::movement::orders::is_movement_command(word) => Some(Intent::Move {
            steps: forms::read_move_line(command, arguments)?,
        }),
        _ => None,
```

`name` is already upper-cased (`:150`), so the guard arm sees `"SAIL"`. The `?` on
`read_move_line` keeps today's behaviour for a MOVE/ADVANCE/SAIL whose route cannot be read (no
intent), which is what `read_move_line` (`forms.rs:177`) has always done for MOVE.

**`crates/core/src/movement/plan.rs`** — the order text on the plan:

```rust
pub struct RoutePlan {
    pub from: Coordinate,
    pub to: Coordinate,
    pub mode: MovementMode,
    pub steps: Vec<RouteStep>,
    pub total_cost: u32,
    pub months: Vec<MonthLeg>,
    /// The order this route becomes, exactly as the shell writes it into the unit's block:
    /// `SAIL …` for a fleet, `MOVE …` for everything else (a flier and a rider MOVE too).
    pub order: String,
}
```

Filled at the one construction site (`:200`), from the existing renderers:

```rust
    let moves: Vec<MoveStep> = steps.iter().map(|step| MoveStep::Go(step.direction)).collect();
    let order = if matches!(mode, MovementMode::Sail) {
        crate::movement::orders::render_sail(&moves)
    } else {
        crate::movement::orders::render_move(&moves)
    };
```

`RoutePlan` is `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` and passes through core-tauri and core-wasm
unchanged (`packages/core-client/src/index.ts:1971` "Returned as-is … the core already serializes
this shape"), so **no DTO, no adapter and no wasm stub changes** — the field simply appears in
TypeScript once the type says it does.

**`crates/core/tests/generated_ts.rs`** (new integration test — `crates/core/tests/` already holds
`movement_orders.rs` etc.). This is the generator *and* the freshness check:

```rust
//! The TypeScript vocabulary `@atlantis/core-client` re-exports is generated from the core's own
//! constants, here, and this test fails whenever the committed file no longer matches them.

use std::path::PathBuf;

use atlantis_hud_core::movement::orders::MOVEMENT_ORDER_COMMANDS;
use atlantis_hud_core::orders::semantics::codes;

const RELATIVE_PATH: &str = "../../packages/core-client/src/coreVocabulary.generated.ts";
const REGENERATE: &str = "ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test generated_ts";

fn render() -> String { /* builds the exact text below */ }

#[test]
fn core_client_vocabulary_matches_the_core() {
    let path = PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join(RELATIVE_PATH);
    let expected = render();
    if std::env::var_os("ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED").is_some() {
        std::fs::write(&path, &expected).expect("writes the generated vocabulary");
        return;
    }
    let actual = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap_or_default();
    assert_eq!(
        actual, expected,
        "packages/core-client/src/coreVocabulary.generated.ts is stale; regenerate it with:\n  {REGENERATE}"
    );
}
```

The generated file's exact text (with `\n` line endings, ending in one newline; the arrays are one
element per line, two-space indent, no trailing comma — this repository has no formatter that
would rewrite it, and ESLint's only rule is `no-unused-vars`):

```ts
// GENERATED by crates/core/tests/generated_ts.rs from the Rust core. Do not edit by hand.
// Regenerate with: ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test generated_ts

/** Advisory order-check codes: `codes::ALL` in crates/core/src/orders/semantics.rs, in that order. */
export const ADVISORY_CHECK_CODES = [
  "not-enough-silver",
  "not-enough-items",
  "guard-dropped",
  "hex-unguarded",
  "taught-not-here",
  "taught-not-studying",
  "teacher-cannot-teach",
  "teaching-oversubscribed",
  "teacher-has-free-slots"
] as const;

export type AdvisoryCheckCode = (typeof ADVISORY_CHECK_CODES)[number];

/** The order words that move a unit: `MOVEMENT_ORDER_COMMANDS` in crates/core/src/movement/orders.rs. */
export const MOVEMENT_ORDER_COMMANDS = [
  "MOVE",
  "ADVANCE",
  "SAIL"
] as const;

export type MovementOrderCommand = (typeof MOVEMENT_ORDER_COMMANDS)[number];
```

`render()` builds this from `codes::ALL.iter().map(Code::as_str)` and `MOVEMENT_ORDER_COMMANDS`;
nothing in it is a literal list. Commit the generated file — it is source as far as the TS build is
concerned, and CI's cargo job proves it fresh.

### TypeScript

**`packages/core-client/src/coreVocabulary.generated.ts`** — new, generated as above.

**`packages/core-client/src/index.ts`** — delete lines `601–614` (the comment,
`ADVISORY_CHECK_CODES`, `AdvisoryCheckCode`) and put in their place:

```ts
export {
  ADVISORY_CHECK_CODES,
  MOVEMENT_ORDER_COMMANDS,
  type AdvisoryCheckCode,
  type MovementOrderCommand
} from "./coreVocabulary.generated";
```

`OrderCheckOptions.disabledCodes` (`:625`) keeps its `readonly AdvisoryCheckCode[]` type. Every
existing importer (`settingsStore.ts:13`, `AppShell.tsx:14`, `SettingsDialog.tsx:2`, the three
tests) is untouched — the names and the package they come from do not change.

`RoutePlan` (`:191–198`) gains `order: string;` with the doc comment "The order this route becomes,
as core writes it — `SAIL …` for a fleet, `MOVE …` for everyone else."

**`packages/shared/src/ordersDocument.ts:244`**:

```ts
import { MOVEMENT_ORDER_COMMANDS } from "@atlantis/core-client";

/** A line that is one of the core's movement orders, `@`-repeated or not. */
const MOVEMENT_ORDER_LINE = new RegExp(`^\\s*@?\\s*(${MOVEMENT_ORDER_COMMANDS.join("|")})\\b`, "iu");
```

`@atlantis/core-client` is already a dependency of `@atlantis/shared` (`packages/shared/package.json`).
`stripMovementOrderLines` and its comment are unchanged.

**`packages/shared/src/workspace/PlannerPanel.tsx`** — delete `routeAsOrder` (`:134–139`) and the
now-unused `abbreviateDirection` import *only if* it becomes unused (it does not — `:180` still uses
it for the step labels; keep the import). In `Route` (`:154`): `const order = plan.order;`.

**Test fixtures that spell out a whole `RoutePlan`** need `order` added or TypeScript refuses them.
Grep `totalCost` to find them all; today they are:
- `packages/shared/src/workspace/plannerPanel.test.ts` — the whole
  `describe("writing a route as an order", …)` block (`:58–91`: the `answer()` builder and the two
  `routeAsOrder` tests) is deleted, since core now owns what it pinned and
  `crates/core/tests/movement_plan.rs` pins it instead. `routeAsOrder` leaves the import on `:3`.
- `packages/shared/src/workspace/routeOverlay.test.ts` — one literal: add `order: "MOVE SE"`.
- `packages/core-client/src/index.test.ts` — three literals: add `order: "MOVE SE"` to each.
The value is asserted nowhere in these files; any string satisfies the type, and `"MOVE SE"` reads
as what a one-step fixture would render.

### Layering, in one line each

- `Code` and `MOVEMENT_ORDER_COMMANDS` live in core because core is the owner Bishop named and the
  generator reads them from there.
- The generator is a core *test*, not a `scripts/` tool: it needs the Rust constants, it must fail
  the build when stale, and `cargo test --workspace` already runs in `pnpm test` and in CI's cargo
  job — nothing new to wire.
- The rendered order lives on `RoutePlan` because the plan already crosses the wire as-is and core
  already owns the renderers; a new command would have cost the six-declaration ripple `ah-wxk`
  describes.

## Increments

Each opens with the named failing test. Rust tests run with `cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core`;
TS with `pnpm --filter @atlantis/shared test` / `pnpm --filter @atlantis/core-client test`.

1. **`Code` newtype.** RED: in `semantics.rs` tests, add

   `let code: Code = codes::HEX_UNGUARDED; assert_eq!(code.as_str(), "hex-unguarded"); assert_eq!(code.to_string(), "hex-unguarded");`
   — fails to compile because `Code` does not exist yet, which is the RED. GREEN: the newtype, the const changes, `Finding.code`, `emits`, `Default`, `into_diagnostic`,

## The test plan

Rust (`cargo test --workspace`):

  `a_guard_that_sails_away_drops_the_guard_like_one_that_marches`; every existing test, with the

- `settingsStore.test.ts`, `SettingsDialog.test.tsx`, `core-client/index.test.ts`: unchanged in
  meaning; they iterate `ADVISORY_CHECK_CODES` and now exercise the generated file.

Browser: nothing new. `tests/smoke/workspace.spec.ts:1922` already asserts
`planner-order` has text `MOVE SE NE`; it must keep passing (core renders the identical string).
CI runs it.

## User-facing decisions

None asked. No layout, wording or control changes. One behaviour is settled here as an
architecture call because two core readers disagreed and one had to win: a unit ordered
`SAIL <route>` is treated as leaving its hex by the advisory checks (as the tracer already treats
it), so a guarding unit that sails away is warned `guard-dropped` exactly as one that marches. The
alternative — SAIL is not a departure — would contradict the trace the map draws for the same order.

## Out of scope

- `DIRECTION_SHORTHAND` / `abbreviateDirection` (`hexMapModel.ts:229–246`). Bishop listed it, but
  its two remaining readers after this bead (`RegionPanel.tsx:165`, `PlannerPanel.tsx:180`)
  abbreviate report *exit names* for display, and core never sends those abbreviated. With
  `routeAsOrder` gone it no longer writes an order, which was the mirror that mattered.
- Validating `disabledCodes` against `codes::ALL` at the wire (unknown codes stay ignored).
- Any other hand mirror (`ah-164` report types, `ah-wxk` command declarations, `ah-9n3` ruleset
  schema) — separate beads.
- Generating anything else from Rust; the generator renders exactly the two lists above.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core
ATLANTIS_UPDATE_GENERATED=1 cargo test -p atlantis-hud-core --test generated_ts   # then git diff shows no change
pnpm run check:fast
```

Human check (optional, Psylocke): in the desktop or web shell, give a guarding unit `SAIL N` in the
orders editor — the advisories now show `guard-dropped` for that hex, as they do for `MOVE N`.

## Known traps

- **`codes` must stay a child module of where `Code` is declared** (both in `semantics.rs`). Move it
  to its own file and it can no longer construct `Code(...)`, and the "cannot emit a bare literal"
  guarantee is the very thing you would then be tempted to loosen.
- **The intents `"SAIL" if arguments.is_empty()` arm must come before the `is_movement_command`
  guard arm**, or a bare `SAIL` reads as a move with no steps, `read_move_line` returns `None`, the
  `?` drops the intent, and a unit that spends its month sailing is offered as a spare teacher —
  the regression `is_busy` (`semantics.rs:248`) exists to prevent.
- **The generated file is written with `\n` and one trailing newline; `assert_eq!` compares bytes.**
  If a later editor "fixes" its formatting the test fails — that is the intended signal; regenerate
  rather than hand-edit.
- **`env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")` is `crates/core`**, whichever directory `cargo test` is run from,
  so `../../packages/core-client/src/...` is right from the workspace root and from the crate.
- **`RoutePlan` fixtures in TS are `RoutePlan`-typed literals**; a missed one is a typecheck error,
  not a runtime one — run `pnpm run typecheck` before assuming increment 5 is done.
- **The smoke suite is CI-only** and asserts the rendered order text; do not change the spacing or
  casing `render_move` produces.

title: Refactoring: the store's rules are written twice, in SQL and TypeScript, and diverge
description:
## The cost being paid
The desktop stores through core-persistence (SQLite, Rust) and the web through webStore/webCoreAdapter (IndexedDB, TypeScript); each owns its record shapes, its sighting-building and its whole backup codec, so every rule about what is stored or exported is written in both and can hold in one. One rule already diverged and was paid for as a bug fix inside an unrelated feature; one defect present in both had to be fixed across 13 files by moving the rule into core; every persisted concept since has landed in both codecs.

## Evidence
- 4e7c980 feat(ah-t65): "Also fixes a pre-existing browser defect this feature walks straight into: webStore's putRegionSightings had none of the last_seen_turn guard SQLite has always enforced, so importing an older report silently wrote its older account of a hex over a newer one" — SQL had it from 85fde8a (2026-08-08), the browser lacked it until 2026-08-12
- f153bf3 fix: classify what gets remembered — "both storage adapters built region sightings from the plain parse … the tilde on every merged unit"; 13 files
- 18d7e30 (#75): backup export/import written twice at birth (+577 Rust, +363 TS); 78a2aa7: GameBackupHexNote + SELECT + INSERT in Rust and GameBackupHexNote type + parseBackupJson block + export map + import put in TS
- Four twinned rules today guaranteed only by comments: webStore.ts supersedes ("The rule SQLite has always enforced … spelled the same way here"), latest-turn ranking ("matching the desktop's ORDER BY"), hex-note order, importedAt-preserved-on-reimport

## Where
crates/core-persistence/src/lib.rs (GameBackup* :213–280, export_game :513, import_game :648); packages/browser-core/src/webStore.ts; packages/browser-core/src/webCoreAdapter.ts (parseBackupJson :210, exportGame :695, importGame :775)

## What a refactoring would change
One owner per rule: either the rules that decide what a store keeps and what a backup contains move into core and both stores call them (the shape f153bf3 already used for classification, and serde-defined backup shapes the TS side validates against), or the web store becomes the Rust store behind wasm — which is what the dead wasm persistence arm was for. Not both, and not comments.

title: A core command is declared once per side, and every layer that carries it is checked by compile or test
description:
## The cost being paid
Adding one core call, or changing one argument of one, is a five-to-seven-file edit with nothing generated or type-checked across the language boundary: a `command_*` in core-tauri, a `*_state` fn (plus a wasm32 stub) in core-wasm, a `#[tauri::command]` wrapper and a `generate_handler!` entry in main.rs, six declarations in core-client (CoreAdapter, CoreClient, WasmBindings, createCoreClient, createWasmAdapter, createTauriAdapter), an IndexedDB twin in webCoreAdapter, and a SWEEP row in binding.spec.ts. 22 first-parent commits touched core-tauri + core-wasm + core-client + webCoreAdapter + main.rs together. One 8-field record with three operations cost 16 files / 1634 lines (78a2aa7); one read-only SELECT cost 9 files / 712 lines (9120935); a whole refactor bead was spent (171f13a, 11 files) so that one validate-orders option would stop "growing six signatures per toggle". Rules that live at this boundary are copied per method: 9cb908b (ah-6l2, P0) found two loaders missing the null-vs-undefined guard their sibling already carried.

## Evidence
- 78a2aa7 feat(ah-o1t.1): store manual hex notes with the game and its backup — 16 files, 1634 insertions
- 9120935 feat(ah-jg6.1): enumerate the imported turns of a game — 9 files; bead ah-jg6.1 design "Files to change": "core-client/src/index.ts — six edits, all with an existing neighbour to copy", "webCoreAdapter.ts — the third adapter, easily forgotten"
- 171f13a refactor(ah-m9q.1): order-check options cross the validation wire as one object — 11 files; bead ah-m9q.1 design §Context: "crosses the client/core boundary as a bare positional boolean through six signatures on two platforms"
- ce6150a feat(#113), f153bf3, 8b59d1d, 6ea7f50, f917be8, 07701e2, 55bc1c9 — each 5–6 of the same files
- 9cb908b fix(ah-6l2): "loadOrderDraft had the identical gap one function below and gets the same fix"; bead ah-6l2 notes, "CONFIRMED, real code defects" #2
- docs/retrospectives/ah-o1t.1.md §"A new Tauri command needs a matching entry in the native binding sweep" — "Every earlier layer (SQLite, backup, core-tauri, core-wasm, core-client, browser-core, shared)…"

## Where
apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs; crates/core-tauri/src/lib.rs; crates/core-wasm/src/lib.rs; packages/core-client/src/index.ts; packages/browser-core/src/webCoreAdapter.ts; tests/native/binding.spec.ts

## What a refactoring would change
One declaration of each command (name, arguments, result) that the Rust entry points, the handler list and the TypeScript adapters are generated from or checked against, so a new command is one edit and a missing layer is a compile or test failure. One result-normalising step in core-client (null/undefined, casing) instead of a guard per method. Sibling beads cover the SWEEP mirror, the dead wasm arm and the twin store separately.

Filed by Bishop, weekly sweep of 2026-08-15 (first sweep, whole of origin/main), range e60bbbd..150ba17.

notes:
Beast, 2026-08-16: this bead was labelled `planning` by Beast at 16:31 and split into ah-wxk.1–3 by Xavier at 16:39; the split stands and the children carry the plans. Beast's pre-split plan follows as reference — its TypeScript designs (a `TAURI_COMMANDS` table whose row arity is checked by a mapped tuple type, and `CoreAdapter` derived from `CoreClient` with three overrides) were verified to typecheck under TS 5.9 strict on 2026-08-16 and are reusable by ah-wxk.2/.3, whichever direction the derivation runs.

-----

## Context

Bishop, weekly sweep 2026-08-15: adding one core command, or changing one argument of one, is a
five-to-seven-file edit with nothing checked across the language boundary except the command's
*name* (`scripts/tauriCommands.test.ts` holds `main.rs`'s `generate_handler!` list, the sweep table
and `createTauriAdapter`'s `invoke("…")` literals to the same set — ah-ga6). Argument names are
checked only by the native sweep, over real IPC, on the Linux CI job. Planned by Beast on
2026-08-16.

What each layer is for, and what this bead does about it:

| Layer | Today | After |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/core-tauri` `command_*` | the desktop's logic, testable without Tauri | unchanged — it is the work |
| `crates/core-wasm` `*_state` | the web's entry to core logic | unchanged (ah-350 already removed the dead twin) |
| `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs` | 32 wrappers, **each under its own 4-line `#[cfg(all(…))]`**, + `generate_handler!` | the same 32 wrappers and list inside **one** cfg'd `mod desktop`; the file halves and a new wrapper is a plain `fn` |
| `packages/core-client` `CoreClient` | the shell's typed API | unchanged — **the one declaration** |
| `packages/core-client` `CoreAdapter` | 32 method signatures hand-copied from `CoreClient` (:861–971) | **derived** from `CoreClient` by a mapped type; the three methods the client pre-serialises for are the only ones spelled out |
| `packages/core-client` `createTauriAdapter` | 32 hand-written `invoke("cmd", { snake_key: camelArg, … })` bodies (:2026–2291) | **a table**, `TAURI_COMMANDS`, one row per method: command name + argument keys, arity **checked by the type system** against `CoreAdapter`; `createTauriAdapter` is built from the table |
| `packages/core-client` `createCoreClient` | a null/undefined guard and an array guard copied per method (ah-6l2 found two loaders without theirs) | two helpers, `optional()` and `list()`, used by every such method |
| `packages/browser-core` `webCoreAdapter` | implements `CoreAdapter` | unchanged; a method missing is already a typecheck failure and stays one |
| `scripts/tauriCommands.ts` | names only | also **parameter names**: reads each `#[tauri::command] fn` in `main.rs`, and holds `TAURI_COMMANDS`' keys and the sweep's argument keys to them — on every machine, in `test:tooling` |
| `tests/native/sweep.ts` | hand table | unchanged (its keys are now checked against `main.rs`, so a drift is caught before the Linux job) |

**Rejected: `tauri-specta`** (generated typed `commands.ts` from `#[tauri::command]`). It needs
`specta::Type` on every DTO that crosses — a second type generator beside the `ts-rs` that ah-164.2
(in progress) is putting on the core types — and it types the web adapter not at all. **Rejected: a
`macro_rules!` DSL in `main.rs`** generating the wrappers: each row would still declare the
signature and the call, and the tooling parser would have to learn the DSL. The plain wrappers
stay because they are what the tooling reads.

After this bead a new command touches: `command_*` (the work), one `fn` in `main.rs` plus its
`generate_handler!` entry (name and parameter names both checked), one `CoreClient` method + its
`createCoreClient` body (the API), one `TAURI_COMMANDS` row (arity checked at compile time, keys
checked against `main.rs`), the web adapter method (compile-checked), and one sweep row (checked).
Every layer that used to be forgotten silently now fails a typecheck or `test:tooling`.

**Coordinate with ah-164.2** (Storm, in progress at planning time): it rewrites the report-family
types and normalisers in `index.ts` and leaves `CoreAdapter`, `createTauriAdapter` and the
game/turn/draft/note normalisers alone. Branch after it merges; the line numbers here are `main` at
706ea51 and will have moved — search by symbol.

## Files to change, and what to reuse

### `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs`

Move everything currently under the repeated
`#[cfg(all(any(target_os = "linux", target_os = "macos", target_os = "windows"), feature = "desktop-runtime"))]`
into one module carrying that attribute once:

```rust
#[cfg(all(
    any(target_os = "linux", target_os = "macos", target_os = "windows"),
    feature = "desktop-runtime"
))]
mod desktop {
    use atlantis_hud_core::{EngineInfo, OrderValidationResult, ReportParseResultWire};
    use atlantis_hud_core_tauri::{ /* the existing two import lists, merged */ };

    /// Where this installation keeps its games. (doc unchanged)
    fn games_root(app: &tauri::AppHandle) -> Result<String, String> { /* unchanged */ }

    #[tauri::command(rename_all = "snake_case")]
    fn get_engine_info() -> EngineInfo { command_get_engine_info() }
    // … every wrapper exactly as it is, minus its own #[cfg] …

    pub fn run() {
        tauri::Builder::default()
            /* the existing builder chain, :5xx, unchanged */
            .invoke_handler(tauri::generate_handler![ /* the existing list, unchanged */ ])
            .run(tauri::generate_context!())
            .expect("error while running atlantis-hud desktop shell");
    }
}

#[cfg(all(any(target_os = "linux", target_os = "macos", target_os = "windows"), feature = "desktop-runtime"))]
fn main() { desktop::run(); }

#[cfg(not(all(/* same */)))]
```
